title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
浙江鄉試錄序
皇上御極四十年于兹歲應大比
畿省之士以貢于
朝維浙江巡按監察御史崔棟
寔祗厥載走幣數千里外聘
呈英及教諭管惟乾爲考試
官學正李棟教諭蘇黎庶周
===
南韓孜張廷儀楊保慶任賢
蔣自觀爲同考試官比至間
御史所徵簾以外百執事具
在一切筦鑰動中繩畫惟謹
惟毖且各籍其所司俾守之
籍既定檄布政使司左布政
使胡堯臣右參政杜拯知提
punctuated:
浙江鄉試錄序

皇上御極四十年于兹，歲應大比，畿省之士以貢于朝。維浙江巡按監察御史崔棟，寔祗厥載，走幣數千里外，聘呈英及教諭管惟乾爲考試官，學正李棟、教諭蘇黎庶、周南、韓孜、張廷儀、楊保慶、任賢、蔣自觀爲同考試官。比至間，御史所徵簾以外百執事具在，一切筦鑰，動中繩畫，惟謹惟毖，且各籍其所司，俾守之。籍既定，檄布政使司左布政使胡堯臣、右參政杜拯知提
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Zhejiang Provincial Examination

It was now forty years since His Majesty had ascended the throne, and the year fell due for the triennial examination, through which scholars from the metropolitan regions and provinces were presented to the court. Cui Dong, the Regional Inspector of Zhejiang and Investigating Censor, faithfully discharged his responsibilities, sending betrothal gifts for the appointments over several thousand li to engage Chengying and the School Instructor Guan Weiqian as Examiners, and School Director Li Dong and School Instructors Su Lishu, Zhou Nan, Han Zi, Zhang Tingyi, Yang Baoqing, Ren Xian, and Jiang Ziguan as Associate Examiners.

By the time we arrived [?], all the personnel whom the Censor had summoned to serve outside the examination curtain were present. Every arrangement for locks and keys conformed to the prescribed rules, with care and vigilance throughout. Each person's responsibilities were also entered in a register so that he could adhere to them. Once the register was settled, official instructions were issued to Hu Yaochen, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, and Du Zheng, Right Administration Vice Commissioner, of the Provincial Administration Commission, to take charge of the proctoring …

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
調按察司副使王春澤僉事
陳宗虞監試事維日丙寅迺
羣提學副使范惟一所選校
諸郡縣之士四千有奇而試
之越明日丁卯恭逢我
皇上萬歲聖節御史合呈英等稽
首頓首北嚮祝曰願
===
聖天子萬壽永保民又祝曰願得
士之賢者如古俊乂以長佐
聖天子永保民無斁己巳再試壬
申三試得其中式者九十人
間次其文蓋彬彬然洋洋然
昭代之音而經世之具也幾於
道矣爰校其尤者二十篇以
punctuated:
調，按察司副使王春澤、僉事陳宗虞監試事。維日丙寅，迺羣提學副使范惟一所選校諸郡縣之士四千有奇而試之。越明日丁卯，恭逢我皇上萬歲聖節，御史合呈英等稽首頓首，北嚮祝曰：「願聖天子萬壽，永保民！」又祝曰：「願得士之賢者，如古俊乂，以長佐聖天子，永保民無斁！」
己巳再試，壬申三試，得其中式者九十人。間次其文，蓋彬彬然、洋洋然，昭代之音，而經世之具也，幾於道矣！爰校其尤者二十篇以
translation_en:
…proctoring duties, while Wang Chunze, Vice Commissioner of the Provincial Surveillance Commission, and Chen Zongyu, its Assistant Commissioner, oversaw the examination proceedings. On the bingyin day, more than four thousand scholars from the various prefectures and counties, selected and assessed by Fan Weiyi, Vice Commissioner for Education, were assembled and examined. The following day, dingmao, respectfully marked the sacred birthday of our emperor—may he live ten thousand years. The Censor, together with Chengying and the others, bowed their heads to the ground and repeatedly kowtowed. Facing north, they offered this prayer: “May the sagely Son of Heaven enjoy ten thousand years of life and protect the people forever!” They further prayed: “May we obtain worthy scholars, like the outstanding men of antiquity, to assist the sagely Son of Heaven for years to come in protecting the people forever, without weariness!”
On the jisi day the second session was held, and on the renshen day the third. Ninety candidates qualified. On arranging their essays in order [?], we found them refined and abundant: the voice of an enlightened age and instruments for ordering the world. They came close indeed to the Way! We therefore selected twenty of the finest essays in order to…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
獻屬呈英敘諸首簡呈英廼再
拜稽首颺言曰夫爾諸士之
獲升于斯也其亦知我
皇上所以作新之功矣乎棫樸之
詩曰周王壽考遐不作人蓋
言維文王之德之純之久久
則徵徵則動動則變而化故
===
四海九州之士因以有作而
莫不追琢其章金玉其相瑟
然濟濟以無負周之王國焉
時楨榦而敷天下之化卽天
下之民亦皆惠鮮怙冒如萬
物之覆燾澤露於天地風雨
號稱至治故曰唐虞之際於
punctuated: 獻，屬呈英敘諸首簡。呈英廼再拜稽首，颺言曰：「夫爾諸士之獲升于斯也，其亦知我皇上所以作新之功矣乎？《棫樸》之詩曰：『周王壽考，遐不作人。』蓋言維文王之德之純之久，久則徵，徵則動，動則變而化。故四海九州之士因以有作，而莫不追琢其章，金玉其相，瑟然濟濟，以無負周之王國焉。時楨榦而敷天下之化，卽天下之民亦皆惠鮮怙冒，如萬物之覆燾澤露於天地風雨，號稱至治。故曰：『唐虞之際，於
translation_en: …to present them, and entrusted Chengying with writing a preface at the beginning of the volume. Chengying then bowed twice, knocked his head to the ground, and proclaimed: “You scholars who have gained advancement here—do you understand the achievement by which our Emperor has renewed and inspired you? The poem ‘Luxuriant Oaks’ (Yupu) says: ‘May the king of Zhou live long! Does he not nurture men of talent?’ This speaks of the purity and enduring constancy of King Wen’s virtue: enduring, it becomes manifest; manifest, it moves others; moving them, it changes and transforms them. Thus scholars throughout the Four Seas and Nine Provinces were stirred to rise, all carving and polishing their accomplishments and making their substance like gold and jade, solemn and dignified, so as not to fail the royal state of Zhou. Serving as its pillars [?], they spread its transforming influence throughout the realm. Even the common people everywhere received kindness and renewal, finding support and shelter, just as all things are sheltered and moistened by Heaven and Earth, wind and rain. This was acclaimed as the perfection of government. Hence the saying: ‘In the time of Tang and Yu, at …

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
斯爲盛仲尼蓋深幸竊歎之
矣寥寥數千載
聖天子迓續靈承餘四十年所治
極而徵靈貺疊應而
神武明聖羣臣震慴亦奚羨於唐
虞之理〔呈英〕嘗竊跡後先所
下
===
詔令戒敕箴儆賦詠其所爲拳拳
乎正人心而易士習者總之
追琢磨切天下之士俾之乃
玉乃金精純輝瑩大者爲圭
爲璋次者爲瑚爲璉以恭事
天地百神
宗廟社稷以共保我
punctuated: 斯爲盛，仲尼蓋深幸竊歎之矣。寥寥數千載，聖天子迓續靈承餘四十年，所治極而徵，靈貺疊應，而神武明聖，羣臣震慴，亦奚羨於唐虞之理？〔呈英〕嘗竊跡後先所下詔令、戒敕、箴儆、賦詠，其所爲拳拳乎正人心而易士習者，總之，追琢磨切天下之士，俾之乃玉乃金，精純輝瑩，大者爲圭爲璋，次者爲瑚爲璉，以恭事天地百神、宗廟社稷，以共保我
translation_en:
…at this time it flourished most. Zhongni [Confucius] surely rejoiced deeply in this and privately sighed in admiration. Several thousand years have elapsed since then. Our sagely Son of Heaven has received and continued the sacred succession for more than forty years. His governance has reached its highest perfection and manifests auspicious signs [?]; heavenly blessings have responded in succession. Divinely martial, perspicacious, and sagely, he inspires awe and trembling among his assembled ministers. What cause, then, is there to envy the governance of Tang and Yu [Yao and Shun]?

〔Chengying〕 has ventured to trace the edicts and commands, admonitory instructions, exhortations and warnings, and rhapsodies and poems issued over this time. Their earnest concern has been to rectify people’s hearts and transform the habits of scholars. Taken together, they carve, polish, grind, and refine the scholars of the realm, making them jade and gold, pure in substance and radiant in brilliance. The greatest become gui and zhang jade tablets; the next become hu and lian ritual vessels. Thus they may reverently serve Heaven and Earth and the hundred divinities, the ancestral temples, and the altars of soil and grain, and together safeguard our…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
皇烈祖所遺之羣黎萬姓蓋靡一
念不斯勤焉此其勞其久視
周王百矣爾多士乃或不能
精純輝瑩瑚璉圭璋如彼中
林兔罝之士所以報周王者
則
皇上曷以寧爾多士曷以宴焉夫
===
上以圭璋瑚璉精純輝瑩相追琢
磨切而固自菲薄弗能仰副
且甘為碔若砆焉則惡乎取
夫碔之與砆雖其疎厲觕駁
不足登
宗廟明堂之用然其體質分量未
嘗敢鑿損其天人未深病也
punctuated: 皇烈祖所遺之羣黎萬姓，蓋靡一念不斯勤焉。此其勞其久，視周王百矣。爾多士乃或不能精純輝瑩，瑚璉圭璋，如彼中林兔罝之士所以報周王者，則皇上曷以寧？爾多士曷以宴焉？夫上以圭璋瑚璉精純輝瑩相追琢磨切，而固自菲薄，弗能仰副，且甘為碔若砆焉，則惡乎取？夫碔之與砆，雖其疎厲觕駁，不足登宗廟明堂之用，然其體質分量，未嘗敢鑿損其天，人未深病也。
translation_en: … the multitudes of common people bequeathed by the august and illustrious ancestors. Surely not a single thought fails to attend diligently to this. In the toil and duration of these efforts, he surpasses the king of Zhou a hundredfold. Yet some among you scholars cannot attain purity and radiant brilliance, becoming sacrificial vessels of jade and millet or ceremonial jade tablets, as did those rabbit-net setters in the forest in their service to the king of Zhou. How, then, can His Majesty find peace? How can you scholars rest at ease? His Majesty carves, polishes, and refines you to make you into ceremonial jades and sacrificial vessels, pure and radiant; yet you persist in belittling yourselves, unable to fulfill his expectations, and willingly become mere stones resembling jade. What use, then, can be made of you? Such imitation-jade stones, though coarse, rough, and mottled, and unfit for use in the ancestral temple or the Hall of Enlightenment, have nevertheless never presumed to chisel away or damage their natural substance and measure. People therefore find no grave fault with them.

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
至廼掩玉以爲表而匿其繆
戾罔知懷仁義以事君甚自
湛穢次滓壤而莫之灑祓則
世且掩面疾趨惟恐其投畀
之弗逖矣今爾多士之文美
則美矣余懼殆於所稱巧笑
之瑳雜珮之儺而將貽
===
聖世風人之刺也故特重申儆焉
卷阿之什曰顒顒卬卬令聞
令望豈弟君子四方爲綱如
此卽爾多士信周之士而余
主司輩蓋亦洵美且華矣於
乎其勗諸於乎其尚勗諸時
總督撫巡則太子太保兵部
punctuated:
至廼掩玉以爲表，而匿其繆戾，罔知懷仁義以事君，甚自湛穢，次滓壤而莫之灑祓，則世且掩面疾趨，惟恐其投畀之弗逖矣。今爾多士之文，美則美矣，余懼殆於所稱「巧笑之瑳，雜珮之儺」，而將貽聖世風人之刺也，故特重申儆焉。
《卷阿》之什曰：「顒顒卬卬，令聞令望，豈弟君子，四方爲綱。」如此，卽爾多士信周之士，而余主司輩蓋亦洵美且華矣。於乎，其勗諸！於乎，其尚勗諸！
時總督撫巡，則太子太保兵部
translation_en:
Yet when someone uses jade as an outward covering to conceal his perversity, knowing nothing of cherishing benevolence and righteousness in serving his ruler, deeply immersing himself in filth and dwelling amid dregs and dirt [?] without cleansing himself, people will cover their faces and hurry away, fearing only that he has not been cast far enough off. Now, you gentlemen’s compositions are indeed beautiful. But I fear that they approach what is described as “the brilliance of her charming smile, the graceful sway of her assorted pendants,” and will invite a poet’s censure in this sage age. I therefore expressly repeat this warning.
The ode “Winding Hills” (Juan E) says: “Dignified and lofty, of excellent reputation and prestige, these amiable gentlemen serve as a guiding cord for the four quarters.” If you conduct yourselves thus, you gentlemen will truly be like the worthy men of Zhou, and we who preside over the examination may likewise be deemed “truly beautiful and splendid.” Ah, strive for this! Ah, may you indeed strive for this!
At this time, supreme command and provincial supervision were in the charge of the Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, Ministry of War …

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
尚書兼右都御史胡宗憲載
揚
天子之命揆文奮武士克安其業
總理鹽法左副都御史鄢懋
卿巡鹽監察御史袁淳所至
問俗崇道右儒學者嚮風焉
乃若戶部員外郎黃乾行工
===
部主事馮符南京戶部主事
黎元中書舍人張元孝行人
鄧楚望趙格則各以使事萃
于斯咸胥嘉樂至右布政使
胡松時雖已被巡撫江西之
命矣而
璽書未至嘗與勤焉其他若參議
punctuated: 尚書兼右都御史胡宗憲，載揚天子之命，揆文奮武，士克安其業。總理鹽法左副都御史鄢懋卿、巡鹽監察御史袁淳，所至問俗，崇道右儒，學者嚮風焉。乃若戶部員外郎黃乾行、工部主事馮符、南京戶部主事黎元、中書舍人張元孝、行人鄧楚望、趙格，則各以使事萃于斯，咸胥嘉樂。至右布政使胡松，時雖已被巡撫江西之命矣，而璽書未至，嘗與勤焉。其他若參議
translation_en:
…Minister [of War] and concurrently Right Censor-in-Chief Hu Zongxian upheld and proclaimed the Son of Heaven’s commands, directing civil affairs and invigorating military endeavors, so that scholars could pursue their studies in peace. Yan Maoqing, Left Vice Censor-in-Chief administering the salt regulations, and Yuan Chun, Investigating Censor for salt surveillance, inquired into local customs wherever they went, honored the Way, and supported Confucian scholars; students looked to their example.

Huang Qianxing, Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue; Feng Fu, Secretary in the Ministry of Works; Li Yuan, Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue; Zhang Yuanxiao, Drafter in the Secretariat; and Deng Chuwang and Zhao Ge, Messengers, each gathered here on official missions and all shared in the rejoicing. As for Hu Song, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner, although he had already been appointed Grand Coordinator of Jiangxi, the imperial letter bearing the seal had not yet arrived, and he too contributed to the work. Others included the Assistant Administration Commissioners…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
唐愛于錦副使劉存德凌雲
翼李燧李僑宋守志僉事歸
大道唐堯臣徐栻署都指揮
僉事鄭維清王顥均之以董
成於外而叅政谷中虛僉事
曹天祐署都指揮僉事管海
則雖先期以入
===
賀行而故事得書廼併錄其名
若氏焉
江西南昌府新建縣儒學敎
諭李呈英謹序
punctuated:
唐愛、于錦，副使劉存德、凌雲翼、李燧、李僑、宋守志，僉事歸大道、唐堯臣、徐栻，署都指揮僉事鄭維清、王顥，均之以董成於外。而叅政谷中虛、僉事曹天祐、署都指揮僉事管海，則雖先期以入賀行，而故事得書，廼併錄其名若氏焉。
江西南昌府新建縣儒學敎諭李呈英謹序。
translation_en:
…Tang Ai and Yu Jin, Assistant Administration Commissioners; Liu Cunde, Ling Yunyi, Li Sui, Li Qiao, and Song Shouzhi, Surveillance Vice Commissioners; Gui Dadao, Tang Yaochen, and Xu Shi, Assistant Surveillance Commissioners; and Zheng Weiqing and Wang Hao, Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners—all supervised the work outside the examination compound and brought it to completion. Although Gu Zhongxu, Administration Vice Commissioner, Cao Tianyou, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner, and Guan Hai, Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner, had departed beforehand to offer congratulations at court, established precedent permits their inclusion, so their names and surnames are recorded together here as well.
Preface respectfully written by Li Chengying, Instructor of the Confucian School of Xinjian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi.

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試
監臨官
巡按浙江監察御史崔棟〔孔材順天府薊州人庚戌進士〕
提調官
浙江等處承宣布政使司左布政使胡堯臣〔伯純四川安居縣人戊戌進士〕
浙江等處承宣布政使司右參政杜拯〔道濟江西豐城縣人戊戌進士〕
監試官
浙江等處提刑按察司副使王春澤〔以潤福建漳浦縣人丁未進士〕
浙江等處提刑按察司僉事陳宗虞〔于韶四川保寧千戶所籍直隸儀真縣人庚戌進士〕
===
考試官
江西南昌府新建縣儒學教諭李呈英〔士發廣西桂林中衛官籍湖廣鍾祥縣人壬子貢士〕
廣東肇慶府高明縣儒學教諭管惟乾〔體仁廣西桂林中衛軍籍湖廣黃梅縣人乙卯貢士〕
同考試官
直隸大名府開州儒學學正李棟〔邦隆江西吉水縣人壬子貢士〕
河南開封府延津縣儒學教諭蘇黎庶〔仁伯廣東番禺縣人丙午貢士〕
湖廣長沙府醴陵縣儒學教諭周南〔化夫四川巴縣人丙午貢士〕
山東濟南府德州德平縣儒學教諭韓孜〔勉之應天府高淳縣人壬子貢士〕
直隸池州府貴池縣儒學教諭張廷儀〔肅之江西浮梁縣人壬子貢士〕
punctuated:
嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試

監臨官
巡按浙江監察御史崔棟〔孔材，順天府薊州人，庚戌進士〕。

提調官
浙江等處承宣布政使司左布政使胡堯臣〔伯純，四川安居縣人，戊戌進士〕。
浙江等處承宣布政使司右參政杜拯〔道濟，江西豐城縣人，戊戌進士〕。

監試官
浙江等處提刑按察司副使王春澤〔以潤，福建漳浦縣人，丁未進士〕。
浙江等處提刑按察司僉事陳宗虞〔于韶，四川保寧千戶所籍，直隸儀真縣人，庚戌進士〕。

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
君子欲訥於言而敏於行
是以聲名洋溢乎中國施及蠻貊舟車所
至人力所通天之所覆地之所載日月
所照霜露所隊凡有血氣者莫不尊親
故曰配天
乃若其情則可以為善矣乃所謂善也
易
===
君子以教思无窮容保民无疆
觀其所聚而天地萬物之情可見矣
引而伸之觸類而長之
兼三才而兩之故易六畫而成卦分陰分
陽迭用柔剛故易六位而成章
書
元首明哉股肱良哉
四海之內咸仰朕德
皇建其有極斂時五福
punctuated:
第壹場

四書
君子欲訥於言而敏於行。
是以聲名洋溢乎中國，施及蠻貊，舟車所至，人力所通，天之所覆，地之所載，日月所照，霜露所隊，凡有血氣者，莫不尊親，故曰配天。
乃若其情，則可以為善矣，乃所謂善也。

易
君子以教思无窮，容保民无疆。
觀其所聚，而天地萬物之情可見矣。
引而伸之，觸類而長之。
兼三才而兩之，故易六畫而成卦；分陰分陽，迭用柔剛，故易六位而成章。

書
元首明哉，股肱良哉！
四海之內，咸仰朕德。
皇建其有極，斂時五福。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books
The gentleman wishes to be slow in speech and quick in action.
Thus his fame spreads abundantly throughout the Central States and extends to the Man and Mo peoples. Wherever boats and carriages reach, wherever human effort penetrates, wherever heaven covers and earth bears, wherever sun and moon shine and frost and dew fall—all who possess blood and breath honor and love him. Hence it is said that he matches Heaven.
As for their inherent dispositions, these enable them to do good. This is what is meant by calling human nature good.

Book of Changes
The gentleman accordingly gives unending thought to teaching and embraces and protects the people without limit.
By observing what things gather together, one can discern the true circumstances of heaven, earth, and the myriad things.
Draw it out and extend it; apply it to analogous cases and enlarge it.
It encompasses the Three Powers—heaven, earth, and humanity—and doubles them; thus, in the Changes, six lines form a hexagram. Yin and yang are distinguished, and yielding and firm lines are employed alternately; thus, in the Changes, the six positions form a patterned whole.

Book of Documents
How enlightened is the head! How worthy are the limbs!
All within the Four Seas look up to my virtue.
The sovereign establishes the supreme standard and gathers these five blessings.

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
立政任人準夫牧作三事虎賁綴衣趣馬
小尹左右攜僕百司庶府大都小伯藝
人表臣百司太史尹伯庶常吉士
詩
南有樛木葛藟縈之樂只君子福履成之
天保定爾以莫不興如山如阜如岡如陵
如川之方至以莫不增
思皇多士生此王國王國克生維周之楨
旣和且平依我磬聲
===
春秋
夏公子慶父帥師伐於餘丘〔莊公二年〕夏
季孫行父如齊〔宣公元年〕
八月公會齊侯宋公鄭伯曹伯邾人于檉
〔僖公元年〕秋齊侯宋公江人黃人會于
陽穀〔僖公三年〕
單伯至自齊〔文公十有五年〕
夏叔孫豹會晉趙武楚屈建蔡公孫歸生
衛石惡陳孔奐鄭良霄許人曹人于宋
punctuated:
立政：任人、準夫、牧，作三事；虎賁、綴衣、趣馬、小尹、左右攜僕、百司庶府、大都小伯、藝人、表臣、百司、太史、尹伯、庶常吉士。

詩
南有樛木，葛藟縈之。樂只君子，福履成之。
天保定爾，以莫不興。如山如阜，如岡如陵，如川之方至，以莫不增。
思皇多士，生此王國。王國克生，維周之楨。
旣和且平，依我磬聲。

春秋
夏，公子慶父帥師伐於餘丘〔莊公二年〕。夏，季孫行父如齊〔宣公元年〕。
八月，公會齊侯、宋公、鄭伯、曹伯、邾人于檉〔僖公元年〕。秋，齊侯、宋公、江人、黃人會于陽穀〔僖公三年〕。
單伯至自齊〔文公十有五年〕。
夏，叔孫豹會晉趙武、楚屈建、蔡公孫歸生、衛石惡、陳孔奐、鄭良霄、許人、曹人于宋
translation_en:
In establishing government, those responsible for appointments, those administering justice, and governors constitute the three principal offices; then come the Tiger Guards, keepers of the robes, overseers of horses, lesser directors, attendant servants to the left and right, the various officials and storehouse officers, lesser chiefs of the great cities, skilled men, officials stationed outside the court, the various officeholders, the Grand Scribe, directors and chiefs, and the worthy men in regular service.

Book of Odes
In the south are trees with drooping branches; kudzu and other vines entwine them. Joyful is the gentleman; blessings bring him fulfillment.
Heaven protects and establishes you, so that nothing fails to flourish. Like mountains and hills, like ridges and high mounds, like a river swelling toward its height—may nothing fail to increase.
How splendid are the many worthy men born in this royal kingdom! The royal kingdom can indeed bring them forth; they are the pillars of Zhou.
Harmonious and balanced, they follow the sound of our chime stones.

Spring and Autumn Annals
In summer, Prince Qingfu led an army to attack Yuyuqiu. 〔Second year of Duke Zhuang.〕 In summer, Jisun Xingfu went to Qi. 〔First year of Duke Xuan.〕
In the eighth month, the duke met the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, and a representative of Zhu at Cheng. 〔First year of Duke Xi.〕 In autumn, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, and representatives of Jiang and Huang met at Yanggu. 〔Third year of Duke Xi.〕
The Earl of Shan arrived from Qi. 〔Fifteenth year of Duke Wen.〕
In summer, Shusun Bao met Zhao Wu of Jin, Qu Jian of Chu, Gongsun Guisheng of Cai, Shi E of Wei, Kong Huan of Chen, Liang Xiao of Zheng, and representatives of Xu and Cao at Song …

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
〔襄公二十有七年〕叔孫豹會晉趙武楚
公子圍齊國弱宋向戌衛齊惡陳公子
招蔡公孫歸生鄭罕虎許人曹人于虢
〔昭公元年〕
禮記
天子祭天地祭四方祭山川祭五祀歲徧
諸侯方祀祭山川祭五祀歲徧大夫祭
五祀歲徧士祭其先
故人情者聖王之田也脩禮以耕之陳義
===
以種之講學以耨之本仁以聚之播樂
以安之
論倫無患樂之情也欣喜歡愛樂之官也
中正無邪禮之質也莊敬恭順禮之制
也若夫禮樂之施於金石越於聲音用
於宗廟社稷事乎山川鬼神則此所與
民同也
尊讓絜敬也者君子之所以相接也
第貳塲
punctuated:
〔襄公二十有七年〕叔孫豹會晉趙武、楚公子圍、齊國弱、宋向戌、衛齊惡、陳公子招、蔡公孫歸生、鄭罕虎、許人、曹人于虢。〔昭公元年〕
禮記
天子祭天地，祭四方，祭山川，祭五祀，歲徧；諸侯方祀，祭山川，祭五祀，歲徧；大夫祭五祀，歲徧；士祭其先。
故人情者，聖王之田也。脩禮以耕之，陳義以種之，講學以耨之，本仁以聚之，播樂以安之。
論倫無患，樂之情也；欣喜歡愛，樂之官也；中正無邪，禮之質也；莊敬恭順，禮之制也。若夫禮樂之施於金石，越於聲音，用於宗廟社稷，事乎山川鬼神，則此所與民同也。
尊讓絜敬也者，君子之所以相接也。
第貳塲
translation_en:
…〔Twenty-seventh year of Duke Xiang〕 Shusun Bao met at Guo with Zhao Wu of Jin, Prince Wei of Chu, Guo Ruo of Qi, Xiang Xu of Song, Qi E of Wei, Prince Zhao of Chen, Gongsun Guisheng of Cai, Han Hu of Zheng, and representatives of Xu and Cao. 〔First year of Duke Zhao〕
Record of Rites (Liji)
The Son of Heaven sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, to the four quarters, to the mountains and rivers, and to the deities of the five household sacrifices, completing the cycle each year. The feudal lords sacrifice within their territories, offering sacrifices to the mountains and rivers and the deities of the five household sacrifices, completing the cycle each year. Great officers offer the five household sacrifices, completing the cycle each year. Men of the shi rank sacrifice to their ancestors.
Thus human feelings are the field of the sage king. He cultivates ritual propriety to plough it, sets forth righteousness to sow it, expounds learning to weed it, takes benevolence as the foundation to gather its harvest, and spreads music to bring it peace.
Ordered human relationships free from trouble are the essential character of music; delight, joy, affection, and love are its functions. Centrality and correctness without perversity are the substance of ritual; solemnity, reverence, respect, and deference are its forms. As for ritual and music being expressed through bells and chime stones, issuing forth in sounds, being employed in ancestral temples and at the altars of soil and grain, and serving the spirits of mountains and rivers and other spiritual beings—these are what the ruler shares with the people.
Esteem, deference, purity, and reverence are the means by which gentlemen engage with one another.
Second Session

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
論
聖人之仁如天地
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢賜民今年田租之半詔〔文帝二年〕
擬唐以房玄齡杜如晦爲僕射誥〔貞觀三年〕
擬宋開天章閣引輔臣入對謝表〔慶曆三年〕
判語〔五條〕
===
選用軍職
隱蔽差役
服舍違式
門禁鎖鑰
盜賊捕限
第叁場
策五道
問帝王之道與天地竝而其學與政韋布不
同故於經綸之迹凡以垂訓當時昭鑒
punctuated:
論
聖人之仁如天地。

詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢賜民今年田租之半詔〔文帝二年〕。
擬唐以房玄齡杜如晦爲僕射誥〔貞觀三年〕。
擬宋開天章閣引輔臣入對謝表〔慶曆三年〕。

判語〔五條〕
選用軍職。
隱蔽差役。
服舍違式。
門禁鎖鑰。
盜賊捕限。

第叁場
策五道。
問：帝王之道與天地竝，而其學與政韋布不同，故於經綸之迹，凡以垂訓當時、昭鑒
translation_en:
Discourse
“The benevolence of the sage is like Heaven and Earth.”

Edicts, proclamations, and memorials 〔One topic from among these [?]〕
Compose an edict in the manner of the Han dynasty remitting half of the people’s land tax for the current year. 〔Second year of Emperor Wen’s reign〕
Compose a proclamation in the manner of the Tang dynasty appointing Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui as Vice Directors of the Department of State Affairs. 〔Third year of Zhenguan〕
Compose a memorial of thanks in the manner of the Song dynasty for opening the Tianzhang Pavilion and summoning the chief ministers to an imperial audience. 〔Third year of Qingli〕

Legal judgments 〔Five topics〕
Selection and appointment of military officers.
Concealment to evade compulsory service.
Clothing and dwellings that violate prescribed standards.
Gate security, locks, and keys.
Time limits for apprehending thieves and bandits.

Third Session
Five policy questions.
Question: The Way of emperors and kings ranks alongside Heaven and Earth, and their learning and governance differ from those of commoners. Thus, among the traces of their ordering of the realm, all that serves to transmit instruction to their own times and provide an illuminating mirror …

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
後世者雖一言動要莫不有所紀也精
一執中之傳典謨訓誥之記唐虞三代
不可尚矣降是英君誼辟間知嚮慕若
石渠集賢崇政諸所舉動為時侈美不
知於帝王之道抑有得乎否耶洪惟我
太祖高皇帝定鼎中夏混一區宇創制立法悉
根理道今考
聖政日曆
皇明政要所載其於易書大學語孟及前代諸
===
史多所發明至於
御製文集
御註洪範
資世通訓
大明集禮之頒宏綱要旨胥不外是誠有以兼
乎古帝王而大備焉
成憲至今煥然可述迨我
皇上光昭鴻烈度越千古憲經崇典制作一新
于稽其大如
punctuated: 後世者，雖一言動，要莫不有所紀也。精一執中之傳，典謨訓誥之記，唐虞三代不可尚矣。降是，英君誼辟間知嚮慕，若石渠、集賢、崇政諸所，舉動為時侈美，不知於帝王之道抑有得乎否耶？洪惟我太祖高皇帝定鼎中夏，混一區宇，創制立法，悉根理道。今考《聖政日曆》《皇明政要》所載，其於《易》《書》《大學》《語》《孟》及前代諸史，多所發明。至於《御製文集》《御註洪範》《資世通訓》《大明集禮》之頒，宏綱要旨，胥不外是，誠有以兼乎古帝王而大備焉。成憲至今，煥然可述。迨我皇上光昭鴻烈，度越千古，憲經崇典，制作一新。于稽其大，如
translation_en:
…later generations: even a single utterance or action was invariably recorded. In the transmission of the teaching to be discerning and single-minded and to hold fast to the mean, and in the records preserved in the canons, counsels, instructions, and announcements, the ages of Tang Yao, Yu Shun, and the Three Dynasties cannot be surpassed. Thereafter, enlightened rulers and righteous sovereigns occasionally showed an understanding of these ideals and an aspiration toward them. Their undertakings at such establishments as Shiqu, Jixian, and Chongzheng were lavishly praised in their day; yet did they attain anything of the Way of emperors and kings, or not?

We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao established his capital in the central lands and unified the realm. His creation of institutions and establishment of laws were all rooted in principle and the Way. Examining what is recorded in the Daily Record of Sagely Governance and the Essentials of Governance of the August Ming, we find that he elucidated much in the Book of Changes, the Book of Documents, the Great Learning, the Analects, the Mencius, and the histories of preceding dynasties. As for the promulgation of the Collected Imperial Writings, the Imperial Commentary on the Great Plan, the General Instructions for Aiding the World, and the Collected Rituals of the Great Ming, their broad principles and essential purport likewise remained within this compass. Truly, he brought together the achievements of the ancient emperors and kings and realized them in full. His established institutions remain illustrious to this day and can still be recounted.

Coming to our reigning Emperor, he has gloriously illuminated these grand achievements and surpassed all past ages. Taking the classics as his standard and honoring the canonical texts, he has renewed institutions and regulations throughout. Examining the major examples, such as…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
敬一有箴五箴有註解大學本末之章以
頒史館揭尚書無逸之篇以勤稼穡
經筵進講每及於諸書
深宮遍閱不遺乎列史旣又
特命儒臣表章
列聖寶訓累朝實錄以藏石室以垂鑒戒凡若
事
天法
祖敬身勤民之實則皆卓有可紀者焉是其心
===
學之淵源純王之政迹真足以匹休唐
虞三代之隆陋漢唐宋於不居者諸士
漸被
聖化訓典之服膺也久矣玆維敷言之際其尚
悉心對揚以鳴我
國家文治之盛
問古昔聖帝明王制為典禮尤慎於交神
明之際經傳所載詳矣論者謂自秦滅
學歷代之祀或取俚儒無根之說雜傳
punctuated:
敬一有箴，五箴有註，解大學本末之章以頒史館，揭尚書無逸之篇以勤稼穡。經筵進講，每及於諸書；深宮遍閱，不遺乎列史。旣又特命儒臣表章列聖寶訓、累朝實錄，以藏石室，以垂鑒戒。凡若事天法祖、敬身勤民之實，則皆卓有可紀者焉。是其心學之淵源、純王之政迹，真足以匹休唐虞三代之隆，陋漢唐宋於不居者。諸士漸被聖化，訓典之服膺也久矣。玆維敷言之際，其尚悉心對揚，以鳴我國家文治之盛。

問：古昔聖帝明王制為典禮，尤慎於交神明之際，經傳所載詳矣。論者謂自秦滅學，歷代之祀，或取俚儒無根之說，雜傳
translation_en:
…there is an admonition on reverent unity and commentary on the Five Admonitions. He explicated the chapter of the Great Learning concerning roots and branches and issued it to the Historiography Institute; he displayed the “Against Idleness” chapter of the Book of Documents to encourage diligence in agriculture. Lectures at the Classics Colloquium regularly encompass the various books; in the inner palace, his extensive reading omits none of the dynastic histories. Moreover, he specially commanded his Confucian officials to bring to prominence the Precious Instructions of the successive sage emperors and the Veritable Records of successive reigns, preserving them in stone chambers and transmitting them as guidance and admonition. Such substantive achievements as serving Heaven, emulating the ancestors, maintaining reverence in his own conduct, and diligently caring for the people are all eminently worthy of record. The profound sources of his learning of the mind and the accomplishments of his purely kingly government truly suffice to rival the flourishing ages of Tang Yao, Yu Shun, and the Three Dynasties. He regards the Han, Tang, and Song as inferior and will not rest content with their achievements. You scholars have long been imbued with his sage influence and have taken these authoritative teachings to heart. Now, as you set forth your words, devote your minds fully to answering and extolling them, thereby proclaiming the flourishing civil governance of our dynasty.

Question: When the sage emperors and enlightened kings of antiquity established canonical rites, they exercised particular care in their dealings with the divine powers. The classics and their commentaries record this in detail. Commentators maintain that, since the Qin destroyed learning, the sacrifices of successive dynasties have sometimes drawn upon the unfounded assertions of vulgar scholars, mingling them with transmitted…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
記非聖之書以致祝多媿詞神不居歆
焉昔人又言征伐不可偃於天下乃稱
南開兩粤西闢五都者或以爲黷除兇
雪耻者晚竟貽悔此曷故也漢唐以來
上下二三千年類多可議如此洪惟我
太祖高皇帝旣定天下首嚴
郊祀之禮正神祇之號精誠對越有赫鑒觀載
在
祖訓及戒諭羣臣者何其具也其控制外夷愼
===
固邊圉貢豐則責請謚則抑大脩甲冑
徧飭城隍
詔令所宣每惓惓加慮焉豈非度越百王迥出
千古者哉
列聖相承永爲恪守迨我
皇上益覲揚而光大之
郊丘特建
享禘肅將明武周君臣之分定孔子稱師之議
古今曠典至是益備屬者外夷犯順則
punctuated: 記、非聖之書，以致祝多媿詞，神不居歆焉。昔人又言征伐不可偃於天下，乃稱南開兩粤、西闢五都者，或以爲黷；除兇雪耻者，晚竟貽悔。此曷故也？漢唐以來，上下二三千年，類多可議如此。洪惟我太祖高皇帝旣定天下，首嚴郊祀之禮，正神祇之號，精誠對越，有赫鑒觀。載在祖訓及戒諭羣臣者，何其具也！其控制外夷，愼固邊圉，貢豐則責，請謚則抑，大脩甲冑，徧飭城隍，詔令所宣，每惓惓加慮焉。豈非度越百王、迥出千古者哉！列聖相承，永爲恪守。迨我皇上，益覲揚而光大之。郊丘特建，享禘肅將，明武周君臣之分，定孔子稱師之議，古今曠典，至是益備。屬者外夷犯順，則
translation_en:
…records and books not written by sages, with the result that sacrificial invocations contained many shameful expressions and the spirits would not remain to receive the offerings. People of old also said that punitive warfare could not be abolished throughout the realm. Yet those praised for opening up the two Yue regions in the south and the Five Capitals [?] in the west were sometimes judged excessively warlike; those who eliminated villains and avenged humiliation ultimately left cause for regret in their later years. Why was this? From the Han and Tang onward, over a span of two or three thousand years [?], there were many similarly questionable matters.

We reverently reflect that, after our Emperor Taizu Gao had pacified the realm, he first made strict provision for the suburban sacrifices and rectified the titles of the celestial and terrestrial deities. With pure sincerity he stood before them, and they looked down upon him with radiant discernment. How comprehensive are the provisions recorded in the Ancestral Instructions and in his admonitions to his ministers! In controlling foreign peoples and taking care to secure the frontiers, he rebuked excessive tribute and restrained requests for posthumous titles. He extensively refurbished armor and helmets and ordered fortifications and moats everywhere put in order. In his proclamations and commands, he repeatedly expressed his earnest concern for these matters. Did he not surpass the hundred kings and stand far above all preceding ages?

The successive sage emperors inherited these provisions and always observed them scrupulously. Our present Emperor has further upheld [?] and magnified them. The suburban sacrificial mound has been specially established, and the xiang and di sacrifices solemnly performed. The distinction between sovereign and minister in the cases of King Wu and the Duke of Zhou has been clarified, and the question of designating Confucius as Teacher has been settled. Exceptional rites, unparalleled in ancient or recent times, have thus become still more complete. Recently, when foreign peoples defied imperial authority, then…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
命將興師南征北討卒皆底定
神功駿烈照耀宇宙蓋不惟同符
高皇抑且增光
先烈矣諸士幸生斯世涵濡
聖澤宜必有得焉其敬陳之
問堯命羲和揭星鳥星火星虛星昴之象
以明時也後世占候之說雜述禨祥無
稱論著惟象緯布列其精魄不遠於人
而太史所職曰察天文紀時政則於天
===
人之際未可謂遠不相謀其所稱舍留
合散嬴縮陵乘歷繞鉤鬭食犯守還之
象皆所必察者也使於垣次之所奠名
稱之所指十二辰十二土二十八舍之
屬一或不詳其說則雖欲察之而無從
也故察之而應則占驗之說端未可以
術數薄之而漢儒之所以失者何居察
之而不應則天文之職又非時政所有
事也而太史之所以兼之者何居二任
punctuated:
命將興師，南征北討，卒皆底定。神功駿烈，照耀宇宙，蓋不惟同符高皇，抑且增光先烈矣。諸士幸生斯世，涵濡聖澤，宜必有得焉，其敬陳之。
問：堯命羲和，揭星鳥、星火、星虛、星昴之象，以明時也。後世占候之說，雜述禨祥，無稱論著。惟象緯布列，其精魄不遠於人，而太史所職曰察天文、紀時政，則於天人之際，未可謂遠不相謀。其所稱舍留、合散、嬴縮、陵乘、歷繞、鉤鬭、食犯、守還之象，皆所必察者也。使於垣次之所奠、名稱之所指、十二辰、十二土、二十八舍之屬，一或不詳其說，則雖欲察之而無從也。故察之而應，則占驗之說端未可以術數薄之，而漢儒之所以失者何居？察之而不應，則天文之職又非時政所有事也，而太史之所以兼之者何居？二任
translation_en:
…he appointed generals and raised armies, campaigning south and north, until all were finally pacified. His divine achievements and mighty exploits illuminate the universe. They not only match those of the Exalted Emperor, but also add lustre to the glorious accomplishments of his predecessors. You gentlemen are fortunate to live in this age and to be steeped in the sage emperor’s beneficence. Surely you must have gained some understanding of these matters; respectfully set it forth.
Question: Yao commanded Xi and He to set out the celestial configurations of the Bird, Fire, Emptiness, and Hairy Head in order to distinguish the seasons. Later theories of celestial prognostication mingled accounts of ill and auspicious omens, with no writings worthy of mention [?]. Yet the celestial bodies are arrayed above, and their vital essences are not remote from human beings. The duties of the Grand Astrologer are described as observing celestial patterns and recording the government’s affairs at the time. Thus, in the relationship between Heaven and humanity, one cannot say that they are so remote as to have no dealings with one another. The phenomena termed lodging and stationing, conjunction and separation, advance and retardation, encroaching and overriding, traversing and circling, hooking and contending, eclipse and infringement, lingering and returning are all things that must be observed. If one fails to understand even one explanation concerning the locations of celestial enclosures and stations, the referents of their names, or such divisions as the twelve celestial sectors, the twelve terrestrial regions, and the twenty-eight lunar lodges, then even if one wishes to observe them, one has no means of doing so. Thus, if observations find corresponding manifestations, theories of prognostication and verification certainly cannot be dismissed as mere divinatory techniques. Where, then, did the Han Confucian scholars go wrong? If observations find no corresponding manifestations, then the duties concerned with celestial patterns have no bearing on contemporary affairs of government. Why, then, did the Grand Astrologer combine the two? The two responsibilities…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之官分於何代占候之術精於何人玆
欲破其推驗之謬而復有裨於敬畏之
實諸士其詳之于篇以盡天人之蘊
問文以載道六經紀載其選矣嗣是代有
作者莫非文也人有言三代之文至戰
國而始紕以戰國視三代不逮遠甚而
論者又謂秦漢以前其氣渾然何耶國
語左傳戰國策非先秦古書乎何爲猶
有非國語之議與左氏浮誇之誚縱橫
===
===
闔闢之譏歟先漢以文名者如過秦論
治安策可謂達矣乃三表五餌失之疎
上林子虛等作詭練奇偉而諷一勸百
人以爲靡三篇大對正誼明道之學也
而柔行巽入或傷於緩焉三子且爾則
班固謂漢文與三代同風然歟至唐宋
以之取士又有可言者阿房賦傑作也
抑置第五顔子論佳製也四試遭黜親
策賢良氣憤詞直而卒之不偶不知當
punctuated:
之官分於何代？占候之術精於何人？玆欲破其推驗之謬，而復有裨於敬畏之實，諸士其詳之于篇，以盡天人之蘊。
問：文以載道，六經紀載其選矣。嗣是代有作者，莫非文也。人有言：「三代之文至戰國而始紕。」以戰國視三代，不逮遠甚，而論者又謂秦漢以前其氣渾然，何耶？《國語》《左傳》《戰國策》非先秦古書乎？何爲猶有《非國語》之議，與左氏浮誇之誚、縱橫闔闢之譏歟？先漢以文名者，如《過秦論》《治安策》，可謂達矣，乃三表五餌失之疎。《上林》《子虛》等作，詭練奇偉，而諷一勸百，人以爲靡。三篇大對，正誼明道之學也，而柔行巽入，或傷於緩焉。三子且爾，則班固謂漢文與三代同風，然歟？至唐宋，以之取士，又有可言者。《阿房賦》，傑作也，抑置第五；《顔子論》，佳製也，四試遭黜。親策賢良，氣憤詞直，而卒之不偶。不知當
translation_en:
…in what dynasty were the offices bearing these two responsibilities separated? Who perfected the techniques of celestial prognostication? We now wish to dispel the errors of their inferences and predictions, while also contributing to the actual practice of reverence and awe. You candidates should explain these matters fully in your essays, bringing out all the subtleties of the relationship between Heaven and humanity.
Question: Writing conveys the Way, and the records contained in the Six Classics are its finest examples. Thereafter, every age had its authors, whose works were all literature. Someone has said, “The literature of the Three Dynasties began to go astray only in the Warring States period.” Compared with the Three Dynasties, the Warring States fell far short; yet critics also say that before the Qin and Han, the vital spirit of writing was whole and undivided. Why is this? Are the Discourses of the States, the Zuo Commentary, and the Strategies of the Warring States not ancient books from before the Qin? Why, then, are there still the objections of the Refutation of the Discourses of the States, the charge that Master Zuo was extravagant and boastful, and criticism of the maneuvering and shifting arguments of the diplomatic strategists?
Among works by those renowned for writing in the Former Han, the Discourse on the Faults of Qin and the Policy Essay on Securing Peace and Order may be called penetrating. Yet the “three demonstrations and five baits” were flawed by impracticality. Works such as the Rhapsody on the Shanglin Park and the Rhapsody of Zixu are unusually polished [?], extraordinary, and magnificent; but for every one part admonition they offer a hundred parts encouragement, and people regard them as extravagant. The three great responses to imperial questions embody the learning of rectifying righteousness and illuminating the Way; yet their gentle approach and deferential insinuation may suffer from excessive mildness. If even these three masters were like this, was Ban Gu right to say that Han writing shared the spirit of the Three Dynasties?
In the Tang and Song, writing was used to select officials, and here too there are matters to discuss. The Rhapsody on the Epang Palace was a masterpiece, yet it was relegated to fifth place. The Discourse on Master Yan was an excellent composition, yet its author was rejected in four examinations. When the emperor personally questioned candidates in the Worthy and Good category, a response was indignant in spirit and forthright in language, yet its author ultimately met with no success. I do not know whether, at the time …

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
時所取果更優耶體號西崐以紕繆被
黜似矣何落韻如蕢亦復見收刑賞一
論以雄才見錄似矣何子韶直言不工
亦居上第凡此者豈文章與時高下而
轉移化導之機由於上歟我
朝設科明經得人邁於前代二百年間培養
栽植眞才輩出郁郁乎莫可尚矣然邇
年以來求其氣象之渾厚辭章之典實
者或不多得夫學蕪則氣漓氣漓則文
===
卑文卑則習敝誠有關世敎不可不加
之意也伊欲變今復古刬偽還醇俾得
眞才如昔以適世用必有道矣願詳言
之勿讓
問兩浙介在吳越襟帶江海而地瀕斥鹵
田資灌溉故水利之政不可一日不講
昔胡安定敎授蘇湖以之分科可謂知
重于此矣夫水利之興本以備乾旱而
霖雨少霪水輒汎溢反以為患焉何也
punctuated:
時所取果更優耶？體號西崐，以紕繆被黜，似矣；何落韻如蕢，亦復見收？刑賞一論，以雄才見錄，似矣；何子韶直言不工，亦居上第？凡此者，豈文章與時高下，而轉移化導之機由於上歟？我朝設科明經，得人邁於前代，二百年間培養栽植，眞才輩出，郁郁乎莫可尚矣！然邇年以來，求其氣象之渾厚、辭章之典實者，或不多得。夫學蕪則氣漓，氣漓則文卑，文卑則習敝，誠有關世敎，不可不加之意也。伊欲變今復古，刬偽還醇，俾得眞才如昔，以適世用，必有道矣。願詳言之，勿讓。

問：兩浙介在吳越，襟帶江海，而地瀕斥鹵，田資灌溉，故水利之政不可一日不講。昔胡安定敎授蘇湖，以之分科，可謂知重于此矣。夫水利之興，本以備乾旱，而霖雨少霪，水輒汎溢，反以為患焉，何也？
translation_en:
…were those selected at the time really superior? That writing in the style called Xikun should be rejected for errors seems reasonable; yet why was Kui [?] accepted despite faulty rhyming? That a discourse on punishments and rewards should win selection through its author's outstanding talent seems reasonable; yet why did Zishao also rank among the highest when his forthright statements lacked literary polish? In all these cases, does literary quality rise and fall with the times, while the power to redirect and guide it rests with those above?

Our dynasty established examinations to elucidate the Classics, and its recruitment of worthy men has surpassed that of earlier dynasties. Through two hundred years of cultivation and nurture, men of true talent have emerged in succession—a flourishing beyond anything that could surpass it! In recent years, however, works combining a full and substantial spirit with dignified and solidly grounded expression have perhaps become difficult to find. When learning becomes neglected, the spirit grows thin; when the spirit grows thin, writing becomes debased; when writing becomes debased, prevailing habits deteriorate. This truly bears upon the moral instruction of society and cannot be left unattended. If we wish to transform present practice and restore that of antiquity, eliminate artificiality and return to integrity, and thereby obtain true talent as in former times to meet the needs of the age, there must be a way. Please explain it fully, without holding back.

Question: The two Zhe regions lie amid Wu and Yue, with the river and sea girdling them. Their lands border saline tracts, and their fields depend upon irrigation; thus the administration of water conservancy cannot go unconsidered for even a day. When Hu Anding taught in Suzhou and Huzhou, he made it a separate field of study: he may indeed be said to have understood its importance. Water-conservancy works are undertaken to guard against drought; yet when steady rains persist even a little, the waters promptly overflow, turning the works instead into a source of harm. Why is this?

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
議者謂不障其患則利不興然與昔人
開鏡湖復漢陂捍錢塘浚廣德濬靈濟
又有開南湖疊龍潭築陽陂導新河增
斗門漢晉而下作者接踵全浙賴焉可
指而言之歟邇檇李吳興之間行潦潢
沒大無麥禾則患屬太湖矣夫太湖東
南巨浸自禹跡後歷代疏治之者非一
人而單鍔郟亶其著也今其為議指掌
可稽可倣而行之歟
===
國朝鑿溧水石河而干五堰築壩後復遣大
臣相繼治之昭有成績吳民頌焉非不
配禹功乃其患如故若無所為力者何
也玆其疏滯之由果在三江耶古有三
十六浦以分其流今果一一不壅其故
耶或又謂治田治水相須為功然耶梁
大通間欲分瀉浙江以殺其積已遣使
欲行而止不知其議尚可施之今歟而
呼門出丁之慮其在此日復何如也諸
punctuated: 議者謂不障其患則利不興，然與昔人開鏡湖、復漢陂、捍錢塘、浚廣德、濬靈濟，又有開南湖、疊龍潭、築陽陂、導新河、增斗門，漢晉而下，作者接踵，全浙賴焉，可指而言之歟？邇檇李、吳興之間，行潦潢沒，大無麥禾，則患屬太湖矣。夫太湖，東南巨浸，自禹跡後，歷代疏治之者非一人，而單鍔、郟亶其著也。今其為議，指掌可稽，可倣而行之歟？國朝鑿溧水石河，而干五堰築壩，後復遣大臣相繼治之，昭有成績，吳民頌焉，非不配禹功，乃其患如故，若無所為力者，何也？玆其疏滯之由，果在三江耶？古有三十六浦以分其流，今果一一不壅其故耶？或又謂治田治水相須為功，然耶？梁大通間，欲分瀉浙江以殺其積，已遣使，欲行而止。不知其議尚可施之今歟？而呼門出丁之慮，其在此日復何如也？諸
translation_en:
Those who discuss the matter say that unless the harm is checked, the benefits cannot be realized. Yet consider the works of earlier men: opening Jing Lake, restoring Han Embankment, defending Qiantang against the waters, dredging Guangde and Lingji, as well as opening Nan Lake, building up Longtan, constructing Yang Embankment, channeling the Xin River, and adding sluice gates. From the Han and Jin onward, those undertaking such works followed one another, and all Zhejiang depended upon them. Can you identify and discuss these works? Recently, between Zuili and Wuxing, surface runoff has spread and submerged the land, causing widespread failure of the wheat and grain crops; this calamity is attributable to Lake Tai. Lake Tai is the great expanse of water in the southeast. Since Yu left his traces there, many men in successive dynasties have dredged and regulated it; Shan E and Jia Dan were particularly distinguished among them. Their proposals can now be examined as clearly as something pointed out in one's palm. Can they be emulated and put into practice?

Our dynasty excavated the Shi River in Lishui and drained the five weirs [?] to construct dams. Subsequently, it repeatedly dispatched high ministers to regulate the waters. Their achievements were manifest, and the people of Wu praised them. Their accomplishments were indeed comparable to Yu's. Why, then, does the calamity persist as before, as though no effective effort had been made? Does the cause of the impeded drainage truly lie in the Three Rivers? In antiquity there were thirty-six channels to divide the flow. Are all their former courses truly unobstructed today? Some also say that managing farmland and managing water depend upon one another for success. Is this so? During the Datong era of the Liang dynasty, it was proposed to divert and discharge the waters of the Zhe River to reduce their accumulation. An envoy had already been dispatched, but the undertaking was halted just as it was about to proceed. Could that proposal still be implemented today? And what, at present, of the concern over calling at households' gates to requisition adult males for labor [?]? You …

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
君子欲訥於言而敏於行
鄭秉厚
同考試官教諭韓批訥言敏行是君子用心
體道處此作得之宜錄以式
同考試官教諭蘇批發揮君子欲字意最爲
真切必甞致力於言行者取之
考試官教諭管批典雅
===
考試官教諭李批認理之作
聖人論君子之用心慎言勵行而已矣夫言易
而行難也君子慎其易者而勵於其難焉敦行
之心何如哉夫子欲學者之審所尚也故爲之
言曰天下之道以言而顯以行而成言與行均
之君子之不可巳也然放言則易而恒失之有
餘力行實難而每病於不足君子之用其心固
深辨乎此矣是故慮口說之易窮而慎密中涵
惟欲藏默以斂其華思大言之可怍而靜專內
punctuated:
第壹塲
四書
君子欲訥於言而敏於行。
鄭秉厚
同考試官教諭韓批：訥言敏行，是君子用心體道處。此作得之，宜錄以式。
同考試官教諭蘇批：發揮君子欲字意，最爲真切。必甞致力於言行者，取之。
考試官教諭管批：典雅。
考試官教諭李批：認理之作。
聖人論君子之用心，慎言勵行而已矣。夫言易而行難也，君子慎其易者而勵於其難焉，敦行之心何如哉！夫子欲學者之審所尚也，故爲之言曰：「天下之道，以言而顯，以行而成。言與行，均之君子之不可巳也。然放言則易，而恒失之有餘；力行實難，而每病於不足。君子之用其心，固深辨乎此矣。是故慮口說之易窮，而慎密中涵，惟欲藏默以斂其華；思大言之可怍，而靜專內
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books
“The gentleman wishes to be slow in speech and diligent in action.”
Zheng Binghou

Comment by Associate Examiner Han, Instructor: “Being slow in speech and diligent in action is where the gentleman directs his mind to embody the Way. This composition grasps that point and should be recorded as a model.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Su, Instructor: “Its exposition of the meaning of ‘wishes’ in the statement about the gentleman is especially authentic and apt. Its author must have devoted effort to his own speech and conduct. Accept it.”

Comment by Examiner Guan, Instructor: “Classical and elegant.”

Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: “A composition that apprehends principle.”

When the sage discusses where the gentleman directs his mind, it is simply toward caution in speech and diligence in action. Speaking is easy, but acting is difficult. The gentleman exercises caution in what is easy and strives at what is difficult. How earnest is his resolve to act! The Master wished students to examine carefully what they esteemed, and therefore spoke to them thus: “The Way of the world is made manifest through speech and accomplished through action. Speech and action alike are indispensable to the gentleman. Yet unrestrained speech is easy and constantly errs through excess; strenuous action is truly difficult and repeatedly suffers from insufficiency. In directing his mind, the gentleman has already discerned this distinction deeply. Thus, considering how readily mere talk exhausts itself, he cultivates caution and discretion within, wishing only to remain silent and restrain his outward brilliance. Reflecting that grand words can bring shame, he inwardly, with stillness and concentration …

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
持惟欲含章以貞其守時未可言固隱焉而不
發矣雖言適其時亦將慎以出之而起羞之患
未甞不誠之于思也理不當言固謹焉而不放
矣雖言幾于理亦將訒以居之而尚口之戒未
甞不研之于慮也此于人之易至有餘者君子
有以矯其常矣至於行則所以履乎其事者也
而非可以怠心乘之也必自强於養辯之餘而
允蹈之勤期日新以脩其業致健於先行之際
而進為之勇務時敏以成乎身道之所在則思
===
遵之不已也而亹亹不倦不敢一息之少懈蓋
凡吾性之所固有者默而成之惟以力之不足
為憂矣義之所在則思見之必為也而孳孳不
已不敢一念之或弛蓋凡吾分之所當為者推
而極之惟以躬之不逮為恥矣是君子非盡廢
乎言也而欲訥者其心也以訥為言不為君子
之善言矣乎非取必於行也而欲敏者其心也
以敏為行不為君子之善行矣乎言行善而君
子之心學盡乎此矣夫人顧忽其易而不勉其
punctuated: 持，惟欲含章以貞其守。時未可言，固隱焉而不發矣；雖言適其時，亦將慎以出之，而起羞之患，未甞不誠之于思也。理不當言，固謹焉而不放矣；雖言幾于理，亦將訒以居之，而尚口之戒，未甞不研之于慮也。此于人之易至有餘者，君子有以矯其常矣。至於行，則所以履乎其事者也，而非可以怠心乘之也。必自强於養辯之餘，而允蹈之勤，期日新以脩其業；致健於先行之際，而進為之勇，務時敏以成乎身。道之所在，則思遵之不已也，而亹亹不倦，不敢一息之少懈。蓋凡吾性之所固有者，默而成之，惟以力之不足為憂矣。義之所在，則思見之必為也，而孳孳不已，不敢一念之或弛。蓋凡吾分之所當為者，推而極之，惟以躬之不逮為恥矣。是君子非盡廢乎言也，而欲訥者其心也。以訥為言，不為君子之善言矣乎？非取必於行也，而欲敏者其心也。以敏為行，不為君子之善行矣乎？言行善，而君子之心學盡乎此矣。夫人顧忽其易而不勉其
translation_en:
…maintain inward composure, wishing only to keep their excellence concealed and remain steadfast in what they uphold. When the time is not right to speak, they certainly keep their thoughts hidden and do not utter them. Even when speech is timely, they speak cautiously, never failing to consider earnestly the danger of bringing shame upon themselves. When principle does not warrant speaking, they certainly exercise restraint and do not speak freely. Even when their words approach what is right, they remain hesitant to speak, never failing to ponder the warning against prizing eloquence. Thus, in something people readily carry to excess, the gentleman has a means of correcting their habitual tendency.

As for action, it is the means by which one puts matters into practice; one cannot undertake it with an indolent mind. One must exert oneself beyond cultivating discernment [?], diligently putting things into practice in earnest, seeking daily renewal to advance one’s work. One must exercise vigor in acting before speaking, courageously pressing forward, striving always for diligence to perfect oneself. Wherever the Way lies, one thinks of following it without cease, working tirelessly and not daring to slacken even for a single breath. All that is inherent in one’s nature is thus brought to fulfillment in silence; one worries only that one’s strength may be insufficient. Wherever righteousness lies, one thinks of acting upon it whenever one sees it, striving unceasingly and not daring to relax even for a single thought. All that one’s proper duties require is thus carried through to the utmost; one feels shame only that one’s own conduct may fall short.

Thus the gentleman does not entirely dispense with speech: it is his heart that desires to be slow in speaking. If he makes such restraint the basis of his speech, is this not the gentleman’s excellence in speaking? Nor does he insist rigidly on carrying out every action: it is his heart that desires to be prompt in acting. If he makes such promptness the basis of his conduct, is this not the gentleman’s excellence in action? When speech and action are good, the gentleman’s learning of the heart is fully realized in this. Yet people treat lightly what is easy and fail to exert themselves in what is…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
難也抑何哉嗟乎夫子蓋屢致意於斯矣以觀
行警宰予以言中惜子貢而文莫猶人躬行未
得則以之自道焉此其爲教何諄切言行之間
哉至他日繫易也指其樞機以通乎天地而記
禮則舉其枝葉以推之世道夫然後知言行本
爲日用之常而其感通則不止一身之故也然
則君子事天達化之學舍是奚以哉
是以聲名洋溢乎中國施及蠻貊舟車所
至人力所通天之所覆地之所載日月
===
所照霜露所隊凡有血氣者莫不尊親
故曰配天
盧漸
同考試官教諭張批講配天處暢達可誦
同考試官學正李批形容聖德感人之意甚備
考試官教諭管批筆力雅健
考試官教諭李批得㫖
中庸極言聖德盡於所感而賛其與天同也甚
矣惟天盡物也至聖之德無遠弗被則亦何異
punctuated:
難也，抑何哉？嗟乎！夫子蓋屢致意於斯矣：以觀行警宰予，以言中惜子貢，而文莫猶人、躬行未得，則以之自道焉。此其爲教，何諄切言行之間哉！至他日繫《易》也，指其樞機以通乎天地；而記《禮》，則舉其枝葉以推之世道。夫然後知言行本爲日用之常，而其感通則不止一身之故也。然則君子事天達化之學，舍是奚以哉？
是以聲名洋溢乎中國，施及蠻貊，舟車所至，人力所通，天之所覆，地之所載，日月所照，霜露所隊，凡有血氣者，莫不尊親，故曰配天。
盧漸
同考試官教諭張批：講配天處，暢達可誦。
同考試官學正李批：形容聖德感人之意甚備。
考試官教諭管批：筆力雅健。
考試官教諭李批：得㫖。
《中庸》極言聖德盡於所感，而賛其與天同也。甚矣，惟天盡物也！至聖之德，無遠弗被，則亦何異
translation_en:
…what is difficult—why is this so? Alas! The Master repeatedly directed attention to this matter. By insisting on observing conduct, he admonished Zai Yu; concerning words that hit the mark, he expressed regret for Zigong. As for being comparable to others in literary learning [?], yet not having attained success in personal practice, he said this of himself. How earnest and searching was his teaching concerning speech and conduct! Later, in appending his statements to the Book of Changes, he identified their pivotal workings as reaching through Heaven and Earth; in the Record of Rites, their branches and leaves were set forth and extended to the conduct of society. Only then do we understand that speech and conduct, though ordinary matters of daily life, exert an influence extending beyond the individual. Thus, in the gentleman’s learning by which he serves Heaven and comprehends transformation, what could he employ apart from these?
“Thus his fame overflows throughout the Central Kingdom and extends to the Man and Mo peoples. Wherever boats and carriages reach, wherever human effort penetrates, wherever Heaven covers and Earth supports, wherever the sun and moon shine and frost and dew fall, all who possess blood and vital breath honor and cherish him. Hence it is said that he matches Heaven.”
Lu Jian
Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “The discussion of matching Heaven is lucid and fluent, well worth reciting.”
Associate Examiner Li, School Director, comments: “The account of how sagely virtue moves people is very full.”
Examiner Guan, Instructor, comments: “The writing is elegant and vigorous.”
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “It captures the essential meaning.”
The Doctrine of the Mean describes to the fullest extent the all-embracing influence of sagely virtue and praises its equality with Heaven. How vast it is! Heaven alone encompasses all things. Since the virtue of the highest sage reaches everywhere, however distant, how could it differ…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
於天也哉中庸發明天道至此若謂德有未盛
者不足以語治化有未洽者不足以盡神今惟
聖德如天如淵而民莫不敬信悅焉則其所及
將何如哉吾見德之所孚聲名著焉其在中國
則聲名洋溢也而聖人之德協之于中國矣其
在蠻貊則聲名施及也而聖人之德播之于蠻
貊矣推之舟車人力之所至所通天地之所覆
所載日月霜露之所照所墜此則盡乎中國蠻
貊之地殆窮之不知其所止也其間凡有血氣
===
心知之性者莫不知聖人之爲可尊肅然戴之
爲元后而尊之之心同知聖人之爲可親翕然
懷之如父母而親之之心同至此則聲名之盛
合華夷而一致而民心敬信悅之深通乎內外
而無間矣謂不可以配天矣乎蓋帲冒不遺天
之化本至廣也而聖德亦如是其廣被則有以
仰符峻極之體而不違範圍無外天之德本至
大也而聖德亦如是其徧覆則有以上契高明
之用而無間以天則盡物也以聖則盡民也至
punctuated: 於天也哉？中庸發明天道至此，若謂德有未盛者不足以語治，化有未洽者不足以盡神。今惟聖德如天如淵，而民莫不敬信悅焉，則其所及將何如哉？吾見德之所孚，聲名著焉。其在中國，則聲名洋溢也，而聖人之德協之于中國矣；其在蠻貊，則聲名施及也，而聖人之德播之于蠻貊矣。推之舟車人力之所至所通，天地之所覆所載，日月霜露之所照所墜，此則盡乎中國蠻貊之地，殆窮之不知其所止也。其間凡有血氣心知之性者，莫不知聖人之爲可尊，肅然戴之爲元后，而尊之之心同；知聖人之爲可親，翕然懷之如父母，而親之之心同。至此則聲名之盛，合華夷而一致，而民心敬信悅之深，通乎內外而無間矣。謂不可以配天矣乎？蓋帲冒不遺，天之化本至廣也，而聖德亦如是其廣被，則有以仰符峻極之體而不違；範圍無外，天之德本至大也，而聖德亦如是其徧覆，則有以上契高明之用而無間。以天則盡物也，以聖則盡民也。至
translation_en: …from Heaven? In elucidating the Way of Heaven to this point, the Doctrine of the Mean seems to say that one whose virtue is not yet full cannot be said to bring about good government, and one whose transforming influence has not yet reached everywhere cannot fully realize spiritual efficacy. Now the sage’s virtue is like Heaven and like a deep pool, and none among the people fails to revere, trust, and delight in him. How far, then, will its influence extend? I see that wherever his virtue inspires trust, his fame becomes manifest. Within the Central States, his fame overflows, and the sage’s virtue brings harmony to the Central States; among the Man and Mo peoples, his fame reaches them, and the sage’s virtue spreads among them. Extend this to wherever boats, carriages, and human strength can reach or pass; to all that Heaven covers and Earth supports; to wherever sun and moon shine and frost and dew descend. This encompasses all the lands of the Central States and the Man and Mo peoples: pursue its extent, and one scarcely knows where it ends. Among them, all beings endowed with blood and breath, mind and understanding, recognize that the sage deserves reverence. In solemn respect they uphold him as their sovereign, sharing the same heart of reverence. They recognize that the sage deserves affection, and together cherish him as their father and mother, sharing the same heart of affection. At this point, the greatness of his fame unites the Hua and Yi peoples, while the people’s profound reverence, trust, and delight extend throughout the inner and outer regions without distinction. Could one say that he cannot be Heaven’s equal? Heaven shelters all without omission: its transforming influence is inherently supremely extensive. The sage’s virtue likewise spreads so widely that it accords above with Heaven’s supremely lofty substance, without deviation. Heaven embraces everything, leaving nothing outside: its virtue is inherently supremely great. The sage’s virtue likewise covers all so completely that it accords above with Heaven’s lofty and luminous operation, without disparity. Heaven encompasses all things; the sage encompasses all people. Supreme…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
德至敎固有異位而同神矣惟天無遺覆也惟
聖無遺施也大順大化不其合一而無二乎謂
之曰配天信乎聖人與昊天爲一道而盛德大
業斯其至矣非至聖其孰能與於此雖然聖人
不特配天已也覆載生成之偏天地不能無憾
而彌綸參贊之責實於聖人有賴焉觀易所謂
后以財成天地之道輔相天地之宜則聖人有
功於天亦大矣天地設位聖人成能豈曰小補
之哉然要其所以致之者一誠而已故曰誠者
===
聖人之本
乃若其情則可以爲善矣乃所謂善也
周思充
同考試官敎諭任批即情論性孟子曉人以
易見者此作能發明之諸說不攻而自破矣
同考試官敎諭楊批講可以爲善迥出諸作
考試官敎諭管批得孟子意
考試官敎諭李批明盡
大賢言巳之道性善徵諸情而得之也蓋善者
punctuated:
德至敎，固有異位而同神矣。惟天無遺覆也，惟聖無遺施也，大順大化，不其合一而無二乎？謂之曰配天，信乎聖人與昊天爲一道，而盛德大業斯其至矣。非至聖，其孰能與於此？雖然，聖人不特配天已也。覆載生成之偏，天地不能無憾，而彌綸參贊之責，實於聖人有賴焉。觀《易》所謂「后以財成天地之道，輔相天地之宜」，則聖人有功於天亦大矣。天地設位，聖人成能，豈曰小補之哉？然要其所以致之者，一誠而已。故曰：「誠者，聖人之本。」
乃若其情，則可以爲善矣，乃所謂善也。
周思充
同考試官敎諭任批：即情論性，孟子曉人以易見者，此作能發明之，諸說不攻而自破矣。
同考試官敎諭楊批：講可以爲善，迥出諸作。
考試官敎諭管批：得孟子意。
考試官敎諭李批：明盡。
大賢言巳之道性善，徵諸情而得之也。蓋善者
translation_en:
…virtue and consummate teaching: though occupying different positions, they share the same spiritual efficacy. Heaven leaves nothing unsheltered; the sage leaves no one untouched by his beneficence. In their supreme harmony and transforming influence, do they not unite as one, without distinction? This is called matching Heaven. Truly, the sage and August Heaven follow one Way, and here abundant virtue and great achievement reach their utmost. Who but the utmost sage could attain this? Yet the sage does more than merely match Heaven. Heaven and Earth cannot be entirely free of shortcomings in the unevenness with which they shelter, support, generate, and nurture things; responsibility for comprehensively ordering their work and assisting their transforming activity depends upon the sage. Consider the statement in the Book of Changes: “The ruler regulates and completes the Way of Heaven and Earth, assisting what is fitting in Heaven and Earth.” The sage’s contribution to Heaven is indeed great. Heaven and Earth establish their positions, and the sage brings their capacities to completion. Could this be called a minor contribution? Yet, in essence, what enables him to accomplish this is sincerity alone. Thus it is said: “Sincerity is the foundation of the sage.”
“As for their actual dispositions, they can do good; this is what I mean by goodness.”
Zhou Sichong
Associate Examiner Ren, Instructor, comments: “Discussing human nature through its dispositions, Mencius enlightens people by means of what is readily observable. This essay can elucidate that point; the various other theories collapse of themselves without being attacked.”
Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor, comments: “Its explanation of ‘can do good’ far surpasses the other essays.”
Examiner Guan, Instructor, comments: “It captures Mencius’s meaning.”
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “Clear and exhaustive.”
The great worthy explains that his assertion of the goodness of human nature [?] is reached by seeking evidence in its dispositions. For goodness is…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
性之本體也徵諸情而善斯著矣論性者復何
疑乎孟子曉公都子之意若曰性之不明言之
者之不得其故也吾謂性之本善何哉蓋論性
於已漓之後則偽而失真論性於未發之前則
隱而難見乃若以其情而觀之天機莫測而隨
感以效天下之動者皆各當於帝則之良思慮
莫及而順應以通天下之故者皆各中乎當然
之則循其端可以充其量本體流通固其幾之
不容已而非有所强也致其曲可以會其全天
===
真呈露固其理之不容遏而非有所待也斯不
謂情之善乎夫使情之未善吾亦無徵而必謂
性之善也今既有是情則必有是性感寂相因
觀諸應物而廓然之公以昭動靜一原驗之中
節而大本之中以著性達諸天若不容易窺其
際也即幾之不容已者而遡其貞靜之常夫固
天精天粹而無有一毫之雜矣性通諸命若不
得易究其微也即理之不容遏者而窮其虛明
之體夫固不二不雜而不容一物之間矣此吾
punctuated: 性之本體也，徵諸情而善斯著矣。論性者復何疑乎？孟子曉公都子之意若曰：性之不明，言之者之不得其故也。吾謂性之本善，何哉？蓋論性於已漓之後，則偽而失真；論性於未發之前，則隱而難見。乃若以其情而觀之，天機莫測，而隨感以效天下之動者，皆各當於帝則之良；思慮莫及，而順應以通天下之故者，皆各中乎當然之則。循其端，可以充其量，本體流通，固其幾之不容已，而非有所强也；致其曲，可以會其全，天真呈露，固其理之不容遏，而非有所待也。斯不謂情之善乎？夫使情之未善，吾亦無徵而必謂性之善也。今既有是情，則必有是性。感寂相因，觀諸應物，而廓然之公以昭；動靜一原，驗之中節，而大本之中以著。性達諸天，若不容易窺其際也，即幾之不容已者而遡其貞靜之常，夫固天精天粹，而無有一毫之雜矣；性通諸命，若不得易究其微也，即理之不容遏者而窮其虛明之體，夫固不二不雜，而不容一物之間矣。此吾
translation_en:
…is the fundamental substance of human nature. When verified through the feelings, its goodness becomes manifest. What further doubt can those who discuss human nature have? The intent of Mengzi’s explanation to Gongduzi was as follows: That human nature is not clearly understood is because those who speak of it fail to grasp its underlying grounds. Why do I say that human nature is originally good? To discuss it after it has become diluted is to encounter artifice and lose its genuineness; to discuss it before it has issued into activity is to find it hidden and difficult to discern. But consider it through the feelings: Heaven’s workings are unfathomable, yet all that responds to stimuli and manifests the movements of the world accords with the goodness of the Supreme Lord’s standard. Deliberation cannot reach them, yet all the responses that follow circumstances and engage with the affairs of the world conform to the principles of what ought to be. By following their beginnings, one can develop them to their full capacity: the fundamental substance flows freely because its incipient impulses cannot cease, not because anything is forced. By fully developing particular manifestations, one can comprehend the whole: innate genuineness reveals itself because its principle cannot be obstructed, not because it awaits anything else. Is this not what we call the goodness of the feelings? If the feelings were not good, I too would have no evidence on which to insist that human nature is good. Since these feelings exist, this nature must exist.

Responsiveness and stillness depend upon one another: observe nature in its responses to things, and its expansive impartiality becomes clear. Activity and tranquillity have a single source: examine feelings in their attainment of due measure, and the equilibrium of the great foundation becomes manifest. Human nature reaches to Heaven, and its bounds may seem difficult to discern. Yet trace those incipient impulses that cannot cease back to their enduring constancy and stillness, and there is indeed Heaven’s refinement and purity, without the slightest admixture. Human nature communicates with Heaven’s mandate, and its subtleties may seem difficult to investigate. Yet follow that principle which cannot be obstructed and probe its empty and luminous substance to the utmost, and it is indeed undivided and unmixed, allowing nothing whatsoever to interpose itself. This is what I…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之謂性善寧非因其已然之迹而徵其固有之
眞也哉噫彼公都子者亦何獨於三說而疑之
抑論體用互發論性之學也動靜交養事心之
功也孟子之學得之子思乍見孺子之情於中
節之和實爲真切觀之戒懼愼獨卽存心養性
之事其天也性學淵源於此可見君子亦毋謂
性之必善而忘其旦晝之梏哉
易
觀其所聚而天地萬物之情可見矣
===
宋文卿
同考試官教諭張批此題作者皆援入卦辭
殊覺浮冗簡潔明暢僅見此篇錄之以甦多士
同考試官學正李批得潔靜精微之旨宜錄
爲式
考試官教諭管批約而盡
考試官教諭李批明暢典雅
彖傳極言萃道而悉其所蘊之大焉夫天地萬
物皆以聚爲情者也觀於此而萃道之大可識
punctuated:
之謂性善，寧非因其已然之迹而徵其固有之眞也哉？噫！彼公都子者，亦何獨於三說而疑之？抑論體用互發，論性之學也；動靜交養，事心之功也。孟子之學得之子思，乍見孺子之情，於中節之和實爲真切。觀之戒懼愼獨，卽存心養性之事其天也。性學淵源於此可見。君子亦毋謂性之必善而忘其旦晝之梏哉！

易
觀其所聚，而天地萬物之情可見矣。
宋文卿

同考試官教諭張批：此題作者皆援入卦辭，殊覺浮冗。簡潔明暢，僅見此篇，錄之以甦多士。
同考試官學正李批：得潔靜精微之旨，宜錄爲式。
