考試官教諭李批：明暢典雅。

彖傳極言萃道，而悉其所蘊之大焉。夫天地萬物皆以聚爲情者也，觀於此而萃道之大可識
translation_en:
…what I call the goodness of human nature. Is this not to verify its inherently possessed truth through the traces of what has already manifested itself? Ah! Why did Gongduzi entertain doubts specifically about those three explanations? To discuss how substance and function illuminate each other is the study of human nature; to nurture both activity and stillness is the work of attending to the heart-mind. Mencius received his learning from Zisi. The feeling arising when one suddenly sees a young child is a particularly concrete instance of harmony in which the feelings attain their proper measure. Consider being watchful and apprehensive and vigilant when alone: these are precisely the means of serving Heaven by preserving the heart-mind and nourishing one's nature. Here we can discern the origins and transmission of the study of human nature. Let the gentleman not assert that human nature is necessarily good and then forget the shackles imposed upon it throughout the day!

Book of Changes
“Observe what they gather around, and the true dispositions of Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things can be seen.”
Song Wenqing

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: Those writing on this topic all bring in the hexagram statement, which makes their work seem particularly superficial and prolix. This is the only essay I have seen that is concise, clear, and fluent. It is included to reinvigorate the many candidates.
Comment by Associate Examiner Li, School Instructor: It grasps the purport of purity, stillness, refinement, and subtlety. It should be included as a model.
Comment by Examiner Guan, Instructor: Concise yet exhaustive.
Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: Clear, fluent, polished, and elegant.

The Commentary on the Judgments expounds fully the Way of Gathering Together, bringing out all the greatness it contains. Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things all have gathering as their inherent disposition. By observing this, one can recognize the greatness of the Way of Gathering Together…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
矣此彖傳所以極言之也蓋曰物理之在天下
至渙者固其散殊之迹至一者則其統會之眞
萃以聚爲義卦辭固已彰其蘊矣然其道甚大
而所以體其撰者未也由是仰觀俯察凡充塞
于兩間者無弗考焉其理至賾而所以類其情
者未也由是遠求近取凡紛紜于宇宙者無弗
究焉此蓋由至約以該至博而欲達觀以悉其
變卽至一以求不一而欲推類以盡其餘其情
豈不可見乎是故法象莫大乎天地其卑高之
===
位雖判矣然下濟上行絪縕之氣自交密而無
間竝育莫衆於萬物其形色之賦雖殊矣然氣
求聲應二五之精自妙合而不離兩其化也而
一實神之固造化之所以不匱也是豈强之使
合哉蓋氣機默運有以生之必有以成之雖天
地不能外是以爲情矣以羣分也而以類聚之
固品彙之所以咸亨也亦豈瀆之使聚哉蓋物
理潜孚有以倡之必有以和之雖萬物不能外
是以爲情矣吁天地萬物且然萃之道其誠大
punctuated: 矣。此彖傳所以極言之也。蓋曰：物理之在天下，至渙者固其散殊之迹，至一者則其統會之眞。萃以聚爲義，卦辭固已彰其蘊矣。然其道甚大，而所以體其撰者未也。由是仰觀俯察，凡充塞于兩間者，無弗考焉。其理至賾，而所以類其情者未也。由是遠求近取，凡紛紜于宇宙者，無弗究焉。此蓋由至約以該至博，而欲達觀以悉其變；卽至一以求不一，而欲推類以盡其餘。其情豈不可見乎？是故法象莫大乎天地，其卑高之位雖判矣，然下濟上行，絪縕之氣自交密而無間；竝育莫衆於萬物，其形色之賦雖殊矣，然氣求聲應，二五之精自妙合而不離。兩其化也，而一實神之，固造化之所以不匱也。是豈强之使合哉？蓋氣機默運，有以生之，必有以成之，雖天地不能外是以爲情矣。以羣分也，而以類聚之，固品彙之所以咸亨也。亦豈瀆之使聚哉？蓋物理潜孚，有以倡之，必有以和之，雖萬物不能外是以爲情矣。吁！天地萬物且然，萃之道其誠大
translation_en:
…indeed. This is why the Commentary on the Judgments expounds it so fully. The point is this: among the principles of things throughout the world, utter dispersion is but the outward trace of their separation and differentiation; ultimate unity is the truth of their integration and convergence. Cui (Gathering Together) means gathering, and the hexagram statement has already made its underlying significance clear. Yet its Way is exceedingly great, and how to comprehend its workings has not yet been explained. Hence one looks upward and examines what is below, investigating everything that fills the space between Heaven and Earth. Its principles are exceedingly profound, and how to classify its essential circumstances has not yet been explained. Hence one seeks far afield and draws upon what is near, exploring everything in the teeming universe. This is to encompass the broadest range through the utmost simplicity, seeking a comprehensive view that fully apprehends its changes; to seek diversity within ultimate unity, extending analogies to exhaust all that remains. Can its essential circumstances not thereby be seen?

Thus, among models and images, none is greater than Heaven and Earth. Although their positions, low and high, are distinct, one descends to assist and the other rises; their intermingling vital energies naturally unite closely, without any gap. Among beings nurtured together, none is more numerous than the myriad things. Although the forms and colors with which they are endowed differ, kindred energies seek one another and like sounds respond to one another; the essences of the two powers and the five phases naturally unite wondrously and remain inseparable. Their transformations are twofold, yet one reality gives them their wondrous efficacy: this is precisely why the creative process is inexhaustible. Could they have been forced to unite? The workings of vital energy operate silently: whatever brings them into being must also bring them to completion. Even Heaven and Earth cannot have an essential nature outside this principle.

Things divide into groups yet gather according to kind: this is precisely why all categories of beings flourish. Could they have been indiscriminately brought together [?]? The principles of things accord unseen: wherever something initiates, something must respond in harmony. Even the myriad things cannot have an essential nature outside this principle. Ah! Since even Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things are thus, the Way of Gathering Together is truly great…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
哉抑造化物理感而後聚聚而後恒其致一也
張子曰天道不窮寒暑已衆動不窮屈信已寒
暑屈信者感聚之理不窮者恒久之義夫子傳
咸恒而皆以天地萬物爲言義固有取也學易
者知此庶幾達天地之命萬物之情
兼三才而兩之故易六畫而成卦分陰分
陽迭用柔剛故易六位而成章
盧漸
同考試官教諭張批理明詞𭰹發成卦成章
之㫖尤爲詳盡
同考試官學正李批說題意明盡殆深於易
者
考試官教諭管批詞意精切
考試官教諭李批清雅
說卦卽易之所由成見理之所以順也蓋卦爻
備而易之所由以成也性命之理有不順于是
者哉此說卦之意也豈不謂易之作也雖若止
于無文之畫而究其蘊也實有以涵乎至理
punctuated:
哉！抑造化物理，感而後聚，聚而後恒，其致一也。張子曰：「天道不窮，寒暑已；衆動不窮，屈信已。」寒暑屈信者，感聚之理；不窮者，恒久之義。夫子傳咸恒，而皆以天地萬物爲言，義固有取也。學易者知此，庶幾達天地之命、萬物之情。
兼三才而兩之，故易六畫而成卦；分陰分陽，迭用柔剛，故易六位而成章。
盧漸
同考試官教諭張批：理明詞𭰹，發成卦成章之㫖，尤爲詳盡。
同考試官學正李批：說題意明盡，殆深於易者。
考試官教諭管批：詞意精切。
考試官教諭李批：清雅。
說卦卽易之所由成，見理之所以順也。蓋卦爻備，而易之所由以成也，性命之理有不順于是者哉？此說卦之意也。豈不謂易之作也，雖若止于無文之畫，而究其蘊也，實有以涵乎至理
translation_en:
…indeed! Moreover, in the workings of creation and the principles governing things, interaction precedes gathering, and gathering precedes constancy: their ultimate purport is one. Master Zhang said: “The Way of Heaven is inexhaustible—merely cold and heat; the manifold movements are inexhaustible—merely contraction and extension.” Cold and heat, contraction and extension, embody the principle of interaction and gathering; inexhaustibility expresses the meaning of enduring constancy. In his commentaries on Influence (Xian) and Constancy (Heng), the Master spoke in both cases of Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things; his choice assuredly had its significance. Those who study the Book of Changes and understand this may approach an understanding of the mandate of Heaven and Earth and the true nature of the myriad things.
“Encompassing the Three Powers and doubling them, the Changes forms a hexagram from six lines; distinguishing yin and yang, and employing the yielding and the firm in alternation, the Changes forms its patterns through six positions.”
Lu Jian.
Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “The principles are clear and the language profound [?]. The exposition of the meaning of forming hexagrams and forming patterns is especially thorough.”
Associate Examiner Li, School Instructor, comments: “The explanation of the topic’s meaning is clear and exhaustive. The author must have a deep understanding of the Changes.”
Examiner Guan, Instructor, comments: “The language and ideas are precise and apt.”
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “Lucid and elegant.”
The Explanation of the Trigrams (Shuogua), by addressing how the Changes is constituted, reveals how principle is followed. For it is through the completeness of its hexagrams and lines that the Changes is constituted. Could any principle of human nature and destiny fail to find accordance here? This is the intention of the Explanation of the Trigrams. Does it not mean that, although the making of the Changes seems to consist merely of lines without written words, when we investigate what they contain, they truly embrace the ultimate principles…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
精是故三才之道固性命之所在也而易何以
順之耶蓋統而觀之易有卦也三畫立而三才
具矣然外體不備卦猶未成也於是引伸於小
成之後而兼三才以兩其畫因重于成列之餘
而倍三畫以成其質上焉天道以兩而成象也
中焉人道以兩而成位也下焉地道以兩而成
形也則原始要終而貞悔備大成之體自本之
末而內外極統體之全不有以成卦矣乎析而
言之易有爻也六畫備而卦固成矣然爻位無
===
別文猶未著也于是三陰三陽而奇偶分對待
之形一剛一柔而彼此妙迭居之用天道相間
而往來于上也人道相間而互用于中也地道
相間而變遷于下也則六位時成而錯綜顯文
明之賁六爻相雜而經緯彰物采之華不有以
成章矣乎是知六畫成卦則性命之渾然者合
之盡其大矣六位成章則性命之燦然者析之
極其精矣易順性命之理也有如是夫抑論易
能順理如此則易也者誠天地人之至妙至妙
punctuated: 精。是故三才之道，固性命之所在也，而易何以順之耶？蓋統而觀之，易有卦也，三畫立而三才具矣。然外體不備，卦猶未成也。於是引伸於小成之後，而兼三才以兩其畫；因重于成列之餘，而倍三畫以成其質。上焉，天道以兩而成象也；中焉，人道以兩而成位也；下焉，地道以兩而成形也。則原始要終，而貞悔備大成之體；自本之末，而內外極統體之全，不有以成卦矣乎？析而言之，易有爻也，六畫備而卦固成矣。然爻位無別，文猶未著也。于是三陰三陽，而奇偶分對待之形；一剛一柔，而彼此妙迭居之用。天道相間而往來于上也，人道相間而互用于中也，地道相間而變遷于下也。則六位時成，而錯綜顯文明之賁；六爻相雜，而經緯彰物采之華，不有以成章矣乎？是知六畫成卦，則性命之渾然者，合之盡其大矣；六位成章，則性命之燦然者，析之極其精矣。易順性命之理也，有如是夫！抑論易能順理如此，則易也者，誠天地人之至妙至妙
translation_en:
…the subtle essence of ultimate principle. Thus the ways of the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humanity—are indeed where human nature and destiny reside. How, then, does the Book of Changes accord with them? Viewed as a whole, the Changes has its hexagrams: once three lines are established, the Three Powers are all present. Yet until the outer trigram is supplied, the hexagram remains incomplete. Accordingly, after the lesser completion, the figure is extended, doubling the lines allotted to each of the Three Powers; after the trigrams have been arrayed, they are further superimposed, doubling the three lines to complete the figure. Above, the way of Heaven forms images through its pair of lines; in the middle, the way of humanity establishes positions through its pair; below, the way of Earth takes shape through its pair. Thus, tracing the beginning and comprehending the end, the inner and outer trigrams, termed zhen and hui, furnish the fully completed structure. From root to tip, the inner and outer parts exhaust the completeness of the unified whole. Is this not how the hexagram is formed?

Considered analytically, the Changes has its individual lines. With all six lines present, the hexagram is indeed complete. Yet unless the line positions are differentiated, its pattern has not yet become manifest. Accordingly, three yin and three yang lines distinguish, through their even and odd numbers, the forms of complementary opposition; firmness and yielding each display the subtle working of alternately occupying positions. The way of Heaven alternates, coming and going above; the way of humanity alternates, functioning reciprocally in the middle; the way of Earth alternates, changing and shifting below. Thus the six positions take shape in their proper times, and their interweaving reveals the adornment of luminous pattern; the six lines intermingle, and their warp and weft display the brilliance of things in their varied colors. Is this not how a distinct pattern is formed?

From this we know that when six lines form a hexagram, what is undivided in human nature and destiny is brought together, exhausting its vastness; when the six positions form a pattern, what is brilliantly differentiated in human nature and destiny is analyzed, reaching the utmost of its subtlety. Such is the way the Changes accords with the principles of human nature and destiny! Furthermore, considering how the Changes can accord with principle in this manner, the Changes truly is the most wondrous, most wondrous of Heaven, Earth, and humanity…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
者也善學者不求之易而神明于心窮理盡性
以至于命焉則三極之道彌綸于我而範圍曲
成之用不能外矣否則徒泥于法象而無黙成
之德則易道豈能以虛行乎哉是故謂其爲卜
筮之書也亦宜
書
元首明哉股肱良哉
周思充
同考試官教諭任批虞庭明良之盛此作能
===
敷揚之宜錄以式
同考試官教諭楊批重人臣自獻意正得臯
謨之旨
考試官教諭管批文體雅暢
考試官教諭李批詞理兼得
君秉哲於上臣奉職於下大臣述歌以告君也
甚矣人臣以奉職爲良也明君在上而臣皆脩
職以自効焉聖世相遇之隆也有如是夫臯陶
述其所以賡歌者陳於帝也以爲人臣之事君
punctuated:
者也。善學者不求之易，而神明于心，窮理盡性，以至于命焉，則三極之道彌綸于我，而範圍曲成之用不能外矣。否則徒泥于法象，而無黙成之德，則易道豈能以虛行乎哉？是故謂其爲卜筮之書也，亦宜。
書
元首明哉，股肱良哉。
周思充
同考試官教諭任批：虞庭明良之盛，此作能敷揚之，宜錄以式。
同考試官教諭楊批：重人臣自獻意，正得臯謨之旨。
考試官教諭管批：文體雅暢。
考試官教諭李批：詞理兼得。
君秉哲於上，臣奉職於下，大臣述歌以告君也。甚矣，人臣以奉職爲良也！明君在上，而臣皆脩職以自効焉，聖世相遇之隆也，有如是夫！臯陶述其所以賡歌者，陳於帝也，以爲人臣之事君
translation_en:
…indeed it is. Those who learn well do not seek this in the Changes, but attain spiritual understanding within their own hearts. By fathoming principle and fully realizing their nature, they reach their allotted destiny. Thus the Way of the Three Ultimates—Heaven, Earth, and humanity—is comprehensively encompassed within oneself, and the operations of embracing all things and bringing each to fulfillment cannot lie outside it. Otherwise, if one merely clings to patterns and images, without the virtue of accomplishing things silently, how could the Way of the Changes operate through empty forms? In that case, it is indeed fitting to call it a book of divination.
Book of Documents
“How enlightened is the head! How worthy are the arms and legs!”
Zhou Sichong
Comment by Associate Examiner Ren, Instructor: “This composition amply expounds the flourishing concord of an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers at the court of Shun. It merits inclusion as a model.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor: “It emphasizes the ministers’ wish to offer their own service, precisely capturing the purport of the ‘Counsels of Gao Yao.’”
Comment by Examiner Guan, Instructor: “The prose is elegant and fluent.”
Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: “Both expression and reasoning are well achieved.”
The ruler exercises wisdom above, while his ministers discharge their duties below: a great minister recounted his song to convey this to his ruler. How profoundly a minister’s worthiness consists in discharging his duties! With an enlightened ruler above, the ministers all attend diligently to their offices to offer their service. Such is the glorious meeting of ruler and ministers in a sage age! Gao Yao explained to the emperor why he had continued the song, holding that, in a minister’s service to his ruler…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
循分以効忠者固其莫逃之義因遇而知奮者
乃其必致之情吾今有感于遇主之盛而不容
已於情也乃歌之曰元首明哉股肱良哉誠以
大君居首出之位以立極其尊如元首也羣臣
任代工之責以從王其分如股肱也爲之元首
者本濬哲之光而聰明是憲獨觀乎化理之原
體文明之懿而視聽惟公疏通乎民物之賾以
之興事則統率之要自我執之清明在躬而所
以示臨御之有赫者何宣朗也以之考成則簡
===
別之公自我精之大觀在上而所以著明哲之
作則者何昭灼也有君如此而人臣將何以自
獻也哉將見爲之股肱者情孚於一體之交而
懷忠良以敬應用輸其弼亮之志義屬於相資
之重而聯官常以祗若各効其精白之忱慶明
王之率作而及時以趨事者不容已焉左右維
持以大溥其昭明之化而敢上負于天子也哉
仰聖主之考成而奉法以脩職者不容緩焉翼
輔賛襄以共成其精明之治而敢自負乎明時
punctuated: 循分以効忠者，固其莫逃之義；因遇而知奮者，乃其必致之情。吾今有感于遇主之盛，而不容已於情也。乃歌之曰：「元首明哉！股肱良哉！」誠以大君居首出之位以立極，其尊如元首也；羣臣任代工之責以從王，其分如股肱也。爲之元首者，本濬哲之光而聰明是憲，獨觀乎化理之原；體文明之懿而視聽惟公，疏通乎民物之賾。以之興事，則統率之要自我執之，清明在躬，而所以示臨御之有赫者何宣朗也！以之考成，則簡別之公自我精之，大觀在上，而所以著明哲之作則者何昭灼也！有君如此，而人臣將何以自獻也哉？將見爲之股肱者，情孚於一體之交，而懷忠良以敬應，用輸其弼亮之志；義屬於相資之重，而聯官常以祗若，各効其精白之忱。慶明王之率作，而及時以趨事者不容已焉，左右維持，以大溥其昭明之化，而敢上負于天子也哉？仰聖主之考成，而奉法以脩職者不容緩焉，翼輔賛襄，以共成其精明之治，而敢自負乎明時
translation_en:
…To fulfill one’s allotted duties with loyalty is indeed an obligation one cannot escape; to be stirred to exertion by encountering such a ruler is a feeling that must find full expression. I am now moved by the greatness of my good fortune in meeting my sovereign, and cannot restrain my feelings. Thus he sang: “How enlightened is the head! How worthy are the arms and legs!” Truly, the great sovereign occupies the foremost position and establishes the supreme standard: in his exalted station he is like the head. His ministers undertake the responsibility of performing Heaven’s work on its behalf and follow their king: in their allotted roles they are like the arms and legs.

He who serves as the head draws upon the radiance of profound wisdom and takes clear perception as his rule, discerning uniquely the source of transforming governance. He embodies the excellence of cultivated enlightenment, remaining wholly impartial in what he sees and hears, and comprehends the intricacies of the people and all things. In initiating undertakings, he himself holds the essentials of command. Clarity and discernment reside in his person: how luminous is the majesty he displays in ruling! In assessing accomplishments, he himself perfects impartial discrimination. Lofty above, he presents a great example: how brilliantly he manifests enlightened wisdom as a governing standard!

With such a ruler, how shall his ministers offer their service? We shall see those who serve as his arms and legs joined to him in the mutual trust of a single body. Cherishing loyalty and goodness, they respond reverently and thereby give full expression to their resolve to assist him. Bound by duty to the weighty task of mutual support, they coordinate their regular official responsibilities in reverent compliance, each offering his utterly pure sincerity. Rejoicing that the enlightened king leads them in their work, they cannot hold back from attending to affairs in timely fashion. Supporting and sustaining him on every side, they spread his radiant transforming influence far and wide. Would they dare fail the Son of Heaven above? Looking up to the sage sovereign as he assesses accomplishments, they cannot delay in observing the laws and fulfilling their duties. Assisting, supporting, and furthering his work, they jointly bring his discerning governance to fruition. Would they dare prove unworthy of this enlightened age…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
也哉是元首而明則人臣獲聖主以爲之宗股
肱而良則大君得賢臣以爲之助一時之相遇
如此臯陶歌之固以寓其屬望之志帝舜聞之
寧不慰其樂成之思也哉抑考大舜重華協帝
百僚師師相讓成風虞之君臣未始不明且良
者何臯陶諄復而歌之也蓋以世貴恒泰而先
事預防忠臣事君未甞頃刻忘者是以都俞吁
咈以共保其修和歌叙之化而大韶之作可以
和神人儀鳳凰者良有以也吁元氣交而天地
===
泰歌咏澈而上下和有虞熈皡之氣象可想見
也夫
皇建其有極斂時五福
張大忠
同考試官教諭任批講斂福感通處親切明
晰是潜心經學者宜冠本房
同考試官教諭楊批皇極既建則福自斂乃
王者自然之應此作得之
考試官教諭管批理明詞整
punctuated:
也哉！是元首而明，則人臣獲聖主以爲之宗；股肱而良，則大君得賢臣以爲之助。一時之相遇如此，臯陶歌之，固以寓其屬望之志；帝舜聞之，寧不慰其樂成之思也哉？抑考大舜重華協帝，百僚師師，相讓成風，虞之君臣未始不明且良者，何臯陶諄復而歌之也？蓋以世貴恒泰，而先事預防，忠臣事君未甞頃刻忘者。是以都俞吁咈，以共保其修和歌叙之化，而大韶之作，可以和神人、儀鳳凰者，良有以也。吁！元氣交而天地泰，歌咏澈而上下和，有虞熈皡之氣象可想見也夫！

皇建其有極，斂時五福。
張大忠

同考試官教諭任批：講斂福感通處，親切明晰，是潜心經學者，宜冠本房。
同考試官教諭楊批：皇極既建，則福自斂，乃王者自然之應，此作得之。
考試官教諭管批：理明詞整。
translation_en:
…could they? Thus, when the head is enlightened, ministers have a sage sovereign to look up to; when the arms and legs are worthy, the great ruler has worthy ministers to assist him. With ruler and ministers so happily brought together, Gao Yao sang to express his hopes and expectations. When Emperor Shun heard him, could this fail to gratify his wish to rejoice in their achievements? Yet consider how the great Shun renewed the brilliance of his predecessor and accorded with Emperor Yao, while the hundred officials learned from one another and mutual deference became customary. The ruler and ministers of Yu were already enlightened and worthy: why, then, did Gao Yao sing his earnest, repeated admonitions? It was because lasting peace is precious to the world, and loyal ministers serving their ruler never for a moment forget to take precautions before events arise. Thus, through exclamations of praise, assent, caution, and dissent, they together sustained a civilizing order in which affairs were regulated, all was harmonious, and these achievements were celebrated in song. There was indeed good reason why the performance of the Great Shao music could bring spirits and people into harmony and cause phoenixes to appear in stately array. Ah! When the primordial vital forces intermingle, Heaven and Earth enjoy peace; when song penetrates throughout, those above and below are in harmony. We can picture the radiant, expansive atmosphere of the age of Yu!

“The sovereign establishes his supreme standard and gathers these five blessings.”
Zhang Dazhong

Comment by Associate Examiner Ren, Instructor: “The explanation of how gathering blessings works through sympathetic resonance is precise and clear. This is someone who has devoted himself to studying the Classics; his essay should rank first in this examining section.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor: “Once the sovereign’s supreme standard is established, blessings gather of themselves: this is the response that naturally attends a true king. This essay grasps that point.”

Comment by Examiner Guan, Instructor: “Clear reasoning and well-ordered phrasing.”

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎諭李批〔純雅〕
王者立人之極因以承天之休焉蓋極本人心
同然之理也極建於君而天休因之以集焉其
理之妙於感通者與箕子衍皇極之疇以告武
王若曰天人有合一之理德福有相因之機洛
書之五數固第之爲建用皇極矣而其義爲何
如哉彼天以至極之理而陰隲於維皇本以率
先天下而會萃諸福者也爲之君者本其帝降
之良以爲表儀之準于以式萬方而飭其規運
===
其同然之懿以爲中正之觀于以刑百辟而貞
其度大而天經極之統會在是也惟聖盡倫中
天下而爲綱常之主使同倫者足於我而觀法
焉小而物則極之散殊在是也惟皇盡制首庶
類而爲紀法之宗使考制者得於我而取衷焉
皇能建極如此而福之所集豈其微哉吾知福
之爲數有五其類不同而同爲天地之和氣也
以吾之和德而導迎之自有以致其繁祉之萃
爲福不同而同爲宇宙之順氣也以吾之順德
punctuated:
考試官敎諭李批〔純雅〕。

王者立人之極，因以承天之休焉。蓋極本人心同然之理也。極建於君，而天休因之以集焉，其理之妙於感通者與！箕子衍皇極之疇以告武王，若曰：天人有合一之理，德福有相因之機。洛書之五數，固第之爲建用皇極矣，而其義爲何如哉？彼天以至極之理而陰隲於維皇，本以率先天下而會萃諸福者也。爲之君者，本其帝降之良，以爲表儀之準，于以式萬方而飭其規；運其同然之懿，以爲中正之觀，于以刑百辟而貞其度。大而天經，極之統會在是也，惟聖盡倫，中天下而爲綱常之主，使同倫者足於我而觀法焉；小而物則，極之散殊在是也，惟皇盡制，首庶類而爲紀法之宗，使考制者得於我而取衷焉。皇能建極如此，而福之所集豈其微哉？吾知福之爲數有五，其類不同，而同爲天地之和氣也。以吾之和德而導迎之，自有以致其繁祉之萃。爲福不同，而同爲宇宙之順氣也。以吾之順德
translation_en:
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: 〔Pure and elegant.〕

The true king establishes the supreme standard for humanity and thereby receives Heaven’s blessings. For this standard is rooted in the principle that all human hearts acknowledge alike. Once the ruler establishes it, Heaven’s blessings accordingly gather around him. How wondrous is this principle in its power to evoke a response!

Jizi expounded the category of the Sovereign’s Supreme Standard to King Wu, saying in effect: Heaven and humanity possess a principle by which they unite; virtue and blessings possess a dynamic by which the latter follow from the former. The fifth number in the Luo Writing is indeed assigned to “establishing and employing the Sovereign’s Supreme Standard.” But what does this mean? Heaven, through the principle of ultimate perfection, secretly establishes the sovereign, intending him to lead all under Heaven and bring together every blessing. He who rules takes the goodness bestowed upon him by the Supreme Lord as the standard for exemplary conduct, thereby furnishing a model for the myriad regions and setting their rules in order. He brings into operation the excellence acknowledged alike by all, making it a visible example of centrality and correctness, thereby providing a model for the hundred lords and rectifying their standards.

On the grand scale are Heaven’s constant principles: here the supreme standard is comprehensively united. Only the sage fully realizes human relationships; occupying the center of all under Heaven, he becomes the master of the cardinal bonds and constant virtues, so that those who share these relationships find in him all they need to observe and emulate. On the smaller scale are the norms inherent in particular things: here the supreme standard is differentiated in its manifestations. Only the sovereign fully establishes institutions; standing at the head of the many kinds of beings, he becomes the source of rules and laws, so that those who examine institutions find in him the proper mean to adopt.

If the sovereign can establish the supreme standard in this way, could the blessings that gather around him be slight? I know that blessings number five. Though their categories differ, all alike are the harmonious vital energy of Heaven and Earth. By guiding and welcoming them with my harmonious virtue, I naturally have the means to bring their abundant blessings together. Though they differ as blessings, all alike are the compliant vital energy of the universe. Through my compliant virtue…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
而感召之自有以膺乎諸福之隆人之所不可
必者天之所不能違也在皇者雖非緣是以獲
福而必致之理在我則隨其所值而迪無不吉
矣其若斂之而會於君之一身矣乎后之所克
綏者天之所寵綏也在聖人雖非藉是以承休
而可致之道在我則任吾所適而動罔不宜矣
其若集之而聚於皇之一人矣乎要之皇極旣
建不必外極以求福也極卽福也五福旣斂不
必外福以觀極也福卽極也理一而已矣君天
===
下者其惟建極而已乎抑考大禹陳謨曰惠迪
吉伊尹告君曰作善降之百祥惠之與善卽極
之理而吉與百祥亦卽五福之斂於極者是以
大禹伊尹得之而致告箕子得之而衍疇皆一
道也吁箕子知極矣能傳之於武而不能行之
於商豈箕子之極不足以斂福與適然之遇也
不可以是以論乎感通之常也
詩
天保定爾以莫不興如山如阜如岡如陵
punctuated:
而感召之，自有以膺乎諸福之隆。人之所不可必者，天之所不能違也。在皇者雖非緣是以獲福，而必致之理在我，則隨其所值而迪，無不吉矣。其若斂之而會於君之一身矣乎！后之所克綏者，天之所寵綏也。在聖人雖非藉是以承休，而可致之道在我，則任吾所適而動，罔不宜矣。其若集之而聚於皇之一人矣乎！要之，皇極旣建，不必外極以求福也，極卽福也；五福旣斂，不必外福以觀極也，福卽極也。理一而已矣。君天下者，其惟建極而已乎！抑考大禹陳謨曰：「惠迪吉。」伊尹告君曰：「作善，降之百祥。」惠之與善，卽極之理；而吉與百祥，亦卽五福之斂於極者。是以大禹、伊尹得之而致告，箕子得之而衍疇，皆一道也。吁！箕子知極矣，能傳之於武，而不能行之於商，豈箕子之極不足以斂福與？適然之遇也，不可以是以論乎感通之常也。

詩

天保定爾，以莫不興。如山如阜，如岡如陵，
translation_en:
…and thereby call them forth, one naturally has the means to receive blessings in their abundance. What human beings cannot guarantee is what Heaven cannot contravene. Although the sovereign does not act on this account in order to obtain blessings, the principle that necessarily brings them lies within himself. Thus, whatever circumstances he encounters, he proceeds with nothing but auspicious results. Is it not as though these blessings were gathered and brought together in the ruler’s single person? What the ruler can secure in peace is what Heaven cherishes and secures in peace. Although the sage does not rely on this in order to receive good fortune, the Way by which it can be brought about lies within himself. Thus, wherever he goes and acts, nothing is unfitting. Is it not as though these blessings were assembled and concentrated in the sovereign alone?

In essence, once the August Standard is established, there is no need to seek blessings outside it: the Standard itself is blessing. Once the Five Blessings are gathered, there is no need to look beyond them to discern the Standard: blessing itself is the Standard. The principle is one, and nothing more. For one who rules all under Heaven, surely the task is simply to establish the Standard!

Consider also how Da Yu, in setting forth his counsels, said, “Following the Way brings good fortune.” Yi Yin admonished his ruler, saying, “Do good, and a hundred auspicious blessings will descend upon you.” Following the Way and doing good are precisely the principle of the Standard; good fortune and the hundred auspicious blessings are precisely the Five Blessings gathered in the Standard. Thus Da Yu and Yi Yin grasped it and offered their admonitions; Jizi grasped it and elaborated the Categories of the Great Plan. All followed a single Way. Ah! Jizi understood the Standard. He could transmit it to King Wu, yet could not put it into practice under the Shang. Could it be that Jizi’s Standard was insufficient to gather blessings? This was a matter of the circumstances he happened to encounter; one cannot use it to judge the constant principle of sympathetic response between Heaven and humanity.

Book of Odes

Heaven protects and establishes you, so that nothing fails to flourish. Like mountains, like hills, like ridges, like high mounds…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
如川之方至以莫不增
秦應驄
同考試官教諭韓批通篇辭藻不浮而詩人
頌禱之意溢於言外文之佳者
同考試官教諭蘇批場中作者類以以莫不
增屬川之方至殊非本旨獨此作有見錄之
考試官教諭管批雅暢
考試官教諭李批辭旨俱到
臣子託天福君之盛必擬諸形容而進之焉夫
===
高大盛長天之福君者至矣而猶欲進之不已
周臣忠愛之心寧有旣乎想其答君之意蓋謂
王者以事天爲心亦以得天爲慶使福有未盛
而莫之有增非所以語於天心之仁愛也吾願
天之福君者本於簡在之隆而宇宙之太和凝
焉單厚多益凡君心之百順者咸以一身而履
其盛原於寵綏之厚而庶徵之熙洽萃焉戩穀
罄宜凡天休之滋至者咸以一人而會其全夫
是福之興也將何以擬之哉彼山阜岡陵天下
punctuated:
如川之方至，以莫不增。

秦應驄

同考試官教諭韓批：通篇辭藻不浮，而詩人頌禱之意溢於言外，文之佳者。

同考試官教諭蘇批：場中作者類以「以莫不增」屬「川之方至」，殊非本旨。獨此作有見，錄之。

考試官教諭管批：雅暢。

考試官教諭李批：辭旨俱到。

臣子託天福君之盛，必擬諸形容而進之焉。夫高大盛長，天之福君者至矣，而猶欲進之不已，周臣忠愛之心寧有旣乎？想其答君之意，蓋謂王者以事天爲心，亦以得天爲慶。使福有未盛，而莫之有增，非所以語於天心之仁愛也。吾願天之福君者，本於簡在之隆，而宇宙之太和凝焉；單厚多益，凡君心之百順者，咸以一身而履其盛。原於寵綏之厚，而庶徵之熙洽萃焉；戩穀罄宜，凡天休之滋至者，咸以一人而會其全。夫是福之興也，將何以擬之哉？彼山阜岡陵，天下
translation_en:
…like a river just coming into full flow, with nothing failing to increase.

Qin Yingcong

Comment by Associate Examiner Han, Instructor: Throughout the piece, the ornamented language is never superficial, and the poet’s intent to praise and pray overflows beyond the words. This is an excellent composition.

Comment by Associate Examiner Su, Instructor: Writers in the examination generally attach “with nothing failing to increase” to “a river just coming into full flow,” which decidedly misses the original meaning. This composition alone shows insight; I select it.

Comment by Examiner Guan, Instructor: Elegant and fluent.

Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: Both expression and meaning are fully realized.

When subjects invoke Heaven to bless their ruler abundantly, they must employ descriptive comparisons and carry these blessings still further. In height and magnitude, abundance and growth, Heaven’s blessings upon the ruler have reached the utmost; yet they still wish to advance them without cease. Could the loyal affection of the ministers of Zhou ever come to an end? If we imagine their intention in responding to their ruler, it was surely this: a king makes serving Heaven his concern and likewise regards obtaining Heaven’s favor as his joy. If his blessings were not yet abundant and nothing increased them, this would not accord with the benevolent love in Heaven’s heart.

I wish that Heaven’s blessings upon our ruler may be rooted in the greatness of Heaven’s choosing him, with the supreme harmony of the universe concentrated in him. Richly abundant and continually increased, may all the countless favorable things his heart desires be enjoyed in their fullness by his own person. May these blessings arise from the depth of Heaven’s favor and its tranquil protection, with the harmonious concord of the manifold signs gathered in him. With happiness and goodness, and all things fitting, may every increasingly abundant blessing bestowed by Heaven be brought together in its entirety in the One Man.

With what, then, shall we compare this flourishing of blessings? Those mountains, mounds, ridges, and hills—all under Heaven …

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之言高大者必歸焉吾君之福實似之蓋敦艮
以厚祉無異於地道之崇高其植本之固夫固
巍然而莫踰也川之方至天下之言盛長者必
歸焉吾君之福實類之蓋瑞慶之大來無異於
川流之不息其發源之深夫固沛然而莫禦也
然山猶不足以盡其高也純嘏之錫天之篤慶
於不窮者且將益其豫大之勢而日見其峻極
矣謂高大而有不增乎川猶不足以盡其深也
慶澤之衍天之申錫于無疆者猶將濬其靈長
===
之源而日見其洋溢矣謂盛長而有不增乎夫
然後為天心之愛吾君而吾臣子藉天寵以承
鹿鳴四牡之澤者又寧有極耶雖然陳善納誨
敬君之大也天保獨侈言其福何哉蓋天者君
之所難諶福者君之所欲斂苟思得天斂福之
故而欽若昭事之心自將翼翼匪懈之無已忠
臣愛君美不忘規實隱然寓矣故知天保為納
約之辭也
思皇多士生此王國王國克生維周之楨
punctuated:
之言高大者必歸焉，吾君之福實似之。蓋敦艮以厚祉，無異於地道之崇高；其植本之固，夫固巍然而莫踰也。川之方至，天下之言盛長者必歸焉，吾君之福實類之。蓋瑞慶之大來，無異於川流之不息；其發源之深，夫固沛然而莫禦也。然山猶不足以盡其高也，純嘏之錫，天之篤慶於不窮者，且將益其豫大之勢，而日見其峻極矣，謂高大而有不增乎？川猶不足以盡其深也，慶澤之衍，天之申錫于無疆者，猶將濬其靈長之源，而日見其洋溢矣，謂盛長而有不增乎？夫然後為天心之愛吾君，而吾臣子藉天寵以承《鹿鳴》《四牡》之澤者，又寧有極耶？雖然，陳善納誨，敬君之大也，《天保》獨侈言其福，何哉？蓋天者，君之所難諶；福者，君之所欲斂。苟思得天斂福之故，而欽若昭事之心，自將翼翼匪懈之無已。忠臣愛君，美不忘規，實隱然寓矣。故知《天保》為納約之辭也。
思皇多士，生此王國。王國克生，維周之楨。
translation_en:
…whenever people throughout the world speak of height and grandeur, they inevitably turn to these. Our lord’s blessings truly resemble them. Firmly grounded and richly blessed [?], he is like the lofty eminence of the earth itself. So securely are their foundations planted that these blessings tower beyond all others. When a river comes surging forward, all who speak of abundance and growth inevitably turn to it. Our lord’s blessings truly resemble this. The great influx of auspicious blessings is like the ceaseless flow of a river. So deep is their source that they surge forth irresistibly.
Yet even mountains cannot fully express their height. As Heaven bestows abundant blessings and lavish favor without end, it will further increase their expansive grandeur, so that each day their towering summit becomes more apparent. Can one say that such height and grandeur do not increase? Nor can a river fully express their depth. As Heaven extends its beneficent bounty and renews its limitless gifts, it will further deepen their enduring source, so that each day their overflowing abundance becomes more apparent. Can one say that such abundance and growth do not increase? Only then is Heaven’s love for our lord fully realized. And could there be any limit to the bounty that we, his servants and subjects, receive through Heaven’s favor—the bounty celebrated in “The Deer Call” and “The Four Stallions”?
Nevertheless, setting forth what is good and offering admonition are the highest expressions of respect for one’s lord. Why, then, does “Heaven Protects” speak so profusely only of his blessings? Heaven is difficult for a ruler to rely upon; blessings are what he desires to gather. If he reflects upon how to gain Heaven’s favor and gather blessings, his resolve reverently to follow and illustriously to serve Heaven will naturally remain cautious and unflagging without end. Here, implicitly, lies the loyal minister’s love for his lord: even in praise, he does not forget admonition. Thus we know that “Heaven Protects” offers counsel that gains the ruler’s trust.
“Splendid are the many worthy men, born in this royal realm. The royal realm can indeed bring them forth: they are the pillars of Zhou.”

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
鄭秉厚
同考試官教諭韓批講王國克生處有識見
有筆力傑作也
同考試官教諭蘇批文體莊嚴措辭雅飭子
其亦勉敬之士與
考試官教諭管批雋永可味
考試官教諭李批得詩人旨
詩人美聖世之士而成輔世之功焉蓋國家以
賢才爲楨幹也周士有功於國其傳世之顯宜
===
矣周公推述文王得人之盛如此蓋曰天之於
我文王也敷錫之命集於孫子而顯世之榮及
於臣庶若是其盛矣然多士之生豈無所自哉
其在當時言之皆秉敬德以自將而謨明弼諧
之具偉然盛世之英懷欽翼以自勵而邁種庶
明之德卓乎王者之佐美哉此多士也吾見其
當貞元之會應運而生咸萃集於文明之世應
聖作之期乘時而起咸誕降於興王之邦夫孰
非我文王之士乎斯時也王國之氣運方隆旣
punctuated:
鄭秉厚

同考試官教諭韓批：講「王國克生」處，有識見，有筆力，傑作也。
同考試官教諭蘇批：文體莊嚴，措辭雅飭，子其亦勉敬之士與？
考試官教諭管批：雋永可味。
考試官教諭李批：得詩人旨。

詩人美聖世之士，而成輔世之功焉。蓋國家以賢才爲楨幹也。周士有功於國，其傳世之顯宜矣。周公推述文王得人之盛如此，蓋曰：天之於我文王也，敷錫之命集於孫子，而顯世之榮及於臣庶，若是其盛矣！然多士之生，豈無所自哉？其在當時言之，皆秉敬德以自將，而謨明弼諧之具，偉然盛世之英；懷欽翼以自勵，而邁種庶明之德，卓乎王者之佐。美哉，此多士也！吾見其當貞元之會，應運而生，咸萃集於文明之世；應聖作之期，乘時而起，咸誕降於興王之邦。夫孰非我文王之士乎？斯時也，王國之氣運方隆，旣
translation_en:
Zheng Binghou

Comment by Associate Examiner Han, Instructor: “The discussion of ‘the royal kingdom is able to bring them forth’ shows insight and force of expression. A masterful work.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Su, Instructor: “The composition is dignified, its wording elegant and well ordered. Are you, too, a scholar who diligently cultivates reverence?”
Comment by Examiner Guan, Instructor: “Rich in lasting significance and rewarding to savor.”
Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: “It captures the poet’s intent.”

The poet praises the scholars of a sage’s age and thereby accomplishes the work of assisting that age. For the state takes worthy and talented men as its supporting pillars. The scholars of Zhou rendered service to the state; it was fitting that their distinction should endure through the generations. Such was the abundance of worthy men obtained by King Wen that the Duke of Zhou extolled and recounted it. His meaning was this: Heaven’s generously bestowed mandate to our King Wen has descended upon his children and grandchildren, while the glory of distinction through the generations has extended to ministers and common people. How flourishing it is! Yet could the emergence of these many scholars have been without a source? Speaking of them in their own time, they all upheld reverent virtue to guide their conduct. With their capacities for enlightened counsel and harmonious assistance, they stood magnificently as the outstanding men of a flourishing age. They cherished reverence and circumspection to spur themselves onward. With the virtue of diligently cultivating every form of understanding, they stood preeminent as a king’s assistants. Admirable indeed were these many scholars! I see them born in response to the age’s appointed course, at the juncture where one cycle ends and another begins, all gathering in an age of cultural enlightenment. Answering the moment of a sage’s rise, they emerged when the time was right, all born into the realm of a rising king. Who among them was not a scholar of our King Wen? At that time, the royal kingdom’s vital forces and fortunes were just reaching their height, and already …

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
感召之有機而王者之道化方盛復培植之有
自是以能生此多士焉非偶然也吾知彙征于
朝者莫不攄勉敬之猷而弘賛襄之益布列在
位者莫不奮翼勵之志而宣輔理之忠修和有
夏雖文之謨也而疏附後先多士屏翰之功不
可少蓋一代維新之命亦於斯人乎有助矣輯
和邦家雖文之澤也而奔走禦侮多士蕃宣之
績不可誣蓋萬年丕造之基亦於斯人乎有賴
矣非周之所以爲幹者乎夫周士有輔世之功
===
固宜其獲傳世之顯也然非文王之德曷克致
是哉抑於是可以見君臣一體之義焉天人感
應之機焉文之受命不惟佑啓後人而倂及其
下天之祚周不惟昌君之嗣而又及其臣是豈
偶然者哉噫周公旣備述干篇欲成王繹思而
自得之矣然必勉之以念爾祖修厥德以配命
求福焉此成王所以緝熈基命而終底於日靖
之治也歟
春秋
punctuated:
感召之有機，而王者之道化方盛，復培植之有自，是以能生此多士焉，非偶然也。吾知彙征于朝者，莫不攄勉敬之猷而弘賛襄之益；布列在位者，莫不奮翼勵之志而宣輔理之忠。修和有夏，雖文之謨也，而疏附後先，多士屏翰之功不可少，蓋一代維新之命亦於斯人乎有助矣。輯和邦家，雖文之澤也，而奔走禦侮，多士蕃宣之績不可誣，蓋萬年丕造之基亦於斯人乎有賴矣。非周之所以爲幹者乎？夫周士有輔世之功，固宜其獲傳世之顯也。然非文王之德，曷克致是哉？抑於是可以見君臣一體之義焉，天人感應之機焉。文之受命，不惟佑啓後人，而倂及其下；天之祚周，不惟昌君之嗣，而又及其臣。是豈偶然者哉？噫！周公旣備述干篇，欲成王繹思而自得之矣。然必勉之以念爾祖，修厥德，以配命求福焉。此成王所以緝熈基命，而終底於日靖之治也歟？

春秋
translation_en:
…there was a means by which they were called forth; and the king’s transforming influence through the Way was then flourishing, providing a source for their nurture as well. Thus these many worthy men could arise: it was no accident. I know that those who advanced together to court all put forth plans marked by diligence and reverence, magnifying the benefits of their assistance; those arrayed in official positions all roused themselves to vigilant endeavor, displaying their loyalty in assisting government. Though bringing harmony to the lands of Xia was King Wen’s design, the many worthy men’s service as bulwarks—drawing distant people near, attaching them to the ruler, and serving before and behind him—was indispensable. The mandate that renewed the dynasty was indeed aided by these men. Though bringing concord to the realm was King Wen’s beneficence, the achievements of these many worthy men in serving as defenders and spreading his influence, hastening to serve and warding off aggression, cannot be denied. The foundation of the great enterprise that would endure for ten thousand years likewise depended on these men. Were they not those who served as Zhou’s mainstay?

Since the worthy men of Zhou rendered service in sustaining their age, it was surely fitting that they should attain distinction handed down through the generations. Yet without King Wen’s virtue, how could this have been achieved? Here, moreover, we may discern the principle that ruler and ministers form one body, and the workings of the mutual response between Heaven and humanity. King Wen’s receipt of the mandate not only protected his descendants and opened the way for them, but also extended to those beneath him. Heaven’s blessing upon Zhou not only brought prosperity to the ruler’s heirs, but also reached his ministers. Could this have been accidental?

Ah! The Duke of Zhou had already set this forth fully in the poem [?], wishing King Cheng to ponder it and grasp its meaning for himself. Yet he had to exhort him to “remember your ancestor,” cultivate his virtue, and thereby accord with the mandate and seek blessings. Was this not how King Cheng continued and enlarged the foundational mandate, ultimately achieving a government of daily growing tranquility?

Spring and Autumn Annals

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
八月公會齊侯宋公鄭伯曹伯邾人于檉
僖公元年秋齊侯宋公江人黃人會于
陽穀僖公三年
蔡栢齡
同考試官教諭周批威信二字發揮明爽此
必邃于經學者可以式矣
考試官教諭管批得聖人予齊桓管仲之旨
考試官教諭李批文體謹嚴
春秋兩紀伯好善其威信之著焉夫伯者之行
===
乎諸侯非威信莫以也此檉與陽穀之會所以
見取于春秋乎且楚自熊赀以來世為諸姬之
患北向之圖每為鄭病而東方之與則固恃江
黃以為利也創伯其時者當何如攘之耶是故
駕馭之策貴乎先聲非示之威則勢不張桓與
仲也念之若曰伐鄭之師楚方浸強未易挫也
而未可快于一逞也顧可以不集于眾乎于是
合列國而共舉于檉之會志無不同謀無不協
懿親之國必急于簡書而方張之敵務摧其禍
punctuated:
「八月，公會齊侯、宋公、鄭伯、曹伯、邾人于檉。」僖公元年。「秋，齊侯、宋公、江人、黃人會于陽穀。」僖公三年。

蔡栢齡

同考試官教諭周批：威信二字發揮明爽，此必邃于經學者，可以式矣。
考試官教諭管批：得聖人予齊桓、管仲之旨。
考試官教諭李批：文體謹嚴。

春秋兩紀伯好，善其威信之著焉。夫伯者之行乎諸侯，非威信莫以也。此檉與陽穀之會所以見取于春秋乎？且楚自熊赀以來，世為諸姬之患，北向之圖每為鄭病，而東方之與，則固恃江、黃以為利也。創伯其時者，當何如攘之耶？是故駕馭之策貴乎先聲，非示之威，則勢不張。桓與仲也念之，若曰：伐鄭之師，楚方浸強，未易挫也，而未可快于一逞也。顧可以不集于眾乎？于是合列國而共舉于檉之會，志無不同，謀無不協。懿親之國必急于簡書，而方張之敵務摧其禍
translation_en:
“In the eighth month, the duke met with the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, and a representative of Zhu at Cheng.” First year of Duke Xi. “In autumn, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, and representatives of Jiang and Huang met at Yanggu.” Third year of Duke Xi.

Cai Bailing 蔡栢齡

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, an Instructor: “The exposition of the two terms ‘authority’ and ‘trustworthiness’ is clear and lucid. This must be the work of someone deeply versed in classical learning; it may serve as a model.”
Comment by Examiner Guan, an Instructor: “It grasps the Sage’s intention in approving Duke Huan of Qi and Guan Zhong.”
Comment by Examiner Li, an Instructor: “The composition is disciplined and rigorous.”

The Spring and Autumn Annals twice records the hegemon’s friendly alliances, commending the manifest authority and trustworthiness displayed in them. For a hegemon to exercise leadership among the feudal lords, authority and trustworthiness are indispensable. Is this why the meetings at Cheng and Yanggu receive approval in the Spring and Autumn Annals? Since the time of Xiong Zi, Chu had, generation after generation, troubled the states ruled by the Ji lineage. Its designs upon the north repeatedly afflicted Zheng, while for support in the east it relied firmly upon Jiang and Huang to secure its advantage. How should one establishing a hegemony at that time have repelled it?

Thus, in the art of controlling other states, establishing an intimidating reputation beforehand is paramount. Unless authority is displayed, one’s power cannot expand. Duke Huan and Guan Zhong considered the matter as though saying: “As for the army attacking Zheng, Chu is now growing steadily stronger and cannot easily be checked; we cannot indulge ourselves in a single impulsive show of force. Can we possibly fail to assemble the strength of the many?” They therefore brought the various states together for joint action at the meeting at Cheng. Their purposes were united and their plans coordinated. The closely related states had to respond urgently to the written summons, while every effort had to be made to thwart the harm intended by an enemy whose power was expanding…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
心蓋雖未陳師江漢而併力壇坫之間眞有以
作同惡者之氣矣人見于陘之次齊能以威帖
楚孰知震恐之而奪其魄也乃威之振先在勤
鄭之時乎昔湯誓之詞惟聞有衆慮弗集耳不
意檉之會爲近之而楚之北向進無所肆其侫
也至若制勝之謀貴于多助非示之信則勢必
携桓與仲也又念之若曰貫澤之盟江黃初至
未遽孚也而未必樂用于我也顧可以不由其
約乎于是尋貫澤而再締陽穀之好聚而爲正
===
分而爲奇定玆掎角吾之戰守有所資而奪其
右臂彼之進退無所據蓋雖未整旅陘亭而决
策帷幄之中先有以堅按兵者之援矣人見召
陵之盟齊能以信款楚孰知多筭之而離其黨
也乃信之惇先在結江黃之日乎昔牧野之師
遠及微國慮弗恊耳又不意陽穀之舉爲近之
而楚之東方退無所濟其惡也君子曰桓公識
明管仲之才有餘世道所爲賴如此宜其爲春
秋之所取也雖然使其能始終不渝則威不假
punctuated:
心。蓋雖未陳師江漢，而併力壇坫之間，眞有以作同惡者之氣矣。人見于陘之次，齊能以威帖楚，孰知震恐之而奪其魄也，乃威之振先在勤鄭之時乎？昔湯誓之詞，惟聞有衆，慮弗集耳。不意檉之會爲近之，而楚之北向，進無所肆其侫也。至若制勝之謀，貴于多助，非示之信，則勢必携。桓與仲也又念之，若曰：「貫澤之盟，江黃初至，未遽孚也，而未必樂用于我也，顧可以不由其約乎？」于是尋貫澤而再締陽穀之好，聚而爲正，分而爲奇，定玆掎角，吾之戰守有所資，而奪其右臂，彼之進退無所據。蓋雖未整旅陘亭，而决策帷幄之中，先有以堅按兵者之援矣。人見召陵之盟，齊能以信款楚，孰知多筭之而離其黨也，乃信之惇先在結江黃之日乎？昔牧野之師，遠及微國，慮弗恊耳。又不意陽穀之舉爲近之，而楚之東方，退無所濟其惡也。

君子曰：「桓公識明，管仲之才有餘，世道所爲賴如此，宜其爲春秋之所取也。雖然，使其能始終不渝，則威不假
translation_en:
…intentions. Although they had not yet arrayed their armies along the Jiang and Han rivers, by combining their strength at the diplomatic gathering they truly roused the spirits of those who shared a common enemy. People see that, when the army encamped at Xing, Qi could subdue Chu through its might. Who realizes that the might which terrified Chu and broke its spirit had first been displayed during the campaign against Zheng? In the words of the Oath of Tang, we hear only his address to the assembled multitude: his concern was that they might not come together. Unexpectedly, the meeting at Cheng approached this example, leaving Chu, in its northward advance, no opportunity to give free rein to its wickedness.

As for plans to secure victory, these depend upon abundant support; unless one demonstrates trustworthiness, the alliance will inevitably fall apart. Duke Huan and Guan Zhong reflected further, as if saying: “At the covenant of Guanze, Jiang and Huang had only just joined us. Their trust was not immediately secured, and they were not necessarily willing to serve our purposes. How, then, could we fail to abide by our agreement?” Thus they renewed the covenant of Guanze and again cemented friendship at Yanggu. United, their forces would serve as the regular force; divided, as the surprise force. By establishing this coordinated deployment, they provided resources for their own operations in attack and defense, while cutting off Chu’s right arm and leaving it without support in either advance or retreat. Although they had not yet marshaled their troops at Xingting, their deliberations within the command tent had already secured the support of those holding their troops in readiness. People see that, at the covenant of Shaoling, Qi could bring Chu to terms through its trustworthiness. Who realizes that the thorough planning which detached Chu’s allies had its foundation in the trustworthiness cultivated earlier, when Qi bound Jiang and Huang to itself? Formerly, the army at Muye drew upon even the distant state of Wei: the concern was that they might not act in concert. Again, unexpectedly, the undertaking at Yanggu approached this example, leaving Chu, on its eastern flank, no support for carrying out its evil designs when it withdrew.

The gentleman says: “Duke Huan possessed clear discernment, and Guan Zhong had talent in abundance. Such were the services upon which the order of the age depended; it was fitting that the Spring and Autumn Annals should approve of them. Nevertheless, had they remained unwavering from beginning to end, their authority would not have depended upon…”

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
於內政信不假於載書庶幾乎王者之事惜召
陵以後鮮克有終執濤塗則威肆而江黃不救
則信失不惟遠於王事伯業且隳矣蓋齊桓之
量不勝其德管仲之器不勝其才玆伯者所爲
假也然則王道之大如何曰誠而已矣
單伯至自齊文公十有五年
徐廷綬
同考試官敎諭周批孔子作春秋志在尊周
耳此作明悉可式錄之
===
考試官敎諭管批尊王命意藹然詞外可誦
考試官敎諭李批精確渾成
春秋字命卿之歸國所以謹臣禮也夫人臣之
禮莫大于尊君單伯以周之命卿而可以列國
大夫待之哉聖人所以必錄其字以此且單伯
以叔姬之故見執于齊魯請而歸之使來致命
焉經之例大夫執而至則名此獨以字稱豈曰
以巳執之而非其罪與曰尊王命以謹臣禮耳
蓋維王有命所以馭天下之貴者在是焉而降
punctuated:
於內政，信不假於載書，庶幾乎王者之事。惜召陵以後，鮮克有終：執濤塗則威肆，而江黃不救則信失。不惟遠於王事，伯業且隳矣。蓋齊桓之量不勝其德，管仲之器不勝其才，玆伯者所爲假也。然則王道之大如何？曰：誠而已矣。
單伯至自齊，文公十有五年。
徐廷綬。
同考試官敎諭周批：「孔子作《春秋》，志在尊周耳。此作明悉可式，錄之。」
考試官敎諭管批：「尊王命意，藹然詞外，可誦。」
考試官敎諭李批：「精確渾成。」
《春秋》字命卿之歸國，所以謹臣禮也。夫人臣之禮，莫大于尊君。單伯以周之命卿，而可以列國大夫待之哉？聖人所以必錄其字，以此。且單伯以叔姬之故見執于齊，魯請而歸之，使來致命焉。經之例，大夫執而至則名，此獨以字稱，豈曰以巳執之而非其罪與？曰：尊王命以謹臣禮耳。蓋維王有命，所以馭天下之貴者在是焉，而降
translation_en:
…upon internal administration, and his trustworthiness had not depended upon written covenants, he might have approached the achievements of a true king. Regrettably, after Shaoling he seldom carried things through to a worthy conclusion: by arresting Tao Tu he exercised his might without restraint, and by failing to rescue Jiang and Huang he forfeited trust. Not only did he fall far short of kingly achievement; even his enterprise as hegemon was undermined. Duke Huan of Qi’s capacity could not sustain his virtue, and Guan Zhong’s scope could not sustain his talent. This is why a hegemon merely borrows the outward forms of virtue. What, then, constitutes the greatness of the kingly Way? The answer is sincerity alone.
“Shan Bo arrived from Qi.” Fifteenth year of Duke Wen.
Xu Tingshou.
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor: “Confucius composed the Spring and Autumn Annals with the sole intention of honoring Zhou. This essay is clear and thorough and can serve as a model. Include it.”
Comment by Examiner Guan, Instructor: “The intention to honor the king suffuses the essay beyond its explicit wording. Worth reciting.”
Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: “Precise and seamless.”
The Spring and Autumn Annals records the return of a royally appointed minister to his state by his courtesy designation, thereby upholding the proprieties owed by a subject. Among those proprieties, none is greater than honoring one’s ruler. As a minister appointed by Zhou, could Shan Bo be treated as merely a grand master of one of the various states? This is why the Sage insisted upon recording his courtesy designation. Moreover, Shan Bo was detained in Qi on account of Shu Ji. Lu requested his release, and he was sent back to deliver his charge there. According to the Classic’s usual practice, a grand master who returns after being detained is recorded by his personal name. Here alone a courtesy designation is used. Could this be because, although he had been detained, he was innocent of wrongdoing [?]? The answer is that it honors the king’s command and thereby upholds a subject’s proprieties. For it is through the king’s commands that he governs all those of noble rank throughout the realm; and when these descend…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
監于下爲至重矣人臣被命所以揚天子之休
者在是焉而祇若于身爲至榮矣單伯者位雖
列於魯邦爵則詔於周室監國以爲任冊命作
于內史彼貴戚之卿延賞于世者固不得而尚
其尊折邑以爲號章服掌之宗伯彼賜族之臣
建官于私者又惡得而擬其貴故王章之赫奕
彼將奉之終其身焉不得以見執之故而損其
禮數之常蓋有定名焉策之王朝人固不得而
予奪之也天命之簡臨人亦將戴之震其望焉
===
豈容以事變之偶而改其寵遇之舊蓋有定分
焉錫之天吏人固不得而隆殺之也在昔王人
下士以一時之命猶得位侯王之上焉況茲列
爵五服者哉是故春秋特從而字之待之以王
朝大夫之例非尊單伯也尊王命也尊王命以
謹臣禮也孔子敬君可謂無所不用其情矣雖
然人臣以有命爲榮亦以不辱命爲善知君命
之在吾身能自樹以對揚之知君命之在吾國
能自振以丕顯之是乃所謂事君之義而單伯
punctuated: 監于下，爲至重矣。人臣被命，所以揚天子之休者在是焉，而祇若于身，爲至榮矣。單伯者，位雖列於魯邦，爵則詔於周室；監國以爲任，冊命作于內史。彼貴戚之卿，延賞于世者，固不得而尚其尊；折邑以爲號，章服掌之宗伯，彼賜族之臣，建官于私者，又惡得而擬其貴？故王章之赫奕，彼將奉之終其身焉，不得以見執之故而損其禮數之常。蓋有定名焉，策之王朝，人固不得而予奪之也。天命之簡臨，人亦將戴之，震其望焉，豈容以事變之偶而改其寵遇之舊？蓋有定分焉，錫之天吏，人固不得而隆殺之也。在昔王人下士，以一時之命，猶得位侯王之上焉，況茲列爵五服者哉！是故《春秋》特從而字之，待之以王朝大夫之例，非尊單伯也，尊王命也。尊王命以謹臣禮也。孔子敬君，可謂無所不用其情矣。雖然，人臣以有命爲榮，亦以不辱命爲善。知君命之在吾身，能自樹以對揚之；知君命之在吾國，能自振以丕顯之，是乃所謂事君之義，而單伯
translation_en:
…exercising oversight below is a matter of the utmost gravity. A minister receives a royal commission as the means of proclaiming the Son of Heaven’s glory; reverently fulfilling it in his own person is the highest honor. Although Shan Bo held a position in the state of Lu, his rank was conferred by command of the royal house of Zhou. His charge was to oversee the state, and his document of investiture was drawn up by the Court Scribe. Even ministers from the ruler’s noble kin, whose rewards continued through successive generations, could not surpass him in dignity. An apportioned domain supplied his title, and the Minister of Rites had charge of his ceremonial insignia and robes. How, then, could retainers granted clan names and appointed to offices in private households compare with him in nobility?

Thus he was to uphold the splendor of the royal insignia throughout his life. The fact that he had been taken captive could not diminish the customary ceremonial treatment due to him. His established status had been recorded at the royal court: others certainly had no authority to grant or withdraw it. When Heaven’s mandate deigned to descend upon him, others were to honor it and stand in awe of his prestige. How could an accidental turn of events be allowed to alter the favor he had previously enjoyed? His established standing had been bestowed upon him as an officer of Heaven: others certainly had no authority to exalt or diminish it. In former times, a royal envoy who was merely a junior serviceman could, by virtue of a temporary commission, take precedence even over lords and kings. How much more must this apply to one invested with rank among the five grades of ceremonial dress!

For this reason, the Spring and Autumn Annals specifically refers to him by his courtesy name, treating him according to the convention for grand masters of the royal court. This honors not Shan Bo himself, but the royal command. It honors the royal command in order to uphold the ritual obligations of ministers. Confucius’s reverence for the ruler may indeed be said to have engaged his feelings in every possible way.

Nevertheless, while a minister takes honor in receiving a commission, his excellence also lies in not disgracing it. Knowing that the ruler’s command rests upon his person, he must establish himself so as to acknowledge and proclaim it; knowing that the ruler’s command rests upon his state, he must rouse himself so as to make it greatly manifest. This is what is meant by the duty of serving one’s ruler. But Shan Bo…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
者俛首就執曾不能上告下訴奉天討以正商
人之罪而自直其誣也則何取焉然則歸魯告
至亦倖焉耳此又春秋警臣道之意
禮記
故人情者聖王之田也脩禮以耕之陳義
以種之講學以耨之本仁以聚之播樂
以安之
鄭復亨
同考試官教諭蔣批詞旨醇鬯氣象渾融發
聖王治情之意殆盡宜錄以式
考試官教諭管批義精詞健當是作者
考試官教諭李批理到
記者喻聖王之治人情必詳其所治之道焉甚
矣人情未易以治也聖王備舉其道以治之斯
其有弗治者哉禮運之意若謂夫人之情每遷
於多變而聖王之心必先於化中是故聖王以
人情之易流而無節也於是即其應感之發而
裁成之有術因其念慮之形而範圍之不過是
===
[]
punctuated:
者俛首就執，曾不能上告下訴，奉天討以正商人之罪，而自直其誣也，則何取焉？然則歸魯告至，亦倖焉耳。此又《春秋》警臣道之意。

禮記

故人情者，聖王之田也。脩禮以耕之，陳義以種之，講學以耨之，本仁以聚之，播樂以安之。

鄭復亨

同考試官教諭蔣批：詞旨醇鬯，氣象渾融，發聖王治情之意殆盡，宜錄以式。
考試官教諭管批：義精詞健，當是作者。
考試官教諭李批：理到。

記者喻聖王之治人情，必詳其所治之道焉。甚矣，人情未易以治也！聖王備舉其道以治之，斯其有弗治者哉？《禮運》之意若謂：夫人之情，每遷於多變，而聖王之心，必先於化中。是故聖王以人情之易流而無節也，於是即其應感之發，而裁成之有術；因其念慮之形，而範圍之不過。是

[]
translation_en:
… yet he bowed his head and submitted to arrest. He could not even appeal to those above or plead with those below, carry out Heaven’s punishment to bring Shangren to account for his crime, and clear himself of the false accusation. What, then, is there to commend in him? His return to Lu and announcement of his arrival were thus merely a stroke of good fortune. Here again the Spring and Autumn Annals intends to admonish ministers concerning their proper conduct.

Record of Rites

“Thus human feelings are the field of the sage kings. They cultivate ritual to plow it, set forth righteousness to sow it, expound learning to weed it, take benevolence as the foundation to gather its harvest, and spread music to bring it peace.”

Zheng Fuheng

Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, an Instructor: “The language and meaning are pure and fluent; the overall quality is integrated and harmonious. It brings out almost completely the meaning of the sage kings’ ordering of human feelings. It should be recorded as a model.”
Comment by Examiner Guan, an Instructor: “The meaning is refined and the language vigorous. Surely this is an accomplished writer.”
Comment by Examiner Li, an Instructor: “The principle is fully grasped.”

In illustrating how the sage kings order human feelings, the author of the Record necessarily explains in detail the means by which they do so. How very difficult human feelings are to govern! Yet when the sage kings employ all their methods to govern them, could any remain ungoverned? The meaning of “The Evolution of Rites” seems to be this: human feelings continually shift amid manifold changes, while the sage kings’ minds must take the lead in transforming them toward the mean [?]. Therefore, recognizing how readily human feelings drift without restraint, the sage kings apply methods to shape them as they arise in response to external stimuli; as thoughts and deliberations take form, they keep them within bounds so that they do not go too far. title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
聖王以治人情爲己責其諸農夫以百畝之不
易爲己憂者也人情不爲聖王之田乎然是田
也其治之當何如哉夫田未有不先之以耕者
而耕則必脩之以禮焉本秩敘以植其規謹節
文以辨其則品式昭而天下之率履不越者在
是矣非卽秉耒耜以耕之者乎耕未有不繼之
以種者而種則必陳之以義焉協時措以適其
宜妙化裁以達其變裁制定而天下之順應無
方者在是矣非卽隨田之宜而種之者乎然禮
===
耕義種矣而不以講學耨之則眞妄莫辨其能
殽雜之是免耶于是研究以析其精而黜欲以
存理討論以致其極而去非以存是其於田之
去草以養苗者蓋未可以差殊觀也耨而曰講
學可謂博矣而約之則未也必會萬殊於一本
之妙要衆善於克一之歸散見之理自將兼統
之而不遺矣其穀之熟而斂之者與此何以異
耶聚而曰本仁利焉爾矣而安之則未也必涵
泳以陶其性情和順以純於道德物累之忘自
punctuated: 聖王以治人情爲己責，其諸農夫以百畝之不易爲己憂者也。人情不爲聖王之田乎？然是田也，其治之當何如哉？夫田未有不先之以耕者，而耕則必脩之以禮焉。本秩敘以植其規，謹節文以辨其則，品式昭而天下之率履不越者在是矣，非卽秉耒耜以耕之者乎？耕未有不繼之以種者，而種則必陳之以義焉。協時措以適其宜，妙化裁以達其變，裁制定而天下之順應無方者在是矣，非卽隨田之宜而種之者乎？然禮耕義種矣，而不以講學耨之，則眞妄莫辨，其能殽雜之是免耶？于是研究以析其精，而黜欲以存理；討論以致其極，而去非以存是。其於田之去草以養苗者，蓋未可以差殊觀也。耨而曰講學，可謂博矣，而約之則未也。必會萬殊於一本之妙，要衆善於克一之歸，散見之理自將兼統之而不遺矣。其穀之熟而斂之者，與此何以異耶？聚而曰本仁，利焉爾矣，而安之則未也。必涵泳以陶其性情，和順以純於道德，物累之忘自
translation_en:
…The sage kings take the ordering of human feelings as their own responsibility, much as farmers make the failure to cultivate their hundred mu their own concern. Are human feelings not the sage kings’ fields? How, then, should these fields be cultivated? Work on a field invariably begins with plowing, and this plowing must be carried out through ritual propriety. They establish its standards upon the proper ordering of ranks and attend carefully to its measured forms to distinguish its rules. Herein lie the clear patterns that enable all under Heaven to follow the proper course without transgression. Is this not precisely like taking up plowing implements to till the soil? Plowing is invariably followed by sowing, and this sowing must be carried out through righteousness. They accord with timely action to suit what is appropriate and exercise subtle discernment in adapting to change. Herein lie the settled principles of judgment that enable all under Heaven to respond fittingly without being confined to a single method. Is this not precisely like sowing according to the suitability of the field?
Yet once they have plowed with ritual propriety and sown with righteousness, unless they weed through the discussion of learning, truth and falsehood remain indistinguishable. How could they avoid their becoming mixed together? Thus they investigate to discern the finest points, rejecting desires to preserve principle; they discuss to reach the fullest understanding, removing what is wrong to preserve what is right. This surely cannot be regarded as different from removing weeds from a field to nourish the seedlings. To speak of weeding as discussing learning may be called comprehensive, but it does not yet bring that learning to its essential unity. They must bring the myriad differences together in the subtle unity of a single root and gather the many forms of goodness into the attainment of oneness. The principles appearing in diverse places will then naturally be comprehended together, with none omitted. How does this differ from gathering grain when it has ripened?
To speak of gathering as taking benevolence as the root means only that they find benefit in it; they are not yet at ease in it. They must immerse themselves deeply to cultivate their dispositions and feelings, becoming harmonious and compliant so as to attain purity in the Way and virtue. Through forgetting the encumbrances of external things, they will naturally…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
有以造於自然之域矣其穀之食而厭飫者於
此何以殊耶夫禮耕義種治情有以開其始矣
仁聚樂安治情有以成其終矣而又以學講明
其間聖王治情之道備具如此則夫人情之無
不治也固其宜哉大抵人情有欲易發而難制
而聖王獨致詳於此脩道之敎始終備其條理
其所以懼夫陷溺其心者良亦切矣然此豈直
以情之不流於僻而已耶是故人情治而大順
致順道達而三才應太和雍熈之盛固皆由此
===
其選矣雖然猶有要焉亦曰立人極而已
論倫無患樂之情也欣喜歡愛樂之官也
中正無邪禮之質也莊敬恭順禮之制
也若夫禮樂之施於金石越於聲音用
於宗廟社稷事乎山川鬼神則此所與
民同也
張𦬊
同考試官敎諭蔣批詞格精健且意義肯綮
是必究心於禮樂之義者
punctuated:
有以造於自然之域矣。其穀之食而厭飫者，於此何以殊耶？夫禮耕義種，治情有以開其始矣；仁聚樂安，治情有以成其終矣；而又以學講明其間。聖王治情之道備具如此，則夫人情之無不治也，固其宜哉！大抵人情有欲，易發而難制，而聖王獨致詳於此，脩道之敎，始終備其條理，其所以懼夫陷溺其心者，良亦切矣。然此豈直以情之不流於僻而已耶？是故人情治而大順致，順道達而三才應，太和雍熈之盛，固皆由此其選矣。雖然，猶有要焉，亦曰立人極而已。
論倫無患，樂之情也；欣喜歡愛，樂之官也。中正無邪，禮之質也；莊敬恭順，禮之制也。若夫禮樂之施於金石，越於聲音，用於宗廟社稷，事乎山川鬼神，則此所與民同也。
張𦬊
同考試官敎諭蔣批：詞格精健，且意義肯綮，是必究心於禮樂之義者。
translation_en:
…thereby attaining the realm of natural spontaneity. How does eating one’s grain until fully satisfied differ from this? Plowing with ritual and sowing with righteousness initiate the ordering of the emotions; gathering with benevolence and finding repose through music bring that ordering to completion. Learning, moreover, elucidates what lies between. Since the sage kings’ way of ordering the emotions is so fully furnished, it is surely fitting that no human emotion should remain unordered! Generally, human emotions involve desires that are easily aroused but difficult to control. The sage kings therefore devoted particular attention to this. Their teaching for cultivating the Way provided an orderly framework from beginning to end: their concern lest people’s hearts become engulfed and submerged was indeed profound. Yet could its purpose have been merely to prevent the emotions from straying into perversity? Thus, when human emotions are ordered, great accord is achieved; when the way of accord prevails, the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humanity—respond. The flourishing of supreme harmony and concord surely all proceeds from this [?]. Nevertheless, there remains an essential point: simply to establish the ultimate standard for humanity.
“Harmony and order without distress are the inner nature of music; delight, joy, gladness, and love are its functions. Centrality and correctness without perversity are the substance of ritual; solemnity, reverence, respect, and compliance are its forms. As for ritual and music being expressed through bronze bells and stone chimes, issuing in sounds, employed in the ancestral temples and at the altars of soil and grain, and used to serve the mountains, rivers, ghosts, and spirits—these are what are shared with the people.”
Zhang Qi 張𦬊.
Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor: “The diction and style are refined and vigorous, and the meaning strikes the essential points. This must be someone who has earnestly investigated the significance of ritual and music.”

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎諭管批體認真切錄之
考試官敎諭李批詞𢠢而意婉
記者詳禮樂之義而因及其數之易知者焉夫
禮樂之義和序盡之矣故知此者非君則莫與
焉豈其民之可同也耶樂記君子記此若謂先
王之制禮樂也有義焉有數焉數以顯其象義
以涵其精是故觀於其義而豈君之所可已者
乎自其樂而言之雅頌陳盛世之章律呂適後
先之度太和協暢而怗懘之不形此固樂之本
===
情在是矣以至順其心而有欣喜焉得所悅而
有歡愛焉是聲氣之元含於吾心而其論倫之
播被固皆由之以主宰也不曰樂之官乎自其
禮而言之本之中以推行循之正以自立至序
周旋而邪僻之不作此固禮之本質在是矣以
至莊敬焉以之作吾肅也恭順焉以之作吾讓
也是無體之節體諸於身而其中正之措施固
皆由之以綱維也不曰禮之制乎斯則和序肇
禮樂之原而非人無以通其奧禮樂妙身心之
punctuated:
考試官敎諭管批：體認真切，錄之。
考試官敎諭李批：詞𢠢而意婉。
記者詳禮樂之義，而因及其數之易知者焉。夫禮樂之義，和序盡之矣。故知此者，非君則莫與焉，豈其民之可同也耶？樂記君子記此，若謂先王之制禮樂也，有義焉，有數焉。數以顯其象，義以涵其精。是故觀於其義，而豈君之所可已者乎？自其樂而言之，雅頌陳盛世之章，律呂適後先之度，太和協暢，而怗懘之不形，此固樂之本情在是矣。以至順其心而有欣喜焉，得所悅而有歡愛焉，是聲氣之元含於吾心，而其論倫之播被，固皆由之以主宰也。不曰樂之官乎？自其禮而言之，本之中以推行，循之正以自立，至序周旋，而邪僻之不作，此固禮之本質在是矣。以至莊敬焉，以之作吾肅也；恭順焉，以之作吾讓也。是無體之節，體諸於身，而其中正之措施，固皆由之以綱維也。不曰禮之制乎？斯則和序肇禮樂之原，而非人無以通其奧；禮樂妙身心之
translation_en:
Examiner Guan, Instructor, comments: “The understanding is genuine and precise. Accept it.”
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “The wording is [?], and the meaning is subtly expressed.”
The recorder explains in detail the principles of ritual and music, and consequently touches upon their readily understood formal particulars. Harmony and order fully encompass the principles of ritual and music. Thus, none but the ruler can participate in understanding them. How could the common people share equally in this? In recording this, the gentleman who composed the Record of Music seems to be saying that the former kings’ establishment of ritual and music involved both principles and formal particulars. The particulars display their outward forms; the principles contain their essential spirit. How, then, could the ruler ever cease attending to their principles?
Speaking of music: the Elegantiae and Hymns set forth the compositions of a flourishing age; the pitch standards bring earlier and later notes into due measure. Supreme harmony flows freely, and no discord appears. Here indeed lies the fundamental nature of music. Further, when the heart is at ease, joy and delight arise; when it obtains what pleases it, gladness and affection arise. The source of sound and vital energy is contained within our hearts, and the diffusion of music’s ordered patterns [?] is governed entirely by it. Is this not what is called the functioning of music?
Speaking of ritual: one takes equilibrium as the basis for carrying it out and follows rectitude in establishing oneself. Perfect order governs every movement, and perversity does not arise. Here indeed lies the fundamental substance of ritual. Further, solemnity and reverence awaken our gravity; respectfulness and compliance awaken our deference. These measures, though without bodily form, are embodied in our persons, and all practical expressions of equilibrium and rectitude depend upon them for their governing framework. Is this not what is called the regulation of ritual?
Thus harmony and order constitute the source of ritual and music, yet without the human person their profundity cannot be comprehended; ritual and music give wondrous efficacy to the … of body and mind…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
用而惟君有以契其深若夫禮樂之被於金石
越之聲音而搏拊之有節用之宗廟社稷事於
山川鬼神而駿奔之有秩此特其數之可陳者
耳不必其君而後知也而凡民之得於共聞者
皆可以與聞其聲矣亦不必獨於君而有知也
而凡民之得於共見者皆可以與見其文矣其
夫情官質制之妙寓於器數之中是豈可得而
同哉由是觀之禮樂之義惟君所獨知而不與
民同則夫本和序以為禮樂先者其責誠有所
===
歸矣而不明其義可乎雖然禮樂亦豈可以偽
為者哉蓋樂者吾心之和禮者吾身之序必其
內而無斯須之不和外而無斯須之不敬推其
精神心術之蘊以顯於制作之間而後禮樂之
道得矣故君子之中正是履和平是樂者良以
此耳不然欣喜歡愛則為導慾莊敬恭順則為
象恭而其論倫之詞中正之節亦數焉爾也其
何禮樂之足云
第貳場
punctuated:
用，而惟君有以契其深。若夫禮樂之被於金石，越之聲音，而搏拊之有節；用之宗廟社稷，事於山川鬼神，而駿奔之有秩：此特其數之可陳者耳，不必其君而後知也。而凡民之得於共聞者，皆可以與聞其聲矣，亦不必獨於君而有知也。而凡民之得於共見者，皆可以與見其文矣。其夫情官質制之妙，寓於器數之中，是豈可得而同哉？由是觀之，禮樂之義，惟君所獨知，而不與民同，則夫本和序以為禮樂先者，其責誠有所歸矣，而不明其義可乎？雖然，禮樂亦豈可以偽為者哉？蓋樂者，吾心之和；禮者，吾身之序。必其內而無斯須之不和，外而無斯須之不敬，推其精神心術之蘊，以顯於制作之間，而後禮樂之道得矣。故君子之中正是履、和平是樂者，良以此耳。不然，欣喜歡愛則為導慾，莊敬恭順則為象恭，而其論倫之詞、中正之節，亦數焉爾也，其何禮樂之足云？

第貳場
translation_en:
…their operation, yet only the ruler can grasp their profundity. As for ritual and music being expressed through bells and chimes, issuing forth in sound [?], with the striking and tapping kept to a measured rhythm; their use in ancestral temples and at the altars of soil and grain, in serving the spirits of mountains and rivers, with those hastening to perform their duties maintaining proper order: these are merely their observable procedures, which can be set forth. One need not be the ruler to understand them. Whatever ordinary people can hear in common, they can all share in hearing its sounds; knowledge of these is not confined to the ruler. Whatever ordinary people can see in common, they can all share in seeing its outward forms. But the subtleties of feeling and function, substance and regulation [?], reside within these instruments and procedures: how could understanding of these be shared equally? Seen in this light, the meaning of ritual and music is known uniquely to the ruler, whose understanding differs from that of the people. Thus the responsibility for taking harmony and order as the foundation that precedes ritual and music truly has someone upon whom it rests. Can he then fail to understand their meaning?

Nevertheless, how could ritual and music be counterfeited? Music is the harmony of one's heart; ritual is the order of one's person. Inwardly, there must not be a single moment without harmony; outwardly, not a single moment without reverence. One must bring forth the accumulated resources of one's spirit and mind, manifesting them in the establishment of institutions and forms. Only then is the Way of ritual and music attained. This is precisely why the gentleman practices centrality and correctness and delights in harmony and peace. Otherwise, joy and affection merely incite desire, solemn reverence and humble compliance become a mere semblance of respect, and words setting forth human relationships and measured expressions of centrality and correctness are likewise nothing more than outward procedures. How could these deserve to be called ritual and music?

Second Session

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
論
聖人之仁如天地
盧漸
同考試官教諭張批博雅之才昌大之氣且
發揮聖人天地之仁懇切詳盡仁而壽之理躍如目
前矣敬服敬服
同考試官學正李批議論充贍思致精瑩眞
有見於聖人天地之仁者
考試官教諭管批體格高古辭氣冲雅可
以爲式矣
===
考試官教諭李批理融見澈且中矩矱錄
之
聖人以其身成位天地之中而與天地同悠久
者何也蓋天地之心獨鍾於聖人而聖人以天
地之心倂包乎天下夫天地何心也所謂天地
之大德曰生者是也是太極之理也卽所謂仁
也天地以太極之理乘之而爲氣是故兩儀久
奠而不易聖人以天地之心運之而爲氣是故
punctuated:
論
聖人之仁如天地
盧漸

同考試官教諭張批：博雅之才，昌大之氣，且發揮聖人天地之仁，懇切詳盡，仁而壽之理躍如目前矣。敬服！敬服！

同考試官學正李批：議論充贍，思致精瑩，眞有見於聖人天地之仁者。

考試官教諭管批：體格高古，辭氣冲雅，可以爲式矣。

考試官教諭李批：理融見澈，且中矩矱，錄之。

聖人以其身成位天地之中，而與天地同悠久者，何也？蓋天地之心獨鍾於聖人，而聖人以天地之心倂包乎天下。夫天地何心也？所謂天地之大德曰生者，是也。是太極之理也，卽所謂仁也。天地以太極之理乘之而爲氣，是故兩儀久奠而不易；聖人以天地之心運之而爲氣，是故
translation_en:
Discourse
“The Sage’s Benevolence Is Like Heaven and Earth”
By Lu Jian

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “Erudite and cultivated talent, expansive and vigorous spirit. Moreover, his exposition of the benevolence of the sage and of Heaven and Earth is earnest, thorough, and detailed. The principle that benevolence brings longevity appears vividly before our eyes. My admiration! My admiration!”

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: “The argument is rich and ample, the thought refined and lucid. Here is someone who truly understands the benevolence of the sage and of Heaven and Earth.”

Comment by Examiner Guan, Instructor: “The composition’s form is lofty and antique; its diction and tone are mild and elegant. It may serve as a model.”

Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: “The principles are coherently integrated, the insight penetrating; it also conforms to the established standards. Include it.”

How is it that the sage, in his own person, takes his proper place between Heaven and Earth and endures as long as they do? It is because the heart of Heaven and Earth is concentrated uniquely in the sage, and with that heart the sage embraces all under Heaven. What, then, is the heart of Heaven and Earth? It is what is meant by the saying, “The great virtue of Heaven and Earth is called generation.” This is the principle of the Supreme Ultimate (taiji); it is precisely what is called benevolence. Heaven and Earth employ the principle of the Supreme Ultimate to ride upon and constitute vital force (qi); thus the Two Modes are enduringly established and do not change. The sage employs the heart of Heaven and Earth to set it in motion and constitute vital force; thus…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
三才竝立而無疆理以主氣氣以載理理不息
則氣亦不息天地之理以神運者也聖人之仁
以心運者也天地以神運故普萬物而不宰其
功聖人以心運故體萬物而不息其道此聖人
之仁所以同天地而其身與天地相爲悠久者
此也臨川吳氏曰聖人之仁如天地蓋言聖人
之壽而推本於仁也嗟乎其知言哉今夫天地
普萬物而無心者也人見其冲然穆然無聲無
臭奠位於兩間歷萬古而不磨矣乃自其二氣
===
之播盪萬象之糾紛輪輪駪駪以至於姤剝之
際若是其微甚也而一陽之氣眇於重淵如車
旋而轂運飜然無端焉此曷故也理運而不息
也天地以一元之理宰萬物旁皇周浹流動充
滿而不可以窮盡凡以弘其發育之神而物之
稟仰煦息生育收聚於其間者轉化推移而無
窮故曰復其見天地之心乎斯大生廣生之心
卽所謂仁也恒久而不已者也傳曰仁者人也
是天地之仁人皆得之以爲心者也乃獨聖人
punctuated:
三才竝立而無疆。理以主氣，氣以載理；理不息，則氣亦不息。天地之理，以神運者也；聖人之仁，以心運者也。天地以神運，故普萬物而不宰其功；聖人以心運，故體萬物而不息其道。此聖人之仁所以同天地，而其身與天地相爲悠久者，此也。臨川吳氏曰：「聖人之仁如天地。」蓋言聖人之壽，而推本於仁也。嗟乎，其知言哉！

今夫天地，普萬物而無心者也。人見其冲然穆然，無聲無臭，奠位於兩間，歷萬古而不磨矣。乃自其二氣之播盪，萬象之糾紛，輪輪駪駪，以至於姤剝之際，若是其微甚也，而一陽之氣眇於重淵，如車旋而轂運，飜然無端焉。此曷故也？理運而不息也。天地以一元之理宰萬物，旁皇周浹，流動充滿，而不可以窮盡。凡以弘其發育之神，而物之稟仰煦息、生育收聚於其間者，轉化推移而無窮。故曰：「復，其見天地之心乎！」斯大生廣生之心，卽所謂仁也，恒久而不已者也。傳曰：「仁者，人也。」是天地之仁，人皆得之以爲心者也。乃獨聖人
translation_en:
…the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humanity—stand together without limit. Principle governs vital force, and vital force bears principle; if principle does not cease, neither does vital force. The principle of Heaven and Earth operates through numinous efficacy; the sage’s benevolence operates through the mind. Because Heaven and Earth operate through numinous efficacy, they extend to all things without claiming mastery over their achievements. Because the sage operates through the mind, he embodies all things and never ceases to practice his Way. This is why the sage’s benevolence is the same as that of Heaven and Earth, and why his person endures together with them. Master Wu of Linchuan said, “The sage’s benevolence resembles Heaven and Earth.” In speaking of the sage’s longevity, he traced its root to benevolence. Ah, how well he understood these words!

Now Heaven and Earth extend to all things without deliberate intent. People see them as empty and reverent, soundless and scentless, established in their places within the cosmos, enduring through myriad ages without wearing away. Yet amid the surging of their two vital forces and the tangled profusion of all phenomena, turning and thronging [?], there comes the time of Encounter (Gou) and Stripping Away (Bo), when yang has become exceedingly faint. A single yang force lies minute within the layered depths; yet, like a turning carriage and its revolving hub, it wheels about without a discernible beginning. Why is this? Because principle operates without ceasing. Heaven and Earth govern all things through the principle of the single primal unity. It ranges everywhere and penetrates throughout, flowing and filling all space, inexhaustibly. All this extends their numinous power of generation and nourishment. The things that receive and depend upon it, warmed and sustained, born and nurtured, gathered and stored within it, transform and succeed one another without end. Thus it is said, “In Return (Fu), do we not see the heart of Heaven and Earth!” This heart, which gives life in its greatness and breadth, is what is called benevolence: it endures perpetually without ceasing. The commentary says, “Benevolence is humanity.” This benevolence of Heaven and Earth is something all people receive as their own mind. Yet only the sage…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之仁與天地竝何哉今夫盆水在庭清之終日
未能見眉睫濁之不過一撓而不能察方圓人
心易濁而難清猶盆水之類也若夫聖人之心
則龍門之津混沌之源也滔滔霍霍亘天地彌
古今行而不可得窮極也運而不可得把握也
嗚呼大哉其卽天地之心乎蓋聖人通天下爲
一身而其心以天地萬物爲一體身居九重之
尊而慮周四海之外高拱穆清之上而神馳闉
闔之微思天下之有震風凌雨若塗泥之被已
===
視民之有疾痛疴癢若熛疽之刺心兼容倂包
與天地同其鴻洞也蟠委錯綜與萬物要其終
始也然聖人之仁非徒有是心也於是以治日
月之行調陰陽之氣節四時之度正律曆之數
以財成天地之道輔相天地之宜此聖人之仁
所以範圍天地也於是以明上下正百官訓三
農飭百工通商賈使男女不失時以偶老幼不
失時以養此聖人之仁所以保萬民也於是以
擾五典開三物聯師儒節以禮和以樂糾以刑
punctuated: 之仁與天地竝，何哉？今夫盆水在庭，清之終日，未能見眉睫；濁之不過一撓，而不能察方圓。人心易濁而難清，猶盆水之類也。若夫聖人之心，則龍門之津、混沌之源也。滔滔霍霍，亘天地，彌古今，行而不可得窮極也，運而不可得把握也。嗚呼，大哉！其卽天地之心乎！蓋聖人通天下爲一身，而其心以天地萬物爲一體。身居九重之尊，而慮周四海之外；高拱穆清之上，而神馳闉闔之微。思天下之有震風凌雨，若塗泥之被已；視民之有疾痛疴癢，若熛疽之刺心。兼容倂包，與天地同其鴻洞也；蟠委錯綜，與萬物要其終始也。然聖人之仁，非徒有是心也。於是以治日月之行，調陰陽之氣，節四時之度，正律曆之數，以財成天地之道，輔相天地之宜。此聖人之仁所以範圍天地也。於是以明上下，正百官，訓三農，飭百工，通商賈，使男女不失時以偶，老幼不失時以養。此聖人之仁所以保萬民也。於是以擾五典，開三物，聯師儒，節以禮，和以樂，糾以刑，
translation_en:
…benevolence stands alongside Heaven and Earth—why is this so? Consider a basin of water in a courtyard: let it settle clear all day, and one may still be unable to see one’s eyebrows and eyelashes reflected in it; muddy it with a single stirring, and one can no longer distinguish square from round. The human heart is easily muddied and difficult to clear, much like the water in this basin. The sage’s heart, however, is like the waters at Longmen, the wellspring of primordial undifferentiation. Surging and rushing, it extends throughout Heaven and Earth and spans past and present. Its flow cannot be exhausted; its movement cannot be grasped. Ah, how great it is! Is this not the very heart of Heaven and Earth?
The sage regards all under Heaven as a single body, and in his heart takes Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things as one whole. Though he occupies the exalted position within the ninefold palace, his concern encompasses what lies beyond the Four Seas. Though he sits with hands folded on high in solemn purity, his spirit reaches into the obscure places by the gates [?]. When he thinks of violent winds and harsh rains afflicting the world, it is as though mud were covering his own body. When he sees the people suffering from illness, pain, ailments, and itching, it is as though a burning ulcer [?] were piercing his heart. Embracing and encompassing all, he shares the vastness of Heaven and Earth; winding, extending, and interweaving, he comprehends the endings and beginnings of the myriad things.
Yet the sage’s benevolence does not consist merely in possessing this heart. Thus he regulates the courses of the sun and moon, harmonizes the vital forces of yin and yang, orders the measures of the four seasons, and rectifies the calculations of the pitch standards and calendar. In this way he shapes and completes the Way of Heaven and Earth and assists what is fitting to them. This is how the sage’s benevolence gives order to Heaven and Earth.
Thus he clarifies the distinctions between superior and inferior, rectifies the hundred officials, instructs the farmers of the three kinds of land, directs the many artisans, and facilitates trade among merchants. He ensures that men and women do not miss the proper time to marry, and that the old and young receive care when it is due. This is how the sage’s benevolence safeguards all the people.
Thus he fosters observance of the five moral norms [?], opens up instruction in the three subjects, brings teachers and scholars into association, regulates through ritual, harmonizes through music, and corrects through punishments…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
此聖人之仁所以敎萬民也於是以蕃草木育
鳥獸斧斤不妄斷數罟不得用使兕無所用其
角螫蟲無所輸其毒此聖人之仁所以及庶物
也於是以播聲敎流仁惠使王人風舉之使觀
星望路憑雲遡波枅日月之陲窮昏明之際此
聖人之仁所以被遐荒也嗚呼聖人之仁如此
乎其大也其諸天之無不覆幬地之無不持載
乎其諸建日月風雨以和之經陰陽寒暑以成
之列山川疆域以奠之者乎蓋天地之仁雖均
===
賦於人而實獨鍾於聖人之心聖人之心推天
地之仁四達於天下而實無異於天地之心故
夫元氣元形交附於兩間而混闢無窮者天地
之壽所以獨異於萬物也至德至命參立乎三
才而常永貞固者聖人之壽所以獨異於萬民
也此之謂聖人之仁壽也其諸辰極之位玄樞
日薄星迴而衡軸常執其中者乎其諸嶽鎮之
奠寰區陵遷谷變而方維不易其度者乎易之
贊乾曰天行健君子以自强不息其論坤曰坤
punctuated: 此聖人之仁所以敎萬民也。於是以蕃草木，育鳥獸，斧斤不妄斷，數罟不得用，使兕無所用其角，螫蟲無所輸其毒，此聖人之仁所以及庶物也。於是以播聲敎，流仁惠，使王人風舉之使，觀星望路，憑雲遡波，枅日月之陲，窮昏明之際，此聖人之仁所以被遐荒也。嗚呼！聖人之仁如此乎其大也！其諸天之無不覆幬，地之無不持載乎？其諸建日月風雨以和之，經陰陽寒暑以成之，列山川疆域以奠之者乎？蓋天地之仁雖均賦於人，而實獨鍾於聖人之心。聖人之心推天地之仁，四達於天下，而實無異於天地之心。故夫元氣元形交附於兩間，而混闢無窮者，天地之壽所以獨異於萬物也；至德至命參立乎三才，而常永貞固者，聖人之壽所以獨異於萬民也。此之謂聖人之仁壽也。其諸辰極之位玄樞，日薄星迴，而衡軸常執其中者乎？其諸嶽鎮之奠寰區，陵遷谷變，而方維不易其度者乎？《易》之贊乾曰：「天行健，君子以自强不息。」其論坤曰：「坤
translation_en:
This is how the sage’s benevolence instructs all the people. Thus he causes plants and trees to flourish and nurtures birds and beasts. Axes and hatchets do not cut indiscriminately, and fine-meshed nets may not be used, so that rhinoceroses have no occasion to use their horns, nor stinging creatures to discharge their poison. This is how the sage’s benevolence extends to all living things. Thus he spreads his civilizing influence and diffuses benevolent favors, sending royal emissaries on missions swift as the wind [?]. They observe the stars and look out for their routes, ride the clouds and journey upstream, reaching [?] the farthest bounds of sun and moon and the utmost limits of darkness and light. This is how the sage’s benevolence reaches the remote wilderness. Ah! So great is the sage’s benevolence! Is it not like Heaven, which leaves nothing unsheltered, and Earth, which leaves nothing unsupported? Is it not that which establishes sun and moon, wind and rain to bring harmony; orders yin and yang, cold and heat to bring things to completion; and arrays mountains and rivers, boundaries and territories to give them stability?

Although the benevolence of Heaven and Earth is bestowed equally upon human beings, it is in fact concentrated uniquely in the sage’s heart. The sage’s heart extends the benevolence of Heaven and Earth throughout the world in all four directions, and is in truth no different from the heart of Heaven and Earth. Thus primordial vital force and primordial form join together in the space between Heaven and Earth, with their merging and unfolding continuing without end: this is why the longevity of Heaven and Earth differs uniquely from that of all things. Supreme virtue and the supreme endowment of life stand alongside Heaven and Earth among the Three Powers, remaining forever constant and firm: this is why the sage’s longevity differs uniquely from that of all the people. This is what is meant by the sage’s benevolence and longevity. Is it not like the celestial pole occupying the mysterious pivot, where, though the sun approaches and the stars revolve, the axis of the heavens always holds the center? Is it not like the great guardian mountains stabilizing the world, where, though hills shift and valleys change, the supports of the four quarters do not alter their measure?

text:

天地之所以不息無疆者乃其心也而聖人之
心與之同不息無疆焉此仁之所以爲純也所

地焉豈直如之而已哉蓋自其醇德流乎四海
而誠信著於天下天不變經矣地不易形矣陰
陽訢合日月昭明上下輯睦而兵不試人民悅
懌而命無夭田者不侵畔漁者不爭隈鄙旅之

translation_en:
…in its fullness bears all things; its virtue accords with the boundless.” It also says: “The good fortune of abiding in steadfastness corresponds to the boundlessness of Earth.” What makes Heaven and Earth unceasing and boundless is their heart; the sage’s heart is likewise unceasing and boundless. This is why his benevolence is pure—what is meant by “purity, too, never ceases.” Yet the sage’s benevolence also contributes to the work of Heaven and Earth. How could it merely resemble them?

For once his pure virtue spreads throughout the Four Seas and his sincerity and trustworthiness become manifest throughout the world, Heaven does not alter its regular courses, and Earth does not change its form. Yin and yang unite harmoniously; the sun and moon shine brightly. Those above and below live in concord, and weapons are never put to use. The people rejoice, and their lives are not cut short. Farmers do not encroach upon field boundaries; fishermen do not contend over bends in the waters; people in the countryside and travelers do not compete for gain. Harmonious vital energies suffuse all things, gathering into supreme harmony. All the people and creatures under Heaven flourish together in the realm of longevity, without themselves knowing it. This is what is meant by “having no bolts or bars, yet being impossible to open; having no binding cords, yet being impossible to untie.”

At this point, the sage’s achievements not only reach upward to the Nine Heavens and accord below with the yellow earth, but also assist Heaven and Earth in their work. Ah! This is how the sage brings the work of Heaven and Earth to completion, and none of it is other than benevolence. As the saying goes, “It is simply a matter of extending this heart to others.” How could the Way be far away?

Associate Examiner Ren, Instructor, comments: “The form is dignified and solemn, the language and sentiments earnest and thorough. It truly conveys the spirit of an assisting minister offering counsel.”
Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor, comments: “Within its ornate parallel prose there are classical standards: this is the work of someone skilled in four-and-six prose.”
