On a certain day of a certain month in the third year of Qingli [1043], we, your servants So-and-so and others, humbly received your sagely favor in being admitted to an audience in the Tianzhang Pavilion.

We humbly reflect that the assembled officers cherish plans to present before you, rejoicing that they advance together in an age of harmonious prosperity; the sovereign upholds the principle of engaging with those below, graciously undertaking to receive them in this enlightened time. Your first inquiry concerns the common people; your first gift is a writing brush. With exceptional solicitude, you move forward on your mat, thereby extending your policy of consulting the many. Your appearance before us marks a ceremony rarely witnessed, giving particular urgency to our duty to correct your errors. Conscious of our own rashness and blindness, how could we be worthy of such an exchange of counsel and assent? We, your servants So-and-so and others, are truly joyful and truly fearful; we bow our heads to the ground and repeatedly kowtow.

We venture to reflect that Shun consulted his five ministers, who indeed diligently cultivated virtue; Tang took as his teacher a man of undivided virtue, and thus appointed him Aheng, the chief minister …

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
精神聚而相得章上下交而致理易自願
治之君間見乃格心之佐亦疎賈生負通
達之才竟對釐於宣室董子究天人之蘊
且出相於江都顧玆襪線之微材何補

兆瑞於蒼龍屢

侔辟王之壽考，取雅詠之文昭。肇建天章，爰藏御籍。蟠猊龍於四極，跨箕斗之二星。蒼華積翠於青陽，連雲琰琬；玓瓅凝輝於少皥，充棟珠璣。南延康樂之居，頌遊休於夏諺；北構壽昌之殿，祝秩祜於湯孫。列祖遺容，旣總宅中之位，
translation_en:
…When their spirits converge, their mutual accord becomes manifest; when those above and below communicate, good government becomes easy. Rulers who desire good government appear only occasionally, and assistants able to rectify their sovereign’s heart are likewise scarce. Master Jia possessed comprehensive understanding, yet in the end answered questions about sacrificial blessings [?] in the Xuanshi Hall. Master Dong explored the profound relationship between Heaven and humanity, yet was sent out to serve as Chancellor of Jiangdu. Considering our own meager talents, as slight as thread for stockings, what can we contribute to the great work of ordering all affairs? Summoned to answer in the great court, we lack the magnificent eloquence of Han officials; with the imperial library thrown wide open, we feel ashamed of our narrow learning, like that of the scholar Hong [?]. Looking up, we find Heaven’s sun close at hand; turning back, we see clouds stretching far away. Auspicious signs first appeared in the Azure Dragon [?], and repeatedly summonses were issued on yellow silk.

Matching the sovereign’s longevity, and taking the phrase “luminous culture” from the Elegantiae of the Book of Odes, you first established Tianzhang, “Heavenly Writings,” to house the imperial books. Coiling lion-like beasts and dragons extend to the four limits, spanning the two constellations Winnowing Basket and Dipper. Verdant splendor gathers its green in the eastern quarter of Qingyang, with precious jade reaching to the clouds; sparkling brilliance concentrates its radiance in the western quarter of Shaohao, with pearls and gems filling the buildings. To the south, you extended the residence of Kangle, “Peace and Joy,” celebrating royal excursions and repose in the proverb of Xia; to the north, you built the hall of Shouchang, “Enduring Longevity,” invoking abundant blessings upon the descendant of Tang. The portraits of the imperial ancestors have already all been placed in their central positions…

視民切如傷之念有災密禱於禁中大辟
punctuated:
潛邸賜節，共崇保大之規。符瑞集景德以來，何啻天球大訓；圖書等乾亨而上，寧推帝典神謨。黃樞彤管之藏，願治特存乎三鑑；玉牒青緗之貯，貽謀燕及於百支。顧石生文，動桃花之綽約；臨流釃酒，效蘭社以歡榮。協上下以承天休，先帝肇基之志；和神人以光祖考，今皇肯構之心。
號侈天開，猶妨帶職；尊臨日表，何幸致身！兹蓋伏遇〇〇〇〇，堯仁舜哲，禹儉湯寬。望道懷未見之憂，無逸寓書於座右；視民切如傷之念，有災密禱於禁中。大辟
translation_en:
…The insignia bestowed upon the residence occupied before accession together exalt the design for preserving imperial greatness. Auspicious tokens gathered since Jingde are far more than the celestial jade sphere and the Great Admonition; the books and charts rank with those of Qianheng and earlier—why should precedence be conceded to the Canons of the Emperors and the Counsels of the Sages? Among the writings preserved in the central offices and the records of the vermilion brush, the desire for good government is especially embodied in the Three Mirrors. The jade genealogies and books wrapped in blue silk store plans bequeathed to posterity, bringing peace to the hundred branches of the imperial lineage. Looking upon patterned stones evokes the graceful beauty of peach blossoms [?]; beside the flowing water, we pour wine, emulating the Orchid Pavilion gathering in its joy and splendor. To unite those above and below in receiving Heaven’s blessing was the late emperor’s purpose in laying the foundations; to harmonize spirits and men and bring glory to the ancestors is the present emperor’s resolve in carrying on the construction.
The designation magnificently proclaims Heaven’s opening, yet still impedes the holding of office [?]; as Your Majesty presides with sunlike countenance, how fortunate we are to be present! This is because we have humbly encountered 〇〇〇〇: the benevolence of Yao and wisdom of Shun, the frugality of Yu and generosity of Tang. Looking toward the Way, you cherish the anxious sense that you have not yet seen it, and keep the chapter Against Idleness inscribed beside your seat. You regard the people with the heartfelt concern one feels for the injured, and when calamity occurs, pray privately within the palace. In capital cases …

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
讞疑罪惟嚴於失入諸羌招討人惟任乎推
誠
宮庭施絁繪之輕帷苑囿惜
玉清之舊地
煦媮求諫特除越職之條
寤寐親賢屢下直言之
詔崇
三朝之寶訓
顯謨丕啓於後人購
===
三館之逸書資善不衰於幼學當平世而
揚推溝之慮撫治民而
勞馭朽之思
巽命重申期有懷而必吐
豐亨長保責至治以無前
折節敷求
和顏采聽方絮
出和熹之貢慙阮檄以立成鏤毫
頒路扈之工愧禰篇之點綴安世備漢家顧
punctuated: 讞疑罪，惟嚴於失入；諸羌招討，人惟任乎推誠。宮庭施絁繪之輕帷，苑囿惜玉清之舊地。煦媮求諫，特除越職之條；寤寐親賢，屢下直言之詔。崇三朝之寶訓，顯謨丕啓於後人；購三館之逸書，資善不衰於幼學。當平世而揚推溝之慮，撫治民而勞馭朽之思。巽命重申，期有懷而必吐；豐亨長保，責至治以無前。折節敷求，和顏采聽。方絮出和熹之貢，慙阮檄以立成；鏤毫頒路扈之工，愧禰篇之點綴。安世備漢家顧
translation_en:
…in reviewing doubtful convictions, you are especially vigilant against wrongly finding the accused guilty; in conciliating or campaigning against the various Qiang peoples, you entrust the work only to men who act with complete sincerity. In the palace you use light curtains of plain silk [?]; in the imperial parks you spare the former grounds of Yuqing. Graciously seeking remonstrance, you have specifically abolished the provision against speaking beyond one’s official duties; waking and sleeping, you seek the company of worthy men, repeatedly issuing edicts inviting frank speech. You honor the precious instructions of three reigns, whose illustrious counsels open the way magnificently for posterity; you procure lost books for the Three Institutes, providing unfailing resources for cultivating goodness in youthful study. In an age of peace, you still cherish the concern of one who feels he has himself pushed others into a ditch; governing the people, you trouble yourself as though driving with rotten reins. Your gracious commands are reiterated, so that anyone with something on his mind will surely express it; enduring prosperity is maintained, and you demand good government surpassing all precedent. You humble yourself in seeking widely for talent and receive advice with a kindly countenance.

With sheets of silk floss [?] supplied as tribute in the manner of Empress Hexi, we feel ashamed beside Ruan’s proclamation, completed on the spot; with decorated writing brushes bestowed, products of the craftsmanship of Lu and Hu [?], we feel unworthy beside the embellishments of Mi’s composition. Anshi stood ready for the Han court’s consultation…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
問持橐十年仲宣擅魏代文章屬詞一舉
豈其才由天賦或者事匪時艱登對必先
自盟豈以應酬而曲盡兼總而後臨決亦
由料品以施行臣某等同典
樞衡與參
密勿雖後樂先憂之志在昔已存而
上嘉下樂之心於今難稱仰瞻
羣翰炳雲漢之昭回俯鞠微軀奉
天顏於咫尺空言無補豈敢以應
===
側席之求謙讓未遑安得而稱轉樞之義學
不足以待問惟
仁明矜察其愚事有待於條陳望
神聖終成其美庶幾
革孚巳日而文明之化以彰
德積百年而禮樂之功攸建
太平歌頌日聞天保之章
遵養純熈永息采薇之詠
道與天而無極
punctuated: 問，持橐十年；仲宣擅魏代文章，屬詞一舉。豈其才由天賦？或者事匪時艱。登對必先自盟，豈以應酬而曲盡？兼總而後臨決，亦由料品以施行。臣某等同典樞衡，與參密勿。雖後樂先憂之志在昔已存，而上嘉下樂之心於今難稱。仰瞻羣翰，炳雲漢之昭回；俯鞠微軀，奉天顏於咫尺。空言無補，豈敢以應側席之求？謙讓未遑，安得而稱轉樞之義？學不足以待問，惟仁明矜察其愚；事有待於條陳，望神聖終成其美。庶幾革孚巳日，而文明之化以彰；德積百年，而禮樂之功攸建。太平歌頌，日聞天保之章；遵養純熈，永息采薇之詠。道與天而無極，
translation_en:
…in consultation, bearing the attendant’s pouch for ten years; Zhongxuan excelled in literary composition in the Wei era, composing at a single attempt. Was their talent bestowed by Heaven? Or were the affairs they faced free of the difficulties of these times? Before entering the imperial presence to answer questions, one must first pledge oneself: how could mere conventional responses fully meet the occasion? Decisions are made only after comprehensively weighing matters, and their implementation likewise rests on assessment and discrimination.

We, your servants So-and-so and the others, jointly hold the central balance of government and participate in confidential deliberations. Although we have long cherished the resolve to worry before others and rejoice after them, today we find it difficult to fulfill the wish to win approval above and bring joy below. Looking upward, we behold your many writings, brilliant as the luminous sweep of the Milky Way; bowing our humble persons, we attend upon your heavenly countenance at the closest quarters. Empty words are of no help: how dare we offer them in response to your earnest quest for counsel? There is no leisure for modest demurral; how can we adequately fulfill the duty of turning the pivot of government?

Our learning is insufficient to answer your inquiries; we ask only that your benevolence and discernment take compassionate account of our ignorance. Matters await detailed presentation; we hope that your divine sagacity will bring them to a successful conclusion. May reform gain trust when its day has come, so that the transforming influence of enlightened culture becomes manifest; may virtue accumulate for a hundred years, so that the achievements of rites and music are established. Amid songs celebrating great peace, may the ode “Heaven Protects You” (Tian bao) be heard daily; nurturing perfect brilliance, may we forever silence the song “Gathering Bracken” (Cai wei). May the Way be boundless as Heaven…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
治率土以攸同伏願
有大不盈
無斁亦保
明四目達四聰益振合宫之鞀鐸
慎五刑敷五敎丕冒遐服之侏離臣等無任
瞻
天仰
聖激切屛營之至謹奉
表稱
===
謝以
聞
第叄塲
策
第一問
周思充
同考試官敎諭任批我
聖祖
皇上心學淵源純王政迹子能歷歷□□蓋涵濡之久而有得者
punctuated:
治率土以攸同。伏願有大不盈，無斁亦保；明四目，達四聰，益振合宫之鞀鐸；慎五刑，敷五敎，丕冒遐服之侏離。臣等無任瞻天仰聖、激切屛營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
第叄塲
策
第一問
周思充
同考試官敎諭任批：我聖祖皇上心學淵源、純王政迹，子能歷歷□□，蓋涵濡之久而有得者。
translation_en:
…bringing all lands under Heaven into a common order of government. We humbly wish that, possessing greatness, you remain free of complacency, and that, never wearying, you preserve it. May you see clearly and hear freely in all four directions, further sounding the drums and bells of the ceremonial palace to solicit counsel; may you exercise care in the five punishments and spread the five teachings, extending your beneficence far over distant lands of unfamiliar tongues. We, your servants, look up to Heaven and revere the Sage, overcome with fervent emotion and trembling awe. We respectfully submit this memorial to express our gratitude and make it known to you.
Third Session
Policy Essays
First Question
Zhou Sichong
Comment by Associate Examiner Ren, Instructor: The origins of the learning of the mind of our sagely founder and His Majesty, and their acts of purely kingly government—you have been able to set these out distinctly [?; two illegible characters]. Surely this reflects insights gained through long immersion.

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
同考試官敎諭楊批
御製諸書所載者皆我
聖人經綸之迹此作能悉記而敷張之不當以經生目之矣
考試官敎諭管批鋪張得體
考試官敎諭李批頌述得體
帝王之御世有道而所以會其道者存乎
心帝王之傳心有法而所以闡其法者存
乎學學以立政之體政以達心之用則斯
道有全功而天下無遺治矣何則天下之
===
事皆本於道道也者所以善其事者也而
實爲治之根柢也天下之道皆藏於心心
也者所以管是道者也而實爲治之樞機
也治而不循其道固非經世之遠圖道而
未會於心亦匪躬行之實得是故典學之
功明心之要尤有確然其不可誣者古帝
王所以會道之精致治之盛固無出乎此
而我
聖祖
punctuated:
同考試官敎諭楊批：御製諸書所載者，皆我聖人經綸之迹。此作能悉記而敷張之，不當以經生目之矣。
考試官敎諭管批：鋪張得體。
考試官敎諭李批：頌述得體。
帝王之御世有道，而所以會其道者存乎心；帝王之傳心有法，而所以闡其法者存乎學。學以立政之體，政以達心之用，則斯道有全功，而天下無遺治矣。何則？天下之事皆本於道。道也者，所以善其事者也，而實爲治之根柢也。天下之道皆藏於心。心也者，所以管是道者也，而實爲治之樞機也。治而不循其道，固非經世之遠圖；道而未會於心，亦匪躬行之實得。是故典學之功、明心之要，尤有確然其不可誣者。古帝王所以會道之精、致治之盛，固無出乎此。而我聖祖
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor: What is recorded in the imperially composed books consists entirely of the deeds through which our sage sovereign ordered the world. This essay recalls them all and expounds them fully. Its author should not be regarded as a mere student of the classics.
Comment by Examiner Guan, Instructor: The exposition is fittingly developed.
Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: The praise and narration are fittingly expressed.
There is a Way by which emperors and kings govern the world, and the means of comprehending that Way lies in the mind. There is a method by which emperors and kings transmit the mind, and the means of elucidating that method lies in learning. Learning establishes the substance of government, while government gives effect to the workings of the mind. Thus this Way achieves its full efficacy, and nothing under Heaven remains beyond good governance. Why is this so? All affairs under Heaven are rooted in the Way. The Way is that by which affairs are properly conducted, and it is indeed the foundation of governance. The Way of all under Heaven is contained within the mind. The mind is that which holds command over this Way, and it is indeed the pivot of governance. Governing without following the Way is certainly no far-reaching plan for ordering the world; nor does professing the Way without comprehending it in the mind constitute genuine attainment through personal practice. Thus the achievement of steadfast learning and the essential work of illuminating the mind possess a particular certainty that cannot be gainsaid. The means by which the emperors and kings of antiquity comprehended the subtleties of the Way and brought governance to its fullest flourishing never lay outside this. And our sagely founder…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
皇上會千聖於一心通萬古於一理藏諸用為
日新之
盛德顯諸仁為富有之
大業蕩蕩乎無能名巍巍乎不可及者抑非
職此之故哉請因明問所及而敬陳之今
夫天之立君以為民也君之立政以致治
也論治者必基於道論道者必根諸心雖
聖人之治天下亦有不能外者然道豈外
於天乎詩曰維天之命於穆不已言天之
===
神也而聖人心學之精涵於是矣易曰乾
道變化各正性命言天之化也而聖人經
綸之迹蘊於此矣道之大原出於天而道
之精微闡於聖嘗考唐虞三代之世堯舜
禹湯文武之為君率皆本精一執中之傳
衍為聖學之家法由典謨訓誥之著布為
經世之徽猷故語其德則為天德而天下
之言至聖者必歸焉語其道則為王道而
天下之言至治者必歸焉嗚呼遐哉不可
punctuated: 皇上會千聖於一心，通萬古於一理，藏諸用為日新之盛德，顯諸仁為富有之大業。蕩蕩乎無能名，巍巍乎不可及者，抑非職此之故哉？請因明問所及而敬陳之。今夫天之立君，以為民也；君之立政，以致治也。論治者必基於道，論道者必根諸心，雖聖人之治天下，亦有不能外者。然道豈外於天乎？《詩》曰：「維天之命，於穆不已。」言天之神也，而聖人心學之精涵於是矣。《易》曰：「乾道變化，各正性命。」言天之化也，而聖人經綸之迹蘊於此矣。道之大原出於天，而道之精微闡於聖。嘗考唐虞三代之世，堯舜禹湯文武之為君，率皆本精一執中之傳，衍為聖學之家法；由典謨訓誥之著，布為經世之徽猷。故語其德，則為天德，而天下之言至聖者必歸焉；語其道，則為王道，而天下之言至治者必歸焉。嗚呼！遐哉！不可
translation_en:
…Your Majesty unites a thousand sages in a single mind and comprehends all antiquity through a single principle. Hidden in practical operation, it constitutes magnificent virtue renewed daily; manifested in benevolence, it constitutes a great undertaking rich in all things. So vast that none can name it, so lofty that none can reach it—is this not precisely the reason? Allow me respectfully to expound upon the matters raised in your discerning question.

Heaven establishes rulers for the sake of the people; rulers establish government to bring about good order. Those who discuss government must ground it in the Way, and those who discuss the Way must root it in the mind. Even the sages, in governing all under Heaven, could not depart from this. Yet could the Way lie outside Heaven? The Book of Odes says: “Heaven’s mandate—how profound, unceasing!” This speaks of Heaven’s numinous power, and within it is contained the essence of the sages’ learning of the mind. The Book of Changes says: “The Way of Qian changes and transforms; each thing attains its proper nature and allotted destiny.” This speaks of Heaven’s transforming activity, and within it lie the traces of the sages’ ordering of the world.

The great source of the Way comes from Heaven, while its subtle essence is elucidated by the sages. Examining the ages of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties, we find that the rulers Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu all grounded themselves in the transmitted teaching of refinement, single-mindedness, and holding fast to the mean. They developed it into the inherited discipline of sagely learning; through its expression in the Canons, Counsels, Instructions, and Announcements, they promulgated excellent principles for governing the world. Thus, when we speak of their virtue, it is Heavenly virtue, and all under Heaven who speak of the highest sagehood must turn to them. When we speak of their Way, it is the Kingly Way, and all under Heaven who speak of consummate government must turn to them. Ah, how exalted! Impossible to…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
尚已嗣是而降英君誼辟代有作者如石
渠講經制則善矣而表章之徒勤集賢論
道意則美矣而實德之或歉崇政說書亦
可謂願治矣而未免於賢姦之竝立是奚
足以彷彿斯道之萬一哉
昭代繼起
聖人篤生洪惟我
太祖高皇帝應運而興定鼎中夏
鴻謨偉烈卓冠百王精義淵思尚友千古諸
===
所制作悉根理道其於政學尤極講求愚
嘗莊誦
聖政日曆
皇明政要所載而有以仰窺其畧矣自其留
心於經也如
御白虎殿論易則於頤卦而得養民之職焉
於家人而悟誠實威嚴之道焉
御武英殿論書則於無逸而知兢惕之方焉
於洪範而識天人類應之理焉謂大學之
punctuated:
尚已！嗣是而降，英君誼辟，代有作者。如石渠講經，制則善矣，而表章之徒勤；集賢論道，意則美矣，而實德之或歉；崇政說書，亦可謂願治矣，而未免於賢姦之竝立。是奚足以彷彿斯道之萬一哉？
昭代繼起，聖人篤生。洪惟我太祖高皇帝，應運而興，定鼎中夏，鴻謨偉烈，卓冠百王；精義淵思，尚友千古。諸所制作，悉根理道，其於政學，尤極講求。愚嘗莊誦《聖政日曆》《皇明政要》所載，而有以仰窺其畧矣。自其留心於經也，如御白虎殿論《易》，則於《頤》卦而得養民之職焉，於《家人》而悟誠實威嚴之道焉；御武英殿論《書》，則於《無逸》而知兢惕之方焉，於《洪範》而識天人類應之理焉。謂《大學》之
translation_en:
…could not be surpassed! Thereafter, outstanding sovereigns and righteous rulers arose in every age. Lecturing on the classics at Shiqu was a fine institution, yet its efforts amounted merely to promoting their eminence. Discussing the Way at Jixian was admirable in intent, yet substantive virtue was perhaps lacking. Expounding the texts at Chongzheng could also be called an aspiration to good government, yet worthy and treacherous men still stood together at court. How could these even remotely approximate one ten-thousandth of this Way?
Our illustrious dynasty arose in succession, and a sage was duly born. Magnificent indeed was our Emperor Taizu Gao, who rose in response to Heaven’s appointed destiny and established his rule over the Central Lands. His grand designs and mighty achievements towered above those of all preceding kings; through penetrating understanding of moral principles and profound reflection, he took the ancients as his companions across the ages. All that he instituted was rooted in principle and the Way, and he devoted particular attention to studying government. I have reverently read the accounts in the Daily Record of Sagely Government and the Essentials of Government of the August Ming, and thereby gained a glimpse of their broad outlines. As for his attention to the classics: when he presided in Baihu Hall to discuss the Book of Changes, he discerned in the hexagram Yi, “Nourishment,” the duty of nourishing the people, and in Jiaren, “The Family,” the way of sincerity and commanding dignity. When he presided in Wuying Hall to discuss the Book of Documents, he learned from “Against Idleness” the method of remaining vigilant and apprehensive, and from “The Great Plan” the principle by which Heaven and humanity respond to one another according to kind. He said that the Great Learning’s…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
要莫大於脩身矣而至講財用則有德厚
人懷之論謂節用愛人爲治國之良規矣
而至講孟子則有專言仁義之稱自其究
意於史也如
御白虎殿論漢史則於文帝而責以禮樂之
當興焉於武帝而惜其用心之未善焉
御左閣論宋史則於太宗而譏其内藏之治
焉於真宗而鄙其天書之惑焉謂唐之太
宗賞罰服人矣而於玄宗則短其賢能之
===
未用謂元之初年君臣昧道矣而於元季
則傷其致亂之有由是所以發明經史而
稽政事之得失者審矣至於
御製文集究天體七曜之循環以原法象之始
咨天地二儀之高厚以闡運數之精少傅
楊士奇以爲深得古人之精蘊
御註洪範先之五行五事八政五紀以推皇極
之體繼之三德稽疑庶徴福極以昭皇極
之用賛善劉三吾謂其爲萬世開太平
punctuated:
要莫大於脩身矣，而至講財用，則有德厚人懷之論。謂節用愛人爲治國之良規矣，而至講孟子，則有專言仁義之稱。自其究意於史也，如御白虎殿論漢史，則於文帝而責以禮樂之當興焉，於武帝而惜其用心之未善焉；御左閣論宋史，則於太宗而譏其内藏之治焉，於真宗而鄙其天書之惑焉。謂唐之太宗賞罰服人矣，而於玄宗則短其賢能之未用；謂元之初年君臣昧道矣，而於元季則傷其致亂之有由。是所以發明經史而稽政事之得失者審矣。
至於《御製文集》，究天體七曜之循環，以原法象之始；咨天地二儀之高厚，以闡運數之精。少傅楊士奇以爲深得古人之精蘊。《御註洪範》，先之五行、五事、八政、五紀，以推皇極之體；繼之三德、稽疑、庶徴、福極，以昭皇極之用。賛善劉三吾謂其爲萬世開太平。
translation_en:
…among its essentials, nothing is greater than cultivating oneself. Yet when discussing wealth and expenditure, he also argued that abundant virtue wins the people's allegiance. He declared that economizing on expenditure and caring for the people were sound principles for governing a state; when discussing the Mencius, he praised its exclusive emphasis on benevolence and righteousness. As for his close investigation of history: when he attended the White Tiger Hall to discuss Han history, he faulted Emperor Wen for failing to establish rites and music, and regretted that Emperor Wu had not directed his intentions toward good. When he attended the Left Pavilion to discuss Song history, he criticized Emperor Taizong's management of the privy treasury and disparaged Emperor Zhenzong's delusion concerning the celestial writings. He observed that Emperor Taizong of Tang had won people's submission through rewards and punishments, but faulted Emperor Xuanzong for failing to employ worthy and capable men. He declared that the rulers and ministers of the early Yuan had been ignorant of the Way, and lamented the causes that had brought disorder in the dynasty's final years. Thus, in elucidating the classics and histories and examining successes and failures in government, his judgment was discerning.
As for the Imperially Composed Collected Writings, he investigated the cycles of the celestial bodies—the seven luminaries—to trace the origins of their patterns and manifestations. He examined the height and depth of Heaven and Earth, the two cosmic powers, to elucidate the subtleties of cosmic cycles and numerical order. The Junior Preceptor Yang Shiqi considered that he had profoundly grasped the essential wisdom of the ancients. In the Imperial Commentary on the Great Plan, he began with the Five Agents, Five Activities, Eight Affairs of Government, and Five Regulators of Time to explore the substance of the August Standard. He followed these with the Three Virtues, Examination of Doubts, Various Verifications, and Blessings and Extremes to illuminate the functioning of the August Standard. The Admonisher Liu Sanwu said that it opened an era of Great Peace for ten thousand generations.

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
資世通訓嚴君臣上下之等列士農工商之條
無非欲其遷善改過而同享太平之樂
大明集禮正天地百神之祀敘吉凶五禮之式
悉皆斷自
宸衷而期以達天下之中和凡若此者孰非取
於易書大學語孟之要領乎是我
聖祖闡心學之源爲經世之迹
神猷睿訓百世不磨眞天縱之所獨得者矣
列聖祗承後先羽翼肆我
===
皇上聖神睿智超越古今所以儷美前聖而光
昭
祖德者又無不會其極于稽其大如本尚書精
一之㫖
製爲敬一之箴
曰匪敬弗聚存其心而不忽之謂也
曰匪一弗純純乎理而無雜之謂也又推之
郊廟之顯閒居之隱言行之大始終之常無所
不用其交養之功焉此與虞廷儆戒之詞
punctuated:
《資世通訓》嚴君臣上下之等，列士農工商之條，無非欲其遷善改過，而同享太平之樂。《大明集禮》正天地百神之祀，敘吉凶五禮之式，悉皆斷自宸衷，而期以達天下之中和。凡若此者，孰非取於《易》《書》《大學》《語》《孟》之要領乎？是我聖祖闡心學之源，爲經世之迹，神猷睿訓，百世不磨，眞天縱之所獨得者矣！列聖祗承，後先羽翼。
肆我皇上聖神睿智，超越古今，所以儷美前聖而光昭祖德者，又無不會其極。于稽其大，如本《尚書》精一之㫖，製爲《敬一之箴》，曰：「匪敬弗聚。」存其心而不忽之謂也。曰：「匪一弗純。」純乎理而無雜之謂也。又推之郊廟之顯、閒居之隱、言行之大、始終之常，無所不用其交養之功焉。此與虞廷儆戒之詞
translation_en:
The Comprehensive Instructions for Aiding the World (Zishi tongxun) strictly defines the ranks of ruler and minister, superior and inferior, and sets out provisions for scholars, farmers, artisans, and merchants. All this aims to have them advance toward goodness and correct their faults, so that they may share the joys of great peace. The Collected Rituals of the Great Ming (Da Ming jili) regulates sacrifices to Heaven, Earth, and the hundred spirits and sets out the forms of the five categories of rites, auspicious, mourning, and the rest. All were decided by the imperial mind, with the aim of bringing equilibrium and harmony to all under Heaven. Which of these did not draw upon the essential principles of the Book of Changes, the Book of Documents, the Great Learning, the Analects, and the Mencius? Thus our sagely founding ancestor elucidated the source of the learning of the mind and gave it concrete expression in governing the world. His divine plans and sagacious instructions will remain undiminished for a hundred generations: truly, these were insights uniquely granted him by Heaven! Successive sage emperors reverently carried them forward, one after another supporting and furthering them.
Now our emperor, sagely, divine, discerning, and wise, surpasses ancient and modern times. In matching the excellence of earlier sages and making manifest his ancestor’s virtue, he invariably brings these principles to their utmost realization. Considering the major examples [?], he based his Admonition on Reverence and Single-mindedness (Jingyi zhen) on the Book of Documents’ teaching of refinement and single-mindedness. It says: “Without reverence, there is no gathering together.” This means preserving one’s mind without neglecting it. It says: “Without single-mindedness, there is no purity.” This means being pure in principle, without admixture. He further extends this to the public solemnity of the suburban sacrifices and ancestral temple, the privacy of his leisure, the weighty matters of speech and conduct, and constancy from beginning to end. Everywhere he applies the work of nurturing reverence and single-mindedness together. This, compared with the admonitory words of the court of Shun …

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
何以異也取宋儒范浚之心箴與程頤視
聽言動之四箴
親為註釋其於心箴則惜宋君之未能體察
也於四箴則歸重於人君之舉動也又求
之一心之正三才之叅邪正違遜之辨古
今幾微之著無所不致其交脩之力焉此
與論語克復之訓何以別也其論大學也
則於本末終始之條
親為之解以
頒史局誠有以端學者之趨向其
建無逸殿也則取尚書無逸之篇
揭之廡壁以備
觀覽誠欲知乎稼穡之艱難是所以發揮正
學而植政事之根本者固矣至於
經筵密勿其進講也每於大學語孟諸書皆
得隨事而陳說焉所以開萬化之淵源者
何其博也
深宮宥密其
punctuated: 何以異也？取宋儒范浚之心箴與程頤視聽言動之四箴，親為註釋。其於心箴，則惜宋君之未能體察也；於四箴，則歸重於人君之舉動也。又求之一心之正、三才之叅、邪正違遜之辨、古今幾微之著，無所不致其交脩之力焉。此與論語克復之訓何以別也？其論大學也，則於本末終始之條，親為之解，以頒史局，誠有以端學者之趨向。其建無逸殿也，則取尚書無逸之篇，揭之廡壁，以備觀覽，誠欲知乎稼穡之艱難。是所以發揮正學而植政事之根本者固矣。至於經筵密勿，其進講也，每於大學、語、孟諸書，皆得隨事而陳說焉，所以開萬化之淵源者何其博也！深宮宥密，其
translation_en:
…how does this differ? He took the Admonition on the Mind by the Song Confucian Fan Jun and Cheng Yi’s Four Admonitions on Looking, Listening, Speaking, and Acting, and personally annotated them. In treating the Admonition on the Mind, he regretted that the Song rulers had failed to comprehend and embody its teachings; in treating the Four Admonitions, he placed particular weight on the ruler’s conduct. He further pursued the rectification of the mind, participation alongside Heaven and Earth as the Three Powers, the distinction between the deviant and the upright and between disobedience and compliance, and the manifestation of subtle incipient signs in past and present. In all these matters he exerted himself toward their mutual cultivation. How does this differ from the Analects’ teaching on overcoming the self and returning to ritual propriety?
When discussing the Great Learning, he personally explained the passage on roots and branches, endings and beginnings, and distributed his explanation to the Historiography Office, thereby truly setting scholars on the proper course. When he built the Hall of Freedom from Idleness, he took the “Against Idleness” chapter of the Book of Documents and displayed it on the walls of its covered walkways for his inspection, sincerely wishing to understand the hardships of sowing and reaping. These were indeed means of elucidating correct learning and firmly establishing the foundations of government.
As for the diligent work of the Classics Colloquium, whenever lectures were presented to him on the Great Learning, the Analects, the Mencius, and other books, their teachings could be expounded in relation to particular affairs. How comprehensive were these means of opening the wellspring of all transformative governance! Within the secluded stillness of the inner palace, his …

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
燕閒也凡於前代列國諸史皆爲遍
閱而不遺焉所以觀歷代之鑒戒者何其切
也
先朝寶訓創業垂統之家法也乃
命儒臣而表章之一率由舊章之意
累朝實錄言行政事之大記也乃
作石宬而珍藏之一監于成憲之心凡若此
者孰非貫徹典謨訓誥之大旨乎是我
皇上集羣聖之成建
===
君師之極宏綱要紀百王不易眞前代之所未
有者矣若夫本之躬行心得之餘措諸踐
履行事之實則其大者又有四焉是故上
泰壇之號而大報隆恪
郊祀之典而精誠格
欽天有頌揚洪眷也星變有
勅謹時幾也其見於事
天之誠者如此新
御製之大誥而鑒觀以昭疏遺治之五事而繼
punctuated:
燕閒也，凡於前代列國諸史，皆爲遍閱而不遺焉，所以觀歷代之鑒戒者何其切也！先朝寶訓，創業垂統之家法也，乃命儒臣而表章之，一率由舊章之意；累朝實錄，言行政事之大記也，乃作石宬而珍藏之，一監于成憲之心。凡若此者，孰非貫徹典謨訓誥之大旨乎？是我皇上集羣聖之成，建君師之極，宏綱要紀，百王不易，眞前代之所未有者矣！
若夫本之躬行心得之餘，措諸踐履行事之實，則其大者又有四焉。是故上泰壇之號而大報隆，恪郊祀之典而精誠格。欽天有頌，揚洪眷也；星變有勅，謹時幾也。其見於事天之誠者如此。新御製之大誥而鑒觀以昭，疏遺治之五事而繼
translation_en:
…in his leisure, he reads all the histories of earlier dynasties and the various states, omitting none. How earnestly he studies the lessons and warnings of successive ages! The Precious Instructions of Former Reigns contain the house rules for founding the enterprise and transmitting the imperial succession. He therefore commanded Confucian officials to bring them to prominence, wholly intent upon following established precedents. The Veritable Records of Successive Reigns are the great record of imperial words, deeds, and affairs of government. He therefore built a stone archive to preserve them as treasures, wholly intent upon taking established institutions as his guide. Which of these undertakings does not thoroughly embody the great purport of the canons, counsels, instructions, and announcements of the Book of Documents? Thus our Emperor brings together the accomplishments of all the sages and establishes the highest standard as ruler and teacher. His grand principles and essential rules will remain unchanged through a hundred reigns: truly, nothing like this has existed in former ages!
As for grounding these achievements in his personal practice and inward understanding, and putting them into effect through actual conduct and government, there are four further major aspects. Thus he bestowed a designation upon the Great Altar [?], enhancing the great sacrifice of thanksgiving; he reverently observed the rites of the suburban sacrifice, and his perfect sincerity reached Heaven. He composed a eulogy on revering Heaven to extol its abundant favor; when anomalies appeared among the stars, he issued an edict, attending carefully to the incipient signs of the times. Such are the manifestations of his sincerity in serving Heaven. He renewed the imperially composed Grand Announcement, making its instructive example clear, and set forth the five matters of government bequeathed by his predecessors [?], thereby continuing…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
述以備
圜丘之配尊崇至也
祖德之和淵源通也其見於法
祖之孝者如此祗
玄穹以立心極一文王之於穆也純至道以凝
元精一成湯之日躋也他如翊學有詩以
匡正道除夕有作以示脩省而所以敬
身者何弗至耶遇旱澇則祈禱必
躬卽桑林自責之心也重民命則欽恤屢
===
詔卽刑期無刑之意也他如憫農之作以念民
天
內帑之發以溥賑恤而所以勤民者何弗至
耶蓋合
中和而交致舉倫制以兼脩肫肫乎以
心會之而天下之道不見其有餘亹亹然以
身體之而天下之治不見其不足此其
學其政卽
聖祖純天之學也謂之卽天之神可也卽
punctuated: 述以備。圜丘之配，尊崇至也；祖德之和，淵源通也。其見於法祖之孝者如此。祗玄穹以立心極，一文王之於穆也；純至道以凝元精，一成湯之日躋也。他如翊學有詩，以匡正道；除夕有作，以示脩省，而所以敬身者何弗至耶？遇旱澇則祈禱必躬，卽桑林自責之心也；重民命則欽恤屢詔，卽刑期無刑之意也。他如憫農之作，以念民天；內帑之發，以溥賑恤，而所以勤民者何弗至耶？蓋合中和而交致，舉倫制以兼脩，肫肫乎以心會之，而天下之道不見其有餘；亹亹然以身體之，而天下之治不見其不足。此其學其政，卽聖祖純天之學也，謂之卽天之神可也，卽
translation_en:
…so that the work of carrying on his predecessors’ achievements is complete. Associating his ancestor with the sacrifice at the Circular Mound brings veneration to its utmost; composing verses in response to those on ancestral virtue connects him with its source. Such are the manifestations of his filial devotion in following his ancestors’ example. Revering august Heaven to establish the supreme standard for his mind, he equals King Wen in profound reverence; making the ultimate Way pure and concentrating the primal essence, he equals Cheng Tang in daily advancement. Moreover, he composed a poem supporting learning to uphold the correct Way, and a work for New Year’s Eve to demonstrate self-cultivation and introspection. In showing reverence toward his own person, what has he left undone? When droughts or floods occur, he invariably offers prayers in person: this is the very spirit of self-reproach that Tang displayed at Sanglin. Cherishing the people’s lives, he repeatedly issues edicts enjoining reverent care and compassion in administering punishments: this embodies the intention of using punishment to bring about an end to punishment. Moreover, his composition expressing concern for farmers shows his care for food, which the people regard as Heaven; his disbursement of funds from the Privy Treasury extends relief widely. In laboring for the people, what has he left undone?

He unites equilibrium and harmony, bringing both to full realization, and cultivates human relationships and institutions together. With utter sincerity he apprehends them in his mind, and nothing in the Way of all under Heaven lies beyond his grasp; with unremitting diligence he embodies them in his person, and his governance of all under Heaven is found wanting in nothing. His learning and government are thus the sagely ancestor’s learning of pure accord with Heaven. One may call this the very numinous efficacy of Heaven; it is…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
聖祖憲天之政也謂之即天之化可也大哉
皇上之道所以光前烈而參造化者豈不真有
以此隆唐虞三代之上而陋漢唐宋於不
居者哉雖然有本焉亦曰敬一而已蓋政
本於學學本於心而敬一也者又所以立
此心之極而內聖外王之大本大原也惟
敬則靜靜則有天地翕聚之道焉惟一則
定定則有天地恒久之道焉我
皇上會翕聚恒久之理於一心則天下之精神
===
命脉愈久愈昌而
祖宗德業之隆上下同流之化萬世無疆矣所
謂諸福之物可致之祥又豈待求而得者
哉故曰至誠無息不息則久又曰聖人久
于其道而天下化成請以是為
今日頌
第二問
盧漸
同考試官教諭張 批 禮典戎政迫然
punctuated:
聖祖憲天之政也，謂之即天之化可也。大哉，皇上之道！所以光前烈而參造化者，豈不真有以此隆唐虞三代之上，而陋漢唐宋於不居者哉！雖然，有本焉，亦曰敬一而已。蓋政本於學，學本於心，而敬一也者，又所以立此心之極，而內聖外王之大本大原也。惟敬則靜，靜則有天地翕聚之道焉；惟一則定，定則有天地恒久之道焉。我皇上會翕聚恒久之理於一心，則天下之精神命脉愈久愈昌，而祖宗德業之隆、上下同流之化，萬世無疆矣。所謂諸福之物、可致之祥，又豈待求而得者哉！故曰：「至誠無息，不息則久。」又曰：「聖人久于其道，而天下化成。」請以是為今日頌。

第二問
盧漸

同考試官教諭張批：禮典戎政迫然
translation_en:
…the Sagely Founder's government, which took Heaven as its model; it may be called the very transforming activity of Heaven. Great indeed is Your Majesty's Way! Through it you glorify the achievements of your predecessors and participate in the work of creation and transformation. Does this not truly enable you to rise above the ages of Tang Yao, Yu Shun, and the Three Dynasties, regarding the Han, Tang, and Song as too low a standard to settle for? Yet this has a foundation: reverence and unity of purpose, nothing more. Government is rooted in learning, and learning in the mind. Reverence and unity of purpose establish the ultimate standard for this mind; they are the great foundation and source of inward sagehood and outward kingliness. Reverence brings stillness, and in stillness lies the Way by which Heaven and Earth draw together and concentrate their powers. Unity of purpose brings stability, and in stability lies the Way by which Heaven and Earth endure. Your Majesty unites the principles of concentration and endurance within your single mind. Thus the vital spirit and lifeblood of all under Heaven flourish ever more with the passage of time, while the exalted virtue and achievements of your ancestors, and the transforming influence flowing alike through those above and below, endure without limit for ten thousand generations. As for what are called the blessings that may be brought forth and the auspicious signs that may be elicited, how could their attainment depend on seeking them? Thus it is said: “Utmost sincerity never ceases; never ceasing, it endures.” It is also said: “The sage endures in his Way, and all under Heaven is transformed and brought to completion.” Allow me to offer these words as a eulogy for the present day.

Second Question
Lu Jian

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
皇上裁酌至精誠萬世彝憲也此篇援古證今鋪張曲盡可謂學識其大矣
同考試官學正李批場中多華奢關能詳
昭代之制者僅見是篇宜錄以式
考試官教諭管批發明祀典戎務詳盡
考試官教諭李批學俎豆軍旅而有得者
帝王承天以御世也統宗百神有崇祀之
大禮焉控制六合有經武之大政焉夫禮
以虔祀非徒以備文也由內心之敬而致
外典之仁敬則禮不瀆仁則恩不遺此王
===
者所以建中和之極而精誠達於兩間者
也政以飭戎非徒以耀武也脩內治之德
而振外攘之威德則懷其衷威則懲其玩
此王者所以弘招携之略而神武著於四
國者也是故祀典行則百神受職而天下
莫不化矣戎政飭則萬方順軌而天下莫
不肅矣然訏謨默運神經緯於一心猶之
化工潛孚宰陰陽於一元者也皇皇哉豈
非帝王之宏謨神聖之殊軌哉知此則我
punctuated:
皇上裁酌至精，誠萬世彝憲也。此篇援古證今，鋪張曲盡，可謂學識其大矣。
同考試官學正李批：場中多華奢關，能詳昭代之制者，僅見是篇，宜錄以式。
考試官教諭管批：發明祀典戎務詳盡。
考試官教諭李批：學俎豆軍旅而有得者。
帝王承天以御世也，統宗百神，有崇祀之大禮焉；控制六合，有經武之大政焉。夫禮以虔祀，非徒以備文也。由內心之敬，而致外典之仁，敬則禮不瀆，仁則恩不遺，此王者所以建中和之極，而精誠達於兩間者也。政以飭戎，非徒以耀武也。脩內治之德，而振外攘之威，德則懷其衷，威則懲其玩，此王者所以弘招携之略，而神武著於四國者也。是故祀典行，則百神受職，而天下莫不化矣；戎政飭，則萬方順軌，而天下莫不肅矣。然訏謨默運，神經緯於一心，猶之化工潛孚，宰陰陽於一元者也。皇皇哉！豈非帝王之宏謨、神聖之殊軌哉？知此，則我
translation_en:
…His Majesty has weighed and determined these matters with the utmost precision; they truly constitute enduring standards for ten thousand generations. This essay adduces antiquity to substantiate the present and develops its exposition fully in every detail. Its author's learning and discernment may indeed be called extensive.

Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: Among the examination essays, many indulge in florid extravagance [?]. This is the only essay I have seen that explains the institutions of our illustrious dynasty in detail. It should be recorded as a model.

Examiner Guan, Instructor, comments: Its elucidation of sacrificial institutions and military affairs is detailed and exhaustive.

Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: Here is someone who has studied sacrificial ritual and military affairs and gained understanding.

Emperors and kings receive Heaven's mandate to govern the world. Presiding over the hundred spirits, they possess the great rites for honoring them with sacrifice; commanding the six directions, they possess the great policies for ordering military affairs. Ritual serves to offer sacrifices reverently, not merely to furnish outward forms. From reverence within the heart proceeds the benevolence embodied in outward observances. With reverence, ritual is not profaned; with benevolence, none is omitted from gracious favor. Through these, the king establishes the supreme standard of centrality and harmony, and his perfect sincerity reaches throughout the space between Heaven and Earth. Government serves to put military affairs in order, not merely to display martial might. By cultivating the virtue of domestic government, he manifests the authority needed to repel external threats. Virtue wins their hearts; authority chastises their insolence. Through these, the king extends his strategy for drawing in those who have become estranged, and his divine martial prowess becomes manifest throughout the lands in all four directions.

Thus, when sacrificial institutions are put into practice, the hundred spirits receive their appointed duties, and none beneath Heaven remains untransformed. When military administration is put in order, all regions follow the proper course, and none beneath Heaven fails to show due respect. Yet these great designs operate silently, their wondrous ordering proceeding within a single mind, just as the work of creation takes effect unseen, governing yin and yang within the primal unity. How magnificent! Are these not the grand designs of emperors and kings, the extraordinary ways of divine sages? Understanding this, then our…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
聖祖建制立法特詳慎於創垂之初
皇上纘武弘文益光大於純熈之會所以德眇
百王功高千古者可得而闚觀其萬一矣
自昔聖王制祭祀以交神明也以一純二
精三牲四時五色六律七事八種九祭十
日十二辰以致之千品萬官億醜兆民經
入咳數以奉之又使先聖之後能知山川
之號昭穆之世禮節之宜威儀之則忠信
之質禋潔之服而致恭明神者為之祝使
===
名姓之後能知犧牲之物玉帛之類采服
之宜彝器之量壇場之所屏攝之位而心
率舊典者為之宗若是乎其慎也在易渙
之象曰風行水上渙先王以享帝立廟蓋
享帝而與天神接立廟而與祖禰交皆聚
已之精神以合其渙者也故祝史求於宗
祊而非以為誕也簠簋新於黃目而非以
為侈也犧象登於太室而非以為繁也凡
以致吾仁敬之道而已矣古者制邊縣以
punctuated:
聖祖建制立法，特詳慎於創垂之初；皇上纘武弘文，益光大於純熈之會。所以德眇百王、功高千古者，可得而闚觀其萬一矣。
自昔聖王制祭祀以交神明也，以一純、二精、三牲、四時、五色、六律、七事、八種、九祭、十日、十二辰以致之，千品、萬官、億醜、兆民、經入咳數以奉之。又使先聖之後，能知山川之號、昭穆之世、禮節之宜、威儀之則、忠信之質、禋潔之服，而致恭明神者，為之祝；使名姓之後，能知犧牲之物、玉帛之類、采服之宜、彝器之量、壇場之所、屏攝之位，而心率舊典者，為之宗。若是乎其慎也！在《易》，渙之象曰：「風行水上，渙；先王以享帝立廟。」蓋享帝而與天神接，立廟而與祖禰交，皆聚已之精神以合其渙者也。故祝史求於宗祊，而非以為誕也；簠簋新於黃目，而非以為侈也；犧象登於太室，而非以為繁也。凡以致吾仁敬之道而已矣。
古者制邊縣以
translation_en:
…our Sagely Ancestor established institutions and laws, exercising particular care and thoroughness at the outset, when founding the dynasty and bequeathing its order to posterity. His Majesty continues his martial achievements and expands civil culture, bringing them still greater glory in this age of pure splendor. Thus we may glimpse some tiny fraction of what makes their virtue surpass that of a hundred kings and their achievements rise above those of a thousand ages.
From ancient times, sage kings instituted sacrifices to communicate with divine powers. They brought this about through single-minded purity, the two pure offerings, the three sacrificial animals, the four seasons, the five colors, the six pitch standards, the seven ritual services, the eight kinds of grain, the nine forms of sacrifice, the ten days, and the twelve earthly branches. They supported these rites with a thousand categories of things, ten thousand officials, countless multitudes, myriads of people, and further vast numbers [?]. They also appointed as invocators descendants of former sages who knew the names of mountains and rivers, the generations in the alternating zhao and mu ranks of ancestral succession, appropriate ritual observances, the rules of dignified deportment, the substance of loyalty and trustworthiness, and the purified garments for sacrifice, and who could show reverence to the radiant spirits. They appointed as ritual masters descendants of distinguished lineages who knew the kinds of sacrificial animals, the categories of jade and silk, appropriate colored vestments, the capacities of ritual vessels, the locations of altars and sacrificial grounds, and the positions of screens, and who followed the ancient canons in their hearts. Such was their care!
In the Book of Changes, the Image commentary on Huan, Dispersion, says: “Wind moves over water: Dispersion. The former kings accordingly offered sacrifice to the Supreme Deity and established ancestral temples.” Through sacrifice to the Supreme Deity they made contact with the celestial spirits; by establishing ancestral temples they communed with their ancestors and deceased fathers. In both cases, they concentrated their own spiritual energies to bring together what was dispersed. Thus, when invocators and scribes sought the spirits at the ancestral temple’s gate, this was no empty extravagance; when fu and gui grain vessels were freshly arrayed alongside the Yellow-Eye wine vessels [?], this was no luxury; and when ox-shaped and elephant-shaped wine vessels were presented in the Great Chamber, this was no needless elaboration. All this served only to fulfill the way of benevolence and reverence.
