title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
禦夷也使五家爲伍伍有長十長一里里
有假士四里一連連有假五百十連一邑
邑有假侯皆擇其邑之賢材有識習地形
知民心者居則習民於射法出則教民於
應敵故卒伍成於內而軍政定於外服習
以成勿令遷徙若是乎其備也在易萃之
象曰澤上於地萃君子以除戎器戒不虞
夫當萃聚之世而預爲武事之修所以肅
內外之紀而保其萃者也故戎車飭於六
===
月而不以爲棘也干羽舞於兩階而不以
爲弛也采薇戍於再朞而不以爲黷也凡
以善吾威懷之經而已矣蓋自載籍以來
所可睹記者祀有執膰戎有受脤而不知
帝王昭假之精神武之烈固非徒備文而
耀武者矣乃以考後世之所沿襲吾惑滋
甚焉夫秦漢代興舉祀典者非不知陳其
儀也然東封西祀者昧崇報之典檢玉泥
金者溺紛紜之論祀天於汾陰而又有五
punctuated:
禦夷也，使五家爲伍，伍有長；十長一里，里有假士；四里一連，連有假五百；十連一邑，邑有假侯。皆擇其邑之賢材有識、習地形、知民心者，居則習民於射法，出則教民於應敵。故卒伍成於內，而軍政定於外，服習以成，勿令遷徙。若是乎其備也！在《易》，萃之象曰：「澤上於地，萃。君子以除戎器，戒不虞。」夫當萃聚之世，而預爲武事之修，所以肅內外之紀而保其萃者也。故戎車飭於《六月》，而不以爲棘也；干羽舞於兩階，而不以爲弛也；《采薇》戍於再朞，而不以爲黷也。凡以善吾威懷之經而已矣。
蓋自載籍以來，所可睹記者，祀有執膰，戎有受脤，而不知帝王昭假之精、神武之烈，固非徒備文而耀武者矣。乃以考後世之所沿襲，吾惑滋甚焉。夫秦漢代興，舉祀典者非不知陳其儀也，然東封西祀者昧崇報之典，檢玉泥金者溺紛紜之論。祀天於汾陰，而又有五
translation_en:
…to defend against the barbarians. Five households were constituted as a squad, each with a head; ten such heads formed a village, with an acting officer; four villages formed a company, with an acting commander of five hundred; and ten companies formed a district, with an acting lord. For all these posts, they selected worthy and capable men of the district who possessed discernment, knew the terrain, and understood the people's dispositions. At home, these men trained the people in archery; when taking the field, they taught them to confront the enemy. Thus the ranks were organized internally, while military administration was established externally. Through repeated practice they became proficient, and they were not permitted to move elsewhere. Such was the thoroughness of their preparations! In the Book of Changes, the Image of Gathering Together says: “The lake rises above the earth: Gathering Together. The noble man accordingly puts weapons in order and guards against the unforeseen.” To prepare military affairs in advance during an age of gathering together is to maintain strict order within and without and preserve that unity. Thus war chariots were put in order in “Sixth Month,” without this being deemed impetuous; shields and plumes were wielded in dances between the two stairways, without this being deemed lax; and the garrison service in “Gathering Ferns” extended into a second year, without this being deemed an abuse of warfare. All this served only to perfect our enduring principles of inspiring awe and winning allegiance.
Ever since written records began, what can be seen recorded includes the bearing of sacrificial meat in worship and the receiving of sacrificial meat before military action. Yet people fail to understand that the spiritual concentration through which emperors and kings reached the divine, and the achievements of their spirit-like martial power, were assuredly more than mere displays of ceremonial form and military might. When I examine what later ages inherited and perpetuated, my perplexity grows still greater. As Qin and Han rose in succession, those conducting the prescribed sacrifices certainly knew how to set out their ceremonies. Yet those who performed the Feng sacrifice in the east and sacrifices in the west failed to understand the rites of reverent recompense; those who used jade sealing tablets and gold sealing clay became mired in conflicting arguments. They sacrificed to Heaven at Fenyin, yet also had the five…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
祀之禱祀帝於玉清者又有上帝之說以
時言或春秋天地同祀於南郊冬夏天地
分祀於南北以地言或南郊兆于洛陽之
南北郊兆于洛陽之陰唐雖罷六天之謬
論而朝獻太清宮朝獻太廟至用盂蘭之
禮宋雖循三世之常儀而朝獻景靈宮朝
獻太廟乃有迭配之殊此皆眩於難明之
義雜以非聖之書則內心不慤旣自違于
對越矣又安望乎神聽而右享之也夫明
===
於義理之原者不可惑以謬論通乎萬物
之理者不可罔以非類而乃徒察於制度
之細以致祝多媿詞焉蓋由下多聚訟道
謀之議且無據經守禮之倡則其祀典之
不脩固然哉其稱肆伐者亦非不知道其
事也然犁庭掃穴者竭民膏以潤狼望之
野窮追遠討者委府庫以塡盧山之壑漢
之武帝史稱其南開兩粵西闢五都矣唐
之太宗自以爲雪耻酬百王除兇報千古
punctuated:
祀之禱；祀帝於玉清者，又有上帝之說。以時言，或春秋天地同祀於南郊，冬夏天地分祀於南北；以地言，或南郊兆于洛陽之南，北郊兆于洛陽之陰。唐雖罷六天之謬論，而朝獻太清宮、朝獻太廟，至用盂蘭之禮；宋雖循三世之常儀，而朝獻景靈宮、朝獻太廟，乃有迭配之殊。此皆眩於難明之義，雜以非聖之書，則內心不慤，旣自違于對越矣，又安望乎神聽而右享之也？夫明於義理之原者，不可惑以謬論；通乎萬物之理者，不可罔以非類。而乃徒察於制度之細，以致祝多媿詞焉。蓋由下多聚訟道謀之議，且無據經守禮之倡，則其祀典之不脩固然哉！
其稱肆伐者，亦非不知道其事也。然犁庭掃穴者，竭民膏以潤狼望之野；窮追遠討者，委府庫以塡盧山之壑。漢之武帝，史稱其南開兩粵，西闢五都矣；唐之太宗，自以爲雪耻酬百王，除兇報千古
translation_en:
…prayers at the [Five] Sacrifices; those who sacrificed to the divine ruler at Yuqing also advanced a doctrine concerning the Supreme Lord. In terms of timing, some sacrificed jointly to Heaven and Earth at the southern suburb in spring and autumn, while sacrificing to them separately at the southern and northern suburbs in winter and summer. In terms of location, some laid out the southern suburban sacrificial precinct south of Luoyang and the northern precinct north of Luoyang. Although the Tang abolished the erroneous doctrine of the Six Heavens, its court offerings at Taiqing Palace and the Imperial Ancestral Temple went so far as to employ the Buddhist Ullambana rite. Although the Song followed the customary ceremonies of the three ages [?], its court offerings at Jingling Palace and the Imperial Ancestral Temple introduced distinctions through alternating the associated recipients of sacrifice. All this arose from confusion over meanings difficult to elucidate and the admixture of writings not sanctioned by the sages. With no sincerity in their hearts, they had already departed from the proper spirit of standing reverently before the divine. How, then, could they expect the spirits to hear them and graciously accept their offerings? Those who understand the source of moral principle cannot be misled by erroneous doctrines; those who comprehend the principles of all things cannot be deceived by inappropriate analogies. Yet they merely scrutinized the minutiae of institutions and regulations, so that their sacrificial prayers contained much that gave cause for shame. This was because those below engaged in contentious disputes and ill-considered deliberations, while no one championed adherence to the Classics and observance of ritual. Was it not inevitable, then, that their sacrificial ordinances should fall into disorder?
Those who spoke of launching punitive campaigns were likewise not ignorant of the undertaking. Yet those who ploughed up enemy courts and swept out their lairs drained the people’s lifeblood to enrich the plains of Langwang; those who pursued enemies relentlessly and campaigned far afield poured out the treasuries and storehouses to fill the ravines of Lushan. Of Emperor Wu of the Han, the histories say that he opened up the two Yue territories in the south and the Five Capitals [?] in the west. Emperor Taizong of the Tang considered himself to have avenged humiliation on behalf of a hundred kings and eliminated evildoers in requital for the wrongs of a thousand ages…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
矣夫百戰百勝玄荒懾服志非不雄也連
兵邊陲宿軍遼絕之野力非小弱也葱嶺
龍堆宣揚聲敎雕題卉服奔走域中威非
輕鮮也然無救於虛耗之悔而竟沮喪於
遼左之歸則黷武喜功徒基禍於生民耳
果何能光晉伐而章大烈也夫兵凶器也
爭逆德也故聖人不務遠略以固其本而
乃敝所恃以勤無用蓋君以窮兵爲駿功
臣以拓地爲勝畫則其戎事之召釁奚疑
===
哉嗟乎執事有慨於後世之可議蓋誠見
其謬迷剌戾者多矣洪惟我
太祖高皇帝受
天明命建極開人旣定天下首正祀典考諸聖
賢之經傳斷以
淵衷之獨得
命陶安定
郊社羣祀之禮
命詹同定
punctuated:
矣。夫百戰百勝，玄荒懾服，志非不雄也；連兵邊陲，宿軍遼絕之野，力非小弱也；葱嶺龍堆，宣揚聲敎，雕題卉服，奔走域中，威非輕鮮也。然無救於虛耗之悔，而竟沮喪於遼左之歸，則黷武喜功，徒基禍於生民耳，果何能光晉伐而章大烈也？夫兵，凶器也；爭，逆德也。故聖人不務遠略，以固其本，而乃敝所恃以勤無用。蓋君以窮兵爲駿功，臣以拓地爲勝畫，則其戎事之召釁奚疑哉？
嗟乎！執事有慨於後世之可議，蓋誠見其謬迷剌戾者多矣。洪惟我太祖高皇帝受天明命，建極開人，旣定天下，首正祀典，考諸聖賢之經傳，斷以淵衷之獨得。命陶安定郊社羣祀之禮，命詹同定
translation_en:
…To win every battle and cow the remote wilderness into submission—such ambition was certainly heroic. To maintain continuous warfare along the frontiers and station armies in far distant lands—such strength was certainly no small thing. To proclaim imperial authority and civilizing instruction throughout Congling and Longdui, and have peoples with tattooed foreheads and garments of plant fibre hastening to serve within the realm—such power was certainly considerable. Yet none of this could avert regret over depletion and exhaustion, and in the end there was dejection upon returning from Liaozuo. Reckless warfare and delight in military achievement merely laid the foundations of disaster for the people. How, indeed, could they bring glory to military advances and manifest great accomplishments? Weapons are instruments of ill omen; contention runs counter to virtue. Thus the sage does not pursue distant conquests, thereby securing his foundations. Yet these rulers instead exhausted what they depended upon, labouring at what was useless. When the ruler regards exhausting military campaigns as splendid achievements, and his ministers regard territorial expansion as the finest strategy, how can there be any doubt that their military undertakings will provoke trouble?
Alas! You, sir, lament the conduct of later ages that invites criticism, surely because you have seen so much error, delusion, and perversity. We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao received Heaven’s luminous mandate, established the supreme standard of rule, and inaugurated a new order for the people. Having pacified All-under-Heaven, he first rectified the sacrificial canon, examining the classics and commentaries of the sages and worthies and deciding matters through the unique insights of his profound imperial mind. He ordered Tao An to establish the rites for the suburban sacrifices, the altars of the soil, and the various other sacrifices; he ordered Zhan Tong to establish…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
四廟祫祭之禮嶽鎮海瀆惟稱山水之本名先
代名臣惟稱受封之始號城隍旗纛之祭
以義而起先農太歲之祀稱情而立至於
有事
圜丘則反視却聽上契冲漠旣謹於致齋之時
有赫其臨莫敢仰視尤嚴於對越之際嘗
莊誦
祖訓嚴祭祀章曰精誠則福至怠慢則禍生大
哉
===
王者之言即虞舜寅清之心法也然猶慮羣臣
或怠於駿奔而忽於陟降也則又有
存心錄以戒諭之凡古人敬怠誠忽皆列其
事以示其應焉我
皇祖虔祀之心誠肅乎昭懷柔之義矣至其控
制外夷而慎固邊圉也責安南奉貢之豐
抑高麗請謚之失嚴陝西甲胄之脩飭河
南城隍之險萬年丕基於斯乎肇于時義
戈初指羣夷懾服月羽一麾百蠻底定東
punctuated:
四廟祫祭之禮。嶽鎮海瀆，惟稱山水之本名；先代名臣，惟稱受封之始號。城隍旗纛之祭，以義而起；先農太歲之祀，稱情而立。至於有事圜丘，則反視却聽，上契冲漠，旣謹於致齋之時；有赫其臨，莫敢仰視，尤嚴於對越之際。嘗莊誦《祖訓》嚴祭祀章曰：「精誠則福至，怠慢則禍生。」大哉，王者之言！即虞舜寅清之心法也。然猶慮羣臣或怠於駿奔，而忽於陟降也，則又有《存心錄》以戒諭之。凡古人敬怠誠忽，皆列其事，以示其應焉。我皇祖虔祀之心，誠肅乎昭懷柔之義矣。
至其控制外夷，而慎固邊圉也，責安南奉貢之豐，抑高麗請謚之失，嚴陝西甲胄之脩，飭河南城隍之險。萬年丕基，於斯乎肇。于時義戈初指，羣夷懾服；月羽一麾，百蠻底定。東
translation_en:
…the rites for the joint ancestral sacrifice in the four temples. The sacred peaks, guardian mountains, seas, and rivers were designated solely by their original geographical names; eminent ministers of former dynasties, solely by the titles first conferred upon them. Sacrifices to the city gods and military banners were instituted according to righteousness; worship of the First Farmer and the Grand Year deity was established in accordance with proper sentiments. When performing sacrifices at the Circular Mound, he turned his sight inward and withdrew his hearing, inwardly attaining communion with the silent void above. He was already scrupulous during the period of strict purification; when the radiant presence descended, none dared look upward, and he was especially reverent when facing the divine presence. I have reverently recited the chapter on solemnizing sacrifices in the Ancestral Injunctions: “With perfect sincerity, blessings arrive; with negligence and disrespect, calamity arises.” How great are the words of a true king! They embody the very discipline of reverence and purity transmitted by Shun of Yu. Yet he still feared that his ministers might slacken in hastening to their ritual duties and grow careless in ascending and descending the ceremonial steps. He therefore also produced the Record of Preserving the Mind (Cunxin lu) to admonish and instruct them. It sets out instances of reverence and negligence, sincerity and carelessness among people of antiquity, showing the consequences of each. Our imperial ancestor’s devotion to sacrifice truly gave solemn expression to the principle of manifest reverence and conciliating the spirits.
As for his control of foreign peoples and his care in securing the frontiers, he reproved Annam for the excessive lavishness of its tribute, checked Goryeo’s improper request for a posthumous title, rigorously required the maintenance of armor in Shaanxi, and ordered the strengthening of walls and moats in Henan. Here began the great foundation for ten thousand years. At that time, as soon as his righteous weapons were directed against them, the foreign peoples submitted in awe; with one wave of the “moon-feather” standard [?], the many southern peoples were pacified. Eastward…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
極蒙汜西盡崦嵫南罄丹垠北窮玄朔皆
九譯以獻琛效三苗之格面故燕雲河朔
數百年腥穢之郊圻也靈夏寧州姦宄窟
穴之外鄙也河隍西域終漢之所經營而
弗靖也北韓南粵唐室所爲竭財力以求
服役者也而今皆入我版圖供職貢焉是
誠可以仰見
皇靈之丕振而
聖謨之宏遠矣
===
列聖相承二百年來道化隆洽幽明交贊祀典
敬承武功克競迨我
皇上嗣統中興尤稽乾履泰之會也
聖心獨運誠建諸
天地而同其神
聖制大成實考諸古今而總其貫
郊丘分祀三代之所竝隆
廟享肇禋千古之所希覯舉
大禘之典尊祀
punctuated:
極蒙汜，西盡崦嵫，南罄丹垠，北窮玄朔，皆九譯以獻琛，效三苗之格面。故燕雲河朔，數百年腥穢之郊圻也；靈夏寧州，姦宄窟穴之外鄙也；河隍西域，終漢之所經營而弗靖也；北韓南粵，唐室所爲竭財力以求服役者也。而今皆入我版圖，供職貢焉。是誠可以仰見皇靈之丕振，而聖謨之宏遠矣。
列聖相承二百年來，道化隆洽，幽明交贊，祀典敬承，武功克競。迨我皇上嗣統中興，尤稽乾履泰之會也。聖心獨運，誠建諸天地而同其神；聖制大成，實考諸古今而總其貫。郊丘分祀，三代之所竝隆；廟享肇禋，千古之所希覯。舉大禘之典，尊祀
translation_en:
…reaching Mengsi, extending west to Yanzi, south to the red borderlands, and north to the dark northern reaches, all presented precious treasures through successive interpreters, emulating the Sanmiao in coming to submit in person. Thus Yan, Yun, and Heshuo were frontier territories befouled for several hundred years; Ling, Xia, and Ningzhou were outlying borderlands where rebels and malefactors had their lairs; Hehuang [?] and the Western Regions were places that the Han strove throughout its rule to administer but never pacified; and Han in the north and Yue in the south were places whose service the Tang court exhausted its wealth and strength to secure. Yet now all have entered our imperial domain and discharge their obligations of tribute. Here one may indeed behold the mighty manifestation of imperial power and the breadth and foresight of the sagely plans.
For two hundred years, successive sage sovereigns have inherited the throne. Moral transformation has flourished and spread everywhere; the unseen and visible realms have joined in offering support; the sacrificial rites have been reverently maintained; and martial achievements have been vigorously pursued. With our present Emperor’s succession and restoration of flourishing rule, this is especially an occasion of accord with Qian, the Creative, and attainment of Tai, Peace [?]. His sagely mind acts through its own insight: his sincerity is established before Heaven and Earth and shares their numinous efficacy. His sagely institutions have reached full accomplishment: they have truly been tested against past and present and encompass their unifying principles. Separate sacrifices at the suburban altars and sacrificial mounds are rites equally exalted under the Three Dynasties; the inauguration of pure offerings in the ancestral temple is something rarely witnessed through the ages. He has instituted the great di ancestral sacrifice, reverently offering worship to…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
皇初祖而配以
太祖定
大祫之祭尊祀
德祖而配以
列祖别武周之位則君臣之分明易孔子之稱
則先師之義正竊嘗伏讀
敬一之箴有曰
郊則恭誠
廟嚴孝趨肅於明廷慎於閒居至哉
===
聖人之作即唐堯精一之正傳也然猶以羣臣
多沿習於舊聞而拘攣於曲說也則又有
明堂或問以昭示之凡先聖精微統紀悉闡其
微而發其祕焉我
皇上禋祀之禮誠卓然為曠世之典矣頃者南
北之夷間乘其飈舉之勢而擾我邊鄙或
鼓其烏集之羣而犯我海壖北則有花當
把兒孫之類窺隙而動也南則有倭奴之
種勾引而入也羽檄一聞
punctuated:
皇初祖，而配以太祖；定大祫之祭，尊祀德祖，而配以列祖。别武周之位，則君臣之分明；易孔子之稱，則先師之義正。竊嘗伏讀《敬一》之箴，有曰：「郊則恭誠，廟嚴孝趨，肅於明廷，慎於閒居。」至哉，聖人之作！即唐堯精一之正傳也。然猶以羣臣多沿習於舊聞，而拘攣於曲說也，則又有《明堂或問》以昭示之。凡先聖精微統紀，悉闡其微而發其祕焉。我皇上禋祀之禮，誠卓然為曠世之典矣。
頃者，南北之夷間乘其飈舉之勢而擾我邊鄙，或鼓其烏集之羣而犯我海壖。北則有花當、把兒孫之類窺隙而動也；南則有倭奴之種勾引而入也。羽檄一聞，
translation_en:
…the imperial primordial ancestor, with Taizu as the associated recipient; he established the great collective ancestral sacrifice, honoring Dezu with the successive ancestors as associated recipients. By distinguishing the ritual positions of King Wu and the Duke of Zhou, he clarified the distinction between ruler and subject; by changing Confucius’s title, he rectified the meaning of his status as the First Teacher. I have humbly read the Admonition on Reverence and Unity (Jingyi), which says: “At the suburban sacrifices, be reverent and sincere; in the ancestral temple, solemnly practice filial devotion [?]; be respectful in the illustrious court and circumspect in private.” How consummate is this work of the sage! It is the authentic transmission of Tang Yao’s teaching of refinement and unity. Yet, because his ministers still largely followed inherited learning and were constrained by distorted interpretations, he further provided Questions and Answers on the Hall of Enlightenment (Mingtang huowen) to instruct them clearly. He fully elucidated the subtleties and revealed the hidden meanings of the former sages’ profound guiding principles. Our Emperor’s sacrificial rites are indeed outstanding ceremonies without parallel in the ages.
Recently, the barbarians to the south and north have at times exploited the momentum of their whirlwind advances to trouble our borderlands, or rallied their crow-like throngs to invade our shores. In the north, the likes of Huadang and Ba’ersun watch for openings and then act; in the south, bands of Japanese marauders enter with the aid of colluding guides. As soon as an urgent military dispatch arrives…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
天威迅發以議將爲首務則於文武督總之臣
必極一時之選而一不稱則易置之以軍
供爲急需則於兵士糧餉之備悉從諸臣
之議而請
內帑則速給之於是封豕殪於塵沙漸以銷
其彎弓竊視之念長鯨斬於瀚海竟以寢
其揚帆鼓譟之謀
神功耀於宇宙而駿烈震乎雷霆豈非增光往
號流聲來諜者哉夫我
===
聖祖開創於往初而
皇上覲揚於今日後先相映寖明寖昌非偶然
也蓋精玄之極孚感百靈合仁與敬而咸
備者
聖人之所以同天德也鼓舞之機光濟六合兼
德與威而竝盛者
聖人之所以同王道也猗與盛哉然愚聞之動
天地感鬼神莫近乎禮樂今
國家禮制誠明備矣而樂猶有待焉
punctuated:
天威迅發，以議將爲首務，則於文武督總之臣，必極一時之選，而一不稱則易置之；以軍供爲急需，則於兵士糧餉之備，悉從諸臣之議，而請內帑則速給之。於是封豕殪於塵沙，漸以銷其彎弓竊視之念；長鯨斬於瀚海，竟以寢其揚帆鼓譟之謀。神功耀於宇宙，而駿烈震乎雷霆，豈非增光往號、流聲來諜者哉！
夫我聖祖開創於往初，而皇上覲揚於今日，後先相映，寖明寖昌，非偶然也。蓋精玄之極，孚感百靈，合仁與敬而咸備者，聖人之所以同天德也；鼓舞之機，光濟六合，兼德與威而竝盛者，聖人之所以同王道也。猗與盛哉！
然愚聞之，動天地、感鬼神，莫近乎禮樂。今國家禮制誠明備矣，而樂猶有待焉。
translation_en:
…the imperial might was swiftly unleashed. Regarding the selection of commanders as the foremost task, His Majesty invariably chose the finest men of the age among the civil and military officials charged with overall command; whenever one proved unequal to the task, he replaced him. Regarding military supplies as an urgent necessity, he accepted all the officials’ proposals for provisioning the troops with grain and pay, and promptly granted requests for funds from the imperial treasury. Thus the great boars were slain amid dust and sand, gradually extinguishing their desire to bend their bows and watch for an opening; the mighty whales were beheaded upon the vast sea, finally putting an end to their schemes to hoist their sails and raise their battle cries. His divine achievements illuminate the universe, and his mighty exploits resound like thunder. Do they not add glory to earlier renown [?] and transmit his fame to the records of posterity [?]?
Our sagely ancestor founded the dynasty in former times, and His Majesty now carries its glory forward [?]. Predecessor and successor illuminate one another, growing ever more brilliant and flourishing: this is no accident. Utmost spiritual profundity moves the hundred spirits through sincerity; the complete union of benevolence and reverence is how the sage shares Heaven’s virtue. The power to inspire brings glorious succor throughout the six directions; the joint flourishing of virtue and awe is how the sage accords with the Kingly Way. Ah, how magnificent!
Yet I have heard that nothing comes closer than ritual and music to moving Heaven and Earth and stirring ghosts and spirits. Today the state’s ritual institutions are indeed clearly established and complete, but music still awaits further attention.

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
廟堂之上得無加意於斯乎愚又聞之聖王
貴未然之防而忠臣謹先事之慮今
國家武功誠大振矣然周公克詰戎兵之訓
召公張皇六師之言非羣工所當共勵者
乎愚生媿無鴻筆以宣昭
國家之盛美乃願自效其一得如此惟執事
採焉
第三問
劉伯淵
===
同考試官教諭韓批天人之際未易言者子能
洞究微奧取諸家之說而折衷之可以釋羣疑矣
同考試官教諭蘇批占候一篇場中多勦竊陳言
殊厭觀覽此作析理甚明足以破諸誕而有裨於敬畏者錄之
考試官教諭管批議論□占之法殆盡
考試官教諭李批是曾究心天文者
天有至文聖人有至道至文者垂象著明
而經緯於天者也至道者履信思順而綜
理民物者也天之所示無有災祥愆若而
punctuated:
廟堂之上，得無加意於斯乎？愚又聞之，聖王貴未然之防，而忠臣謹先事之慮。今國家武功誠大振矣，然周公克詰戎兵之訓、召公張皇六師之言，非羣工所當共勵者乎？愚生媿無鴻筆，以宣昭國家之盛美，乃願自效其一得如此，惟執事採焉。
第三問
劉伯淵
同考試官教諭韓批：「天人之際，未易言者。子能洞究微奧，取諸家之說而折衷之，可以釋羣疑矣。」
同考試官教諭蘇批：「占候一篇，場中多勦竊陳言，殊厭觀覽。此作析理甚明，足以破諸誕，而有裨於敬畏者，錄之。」
考試官教諭管批：「議論□占之法殆盡。」
考試官教諭李批：「是曾究心天文者。」
天有至文，聖人有至道。至文者，垂象著明，而經緯於天者也；至道者，履信思順，而綜理民物者也。天之所示，無有災祥愆若，而
translation_en:
Should those at court not give special attention to this? I have also heard that sage kings value precautions against troubles before they arise, and loyal ministers carefully consider affairs before they occur. Now the state's military achievements have indeed become greatly illustrious. Yet are not the Duke of Zhou's admonition to put the armed forces in good order and the Duke of Shao's words on enhancing the might of the Six Armies matters in which all officials should encourage one another? I, an unworthy scholar, am ashamed that I lack the literary talent to proclaim the state's magnificent accomplishments. I nevertheless wish to offer what little insight I have, as set forth here, and ask that you, honored examiners, consider it.
Third Policy Question
Liu Boyuan
Associate Examiner Han, Instructor, comments: “The relationship between Heaven and humanity is not easily discussed. You have thoroughly investigated its subtle mysteries, drawing on the explanations of various authorities and weighing them to reach a balanced judgment. This can resolve many doubts.”
Associate Examiner Su, Instructor, comments: “In the essay on divination through celestial observation, many candidates in this examination have plagiarized stale formulations, making the reading exceedingly tiresome. This composition analyzes the principles very clearly, sufficiently refuting the various absurdities and contributing to reverent awe. I select it for inclusion.”
Examiner Guan, Instructor, comments: “The discussion deals almost exhaustively with the methods of □ divination [?].”
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “This is someone who has devoted thought to celestial patterns.”
Heaven possesses the supreme pattern; the sage possesses the supreme Way. The supreme pattern is that which displays images and manifests its brilliance, forming the warp and weft of Heaven. The supreme Way is that by which one acts in good faith, considers what accords with right order, and comprehensively governs the people and all things. As for what Heaven displays, whether calamities or auspicious signs, irregularities or favorable conditions, …

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
皆發邇見遠之應聖人之所爲無有幽深
顯易而皆有感必通之理故曰在天者未
始不爲於人在人者未始不爲於天天人
相與之際蓋微乎微者也惟聖人能順天
之道以治民之情而無所不用其奉若則
天之心日陟降於聖人之左右亦無所不
用其仁愛矣是故昭休敬怒或竝量而議
猷臻符銷譴或比力而建功以其操德一
而求端在我也在然則由推驗以明天道固
===
數所必有惟泥之則窮矣由昭德以奉天
道固理所當爲惟取必之則戾矣聖人所
以與天合一之心其無思無爲之謂乎執
事欲究象數之微以觀於天道則自甘石
而下代致其詳欲察分候之因以達於民
故則自堯舜之君序脩其業請得而終言
之夫天地之道貞觀者也日月之道貞明
者也天下之動貞夫一者也王者合天地
之德齊日月之光以正位乎上則所以主
punctuated:
皆發邇見遠之應。聖人之所爲，無有幽深顯易，而皆有感必通之理。故曰：在天者未始不爲於人，在人者未始不爲於天。天人相與之際，蓋微乎微者也。惟聖人能順天之道，以治民之情，而無所不用其奉若，則天之心日陟降於聖人之左右，亦無所不用其仁愛矣。是故昭休敬怒，或竝量而議猷；臻符銷譴，或比力而建功。以其操德一，而求端在我也。在然則，由推驗以明天道，固數所必有，惟泥之則窮矣；由昭德以奉天道，固理所當爲，惟取必之則戾矣。聖人所以與天合一之心，其無思無爲之謂乎？

執事欲究象數之微，以觀於天道，則自甘石而下，代致其詳；欲察分候之因，以達於民故，則自堯舜之君，序脩其業。請得而終言之。夫天地之道，貞觀者也；日月之道，貞明者也；天下之動，貞夫一者也。王者合天地之德，齊日月之光，以正位乎上，則所以主
translation_en:
…all are responses that arise nearby and reveal what is distant. In what the sage does, whether hidden and profound or manifest and readily understood, there is always the principle that every stimulus necessarily elicits a response. Thus it is said: what occurs in Heaven never fails to act upon human beings, and what occurs among human beings never fails to act upon Heaven. The point at which Heaven and humanity interact is indeed subtle beyond subtlety. Only the sage can follow Heaven’s Way to govern the dispositions of the people, omitting nothing in his reverent compliance. Heaven’s heart then daily moves above and below, to the sage’s left and right, likewise omitting nothing in its benevolent care. Thus, in making manifest Heaven’s favor and reverently attending to its anger, some pool their deliberations to devise plans; in bringing auspicious tokens to fulfillment and dispelling heavenly reproaches, some unite their strength to accomplish works. This is because they hold fast to a single virtue and seek the source within themselves. Thus [?], elucidating Heaven’s Way through inference and verification certainly belongs to what numerical regularities necessarily entail; yet clinging rigidly to these leads to an impasse. Serving Heaven’s Way by making virtue manifest is certainly what principle requires; yet insisting upon a guaranteed response runs counter to it. The mind through which the sage becomes one with Heaven—is this not what is meant by being without deliberation and without action?

If you, honored examiners, wish to investigate the subtleties of celestial configurations and numbers in order to observe Heaven’s Way, their details have been elaborated in successive generations from Gan and Shi onward. If you wish to examine the grounds for distinguishing seasonal indications in order to understand human affairs, rulers from Yao and Shun onward have cultivated this undertaking in succession. Allow me to conclude my discussion. The Way of Heaven and Earth is constant in displaying itself; the Way of the sun and moon is constant in its illumination; the movements of all under Heaven are grounded in constancy to the One. When the king accords with the virtue of Heaven and Earth and equals the radiance of the sun and moon, thereby taking his proper position above, the means by which he presides…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
宰羣動以歸大順者其極則天之極也孔
子曰為政以德辟如北辰居其所而衆星
共之言王者之成象於天也彼中宫之星
列於三垣者為紫微太微天市以象帝居
環以后王宰執百官御事各備其人列為
衛掖車肆權量貨貿各備其事則宅中之
位成矣二十八宿復以次分布於外東方
自角以下則為天闕為內庭為路寢為明
堂正位以及後宫之場皆奠其居北方自
===
斗以下則為褒賢為犧牲為布帛為祝禱
天府以至土功之事圖書之祕皆治其職
西方自奎而參則主武庫苑牧內帑外胡
以至天街邊陲三軍主帥之屬莫不秩然
而類聚也南方自井而軫則主水衡天目
厨宰服御以至珍寶樂府輔臣冢宰之司
莫不燦然而羣分也故曰官於中外常明
者百二十有四可名者百有二十為星二
千五百其微則萬有一千五百二十當萬
punctuated: 宰羣動以歸大順者，其極則天之極也。孔子曰：「為政以德，辟如北辰，居其所而衆星共之。」言王者之成象於天也。彼中宫之星，列於三垣者，為紫微、太微、天市，以象帝居。環以后王、宰執、百官、御事，各備其人；列為衛掖、車肆、權量、貨貿，各備其事，則宅中之位成矣。二十八宿復以次分布於外。東方自角以下，則為天闕、為內庭、為路寢、為明堂正位，以及後宫之場，皆奠其居。北方自斗以下，則為褒賢、為犧牲、為布帛、為祝禱、天府，以至土功之事、圖書之祕，皆治其職。西方自奎而參，則主武庫、苑牧、內帑、外胡，以至天街、邊陲、三軍主帥之屬，莫不秩然而類聚也。南方自井而軫，則主水衡、天目、厨宰、服御，以至珍寶、樂府、輔臣、冢宰之司，莫不燦然而羣分也。故曰：「官於中外常明者，百二十有四；可名者，百有二十；為星二千五百；其微則萬有一千五百二十，當萬
translation_en:
…to govern all movements and bring them into great concord: its ultimate standard is the ultimate standard of Heaven. Confucius said, “To govern through virtue is like the North Star: it remains in its place, and the other stars attend upon it.” This means that the king’s rule takes visible form in Heaven. The stars of the central palace, arrayed in the Three Enclosures—Ziwei, Taiwei, and Tianshi—represent the imperial residence. Around it stand rulers, chief councillors, the hundred officials, and those attending to affairs, with every personnel role represented. Arrayed as palace guards and flanking courts, carriage sheds, weights and measures, and commerce, they provide for every function. Thus the position of the ruler dwelling at the center is established.

The Twenty-eight Lunar Lodges are, in turn, distributed in sequence around the outside. In the east, beginning with Jiao, they represent the celestial gate towers, the inner court, the principal sleeping hall, and the central seat in the Hall of Light, extending to the precincts of the rear palace: all are established in their proper places. In the north, beginning with Dou, they represent the honoring of the worthy, sacrificial animals, cloth and silk, prayers, and the celestial treasury, extending to earthworks and the guarded stores of charts and writings: all discharge their respective functions. In the west, from Kui to Shen, they preside over the arsenal, parks and pastures, the inner treasury, and the Hu peoples beyond the realm, extending to the celestial avenue, the frontier, and the commanders of the three armies: all are arranged in order and gathered by kind. In the south, from Jing to Zhen, they preside over water administration, the celestial eye, cooks and stewards, and imperial clothing and equipment, extending to precious objects, the Music Bureau, assisting ministers, and the office of the chief minister: all are distinctly arrayed and divided into groups.

Hence it is said: “Of the celestial offices within and without, those that remain constantly visible number one hundred and twenty-four; those that can be named number one hundred and twenty. Together they comprise two thousand five hundred stars; counting the faint ones, there are eleven thousand five hundred and twenty, corresponding to the myriad …

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
物之數也十二辰之所指本非有星惟自
日月所經之躔推其廣狹之度而分舍以
配之則自軫至氐爲壽星至尾爲大火至
南斗爲析木至須女爲星紀至危爲玄枵
至奎爲娵訾至胃爲降婁至畢爲大梁至
井柳張軫爲實沈鶉首鶉火鶉尾之次則
周天之度已備故曰天之有度猶地之有
里也十二土之所配非有其方蓋欲觀象
者知七政之所行故卽列宿所分之度而
===
畫野以屬之則壽星居鄭而屬兖大火居
宋而屬豫析木居燕而屬幽星紀居吳越
而屬揚玄枵居齊而屬靑娵訾居衛而屬
幷降婁居魯而屬徐大梁居趙而屬冀實
沈居魏鶉首居秦鶉火居周鶉尾居楚而
益雍三河荆州之地以次列焉則十二壤
之域已辨辟之逆旅者不名其所至則無
以知其寄寓也夫象之所考旣有定稱而
星之所行又有常度故於居則曰次曰舍
punctuated: 物之數也。十二辰之所指，本非有星，惟自日月所經之躔，推其廣狹之度，而分舍以配之。則自軫至氐爲壽星，至尾爲大火，至南斗爲析木，至須女爲星紀，至危爲玄枵，至奎爲娵訾，至胃爲降婁，至畢爲大梁，至井、柳、張、軫爲實沈、鶉首、鶉火、鶉尾之次，則周天之度已備。故曰：「天之有度，猶地之有里也。」十二土之所配，非有其方，蓋欲觀象者知七政之所行，故卽列宿所分之度而畫野以屬之。則壽星居鄭而屬兖，大火居宋而屬豫，析木居燕而屬幽，星紀居吳越而屬揚，玄枵居齊而屬靑，娵訾居衛而屬幷，降婁居魯而屬徐，大梁居趙而屬冀，實沈居魏，鶉首居秦，鶉火居周，鶉尾居楚，而益、雍、三河、荆州之地以次列焉，則十二壤之域已辨。辟之逆旅者，不名其所至，則無以知其寄寓也。夫象之所考旣有定稱，而星之所行又有常度，故於居則曰次、曰舍
translation_en: …the number of the myriad things. The twelve celestial stations do not in themselves designate particular stars. Rather, the angular breadth of each is calculated along the path traversed by the sun and moon, and lodgings are apportioned to correspond to them. Thus, the stretch from Zhen to Di constitutes Shouxing; onward to Wei, Dahuo; to Nandou, Ximu; to Xunü, Xingji; to Wei (危), Xuanxiao; to Kui, Zouzi; to Wei (胃), Jianglou; and to Bi, Daliang. The successive stretches ending at Jing, Liu, Zhang, and Zhen constitute the stations Shichen, Chunshou, Chunhuo, and Chunwei. These complete the degrees of the celestial circuit. Hence the saying: “Heaven has degrees just as the earth has li.” The correspondences assigned to the twelve terrestrial divisions do not mean that those regions actually occupy those celestial directions. Their purpose is to enable observers of celestial phenomena to understand the movements of the Seven Regulators—the sun, moon, and five planets. Accordingly, terrestrial regions are demarcated and assigned to the degrees apportioned among the lunar lodges. Shouxing is situated over Zheng and belongs to Yanzhou; Dahuo over Song and belongs to Yuzhou; Ximu over Yan and belongs to Youzhou; Xingji over Wu and Yue and belongs to Yangzhou; Xuanxiao over Qi and belongs to Qingzhou; Zouzi over Wei and belongs to Bingzhou; Jianglou over Lu and belongs to Xuzhou; and Daliang over Zhao and belongs to Jizhou. Shichen is situated over Wei, Chunshou over Qin, Chunhuo over Zhou, and Chunwei over Chu; the territories of Yizhou, Yongzhou, the Three He regions, and Jingzhou are arrayed in that order. Thus the boundaries of the twelve terrestrial divisions are distinguished. This may be compared to a traveler lodging at inns: unless the places he reaches are named, there is no way to know where he is staying. Now, since the celestial configurations under examination have fixed designations, and the movements of the celestial bodies likewise have regular measures, their remaining in a place is termed “stationing” or “lodging”…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
曰留同舍曰合變離曰散經之曰歷相擊
曰鬭出而早上二三宿曰嬴出而晚下二
三宿曰縮自下而上曰陵自上而下曰乘
周匝曰繞東西曰鉤南北曰紀相陵曰食
光芒相射曰犯居其宿曰守守之而久曰
復曰還其消息盈虛之故所謂庶物繁動
各有繫命者也安得謂於人事物理漫不
相及也哉況王者受命於天而為天之子
動靜以道奉順陰陽仁義為理浹洽生類
===
薦禮百神宣懷獷俗嘉瑞珍美之祥紛委
狎至復致濬明端謹之士連茹引用然後
斡機於清穆熈績以凝命則七教敷聞於
下七政貞明於上其有不協玄符之幽贊
而發緯象之禎應也哉是以梓謹裨竈之
徒論述陰陽未為無當京房谷永之傳捃
撫規議亦所不譏若仲舒之敘春秋所謂
明禮義之大宗者也然其事引象以著跡
則謬而寡合卒取疑於當世劉向之明尚
punctuated:
曰留，同舍曰合，變離曰散，經之曰歷，相擊曰鬭，出而早、上二三宿曰嬴，出而晚、下二三宿曰縮，自下而上曰陵，自上而下曰乘，周匝曰繞，東西曰鉤，南北曰紀，相陵曰食，光芒相射曰犯，居其宿曰守，守之而久曰復、曰還。其消息盈虛之故，所謂庶物繁動，各有繫命者也。安得謂於人事物理漫不相及也哉？
況王者受命於天，而為天之子，動靜以道，奉順陰陽，仁義為理，浹洽生類，薦禮百神，宣懷獷俗，嘉瑞珍美之祥紛委狎至，復致濬明端謹之士，連茹引用，然後斡機於清穆，熈績以凝命，則七教敷聞於下，七政貞明於上。其有不協玄符之幽贊，而發緯象之禎應也哉？
是以梓謹、裨竈之徒論述陰陽，未為無當；京房、谷永之傳捃撫規議，亦所不譏。若仲舒之敘《春秋》，所謂明禮義之大宗者也。然其事引象以著跡，則謬而寡合，卒取疑於當世。劉向之明尚
translation_en:
…is called “remaining stationary.” Occupying the same lodge is called “conjunction”; changing position and separating is called “dispersion”; passing through is called “traversal”; striking one another is called “strife.” Emerging early and advancing two or three lodges is called “gain”; emerging late and falling back two or three lodges is called “contraction.” Moving from below upward is called “ascending”; moving from above downward is called “overriding.” Making a complete circuit is called “encircling”; east–west movement is called “hooking”; north–south movement is called “alignment.” One body overlapping another is called an “eclipse”; their rays striking one another is called “encroachment.” Remaining in a lodge is called “guarding”; guarding it for a long time is called “returning” or “coming back.” The causes of their waning and waxing, fullness and emptiness, are what is meant by the saying that, amid the manifold movements of all things, each has something upon which its allotted destiny depends. How could one claim that these have no connection at all with human affairs and the principles of things?
Moreover, the king receives his mandate from Heaven and becomes Heaven’s son. In movement and stillness he follows the Way, reverently accords with yin and yang, and governs through benevolence and righteousness, extending their influence throughout living creation. He presents ritual offerings to the hundred spirits and spreads his influence to win over peoples of fierce customs. Auspicious signs and precious, beautiful portents arrive in profusion and rapid succession. He further attracts men of profound understanding and upright, circumspect conduct, promoting and employing them in succession, like interconnected roots drawn up together. He then directs the workings of government in purity and reverence, bringing his achievements to fruition to secure the mandate. Thus the seven teachings spread and become known below, while the seven celestial regulators shine with constancy above. Could this fail to accord with the hidden assistance of Heaven’s mysterious tokens and bring forth auspicious responses among the planetary signs?
Thus the discussions of yin and yang by men such as Zi Jin [?] and Bi Zao were not without validity. The collected observations and admonitory discussions [?] transmitted by Jing Fang and Gu Yong likewise need not be censured. As for Zhongshu’s exposition of the Spring and Autumn Annals, it may be described as illuminating the great foundation of ritual propriety and righteousness. Yet when he invoked celestial signs to make the traces of events manifest, his accounts were mistaken and seldom corresponded with the facts; ultimately they aroused doubts among his contemporaries. As for Liu Xiang’s elucidation of the Book of Documents…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
書所謂繹六極之妙用者也然其言旁喻
以曲証則博而寡倫卒貽侮於聖言是皆
詳於推驗之故而不務民物之義何惑乎
其不足以達微而濟務哉所以然者天道
遠其示象固不若是之褻人道邇其推步
亦無所用其詳况求之治曆之初意則巳
諄乎此漢儒之所以爲失也昔者黄帝考
定星曆權輿五德之論高陽乃命司正繼
序三辰之規出納日月考中星以正四時
===
堯所以命羲和也而舜在玉璣以齊七政
無非簡其占測以習民聽耳測景中分察
候至以辨國災祥周禮所以命司徒也而
春秋謹始以大一統無非時其教令以警
有位耳初何嘗屑屑於象事以求應哉所
以然者君之治民時爲大時正則民事興
其自治以脩德爲上德脩則捄攘備况求
之紀載之職不有合乎此太史之所以必
兼也自漢以占候著述分爲二司則太史
punctuated: 書，所謂繹六極之妙用者也。然其言旁喻以曲証，則博而寡倫，卒貽侮於聖言。是皆詳於推驗之故，而不務民物之義，何惑乎其不足以達微而濟務哉？所以然者，天道遠，其示象固不若是之褻；人道邇，其推步亦無所用其詳。况求之治曆之初意，則巳諄乎此，漢儒之所以爲失也。昔者黄帝考定星曆，權輿五德之論；高陽乃命司正，繼序三辰之規。出納日月，考中星以正四時，堯所以命羲和也；而舜在玉璣以齊七政，無非簡其占測以習民聽耳。測景中，分察候至，以辨國災祥，周禮所以命司徒也；而春秋謹始以大一統，無非時其教令以警有位耳。初何嘗屑屑於象事以求應哉？所以然者，君之治民，時爲大，時正則民事興；其自治，以脩德爲上，德脩則捄攘備。况求之紀載之職，不有合乎此？太史之所以必兼也。自漢以占候、著述分爲二司，則太史
translation_en:
…Documents—what is called drawing out the subtle workings of the Six Extremes. Yet his statements employ indirect analogies to furnish strained proofs: extensive but lacking coherence, they ultimately bring the words of the sages into disrepute. All these writers examine the grounds for inference and verification in detail, yet neglect the principles governing people and things. Why be surprised that they cannot penetrate subtleties and accomplish practical affairs? The reason is that the Way of Heaven is distant: its manifestations of signs are certainly not so commonplace as this. The human way is near at hand, and such detailed astronomical calculation serves no purpose in it. Moreover, if we seek the original intention behind ordering the calendar, it already insists upon this point. Herein lay the error of the Han scholars.

In antiquity, Huangdi examined and established stellar observations and calendrical calculations, initiating the theory of the Five Powers. Gaoyang then appointed the responsible officials to carry forward the rules governing the sun, moon, and stars. Observing the rising and setting of the sun and moon and examining the culminating stars to set the four seasons correctly were the tasks for which Yao appointed Xi and He. Shun, in attending to the jade astronomical apparatus [?] to bring the Seven Regulators into alignment, likewise sought only to simplify prognostication and measurement so that the people would become familiar with what they were told. Measuring the central shadow and separately observing the arrival of seasonal signs [?], to distinguish calamities and auspicious signs for the state, were the tasks that the Rites of Zhou assigned to the Minister of Education. The Spring and Autumn Annals, by taking care over beginnings and exalting unified rule, likewise sought only to issue instructions and commands at the proper times and admonish those in office. When did these ever fuss over celestial signs and earthly events in search of correspondences?

The reason is that, in a ruler’s governance of the people, proper timing is paramount: when the seasons are correctly determined, the people’s undertakings flourish. In governing himself, cultivating virtue comes first: when virtue is cultivated, provisions for relief and averting calamity are complete. Moreover, if we examine the duties of keeping records, do they not accord with this? This is why the Grand Astrologer must combine these responsibilities. From the Han onward, prognostication and written compilation were divided between two offices; consequently, the Grand Astrologer…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
以令名而不復掌中祕矣再傳而以甘石
巫咸並列三家則星紀遂失其官而不復
達於民故矣其間惟司馬遷盡廢一十七
家之術而本乎星律以脩太初故晦朔弦
望始有其端而粗得乎敬授之意唐一行
盡變二十三家之法而本于蓍策以歸大
衍故章蔀紀元始合於易而不失乎謹始
之義此星數之理最爲獨得而非徒以占
候名者也然則人君者惟能宣節和氣輔
===
相物宜則先天弗違而盡性立命之化昭
矣人臣者惟能祇承上下寅恭協和則後
天時行而調元賛化之功備矣由是夭疾
不作衣食無奪君尊民悅而禮教行則百
姓和於下矣由是而五穀熟桑麻遂草木
茂鳥獸蕃則百物和於野矣其有不迪不
吉不庭不若之徒莫不應德而至又何憂
乎垂象之失軌而亦事於渾蓋以求合耶
其不然者雖合譽晨明終無補於祥符之
punctuated:
以令名，而不復掌中祕矣。再傳而以甘石、巫咸並列三家，則星紀遂失其官，而不復達於民故矣。其間惟司馬遷盡廢一十七家之術，而本乎星律以脩太初，故晦朔弦望始有其端，而粗得乎敬授之意。唐一行盡變二十三家之法，而本于蓍策以歸大衍，故章蔀紀元始合於易，而不失乎謹始之義。此星數之理最爲獨得，而非徒以占候名者也。
然則人君者，惟能宣節和氣，輔相物宜，則先天弗違，而盡性立命之化昭矣。人臣者，惟能祇承上下，寅恭協和，則後天時行，而調元賛化之功備矣。由是夭疾不作，衣食無奪，君尊民悅而禮教行，則百姓和於下矣。由是而五穀熟，桑麻遂，草木茂，鳥獸蕃，則百物和於野矣。其有不迪、不吉、不庭、不若之徒，莫不應德而至，又何憂乎垂象之失軌，而亦事於渾蓋以求合耶？其不然者，雖合譽晨明，終無補於祥符之
translation_en:
…bore the title Director, but no longer had charge of the palace’s confidential collections. With further transmission, Gan, Shi, and Wu Xian came to be ranked together as three schools; astronomical records consequently lost their official custodians and ceased to bear upon the affairs of the people. During this period, only Sima Qian discarded all the techniques of the seventeen schools and based his revision of the Taichu calendar on the regularities of the stars. Thus the last and first days of the lunar month, the quarter moons, and the full moon at last acquired a proper basis, broadly realizing the intention of reverently imparting the seasons to the people. Yi Xing of the Tang completely revised the methods of the twenty-three schools and took yarrow-stalk calculation as his basis, bringing them into accord with the Great Expansion. Thus the calendrical cycles—zhang, bu, ji, and yuan—at last accorded with the Book of Changes, preserving the principle of attending carefully to beginnings. These men attained an exceptionally distinctive understanding of the principles of astronomical calculation; their renown did not rest merely on divination and observation.
If, then, the ruler can circulate and regulate harmonious vital energies and assist all things in attaining their proper conditions, he will anticipate Heaven without contravening it, and the transforming influence of fully realizing one’s nature and establishing one’s destiny will become manifest. If ministers can reverently serve those above and below, working together with respectful vigilance, they will follow Heaven and act in season, fully accomplishing the work of harmonizing the primal forces and assisting transformation. Consequently, premature death and illness will not arise, and the people will not be deprived of clothing and food; the ruler will be honored, the people content, and ritual instruction practiced. Thus the common people below will live in harmony. Consequently, the five grains will ripen, mulberry and hemp thrive, plants and trees flourish, and birds and beasts multiply. Thus all things in the countryside will be in harmony. Even those who are wayward, inauspicious, unwilling to attend court, or disobedient will all respond to virtue and come. Why, then, worry that the signs displayed in Heaven might depart from their courses, or busy oneself with the spherical-heaven and canopy-heaven models in search of agreement?
If this is not so, then even if there is ‘concordant praise and morning brightness’ [?], it will ultimately contribute nothing to the governance of the Xiangfu era …

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
治南極歲見又孰裨乎紹聖之君蓋天有
休象而人無其事則休不足恃也至若太
白以晝見爲異而神爵之間以成漠南之
捷五星以合填爲難而伐吳之役以收渭
北之功則數有適然而人逢其會亦非其
德有以勝之也由此觀之則推驗之說可
以不攻而破矣然鄭夾漈之論至以五行
爲謬妄則失之矯而煕寧之論反以垂象
爲不足徵則失之誣故曰天垂象見吉凶
===
聖人象之言易數之原出於天也又曰觀
乎天文以察時變言易數之用前乎民也
又曰聖人以此洗心齋戒以神明其德言
易數之蘊具於心也王者謹於尊天慎於
養人而以脩復性命爲純心之要是以登
邁邃古光昭兩間巍乎紹天統物之盛者
也兢業抑畏之君莫可尚矣宋景一言而
善而熒曜退舍者三齊景一懼弗及而孛
之滅不淹旬若是乎天人之應雖中德且
punctuated:
治，南極歲見，又孰裨乎紹聖之君？蓋天有休象而人無其事，則休不足恃也。至若太白以晝見爲異，而神爵之間以成漠南之捷；五星以合填爲難，而伐吳之役以收渭北之功，則數有適然而人逢其會，亦非其德有以勝之也。由此觀之，則推驗之說可以不攻而破矣。然鄭夾漈之論至以五行爲謬妄，則失之矯；而煕寧之論反以垂象爲不足徵，則失之誣。故曰：「天垂象，見吉凶，聖人象之。」言易數之原出於天也。又曰：「觀乎天文，以察時變。」言易數之用前乎民也。又曰：「聖人以此洗心，齋戒以神明其德。」言易數之蘊具於心也。
王者謹於尊天，慎於養人，而以脩復性命爲純心之要，是以登邁邃古，光昭兩間，巍乎紹天統物之盛者也。兢業抑畏之君，莫可尚矣。宋景一言而善，而熒曜退舍者三；齊景一懼弗及，而孛之滅不淹旬。若是乎天人之應，雖中德且
translation_en:
…reign. And when the star of the southern pole appeared each year, what benefit did this bring the ruler of the Shaosheng era? When Heaven displays auspicious signs but human affairs do not accord with them, such auspiciousness cannot be relied upon. As for Venus, its appearance in daylight is considered anomalous, yet during the Shenjue era a victory south of the desert was achieved. A conjunction of the five planets with Saturn is considered calamitous [?], yet the campaign against Wu brought success north of the Wei River [?]. These were merely coincidences in celestial configurations that people happened to encounter; it was not that their virtue enabled them to overcome these signs. Viewed in this light, theories of prediction and verification collapse without even being attacked. Yet Zheng Jiaji, in his argument, went so far as to call the Five Phases absurd falsehoods, thus erring through overcorrection; and the argument advanced during the Xining era, conversely, held that celestial signs were insufficient as evidence, thus erring through misrepresentation. Hence the Book of Changes says: “Heaven displays signs, manifesting good and ill fortune; the sage takes them as models.” This means that the numerical patterns of the Changes originate in Heaven. It also says: “Observe the patterns of Heaven to discern the changes of the seasons.” This means that the application of the numerical patterns of the Changes serves to guide the people in advance. It further says: “With this the sage cleanses his heart, purifies himself, and observes abstinence, thereby making his virtue spiritually luminous.” This means that the inner substance of the numerical patterns of the Changes is present within the heart.
The true king is scrupulous in revering Heaven and attentive in nourishing the people. He makes the cultivation and restoration of his nature and destiny the essential means of purifying his heart. Thus he rises above remote antiquity and shines between Heaven and Earth: how lofty is his greatness in succeeding to Heaven’s charge and governing all things! Nothing can surpass a ruler who is vigilant, conscientious, humble, and reverent. Duke Jing of Song uttered a single good word, and Mars [?] retreated three celestial lodges; Duke Jing of Qi feared that he had fallen short, and the comet vanished within ten days. Such is the responsiveness between Heaven and humanity that even one of middling virtue could…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
克享之況於上聖之君以天之心爲心則
天命其永保之眞如父母之於子矣詩曰
君子至止福祿旣同君子萬年保其家邦
此之謂也
第四問
同考試官教諭蔣批張封
我
朝設科明經取士最爲得人近時以文待舉者習趨於敝子獨有志於古
而力挽之非有卓越之識不能也取之以楚多士
===
考試官教諭管批文與道二非文也子獨求
文於道復古還醇有賴矣
考試官教諭李批文有關於世教此作得之
錄以式文之不合于道者
聖賢之學純心之學也惟心有眞見而後
文敷乎自然之章聖賢之文造道之文也
惟道有眞得而後文顯乎經世之用是故
三代無文人非無文人也文與道一不求
文而文自生焉故也六經無文法非無文
punctuated:
克享之，況於上聖之君，以天之心爲心，則天命其永保之，眞如父母之於子矣。《詩》曰：「君子至止，福祿旣同。君子萬年，保其家邦。」此之謂也。

第四問

同考試官教諭蔣批，張封：我朝設科，明經取士，最爲得人。近時以文待舉者，習趨於敝。子獨有志於古而力挽之，非有卓越之識不能也。取之以楚多士。

考試官教諭管批：文與道二，非文也。子獨求文於道，復古還醇有賴矣。

考試官教諭李批：文有關於世教，此作得之。錄以式文之不合于道者。

聖賢之學，純心之學也。惟心有眞見，而後文敷乎自然之章。聖賢之文，造道之文也。惟道有眞得，而後文顯乎經世之用。是故三代無文人，非無文人也，文與道一，不求文而文自生焉故也。六經無文法，非無文
translation_en:
…could enjoy it. How much more, then, could a supremely sagely ruler who takes Heaven’s heart as his own! Heaven’s mandate will surely protect him forever, just as parents protect their child. The Book of Odes says: “The noble lord has arrived; blessings and emoluments gather together. May the noble lord live ten thousand years and preserve his house and state.” This is what it means.

Fourth Question

Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang 蔣, Instructor; Zhang Feng 張封:
Our dynasty established examinations to select men through mastery of the Classics and has been most successful in obtaining worthy men. Recently, those awaiting selection on the strength of their writing have fallen into corrupt habits. You alone aspire to antiquity and strive to reverse this trend. Without exceptional discernment, this would be impossible. I select this piece to admonish [?] the assembled scholars.

Comment by Examiner Guan 管, Instructor:
When writing and the Way are divided, it is not true writing. You alone seek writing in the Way. Upon you we may rely to restore antiquity and return to purity.

Comment by Examiner Li 李, Instructor:
Writing bears upon the moral instruction of the age. This composition grasps that principle. It is included to serve as a model for those whose writing does not accord with the Way.

The learning of sages and worthies is the learning of purifying the heart. Only when the heart possesses genuine insight can writing unfold in patterns that arise naturally. The writing of sages and worthies is writing that attains the Way. Only when one truly apprehends the Way can writing manifest its usefulness in ordering the world. Thus, the Three Dynasties had no men of letters—not because there were no such men, but because writing and the Way were one: without seeking literary accomplishment, writing arose of itself. The Six Classics have no rules of composition—not because they lack literary…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
法也道與心一不求法而法自備焉故也
使心未純乎道斯道弗宣乎文于是心學
晦而精義微枝葉繁而真純喪訓詁組繪
敷陳綴拾言之詳者道益離焉而于聖人
自然之章始日相違而不自覺故曰聖人
文章自然自然云者精神元氣之所會得
之心寓之文而用之以經世天機所發天
章渙焉不自知也夫文至于不自知而後
本心自然之天始見是聖賢之文而非後
===
世之文也執事方以文取士而以文策之
蓋望諸生以見道之文甚盛心也愚則以
爲天地之心不能以自祕也以時而會乎
聖人之心聖人于天地之心不能以徒會
也于是以經而會乎天地之心惟有經以
會天地之心則不惟天地得其所以爲心
聖人亦于是有所憑籍以無負天地之心
而因之立言明道以開來學于天下而與
斯道相尋于無窮是故以道法勝則爲六
punctuated:
法也，道與心一，不求法而法自備焉故也。使心未純乎道，斯道弗宣乎文，于是心學晦而精義微，枝葉繁而真純喪。訓詁、組繪、敷陳、綴拾，言之詳者，道益離焉，而于聖人自然之章，始日相違而不自覺。故曰：「聖人文章自然。」自然云者，精神元氣之所會，得之心，寓之文，而用之以經世。天機所發，天章渙焉，不自知也。夫文至于不自知，而後本心自然之天始見，是聖賢之文，而非後世之文也。

執事方以文取士，而以文策之，蓋望諸生以見道之文，甚盛心也。愚則以爲天地之心不能以自祕也，以時而會乎聖人之心；聖人于天地之心不能以徒會也，于是以經而會乎天地之心。惟有經以會天地之心，則不惟天地得其所以爲心，聖人亦于是有所憑籍，以無負天地之心，而因之立言明道，以開來學于天下，而與斯道相尋于無窮。是故以道法勝，則爲六
translation_en:
…rules of composition; rather, it is because the Way and the heart are one: without seeking rules, the rules are naturally complete. If the heart has not become wholly attuned to the Way, the Way cannot find expression in writing. Then the learning of the heart grows obscure and subtle meanings fade; branches and leaves proliferate, while truth and purity are lost. Through textual glosses, ornate embellishment, elaborate exposition, and collected scraps, the more detailed the words become, the further they depart from the Way. Day by day they diverge from the sages’ natural compositions, without their authors even realizing it. Thus it is said: “The sages’ writing is natural.” What is called “natural” is where spiritual vitality and primal energy converge: apprehended in the heart, embodied in writing, and employed to bring order to the world. As Heaven’s spontaneous workings unfold, Heaven’s patterns shine forth, without conscious awareness. Only when writing reaches this state of unselfconsciousness does the innate, natural Heaven of the original heart become manifest. This is the writing of sages and worthies, not that of later ages.

You, honored examiners, are now selecting men through their writing and testing them with a policy question about writing. You evidently hope that the candidates will produce writing that reveals the Way—a most generous intention. In my humble view, the heart of Heaven and Earth cannot remain concealed: at the proper time it meets with the heart of the sage. Nor can the sage merely encounter the heart of Heaven and Earth and leave it at that; he therefore meets with it through the classics. Only with classics through which to encounter the heart of Heaven and Earth can Heaven and Earth fully realize what constitutes their heart, while the sage also gains something to rely upon so as not to fail that heart. On this basis he establishes teachings and illuminates the Way, opening learning to future generations throughout the world, so that they may follow this Way without end. Thus, when the Way and its principles predominate, the result is the Six…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
經以事詞勝則爲紀載由伏羲以至堯舜
周孔其心同也其道同也自時厥後七十
子喪而微言絕異端起而大義漓一降而
春秋再降而戰國浸淫于秦漢以極于六
朝五季雖曰先秦西漢其尤也唐文三變
其盛也而不知學無得于心則文弗載乎
道輪轅飾而人弗庸殆虛車也而又奚尚
乎論者猶謂秦漢以前渾然殆非知文者
矣是故國語精而弱柳宗元非之以明異
===
左氏辨而富韓愈氏卑之以明浮戰國策
利而巧朱子以縱横闔闢而示譏是先秦
之文也而非三代之文也過秦有論治安
有策賈誼可謂通達國體矣而三表五餌
班固病其失之疎上林子虛諸作司馬相
如可謂詭練奇偉矣而諷一勸百班固病
其失之靡三篇獨對賢良稱首董仲舒正
誼明道之學也而柔行巽入縱陰閉陽朱
子病其失之雜是西漢之文也而非三代
punctuated: 經，以事詞勝則爲紀載。由伏羲以至堯舜、周孔，其心同也，其道同也。自時厥後，七十子喪而微言絕，異端起而大義漓。一降而春秋，再降而戰國，浸淫于秦漢，以極于六朝五季。雖曰先秦西漢其尤也，唐文三變其盛也，而不知學無得于心，則文弗載乎道。輪轅飾而人弗庸，殆虛車也，而又奚尚乎？論者猶謂秦漢以前渾然，殆非知文者矣。是故《國語》精而弱，柳宗元非之以明異；左氏辨而富，韓愈氏卑之以明浮；《戰國策》利而巧，朱子以縱横闔闢而示譏。是先秦之文也，而非三代之文也。《過秦》有論，《治安》有策，賈誼可謂通達國體矣，而三表五餌，班固病其失之疎；《上林》《子虛》諸作，司馬相如可謂詭練奇偉矣，而諷一勸百，班固病其失之靡；三篇獨對，賢良稱首，董仲舒正誼明道之學也，而柔行巽入，縱陰閉陽，朱子病其失之雜。是西漢之文也，而非三代
translation_en:
…Classics; when accounts of events and literary expression predominate, they become historical records. From Fu Xi through Yao and Shun to the Duke of Zhou and Confucius, their minds were the same, and their Way was the same. Thereafter, the seventy disciples died and the subtle teachings ceased; heterodox doctrines arose and the great principles became diluted. One decline brought the Spring and Autumn period, another the Warring States; the deterioration spread through the Qin and Han and reached its extreme in the Six Dynasties and Five Dynasties. Although the writings of the pre-Qin and Western Han periods are called outstanding, and Tang literature in its three transformations is called flourishing, people fail to understand that, unless learning brings inward understanding, writing cannot convey the Way. If the wheels and shafts are ornamented but no one uses the carriage, it is merely an empty carriage. What, then, is there to esteem? Critics still claim that writing before the Qin and Han possessed an integral wholeness; surely they do not understand literature.
Thus, the Discourses of the States is refined but weak: Liu Zongyuan criticized it to expose its deviations. Zuo’s Commentary is discriminating and abundant: Han Yu disparaged it to expose its superficiality. The Stratagems of the Warring States is incisive and ingenious: Master Zhu criticized its manipulative shifts and maneuvers. These are writings of the pre-Qin period, but not writings of the Three Dynasties.
With his discourse On the Faults of Qin and his policy essay On Good Government and Security, Jia Yi may be said to have understood the essentials of statecraft; yet Ban Gu faulted his proposals for the “three demonstrations and five baits” as ill-considered. In such works as Shanglin Park and Sir Vacuous, Sima Xiangru may be said to have achieved ingenious refinement and extraordinary grandeur; yet, for every one part of admonition there were a hundred parts encouraging excess, and Ban Gu faulted their extravagance. With his three individual responses, Dong Zhongshu ranked foremost among the candidates recommended as Worthy and Good, and his learning concerned rectifying moral rightness and elucidating the Way; yet Master Zhu faulted its admixture of other doctrines, citing “acting pliantly and entering compliantly, releasing yin and shutting off yang” [?]. These are writings of the Western Han, but not of the Three Dynasties…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之文也阿房宮賦杜牧傑作也而抑置第
五以賦調之失格顏子克巳昌黎佳論也
而四試遭黜以原道之遺本他如劉蕡以
詞直下第楊億以西崐見遺李迪以落韻
誤收蘇軾以刑賞雄論知名張九成以讜
言不阿拔置第一夫固因時尚以敷言判
心迹而立論或能因文以見道而不能即
道以明心是又唐宋之文也而非三代之
文也大抵三代以上道學本于一心而斯
===
文有實用三代以下心學分于口耳而著
作徼虛名此心無古今之殊而文有古今
之別司世道者不能不為之凝神澄省思
一亟反之也洪惟我
朝設科取士明經得人文教弘敷涵育培養
二百年來至治精華昭融萬國鞭蒲緝柳
之士罔不閉關玄覽統一聖真凡其嗽芳
潤摛清藻以鳴
國家之盛者亶可以挾風雷煥星斗遐軋漢
punctuated:
之文也。《阿房宮賦》，杜牧傑作也，而抑置第五，以賦調之失格。《顏子克巳》，昌黎佳論也，而四試遭黜，以《原道》之遺本。他如劉蕡以詞直下第，楊億以西崐見遺，李迪以落韻誤收，蘇軾以《刑賞》雄論知名，張九成以讜言不阿拔置第一。夫固因時尚以敷言，判心迹而立論，或能因文以見道，而不能即道以明心，是又唐宋之文也，而非三代之文也。大抵三代以上，道學本于一心，而斯文有實用；三代以下，心學分于口耳，而著作徼虛名。此心無古今之殊，而文有古今之別，司世道者不能不為之凝神澄省，思一亟反之也。
洪惟我朝設科取士，明經得人，文教弘敷，涵育培養二百年來，至治精華昭融萬國。鞭蒲緝柳之士，罔不閉關玄覽，統一聖真。凡其嗽芳潤、摛清藻，以鳴國家之盛者，亶可以挾風雷、煥星斗，遐軋漢
translation_en:
…the writing of the Three Dynasties. The Rhapsody on the Efang Palace was Du Mu’s masterpiece, yet it was relegated to fifth place because its rhapsodic manner departed from the prescribed form. Yan Hui’s Mastery of the Self was an excellent discourse by Han Yu of Changli, yet he was rejected in four examinations because his Inquiry into the Way neglected the fundamental [?]. Other examples include Liu Fen, who failed because his language was forthright; Yang Yi, who was passed over because of his Xikun style; and Li Di, who was mistakenly accepted despite a lapse in rhyme. Su Shi won renown through his powerful discourse on punishments and rewards, while Zhang Jiucheng was selected for first place for his upright, uncompromising words. These writers framed their language according to the fashions of their times and constructed their arguments by distinguishing inward intentions from outward conduct. Some could perceive the Way through writing, but could not illuminate the mind through the Way itself. This, again, was the writing of the Tang and Song, rather than that of the Three Dynasties. Broadly speaking, during the Three Dynasties and earlier, learning of the Way was rooted in the undivided mind, and writing had practical use. After the Three Dynasties, learning of the mind became fragmented into what was merely spoken and heard, and literary composition sought empty fame. The mind itself does not differ between antiquity and the present, yet writing does. Those responsible for the moral order of the age cannot but concentrate their spirits and reflect with clarity upon this, seeking urgently to restore it.
We reverently consider how our dynasty established examinations to select scholars and secured worthy men through their understanding of the Classics. Literary and moral education has spread widely, nurturing and cultivating them for two hundred years. The finest achievements of consummate government shine resplendently throughout the myriad lands. Scholars who study with rush leaves and woven willow slips [?] all withdraw behind closed doors for profound contemplation, bringing themselves into unity with the truth of the sages. Those who savor fragrant richness and unfold pure literary ornament to proclaim the flourishing of the state can assuredly harness wind and thunder and make the stars and constellations blaze, surpassing even the distant Han…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
周邇陵晉魏駸駸焉三代竝隆粹乎無以
議爲也而識者尤懼其學蕪則氣漓文卑
則習敝似當反今而復之古者顧愚生章
句何足與論文耶而蠡見管識竊以爲欲
敦文體在正道術欲端士習在崇恬靜而
二者又繫乎重師儒而已夫天章雲漢一
本自然而聖賢敷文要于中正惟夫虚寂
名家騷詞麗則而后文穿天心句攻月脇
者始漸染失真焉蓋背經離本踵謬煽訛
===
大道以多岐亡羊末學以多方喪性而不
知文不法六經雖古猶今也道不師聖賢
雖是猶非也是故莫要乎正道術夫士習
之壞率由徇名而失實實之不孚而名是
徇此所以趨逐聲華汨沒途徑相率競進
而鮮恬退之風耳昔伊呂王佐望也方耕
莘釣濱若將終身及一出而被澤堯舜會
朝清明弼成商周之業者其養素豫也先
正謂靜退之士内有養見善明用心剛者
punctuated:
周，邇陵晉魏，駸駸焉三代竝隆，粹乎無以議爲也。而識者尤懼其學蕪則氣漓，文卑則習敝，似當反今而復之古者。顧愚生章句，何足與論文耶？而蠡見管識，竊以爲欲敦文體，在正道術；欲端士習，在崇恬靜；而二者又繫乎重師儒而已。
夫天章雲漢，一本自然，而聖賢敷文，要于中正。惟夫虚寂名家，騷詞麗則，而后文穿天心、句攻月脇者，始漸染失真焉。蓋背經離本，踵謬煽訛，大道以多岐亡羊，末學以多方喪性，而不知文不法六經，雖古猶今也；道不師聖賢，雖是猶非也。是故莫要乎正道術。
夫士習之壞，率由徇名而失實。實之不孚，而名是徇，此所以趨逐聲華，汨沒途徑，相率競進，而鮮恬退之風耳。昔伊呂，王佐望也，方耕莘、釣濱，若將終身；及一出，而被澤堯舜，會朝清明，弼成商周之業者，其養素豫也。先正謂：「靜退之士，内有養、見善明、用心剛者，
translation_en:
…and Zhou in the distant past, and surpassing Jin and Wei in the nearer past, steadily approaching the flourishing achievement of the Three Dynasties—so pure that there seems nothing to criticize. Yet discerning men are especially concerned that, when learning becomes overgrown with weeds, its vital force grows thin, and when writing becomes debased, scholarly habits deteriorate. It would seem necessary to turn away from the present and return to antiquity. But I, a foolish scholar occupied with textual phrases, am hardly qualified to discuss literature. Nevertheless, with my narrow vision and limited understanding, I venture to think that strengthening literary standards requires rectifying the teachings of the Way; correcting scholars’ habits requires honoring tranquility and composure; and both depend upon esteeming teachers and Confucian scholars.
The patterned heavens and the Milky Way have their sole foundation in nature; when sages and worthies give expression to writing, their essential principle is centrality and correctness. Only with those who made their reputations through emptiness and quiescence [?], and with the ornate yet exemplary poetry of the Songs of Chu, did there subsequently arise writers whose compositions pierced heaven’s heart and whose lines assailed the moon’s flank. Through their influence, writing gradually lost its authenticity. Turning their backs on the classics and abandoning the foundations, they perpetuated errors and spread falsehoods. On the great road, branching paths cause sheep to be lost; in derivative learning, proliferating methods cause people to lose their true nature. They fail to understand that writing which does not take the Six Classics as its model, though ancient, is no better than modern writing; and that a Way which does not take the sages and worthies as its teachers, though apparently right, is still wrong. Thus nothing is more essential than rectifying the teachings of the Way.
The deterioration of scholars’ habits generally results from pursuing reputation at the expense of substance. When substance does not bear out reputation, yet reputation alone is pursued, men chase prestige, become submerged in paths of advancement, and lead one another in competing to rise. Hence the scarcity of a disposition toward tranquility and withdrawal. In former times, Yi Yin and Lü Shang were men of the stature to assist kings. While one plowed at Shen and the other fished by the riverbank, they seemed prepared to spend their entire lives thus. Yet once they emerged, they spread blessings like those of Yao and Shun [?], brought clarity and order to the assembled court, and assisted in establishing the achievements of Shang and Zhou. This was because they had cultivated their unadorned integrity beforehand. A former worthy said: “Scholars who remain quiet and withdrawn, who possess inner cultivation, perceive goodness clearly, and are steadfast in purpose…”

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
以類立朝必有可觀旨哉斯言信夫致身
體國以成天下之治謂不在於恬退士乎
故曰莫要於崇恬靜夫梓哉爲童子之命
而師資係風敎之原昔陽城任國子而士
多興孝歐陽脩知貢舉而習變浮靡分齋
理事窮經致用馳聲秀彥者又安定蘇湖
之敎也使今之槐市皆芝蘭則今之桂籍
皆瓊樹春風一坐而月落萬川蓋洪鍾叩
鳴揚音響應雖不疾而自速也故大司徒
===
以本俗六安萬民四曰聯師儒誠以風化
所關者甚大也是故尤莫要於重師儒夫
重師儒以範其趨則斯文之元命立矣崇
恬靜以勵其節則斯文之元精固矣正道
術以約其旨則斯文之元氣達矣由是本
之學庸語孟以定其歸本之六經以大其
觀參之榖左以勵其氣參之太史以著其
潔時乎章紀而維風鳴道而論學也則出
師表之效忠也陳情表之至孝也元公之
punctuated:
以類立朝，必有可觀。」旨哉斯言！信夫，致身體國，以成天下之治，謂不在於恬退士乎？故曰：「莫要於崇恬靜。」夫梓哉爲童子之命，而師資係風敎之原。昔陽城任國子，而士多興孝；歐陽脩知貢舉，而習變浮靡。分齋理事，窮經致用，馳聲秀彥者，又安定蘇湖之敎也。使今之槐市皆芝蘭，則今之桂籍皆瓊樹。春風一坐，而月落萬川，蓋洪鍾叩鳴，揚音響應，雖不疾而自速也。故大司徒以本俗六安萬民，四曰：「聯師儒。」誠以風化所關者甚大也。是故尤莫要於重師儒。
夫重師儒以範其趨，則斯文之元命立矣；崇恬靜以勵其節，則斯文之元精固矣；正道術以約其旨，則斯文之元氣達矣。由是本之《學》《庸》《語》《孟》，以定其歸；本之六經，以大其觀；參之《榖》《左》，以勵其氣；參之太史，以著其潔。時乎章紀，而維風鳴道而論學也，則《出師表》之效忠也，《陳情表》之至孝也，元公之
translation_en:
…when they stand together at court with others of their kind, they will surely have something worthy to show.” How profound these words are! Indeed, can dedicating oneself to service and taking the state's concerns as one's own, so as to bring order to all under Heaven, be said not to depend upon scholars who are tranquil and retiring? Thus I say: “Nothing is more essential than honoring tranquility.” Now, “timber” determines a child's destiny [?], and teachers are the source of moral influence and instruction. Formerly, when Yang Cheng served as Director of Education, many scholars were inspired to filial conduct; when Ouyang Xiu presided over the examinations, prevailing habits of superficial ornament changed. Dividing students into teaching halls, attending to practical affairs, thoroughly investigating the classics and putting learning to use, and winning renown through outstanding scholars—these, too, characterized the teaching of Hu Yuan, known as Anding, at Suzhou and Huzhou. If all those in today's schools were fragrant angelica and orchids, then all those on today's examination rolls would be trees of precious jade. One sitting in the spring breeze of a teacher's presence brings the moon's reflection to ten thousand streams. It is like striking a great bell: it rings out, and echoes answer its sound. Though there is no haste, the effect is swift of itself. Thus, among the six means by which the Minister of Education secured the people's well-being through local customs, the fourth was: “Bring teachers and scholars into association.” This was truly because their influence upon moral transformation was so great. Hence, above all, nothing is more essential than esteeming teachers and scholars.
By esteeming teachers and scholars to guide their pursuits, the fundamental life of this literary and moral tradition is established. By honoring tranquility to strengthen their integrity, its essential vitality is secured. By rectifying the Way and its methods to discipline their aims, its primal energy flows freely. Accordingly, ground their work in the Great Learning, the Doctrine of the Mean, the Analects, and the Mencius to determine its direction; ground it in the Six Classics to broaden its vision; draw also upon the Guliang Commentary and the Zuo Commentary to invigorate its force, and upon the Grand Historian to manifest its purity. In writings suited to their times [?], they sustain moral influence, give voice to the Way, and discuss learning. Thus there is the devoted loyalty of the Memorial on Taking the Field, the utmost filial devotion of the Memorial Expressing My Feelings, and Duke Yuan's …

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
太極也程氏之易傳也張子之西銘也安
國之序書也以至蔚然而龍翔鳳舞也燦
然而玉珮瓊琚也悠然沛然而大羹玄酒
也長江大河也不事雕琢有心以擬之而
篤實光輝閎中肆外根茂者枝達膏沃者
光燁殆自然而成章者乎所以植天地之
紀宣民物之秘達古今之變竝軼乎三代
之文而真才輩出世道攸賴矣易曰觀乎
天文以察時變觀乎人文以化成天下此
===
聖人用賁之道也愚也竊有望焉
第五問
蔡栢齡
同考試官教諭周批欈李吳興之地一遇水溢
輒不得其疏洩之術是作歷稽往牒參酌時宜真得古
人治水之要經世之略于此覘之竒士竒士
考試官教諭管批浙西近多水患當事者所
隱憂也求其鑿鑿可行以為拯溺之助無踰是篇錄之
考試官教諭李批治水能知源委識時務之
punctuated:
太極也，程氏之易傳也，張子之西銘也，安國之序書也，以至蔚然而龍翔鳳舞也，燦然而玉珮瓊琚也，悠然沛然而大羹玄酒也，長江大河也。不事雕琢，有心以擬之，而篤實光輝，閎中肆外，根茂者枝達，膏沃者光燁，殆自然而成章者乎？所以植天地之紀，宣民物之秘，達古今之變，竝軼乎三代之文，而真才輩出，世道攸賴矣。《易》曰：「觀乎天文，以察時變；觀乎人文，以化成天下。」此聖人用賁之道也，愚也竊有望焉。
第五問
蔡栢齡
同考試官教諭周批：欈李、吳興之地，一遇水溢，輒不得其疏洩之術。是作歷稽往牒，參酌時宜，真得古人治水之要。經世之略，于此覘之。竒士！竒士！
考試官教諭管批：浙西近多水患，當事者所隱憂也。求其鑿鑿可行，以為拯溺之助，無踰是篇，錄之。
考試官教諭李批：治水能知源委，識時務之
translation_en:
…the Supreme Ultimate; Master Cheng’s Commentary on the Changes; Master Zhang’s Western Inscription; and Anguo’s preface to the Documents. Their writing may flourish like soaring dragons and dancing phoenixes, gleam like jade pendants and precious ornaments, or flow serenely and abundantly, with the simplicity of unseasoned broth and plain water offered in sacrifice, and the grandeur of the Yangzi and Yellow Rivers. Without resorting to elaborate embellishment, yet consciously seeking to emulate these models [?], it is substantial and radiant, expansive within and freely expressed without. Luxuriant roots produce spreading branches; rich oil produces a brilliant flame. Is this not literary pattern arising naturally? Such writing establishes the ordering principles of Heaven and Earth, reveals the hidden workings of people and things, and comprehends changes through past and present. It stands alongside and surpasses the writings of the Three Dynasties, while genuine talents emerge in succession, sustaining the moral order of the world. The Changes says: “Observe the patterns of Heaven to discern changes in the seasons; observe human patterns to transform and perfect the world.” This is the sages’ way of applying Adornment, the hexagram Bi. I humbly cherish hopes for this.
Fifth Policy Question
Cai Boling
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor: Whenever flooding occurs in Zuili [?] and Wuxing, no adequate means of draining the water can be found. This essay thoroughly examines earlier records and weighs what is appropriate to present circumstances, truly grasping the essentials of the ancients’ methods of water control. Here one can discern the author’s capacity for statecraft. An exceptional scholar! An exceptional scholar!
Comment by Examiner Guan, Instructor: Western Zhejiang has recently suffered frequent floods, a source of private anxiety to the officials responsible. For proposals that are demonstrably practicable and can help rescue those threatened by drowning, nothing surpasses this essay. Include it in the record.
