punctuated: 矣。此彖傳所以極言之也。蓋曰：物理之在天下，至渙者固其散殊之迹，至一者則其統會之真。萃以聚爲義，卦辭固已彰其蘊矣，然其道甚大，而所以體其撰者未也。由是仰觀俯察，凡充塞于兩間者，無弗考焉。其理至賾，而所以類其情者未也。由是遠求近取，凡紛紜于宇宙者，無弗究焉。此蓋由至約以該至博，而欲達觀以悉其變；卽至一以求不一，而欲推類以盡其餘。其情豈不可見乎？是故法象莫大乎天地，其卑高之位雖判矣，然下濟上行，絪縕之氣自交密而無間。並育莫衆於萬物，其形色之賦雖殊矣，然氣求聲應，二五之精自妙合而不離。兩其化也，而一實神之，固造化之所以不匱也。是豈强之使合哉？蓋氣機默運，有以生之，必有以成之，雖天地不能外是以爲情矣。以羣分也，而以類聚之，固品彙之所以咸亨也。亦豈瀆之使聚哉？蓋物理潛孚，有以倡之，必有以和之，雖萬物不能外是以爲情矣。吁！天地萬物且然，萃之道其誠大
translation_en:
…This is why the Commentary on the Judgments expounds it so fully. Its meaning is this: among the principles of things throughout the world, utter dispersal is indeed the outward trace of their separation and differentiation, while ultimate unity is the underlying reality of their convergence. Cui, Gathering, takes gathering as its meaning. The hexagram statement has already disclosed what it contains; yet its Way is exceedingly great, and how to comprehend its workings has not yet been shown. Thus one looks upward and examines downward, investigating everything that fills the space between Heaven and Earth. Its principles are exceedingly subtle and complex, and how to classify its actual dispositions has not yet been shown. Thus one seeks afar and draws examples from nearby, exploring everything in the teeming universe. This is to encompass the utmost breadth by proceeding from the utmost simplicity, seeking a comprehensive view that grasps all its transformations; to seek multiplicity in ultimate unity, extending analogies so as to exhaust all that remains. Can its actual dispositions not thereby be seen?

Thus, among models and images, none are greater than Heaven and Earth. Although their positions, low and high, are distinct, one descends to aid and the other ascends; their intermingling vital energies naturally interact closely, without any gap. Among things nourished together, none are more numerous than the myriad things. Although the forms and colors allotted to them differ, like energies seek one another and like sounds respond; the essences of the two forces and the five phases naturally unite wondrously and do not separate. Their transformations are twofold, yet unity truly makes them numinous: this is precisely why the work of creation is inexhaustible. Could this be a matter of forcing them to unite? The workings of vital energy move silently: whatever brings them into being must also bring them to completion. Even Heaven and Earth cannot have their dispositions outside this principle.

Things divide into groups yet gather according to kind: this is precisely why all categories of beings flourish. Could this, too, be a matter of indiscriminately making them gather [?]? The principles of things accord unseen: wherever something initiates, something must respond in harmony. Even the myriad things cannot have their dispositions outside this principle. Ah! Since even Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things are thus, the Way of Gathering is truly great…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
循分以効忠者固其莫逃之義因遇而知奮者
乃其必致之情吾今有感于遇主之盛而不容
已於情也乃歌之曰元首明哉股肱良哉誠以
大君居首出之位以立極其尊如元首也羣臣
任代工之責以從王其分如股肱也爲之元首
者本濬哲之光而聰明是憲獨觀乎化理之原
體文明之懿而視聽惟公疏通乎民物之賾以
之興事則統率之要自我執之清明在躬而所
以示臨御之有赫者何宣朗也以之考成則簡
===
別之公自我精之大觀在上而所以著明哲之
作則者何昭灼也有君如此而人臣將何以自
獻也哉將見爲之股肱者情孚於一體之交而
懷忠良以敬應用輸其弼亮之志義屬於相資
之重而聯官常以祗若各効其精白之忱慶明
王之率作而及時以趨事者不容巳焉左右維
持以大溥其昭明之化而敢上負于天子也哉
仰聖主之考成而奉法以脩職者不容緩焉翼
輔賛襄以共成其精明之治而敢自負乎明時
punctuated:
循分以効忠者，固其莫逃之義；因遇而知奮者，乃其必致之情。吾今有感于遇主之盛，而不容已於情也，乃歌之曰：「元首明哉，股肱良哉！」誠以大君居首出之位以立極，其尊如元首也；羣臣任代工之責以從王，其分如股肱也。爲之元首者，本濬哲之光而聰明是憲，獨觀乎化理之原；體文明之懿而視聽惟公，疏通乎民物之賾。以之興事，則統率之要自我執之，清明在躬，而所以示臨御之有赫者何宣朗也！以之考成，則簡別之公自我精之，大觀在上，而所以著明哲之作則者何昭灼也！

有君如此，而人臣將何以自獻也哉？將見爲之股肱者，情孚於一體之交，而懷忠良以敬應，用輸其弼亮之志；義屬於相資之重，而聯官常以祗若，各効其精白之忱。慶明王之率作，而及時以趨事者不容巳焉，左右維持，以大溥其昭明之化，而敢上負于天子也哉？仰聖主之考成，而奉法以脩職者不容緩焉，翼輔賛襄，以共成其精明之治，而敢自負乎明時
translation_en:
…To fulfill one’s allotted duties with loyalty is indeed an obligation one cannot escape; to be stirred to exertion by the favor one has received is a feeling that must find full expression. Now, moved by the greatness of my good fortune in encountering such a sovereign, I cannot contain my feelings, and so I sing: “How enlightened the head! How worthy the arms and legs!” Indeed, the great ruler occupies the foremost position and establishes the supreme standard; in his eminence, he is like the head. The assembled ministers bear responsibility for carrying out the work on his behalf and following their king; in their allotted roles, they are like the arms and legs. He who serves as the head draws upon the radiance of profound wisdom and takes perceptiveness as his rule, discerning uniquely the source of transformation and good order. He embodies the excellence of civilized enlightenment and is wholly impartial in what he sees and hears, penetrating the intricacies of the people and all things. In initiating undertakings, he himself holds the essentials of command. With clarity embodied in his person, how brilliantly he displays the majesty of his sovereign rule! In assessing achievements, he himself refines the impartiality of selection and distinction. Standing above as a grand exemplar, how radiantly he manifests enlightened wisdom as a model!

With such a ruler, how shall his ministers offer their service? We shall see those who serve as his arms and legs joined to him in mutual trust, as parts of a single body: cherishing loyalty and goodness, they respond reverently and devote themselves fully to assisting him. Bound by duty to the weighty task of mutual support, they coordinate their regular official responsibilities in reverent compliance, each offering his utterly pure sincerity. Rejoicing that the enlightened king leads them in their work, they cannot restrain themselves from attending promptly to their tasks. Supporting and sustaining him on either side, they spread his radiant transforming influence far and wide. Would they dare fail the Son of Heaven above them? Looking up to the sage sovereign’s assessment of achievements, they cannot delay in observing the laws and fulfilling their offices. Assisting and supporting him, they together bring his discerning governance to fulfillment. Would they dare fail themselves in such an enlightened age…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎諭李　批〔純雅〕
王者立人之極因以承天之休焉蓋極本人心
同然之理也極建於君而天休因之以集焉其
理之妙於感通者與箕子衍皇極之疇以告武
王若曰天人有合一之理德福有相因之機洛
書之五數固第之爲建用皇極矣而其義爲何
如哉彼天以至極之理而陰隲於維皇本以率
先天下而會萃諸福者也爲之君者本其帝降
之良以爲表儀之準于以式萬方而飭其規運
===
其同然之懿以爲中正之觀于以刑百辟而貞
其度大而天經極之統會在是也惟聖盡倫中
天下而爲綱常之主使同倫者足於我而觀法
焉小而物則極之散殊在是也惟皇盡制首庶
類而爲紀法之宗使考制者得於我而取衷焉
皇能建極如此而福之所集豈其微哉吾知福
之爲數有五其類不同而同爲天地之和氣也
以吾之和德而導迎之自有以致其繁祉之萃
爲福不同而同爲宇宙之順氣也以吾之順德
punctuated:
考試官敎諭李　批〔純雅〕

王者立人之極，因以承天之休焉。蓋極本人心同然之理也，極建於君，而天休因之以集焉，其理之妙於感通者與！箕子衍皇極之疇以告武王，若曰：「天人有合一之理，德福有相因之機。洛書之五數，固第之爲建用皇極矣，而其義爲何如哉？彼天以至極之理而陰隲於維皇，本以率先天下而會萃諸福者也。爲之君者，本其帝降之良，以爲表儀之準，于以式萬方而飭其規；運其同然之懿，以爲中正之觀，于以刑百辟而貞其度。大而天經，極之統會在是也。惟聖盡倫，中天下而爲綱常之主，使同倫者足於我而觀法焉。小而物則，極之散殊在是也。惟皇盡制，首庶類而爲紀法之宗，使考制者得於我而取衷焉。皇能建極如此，而福之所集，豈其微哉？吾知福之爲數有五，其類不同，而同爲天地之和氣也。以吾之和德而導迎之，自有以致其繁祉之萃。爲福不同，而同爲宇宙之順氣也。以吾之順德
translation_en:
Examiner Li, Instructor: comment 〔Pure and elegant〕.

The king establishes the supreme standard for humankind and thereby receives Heaven’s blessings. For this standard is rooted in the principle shared by all human hearts. Once the ruler establishes it, Heaven’s blessings consequently gather upon him. How wondrous is this principle in bringing about sympathetic communication!

Jizi elaborated the category of the August Standard to instruct King Wu, as though saying: “Heaven and humankind have a principle by which they unite; virtue and blessings have a dynamic by which one follows from the other. The fifth number in the Luo Writing is indeed assigned to ‘establishing and employing the August Standard.’ But what does this mean? Heaven, through the principle of ultimate perfection, silently orders affairs for the august sovereign, intending him to lead all under Heaven and gather together the various blessings. The ruler takes the goodness bestowed upon him by the Supreme Lord as the standard for exemplary conduct, thereby setting a model for the myriad regions and putting their norms in order. He brings into operation the excellence common to all, making it a visible model of centrality and correctness, thereby setting an example for the hundred lords and rectifying their standards.

“In their broadest scope, these are Heaven’s constant principles: here the supreme standard is comprehensively united. Only the sage fully realizes human relationships, taking his place at the center of all under Heaven as master of the cardinal bonds and constant virtues, so that those who share these relationships find in me a sufficient example to observe and emulate. In their smallest particulars, these are the norms of things: here the supreme standard is differentiated into its diverse manifestations. Only the august sovereign fully establishes institutions, standing at the head of the many kinds of beings as the fountainhead of rules and laws, so that those who examine institutions find in me the proper measure to adopt.

“If the august sovereign can thus establish the supreme standard, could the blessings that gather upon him be slight? I know that blessings number five. Though their categories differ, all are manifestations of the harmonious vital energy of Heaven and Earth. By guiding and welcoming them with my harmonious virtue, I naturally have the means to bring about the convergence of abundant blessings. Though they differ as blessings, all are manifestations of the concordant vital energy of the universe. Through my concordant virtue…”

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
而感召之自有以膺乎諸福之隆人之所不可
必者天之所不能違也在皇者雖非緣是以獲
福而必致之理在我則隨其所值而迪無不吉
矣其若斂之而會於君之一身矣乎后之所克
綏者天之所寵綏也在聖人雖非藉是以承休
而可致之道在我則任吾所適而動罔不宜矣
其若集之而聚於皇之一人矣乎要之皇極既
建不必外極以求福也極即福也五福既斂不
必外福以觀極也福即極也理一而已矣君天
===
下者其惟建極而已乎抑考大禹陳謨曰惠迪
吉伊尹告君曰作善降之百祥惠之與善即極
之理而吉與百祥亦即五福之斂於極者是以
大禹伊尹得之而致告箕子得之而衍疇皆一
道也吁箕子知極矣能傳之於武而不能行之
於商豈箕子之極不足以斂福與適然之遇也
不可以是以論乎感通之常也
詩
天保定爾以莫不興如山如阜如岡如陵
punctuated:
而感召之，自有以膺乎諸福之隆。人之所不可必者，天之所不能違也。在皇者，雖非緣是以獲福，而必致之理在我，則隨其所值而迪，無不吉矣。其若斂之而會於君之一身矣乎？后之所克綏者，天之所寵綏也。在聖人，雖非藉是以承休，而可致之道在我，則任吾所適而動，罔不宜矣。其若集之而聚於皇之一人矣乎？要之，皇極既建，不必外極以求福也，極即福也；五福既斂，不必外福以觀極也，福即極也。理一而已矣。君天下者，其惟建極而已乎？抑考大禹陳謨曰：「惠迪吉。」伊尹告君曰：「作善，降之百祥。」惠之與善，即極之理；而吉與百祥，亦即五福之斂於極者。是以大禹、伊尹得之而致告，箕子得之而衍疇，皆一道也。吁！箕子知極矣，能傳之於武，而不能行之於商，豈箕子之極不足以斂福與？適然之遇也，不可以是以論乎感通之常也。
詩
天保定爾，以莫不興，如山如阜，如岡如陵。
translation_en:
…and thereby evoke them, one naturally has the means to receive blessings in their abundance. What human beings cannot guarantee is what Heaven cannot contravene. Although the august ruler does not act thus for the sake of obtaining blessings, the principle that must bring them lies within himself. Thus, whatever circumstances he encounters, he proceeds with nothing but auspicious results. Is this not like gathering them together in the ruler’s own person? What the sovereign can secure in peace is what Heaven graciously settles in peace. Although the sage does not rely on this for the sake of receiving favor, the way by which it may be attained lies within himself. Thus, wherever he goes, none of his actions is unfitting. Is this not like assembling them together in the person of the august ruler alone?
In essence, once the August Ultimate—the sovereign’s supreme standard—has been established, there is no need to seek blessings outside it: the Ultimate itself is blessing. Once the five blessings have been gathered, there is no need to look beyond them to discern the Ultimate: blessing itself is the Ultimate. There is but one principle. For one who rules All under Heaven, is the essential task not simply to establish the Ultimate? Consider further how Yu the Great, setting forth his counsels, said: “Following the Way brings good fortune.” Yi Yin admonished his ruler: “Do good, and a hundred auspicious blessings will descend upon you.” Following the Way and doing good embody the principle of the Ultimate; good fortune and the hundred auspicious blessings are likewise the five blessings gathered into the Ultimate. Thus Yu the Great and Yi Yin grasped it and delivered their admonitions, while Jizi grasped it and elaborated the Categories of the Great Plan. All followed the same Way. Alas! Jizi understood the Ultimate. He could transmit it to King Wu but could not put it into practice under the Shang. Could it be that Jizi’s Ultimate was insufficient to gather blessings? This was a matter of the circumstances he happened to encounter; one cannot use it to judge the constant principle of sympathetic response between Heaven and humanity.
Book of Odes
Heaven protects and establishes you, so that nothing fails to flourish; like mountains, like hillocks, like ridges, like great hills…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
如川之方至以莫不增
秦應驄
同考試官教諭韓批通篇辭藻不浮而詩人
頌禱之意溢於言外文之佳者
同考試官教諭蘇批場中作者類以以莫不
增屬川之方至殊非本旨獨此作有見錄之
考試官教諭管批雅暢
考試官教諭李批辭旨俱到
臣子託天福君之盛必擬諸形容而進之焉夫
===
高大盛長天之福君者至矣而猶欲進之不已
周臣忠愛之心寧有既乎想其答君之意蓋謂
王者以事天為心亦以得天為慶使福有未盛
而莫之有增非所以語於天心之仁愛也吾願
天之福君者本於簡在之隆而宇宙之太和凝
焉單厚多益凡君心之百順者咸以一身而履
其盛原於寵綏之厚而庶徵之熙洽萃焉戬穀
罄宜凡天休之滋至者咸以一人而會其全夫
是福之興也將何以擬之哉彼山阜岡陵天下
punctuated:
如川之方至，以莫不增。
秦應驄。
同考試官教諭韓批：通篇辭藻不浮，而詩人頌禱之意溢於言外，文之佳者。
同考試官教諭蘇批：場中作者類以「以莫不增」屬「川之方至」，殊非本旨。獨此作有見，錄之。
考試官教諭管批：雅暢。
考試官教諭李批：辭旨俱到。
臣子託天福君之盛，必擬諸形容而進之焉。夫高大盛長，天之福君者至矣，而猶欲進之不已，周臣忠愛之心寧有既乎？想其答君之意，蓋謂王者以事天為心，亦以得天為慶。使福有未盛，而莫之有增，非所以語於天心之仁愛也。吾願天之福君者，本於簡在之隆，而宇宙之太和凝焉；單厚多益，凡君心之百順者，咸以一身而履其盛。原於寵綏之厚，而庶徵之熙洽萃焉；戬穀罄宜，凡天休之滋至者，咸以一人而會其全。夫是福之興也，將何以擬之哉？彼山阜岡陵，天下
translation_en:
…like a river just beginning to surge, so that nothing fails to increase.

Qin Yingcong.

Associate Examiner Han, Instructor, comments: Throughout the piece, the diction is ornate without being superficial, and the poet’s intention of praise and prayer overflows beyond the words. A fine composition.

Associate Examiner Su, Instructor, comments: Candidates in the examination generally attach “so that nothing fails to increase” to “a river just beginning to surge,” which decidedly misses the original meaning. This composition alone shows insight; I have selected it.

Examiner Guan, Instructor, comments: Refined and fluent.

Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: Both expression and meaning are fully realized.

When subjects invoke Heaven to bless their ruler abundantly, they must find images to describe those blessings and carry them further. Lofty, great, abundant, and enduring: Heaven’s blessings upon the ruler have reached their utmost. Yet the subjects of Zhou still wish to advance them without end. Could their loyal affection ever be exhausted? Imagining their intention in responding to their ruler, we may say that a king sets his heart on serving Heaven and also rejoices in obtaining Heaven’s favor. If his blessings were less than abundant and nothing increased them, this would hardly accord with the benevolent love in Heaven’s heart. I wish that Heaven’s blessings upon our ruler might be rooted in the exalted favor of his being chosen and kept in Heaven’s regard, with the supreme harmony of the universe concentrated in him. Deep and ample, with manifold increase, may all that accords with the ruler’s heart find its abundant fulfillment in his own person. May those blessings originate in the fullness of Heaven’s favor and protection, with the harmonious concurrence of the many signs gathered in him. With happiness and goodness, and all things fitting, may the ever-growing blessings bestowed by Heaven be brought together in their entirety in the one ruler. How, then, shall we find an image for the flourishing of these blessings? Those mountains, mounds, ridges, and hills, beneath Heaven…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
鄭秉厚
同考試官教諭韓批講王國克生處有識見
有筆力傑作也
同考試官教諭蘇批文體莊嚴措辭雅飭子
其亦勉敬之士與
考試官教諭管批雋永可味
考試官教諭李批得詩人旨
詩人美聖世之士而成輔世之功焉蓋國家以
賢才爲楨幹也周士有功於國其傳世之顯宜
===
矣周公推述文王得人之盛如此蓋曰天之於
我文王也敷錫之命集於孫子而顯世之榮及
於臣庶若是其盛矣然多士之生豈無所自哉
其在當時言之皆秉敬德以自將而謨明弼諧
之具偉然盛世之英懷欽翼以自勵而邁種庶
明之德卓乎王者之佐美哉此多士也吾見其
當貞元之會應運而生咸萃集於文明之世應
聖作之期乘時而起咸誕降於興王之邦夫孰
非我文王之士乎斯時也王國之氣運方隆既
punctuated:
鄭秉厚

同考試官教諭韓批：講「王國克生」處，有識見，有筆力，傑作也。

同考試官教諭蘇批：文體莊嚴，措辭雅飭，子其亦勉敬之士與？

考試官教諭管批：雋永可味。

考試官教諭李批：得詩人旨。

詩人美聖世之士，而成輔世之功焉。蓋國家以賢才爲楨幹也，周士有功於國，其傳世之顯宜矣。周公推述文王得人之盛如此，蓋曰：天之於我文王也，敷錫之命集於孫子，而顯世之榮及於臣庶，若是其盛矣。然多士之生，豈無所自哉？其在當時言之，皆秉敬德以自將，而謨明弼諧之具，偉然盛世之英；懷欽翼以自勵，而邁種庶明之德，卓乎王者之佐。美哉，此多士也！吾見其當貞元之會，應運而生，咸萃集於文明之世；應聖作之期，乘時而起，咸誕降於興王之邦。夫孰非我文王之士乎？斯時也，王國之氣運方隆，既
translation_en:
Zheng Binghou

Associate Examiner Han, Instructor, comments: “The discussion of ‘the royal kingdom could bring forth such men’ shows insight and forceful writing. A masterful composition.”

Associate Examiner Su, Instructor, comments: “The composition is dignified, and its phrasing elegant and disciplined. Surely you too are a gentleman who strives to maintain reverence?”

Examiner Guan, Instructor, comments: “Its lasting savor rewards contemplation.”

Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “It captures the poet’s intent.”

The poet praises the gentlemen of a sage-governed age and thereby accomplishes the work of aiding the age. For the state takes worthy and talented men as its pillars. The gentlemen of Zhou rendered service to the state; it was fitting that their distinction should endure through the generations. Such was the abundance of worthy men obtained by King Wen that the Duke of Zhou celebrated in his account. His meaning was this: Heaven’s generously bestowed mandate to our King Wen devolved upon his descendants, while the glory of distinction through the generations extended to his ministers and common people. Such was its abundance. Yet could the birth of these many gentlemen have had no source? Speaking of them in their own time, all upheld reverent virtue to guide themselves. With their capacity for enlightened counsel and harmonious assistance, they stood as magnificent talents of a flourishing age. Cherishing reverence and circumspection to spur themselves onward, and possessing the virtue of diligently cultivating manifold understanding, they were outstanding assistants to a king. Admirable indeed were these many gentlemen! I see them born in response to destiny at the juncture of an old cycle’s ending and a new cycle’s beginning, all gathering in an age of cultivated brilliance. Answering the moment when a sage arose, they rose with the times, all born into the realm of a rising king. Who among them was not a gentleman of our King Wen? At this time, the royal kingdom’s fortunes were just flourishing, and already …

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
八月公會齊侯宋公鄭伯曹伯邾人于檉
〔僖公元年〕秋齊侯宋公江人黃人會于
陽穀〔僖公三年〕
蔡栢齡
同考試官教諭周批威信二字發揮明爽此
必邃于經學者可以式矣
考試官教諭管批得聖人予齊桓管仲之旨
考試官教諭李批文體謹嚴
春秋兩紀伯好善其威信之著焉夫伯者之行
乎諸侯非威信莫以也此檉與陽穀之會所以
見取于春秋乎且楚自熊貲以來世爲諸姬之
患北向之圖每爲鄭病而東方之與則固恃江
黃以爲利也創伯其時者當何如攘之耶是故
駕馭之策貴乎先聲非示之威則勢不張桓與
仲也念之若曰伐鄭之師楚方浸強未易挫也
而未可快于一逞也顧可以不集于眾乎于是
合列國而共舉于檉之會志無不同謀無不協
懿親之國必急于簡書而方張之敵務摧其禍
punctuated:
八月，公會齊侯、宋公、鄭伯、曹伯、邾人于檉。〔僖公元年〕秋，齊侯、宋公、江人、黃人會于陽穀。〔僖公三年〕

蔡栢齡

同考試官教諭周批：威信二字，發揮明爽，此必邃于經學者，可以式矣。
考試官教諭管批：得聖人予齊桓、管仲之旨。
考試官教諭李批：文體謹嚴。

春秋兩紀伯好，善其威信之著焉。夫伯者之行乎諸侯，非威信莫以也。此檉與陽穀之會所以見取于春秋乎？且楚自熊貲以來，世爲諸姬之患，北向之圖，每爲鄭病；而東方之與，則固恃江、黃以爲利也。創伯其時者，當何如攘之耶？是故駕馭之策，貴乎先聲；非示之威，則勢不張。桓與仲也念之，若曰：「伐鄭之師，楚方浸強，未易挫也，而未可快于一逞也。顧可以不集于眾乎？」于是合列國而共舉，于檉之會，志無不同，謀無不協。懿親之國，必急于簡書；而方張之敵，務摧其禍
translation_en:
In the eighth month, the Duke met with the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, and a representative of Zhu at Cheng. 〔First year of Duke Xi.〕 In autumn, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, and representatives of Jiang and Huang met at Yanggu. 〔Third year of Duke Xi.〕

Cai Bailing

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor: “The two terms ‘authority’ and ‘trustworthiness’ are expounded clearly and lucidly. This must be the work of someone deeply versed in classical learning; it may serve as a model.”
Comment by Examiner Guan, Instructor: “It captures the Sage’s intention in approving Duke Huan of Qi and Guan Zhong.”
Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: “The composition is disciplined and rigorous.”

The Spring and Autumn Annals twice records the hegemon’s friendly relations, commending the conspicuous expression of his authority and trustworthiness. For a hegemon to exercise leadership among the feudal lords, there is no means other than authority and trustworthiness. Is this not why the meetings at Cheng and Yanggu receive approval in the Spring and Autumn Annals? Ever since Xiong Zi, Chu had for generations been a menace to the states ruled by the Ji lineage. Its designs toward the north repeatedly afflicted Zheng, while, among its allies to the east, it relied firmly on Jiang and Huang to advance its interests. How should someone establishing hegemonic leadership at that time have repelled it?

Thus, in devising a strategy for keeping others in check, the foremost consideration is to make one’s might known in advance. Unless authority is displayed, one’s power cannot expand. Duke Huan and Guan Zhong reflected on this, as if saying: “As for the forces attacking Zheng, Chu is steadily growing stronger and cannot readily be checked; nor should we seek the satisfaction of a single victorious encounter. Can we possibly fail to gather the strength of the many?” Accordingly, they united the various states for joint action. At the meeting at Cheng, their purposes were entirely shared and their plans fully coordinated. The states closely related by kinship must respond urgently to the written summons for aid; as for the enemy whose power was expanding, they strove to crush the harm it threatened…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
於內政信不假於載書庶幾乎王者之事惜召
陵以後鮮克有終執濤塗則威肆而江黃不救
則信失不惟遠於王事伯業且隳矣蓋齊桓之
量不勝其德管仲之器不勝其才玆伯者所爲
假也然則王道之大如何曰誠而已矣
單伯至自齊文公十有五年
徐廷綬
同考試官敎諭周批孔子作春秋志在尊周
耳此作明悉可式錄之
===
考試官敎諭管批尊王命意藹然詞外可謂
考試官敎諭李批精確渾成
春秋字命卿之歸國所以謹臣禮也夫人臣之
禮莫大于尊君單伯以周之命卿而可以列國
大夫待之哉聖人所以必錄其字以此且單伯
以叔姬之故見執于齊魯請而歸之使來致命
焉經之例大夫執而至則名此獨以字稱豈曰
以已執之而非其罪與曰尊王命以謹臣禮耳
蓋維王有命所以馭天下之貴者在是焉而降
punctuated:
於內政，信不假於載書，庶幾乎王者之事。惜召陵以後，鮮克有終：執濤塗則威肆，而江黃不救則信失。不惟遠於王事，伯業且隳矣。蓋齊桓之量不勝其德，管仲之器不勝其才，玆伯者所爲假也。然則王道之大如何？曰：誠而已矣。
單伯至自齊，文公十有五年。
徐廷綬
同考試官敎諭周批：孔子作《春秋》，志在尊周耳。此作明悉，可式，錄之。
考試官敎諭管批：尊王命意，藹然詞外，可謂。
考試官敎諭李批：精確渾成。
《春秋》字命卿之歸國，所以謹臣禮也。夫人臣之禮，莫大于尊君。單伯以周之命卿，而可以列國大夫待之哉？聖人所以必錄其字，以此。且單伯以叔姬之故，見執于齊，魯請而歸之，使來致命焉。經之例，大夫執而至則名，此獨以字稱，豈曰以已執之而非其罪與？曰：尊王命以謹臣禮耳。蓋維王有命，所以馭天下之貴者在是焉，而降
translation_en:
… in internal administration; his trustworthiness did not depend upon written covenants. This came close to the work of a true king. Regrettably, after Shaoling, he seldom carried things through to a good conclusion: in seizing Taotu, he exercised his authority without restraint; in failing to rescue Jiang and Huang, he forfeited trust. Not only did he fall short of kingly achievement; even his enterprise as hegemon was undermined. Duke Huan of Qi’s capacity was insufficient to sustain his virtue, and Guan Zhong’s breadth of character was insufficient to sustain his talent. This is why a hegemon merely borrows the forms of kingship. What, then, constitutes the greatness of the Kingly Way? The answer is sincerity, and nothing more.
“Shan Bo returned from Qi.” Fifteenth year of Duke Wen.
Xu Tingshou.
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor: “Confucius composed the Spring and Autumn Annals with the sole aim of honoring Zhou. This composition explains the matter clearly and thoroughly and can serve as a model. Include it.”
Comment by Examiner Guan, Instructor: “The intention to honor the king is abundantly apparent beyond the wording. It may be called … [?]”
Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: “Precise and seamlessly composed.”
The Spring and Autumn Annals uses the courtesy name when recording the return of a royally appointed minister to his state in order to uphold strictly the ritual obligations of a subject. Among those obligations, none is greater than honoring one’s ruler. As a minister appointed by Zhou, could Shan Bo be treated merely as a grand master of one of the states? This is why the Sage insisted on recording his courtesy name. Moreover, Shan Bo was detained in Qi on account of Shu Ji; Lu requested his release, and he was sent back to convey the command. The classic’s usual practice is to use the personal name when a grand master returns after being detained. Here alone it uses the courtesy name. Can this be because, although he had been detained, he was not guilty? The answer is that it honors the king’s command in order to uphold strictly the ritual obligations of a subject. For it is through the king’s issuing commands that he governs the noble men of all under Heaven; and in sending down …

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
監于下爲至重矣人臣被命所以揚天子之休
者在是焉而祗若于身爲至榮矣單伯者位雖
列於魯邦爵則詔於周室監國以爲任冊命作
于內史彼貴戚之卿延賞于世者固不得而尚
其尊圻邑以爲號章服掌之宗伯彼賜族之臣
建官于私者又惡得而擬其貴故王章之赫奕
彼將奉之終其身焉不得以見執之故而損其
禮數之常蓋有定名焉策之王朝人固不得而
予奪之也天命之簡臨人亦將戴之震其望焉
===
豈容以事變之偶而改其寵遇之舊蓋有定分
焉錫之天吏人固不得而隆殺之也在昔王人
下士以一時之命猶得位侯王之上焉况玆列
爵五服者哉是故春秋特從而字之待之以王
朝大夫之例非尊單伯也尊王命也尊王命以
謹臣禮也孔子敬君可謂無所不用其情矣雖
然人臣以有命爲榮亦以不辱命爲善知君命
之在吾身能自樹以對揚之知君命之在吾國
能自振以丕顯之是乃所謂事君之義而單伯
punctuated: 監于下，爲至重矣。人臣被命，所以揚天子之休者在是焉，而祗若于身，爲至榮矣。單伯者，位雖列於魯邦，爵則詔於周室。監國以爲任，冊命作于內史，彼貴戚之卿延賞于世者，固不得而尚其尊；圻邑以爲號，章服掌之宗伯，彼賜族之臣建官于私者，又惡得而擬其貴？故王章之赫奕，彼將奉之終其身焉，不得以見執之故而損其禮數之常。蓋有定名焉，策之王朝，人固不得而予奪之也。天命之簡臨，人亦將戴之，震其望焉，豈容以事變之偶而改其寵遇之舊？蓋有定分焉，錫之天吏，人固不得而隆殺之也。在昔王人下士，以一時之命，猶得位侯王之上焉，况玆列爵五服者哉？是故《春秋》特從而字之，待之以王朝大夫之例，非尊單伯也，尊王命也；尊王命以謹臣禮也。孔子敬君，可謂無所不用其情矣。雖然，人臣以有命爲榮，亦以不辱命爲善。知君命之在吾身，能自樹以對揚之；知君命之在吾國，能自振以丕顯之，是乃所謂事君之義。而單伯
translation_en:
…its oversight of those below is therefore of the utmost gravity. A minister receives a royal commission as the means of proclaiming the Son of Heaven’s glory; reverently fulfilling it in his own person is therefore the highest honor. Although Shan Bo held his position in the state of Lu, his rank was conferred by the royal house of Zhou. His charge was to oversee the state, and his patent of appointment was prepared by the Interior Secretary. Even ministers who were royal relatives and whose rewards extended to successive generations could not surpass him in honor. His title derived from an estate within the royal domain, and his ceremonial robes and insignia were under the charge of the Minister of Rites. How could ministers granted lineage names, whose offices were established within subordinate houses, compare with him in nobility?

Thus he was to uphold the splendor of the royal insignia throughout his life. The fact that he had been taken captive could not diminish the customary ceremonial honors due to him. His standing was fixed, recorded in a patent at the royal court; others certainly could not grant or withdraw it. When Heaven’s mandate selects a man and invests him with authority, others must honor him and stand in awe of his prestige. How could an incidental turn of events be allowed to alter the favor he had long enjoyed? His station was fixed, bestowed upon him as an officer of Heaven; others certainly could not exalt or diminish it. In former times, even a royal emissary of the rank of Junior Serviceman, bearing a commission for a particular occasion, could take precedence over the feudal rulers. How much more must this apply to one invested with noble rank and its corresponding ceremonial dress among the five grades!

For this reason, the Spring and Autumn Annals specifically calls him by his courtesy name, treating him according to the precedent for grand masters of the royal court. This honors not Shan Bo himself but the king’s command; it honors the king’s command so as to uphold the ritual obligations of ministers. Confucius may truly be said to have given fullest expression to his devotion in showing reverence for the ruler. Nevertheless, while a minister takes pride in possessing a commission, he must also regard it as a virtue not to disgrace that commission. Knowing that the ruler’s command rests upon his own person, he must establish himself so as to acknowledge and proclaim it; knowing that the ruler’s command rests upon his state, he must rouse himself so as to make it greatly manifest. This is what is meant by the duty of serving one’s ruler. But as for Shan Bo…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
者俛首就執曾不能上告下訴奉天討以正商
人之罪而自直其誣也則何取焉然則歸魯告
至亦倖焉耳此又春秋警臣道之意
禮記
故人情者聖王之田也脩禮以耕之陳義
以種之講學以耨之本仁以聚之播樂
以安之
鄭復亨
同考試官教諭蔣批〔詞旨醇鬯氣象渾融發〕
〔聖王治情之意殆盡宜錄以式〕
考試官教諭管批〔義精詞健當是作者〕
考試官教諭李批〔理到〕
記者喻聖王之治人情必詳其所治之道焉甚
矣人情未易以治也聖王備舉其道以治之斯
其有弗治者哉禮運之意若謂夫人之情每遷
於多變而聖王之心必先於化中是故聖王以
人情之易流而無節也於是卽其應感之發而
裁成之有術因其念慮之形而範圍之不過是
punctuated:
者，俛首就執，曾不能上告下訴，奉天討以正商人之罪，而自直其誣也，則何取焉？然則歸魯告至，亦倖焉耳。此又春秋警臣道之意。

禮記
故人情者，聖王之田也。脩禮以耕之，陳義以種之，講學以耨之，本仁以聚之，播樂以安之。
鄭復亨
同考試官教諭蔣批〔詞旨醇鬯，氣象渾融，發〕〔聖王治情之意殆盡，宜錄以式。〕
考試官教諭管批〔義精詞健，當是作者。〕
考試官教諭李批〔理到。〕

記者喻聖王之治人情，必詳其所治之道焉。甚矣，人情未易以治也！聖王備舉其道以治之，斯其有弗治者哉？禮運之意，若謂夫人之情每遷於多變，而聖王之心必先於化中。是故聖王以人情之易流而無節也，於是卽其應感之發而裁成之有術，因其念慮之形而範圍之不過。是
translation_en:
…yet he bowed his head and submitted to arrest. He could not even appeal to those above or plead with those below, carry out Heaven’s punishment to bring Shangren to account for his crime, and clear himself of the false accusation. What, then, was there to commend in him? Thus, his return to Lu and announcement of his arrival were merely good fortune. Here, too, lies the intention of the Spring and Autumn Annals to admonish ministers concerning their proper conduct.

Record of Rites
“Thus, human feelings are the sage king’s field. He cultivates ritual to plow it, sets forth righteousness to sow it, expounds learning to weed it, takes benevolence as the foundation to gather its harvest, and spreads music to bring it repose.”
Zheng Fuheng
Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor, comments: 〔“The language and purport are pure and lucid; the overall bearing is integrated and harmonious. It develops〕〔almost exhaustively the meaning of the sage king’s ordering of human feelings. It should be selected as a model.”〕
Examiner Guan, Instructor, comments: 〔“The meaning is refined and the language vigorous. This is surely an accomplished writer.”〕
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: 〔“The principle is fully grasped.”〕

In illustrating how the sage king orders human feelings, the author of the Record necessarily explains in detail the means by which he orders them. How very difficult human feelings are to govern! Yet when the sage king brings all his methods to bear upon them, can any remain ungoverned? The meaning of the ‘Evolution of Ritual’ chapter seems to be that human feelings constantly shift amid manifold changes, while the sage king’s mind must take the lead in transforming them toward the mean [?]. Thus, because human feelings readily drift without restraint, the sage king works upon their emergence in response to external stimuli, possessing methods to shape them appropriately; he works upon the manifestation of thoughts and concerns, setting bounds so that they do not go too far. This…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
有以造於自然之域矣其穀之食而厭飫者於
此何以殊耶夫禮耕義種治情有以開其始矣
仁聚樂安治情有以成其終矣而又以學講明
其間聖王治情之道備具如此則夫人情之無
不治也固其宜哉大抵人情有欲易發而難制
而聖王獨致詳於此脩道之敎始終備其條理
其所以懼夫陷溺其心者良亦切矣然此豈直
以情之不流於僻而已耶是故人情治而大順
致順道達而三才應太和雍熙之盛固皆由此
===
其選矣雖然猶有要焉亦曰立人極而已
論倫無患樂之情也欣喜歡愛樂之官也
中正無邪禮之質也莊敬恭順禮之制
也若夫禮樂之施於金石越於聲音用
於宗廟社稷事乎山川鬼神則此所與
民同也
張對
同考試官敎諭蔣批詞格精健且意義肯綮
是必究心於禮樂之義者
punctuated:
有以造於自然之域矣，其穀之食而厭飫者，於此何以殊耶？夫禮耕義種，治情有以開其始矣；仁聚樂安，治情有以成其終矣。而又以學講明其間，聖王治情之道備具如此，則夫人情之無不治也，固其宜哉！大抵人情有欲，易發而難制，而聖王獨致詳於此，脩道之敎，始終備其條理，其所以懼夫陷溺其心者，良亦切矣。然此豈直以情之不流於僻而已耶？是故人情治而大順致，順道達而三才應，太和雍熙之盛，固皆由此其選矣。雖然，猶有要焉，亦曰立人極而已。

論倫無患，樂之情也；欣喜歡愛，樂之官也；中正無邪，禮之質也；莊敬恭順，禮之制也。若夫禮樂之施於金石，越於聲音，用於宗廟社稷，事乎山川鬼神，則此所與民同也。

張對。

同考試官敎諭蔣批：詞格精健，且意義肯綮，是必究心於禮樂之義者。
translation_en:
…thereby attaining the realm of natural spontaneity. How does this differ from eating grain and becoming fully satisfied? Through plowing with ritual and sowing with righteousness, the ordering of the feelings has its beginning; through gathering with benevolence and bringing repose through music, the ordering of the feelings reaches its completion. Learning is also employed to expound and clarify what lies between. Since the sage kings’ way of ordering the feelings is so fully equipped, it is surely fitting that no human feelings should remain unordered! Generally, human feelings involve desires, which are easily aroused but difficult to restrain. The sage kings therefore attended to this matter with particular care. Their teaching of cultivating the Way provided an orderly framework from beginning to end. Their fear that people’s hearts might become engulfed and submerged was indeed acute. Yet could this have been merely to prevent the feelings from straying into perversity? Thus, when human feelings are ordered, great harmony is attained; when the way of harmony prevails, the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humanity—respond. The flourishing of supreme harmony and concord surely all derives from this [the following words, 其選, are doubtful]. Nevertheless, there is still an essential point: it is simply to establish the ultimate standard for humanity.

“Order in human relationships without trouble [?]: this is the essential nature of music. Joy, delight, gladness, and love are the functions of music. Centrality and correctness without perversity are the substance of ritual. Solemnity, reverence, respect, and obedience are the forms of ritual. As for ritual and music being expressed through metal bells and stone chimes, issuing forth in sounds, employed in the ancestral temple and at the altars of soil and grain, and used to serve the spirits of mountains and rivers and other spirits: these are what are shared with the people.”

Zhang Dui.

Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor: “The diction and style are refined and vigorous, and the meaning strikes the essential points. This must be someone who has devoted his mind to the meaning of ritual and music.”

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭管批體認真切錄之
考試官教諭李批詞𢠢而意婉
記者詳禮樂之義而因及其數之易知者焉夫
禮樂之義和序盡之矣故知此者非君則莫與
焉豈其民之可同也耶樂記君子記此若謂先
王之制禮樂也有義焉有數焉數以顯其象義
以涵其精是故觀於其義而豈君之所可巳者
乎自其樂而言之雅頌陳盛世之章律呂適後
先之度太和協暢而忺懘之不形此固樂之本
===
情在是矣以至順其心而有欣喜焉得所悅而
有歡愛焉是聲氣之元含於吾心而其論倫之
播被固皆由之以主宰也不曰樂之官乎自其
禮而言之本之中以推行循之正以自立至序
周旋而邪僻之不作此固禮之本質在是矣以
至莊敬焉以之作吾肅也恭順焉以之作吾讓
也是無體之節體諸於身而其中正之措施固
皆由之以綱維也不曰禮之制乎斯則和序肇
禮樂之原而非人無以通其奧禮樂妙身心之
punctuated:
考試官教諭管批：體認真切，錄之。
考試官教諭李批：詞𢠢而意婉。
記者詳禮樂之義，而因及其數之易知者焉。夫禮樂之義，和序盡之矣。故知此者，非君則莫與焉，豈其民之可同也耶？樂記君子記此，若謂先王之制禮樂也，有義焉，有數焉。數以顯其象，義以涵其精。是故觀於其義，而豈君之所可巳者乎？自其樂而言之，雅頌陳盛世之章，律呂適後先之度，太和協暢，而忺懘之不形，此固樂之本情在是矣。以至順其心而有欣喜焉，得所悅而有歡愛焉，是聲氣之元含於吾心，而其論倫之播被，固皆由之以主宰也。不曰樂之官乎？自其禮而言之，本之中以推行，循之正以自立，至序周旋，而邪僻之不作，此固禮之本質在是矣。以至莊敬焉，以之作吾肅也；恭順焉，以之作吾讓也。是無體之節，體諸於身，而其中正之措施，固皆由之以綱維也。不曰禮之制乎？斯則和序肇禮樂之原，而非人無以通其奧；禮樂妙身心之
translation_en:
Examiner Guan, an Instructor, comments: “The understanding is genuine and precise. Accept it.”
Examiner Li, an Instructor, comments: “The diction is [?], and the meaning delicately expressed.”
The recorder explains the meaning of ritual and music in detail, and accordingly touches upon their readily understood formal particulars. Harmony and order exhaust the meaning of ritual and music. Thus none but the ruler can participate in understanding this: how could it be something shared equally with the common people? In recording this, the gentleman who composed the Record of Music seems to say that the former kings’ establishment of ritual and music possessed both meaning and formal particulars. The particulars manifest their outward forms; the meaning contains their essence. Thus, when considering their meaning, how could the ruler dispense with them?
Speaking of music, the Court Hymns and Eulogies set forth the compositions of a flourishing age, while the pitch standards bring preceding and following tones into proper measure. Supreme harmony flows freely, and discord [?] does not appear. Here indeed lies music’s fundamental emotional character. Furthermore, when the heart is in accord, there is delight and joy; when it obtains what pleases it, there is gladness and love. The source of sound and vital energy is contained within my heart, and the diffusion of its ordered relationships [?] is governed entirely by this. Is this not what is called the functioning of music?
Speaking of ritual, one takes centrality as the basis for putting it into practice and follows correctness in establishing oneself. Perfect order informs every movement, and perversity does not arise. Here indeed lies ritual’s fundamental substance. Furthermore, solemnity and reverence arouse my seriousness; deference and compliance arouse my yielding disposition. These formless measures become embodied in one’s person, and the practical expression of centrality and correctness is entirely structured and sustained by them. Is this not what is called the regulation of ritual?
Thus harmony and order constitute the origin of ritual and music, yet without a person their profundity cannot be penetrated; ritual and music give wondrous efficacy to the body and mind’s…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
用而惟君有以契其深若夫禮樂之被於金石
越之聲音而搏拊之有節用之宗廟社稷事於
山川鬼神而駿奔之有秩此特其數之可陳者
耳不必其君而後知也而凡民之得於共聞者
皆可以與聞其聲矣亦不必獨於君而有知也
而凡民之得於共見者皆可以與見其文矣其
夫情官質制之妙寓於器數之中是豈可得而
同哉由是觀之禮樂之義惟君所獨知而不與
民同則夫本和序以爲禮樂先者其責誠有所
===
歸矣而不明其義可乎雖然禮樂亦豈可以僞
爲者哉蓋樂者吾心之和禮者吾身之序必其
內而無斯須之不和外而無斯須之不敬推其
精神心術之蘊以顯於制作之間而後禮樂之
道得矣故君子之中正是履和平是樂者良以
此耳不然欣喜歡愛則爲導慾莊敬恭順則爲
象恭而其論倫之詞中正之節亦數焉爾也其
何禮樂之足云
第貳場
punctuated:
用，而惟君有以契其深。若夫禮樂之被於金石，越之聲音，而搏拊之有節；用之宗廟社稷，事於山川鬼神，而駿奔之有秩：此特其數之可陳者耳，不必其君而後知也。而凡民之得於共聞者，皆可以與聞其聲矣，亦不必獨於君而有知也。而凡民之得於共見者，皆可以與見其文矣。其夫情官質制之妙，寓於器數之中，是豈可得而同哉？由是觀之，禮樂之義，惟君所獨知，而不與民同，則夫本和序以爲禮樂先者，其責誠有所歸矣，而不明其義可乎？雖然，禮樂亦豈可以僞爲者哉？蓋樂者，吾心之和；禮者，吾身之序。必其內而無斯須之不和，外而無斯須之不敬，推其精神心術之蘊，以顯於制作之間，而後禮樂之道得矣。故君子之中正是履，和平是樂者，良以此耳。不然，欣喜歡愛則爲導慾，莊敬恭順則爲象恭，而其論倫之詞、中正之節，亦數焉爾也，其何禮樂之足云？

第貳場
translation_en:
…operation, yet only the ruler can comprehend their depths. As for rites and music being expressed through metal bells and stone chimes, issuing forth as sounds [?], with the striking and tapping keeping time; or being employed in the ancestral temple and at the altars of soil and grain, in service to the spirits of mountains and rivers, with those hastening to perform their duties maintaining due order—these are merely their enumerable forms, which can be set out for inspection. One need not be the ruler to understand them. Whatever the common people can hear together, they can all share in hearing its sounds; knowledge of these need not belong exclusively to the ruler. Whatever the common people can see together, they can all share in seeing its patterned forms. But the subtleties of their essential feelings, functions, substance, and regulation, lodged within their instruments and prescribed forms—how could understanding of these be shared in the same way?

Seen in this light, the meaning of rites and music is known uniquely to the ruler, whose understanding differs from that of the people. Thus the responsibility for taking harmony and order as the foundation preceding rites and music truly has someone to whom it belongs. Can he then fail to understand their meaning? Nevertheless, how could rites and music be produced through pretense? Music is the harmony of our hearts; ritual is the order of our persons. Inwardly, there must not be a moment without harmony; outwardly, there must not be a moment without reverence. Only when the inner resources of spirit and mind are extended and made manifest in the establishment of institutions can the Way of rites and music be attained. This is precisely why the gentleman practices centrality and correctness and delights in harmony and peace. Otherwise, joy, delight, affection, and love merely become inducements to desire, while solemnity, reverence, deference, and obedience become an outward show of respect. Their words concerning human relationships [?] and their measured observances of centrality and correctness likewise amount only to prescribed forms. How could these deserve to be called rites and music?

Second Session

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
論
聖人之仁如天地
盧漸
同考試官教諭張批博雅之才昌大之氣且
發揮聖人天地之仁懇切詳盡仁而壽之理躍如目
前矣敬服敬服
同考試官學正李批議論充贍思致精瑩眞
有見於聖人天地之仁者
考試官教諭管批體格高古辭氣冲雅可
以為式矣
考試官教諭李批理融見澈且中矩矱錄
之
聖人以其身成位天地之中而與天地同悠久
者何也蓋天地之心獨鍾於聖人而聖人以天
地之心倂包乎天下夫天地何心也所謂天地
之大德曰生者是也是太極之理也卽所謂仁
也天地以太極之理乘之而為氣是故兩儀久
奠而不易聖人以天地之心運之而為氣是故
punctuated:
論

聖人之仁如天地

盧漸

同考試官教諭張批：博雅之才，昌大之氣，且發揮聖人天地之仁，懇切詳盡，仁而壽之理躍如目前矣。敬服！敬服！

同考試官學正李批：議論充贍，思致精瑩，眞有見於聖人天地之仁者。

考試官教諭管批：體格高古，辭氣冲雅，可以為式矣。

考試官教諭李批：理融見澈，且中矩矱，錄之。

聖人以其身成位天地之中，而與天地同悠久者，何也？蓋天地之心獨鍾於聖人，而聖人以天地之心倂包乎天下。夫天地何心也？所謂天地之大德曰生者是也。是太極之理也，卽所謂仁也。天地以太極之理乘之而為氣，是故兩儀久奠而不易；聖人以天地之心運之而為氣，是故
translation_en:
Discourse

The Sage’s Benevolence Is Like That of Heaven and Earth

Lu Jian

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: Talent both broadly learned and refined, and a vast, expansive spirit. Moreover, the exposition of the benevolence of the sage and of Heaven and Earth is earnest and thorough. The principle that benevolence brings longevity stands vividly before our eyes. My admiration! My admiration!

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: The argument is rich and ample, the thought subtle and lucid. This is truly someone who understands the benevolence of the sage and of Heaven and Earth.

Comment by Examiner Guan, Instructor: The form and style are lofty and antique; the language and tone, serene and elegant. This can serve as a model.

Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: The principles are comprehensively understood, the insights penetrating; it also conforms to the prescribed standards. Accept it.

Why is it that the sage, in his own person, establishes his place between Heaven and Earth and endures as long as they do? It is because the heart of Heaven and Earth is uniquely concentrated in the sage, and with that heart the sage embraces all under Heaven. What, then, is the heart of Heaven and Earth? It is what is meant by the saying, “The great virtue of Heaven and Earth is called life-giving.” This is the principle of the Supreme Ultimate—that is, what is called benevolence. Heaven and Earth employ the principle of the Supreme Ultimate, which rides upon and becomes vital force [?]; thus the Two Modes remain established enduringly and without change. The sage employs the heart of Heaven and Earth, setting it in motion as vital force; thus…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
三才並立而無疆理以主氣氣以載理理不息
則氣亦不息天地之理以神運者也聖人之仁
以心運者也天地以神運故普萬物而不宰其
功聖人以心運故體萬物而不息其道此聖人
之仁所以同天地而其身與天地相爲悠久者
此也臨川吳氏曰聖人之仁如天地蓋言聖人
之壽而推本於仁也嗟乎其知言哉今夫天地
普萬物而無心者也人見其冲然穆然無聲無
臭奠位於兩間歷萬古而不磨矣乃自其二氣
===
之播盪萬象之糾紛輪輪駸駸以至於姤剝之
際若是其微甚也而一陽之氣眇於重淵如車
旋而轂運飜然無端焉此曷故也理運而不息
也天地以一元之理宰萬物旁皇周浹流動充
滿而不可以窮盡凡以弘其發育之神而物之
稟仰煦息生育收聚於其間者轉化推移而無
窮故曰復其見天地之心乎斯大生廣生之心
卽所謂仁也恒久而不已者也傳曰仁者人也
是天地之仁人皆得之以爲心者也乃獨聖人
punctuated: 三才並立而無疆。理以主氣，氣以載理；理不息，則氣亦不息。天地之理，以神運者也；聖人之仁，以心運者也。天地以神運，故普萬物而不宰其功；聖人以心運，故體萬物而不息其道。此聖人之仁所以同天地，而其身與天地相爲悠久者，此也。臨川吳氏曰：「聖人之仁如天地。」蓋言聖人之壽，而推本於仁也。嗟乎，其知言哉！今夫天地，普萬物而無心者也。人見其冲然穆然，無聲無臭，奠位於兩間，歷萬古而不磨矣。乃自其二氣之播盪，萬象之糾紛，輪輪駸駸，以至於姤剝之際，若是其微甚也。而一陽之氣，眇於重淵，如車旋而轂運，飜然無端焉。此曷故也？理運而不息也。天地以一元之理宰萬物，旁皇周浹，流動充滿，而不可以窮盡。凡以弘其發育之神，而物之稟仰煦息、生育收聚於其間者，轉化推移而無窮。故曰：「復，其見天地之心乎！」斯大生廣生之心，卽所謂仁也，恒久而不已者也。傳曰：「仁者，人也。」是天地之仁，人皆得之以爲心者也。乃獨聖人
translation_en:
…the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humanity—stand together without limit. Principle governs material force, and material force bears principle; if principle never ceases, material force likewise never ceases. The principle of Heaven and Earth operates through numinous efficacy; the benevolence of the sage operates through his mind. Because Heaven and Earth operate through numinous efficacy, they extend to all things without claiming mastery over their accomplishments. Because the sage operates through his mind, he embodies all things without ceasing to practice his Way. This is why the sage’s benevolence is like Heaven and Earth, and why he himself shares their enduring longevity. Master Wu of Linchuan said: “The sage’s benevolence resembles Heaven and Earth.” In speaking of the sage’s longevity, he traced its source back to benevolence. Ah, how well he understood these words!

Now, Heaven and Earth extend to all things without conscious intention. People see them as empty and serene, without sound or smell, established in their places within the cosmos, enduring through countless ages without wearing away. Yet as their two forces of yin and yang surge and stir, and the myriad phenomena intertwine in complexity, revolving and advancing [?], they reach the stages represented by Encounter (Gou) and Stripping Away (Bo), when yang has become exceedingly faint. Yet the force of the single yang, minute within the deep abyss, is like a turning carriage and its revolving hub, wheeling about without a discernible beginning. Why is this? Because principle operates without ceasing. Heaven and Earth govern all things through the principle of the primal unity, which moves everywhere and permeates everything, flowing and filling all space, inexhaustibly. All this extends their numinous power to bring forth and nurture life. The things within them that receive and depend upon their warming breath, that are born, nourished, gathered, and stored, undergo endless transformation and succession. Thus it is said: “In Return (Fu), do we not see the heart of Heaven and Earth!” This heart, which brings forth life in its greatness and breadth, is what is called benevolence: it endures without ceasing. The Commentary says: “Benevolence is humanity.” This benevolence of Heaven and Earth is something all people receive as their own mind. Yet only the sage…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之仁與天地竝何哉今夫盆水在庭清之終日
未能見眉睫濁之不過一撓而不能察方圓人
心易濁而難清猶盆水之類也若夫聖人之心
則龍門之津混沌之源也滔滔霍霍亘天地彌
古今行而不可得窮極也運而不可得把握也
嗚呼大哉其即天地之心乎蓋聖人通天下爲
一身而其心以天地萬物爲一體身居九重之
尊而慮周四海之外高拱穆清之上而神馳闉
闔之微思天下之有震風凌雨若塗泥之被已
===
視民之有疾痛疴癢若熛疽之刺心兼容倂包
與天地同其鴻洞也蟠委錯綜與萬物要其終
始也然聖人之仁非徒有是心也於是以治日
月之行調陰陽之氣節四時之度正律曆之數
以財成天地之道輔相天地之宜此聖人之仁
所以範圍天地也於是以明上下正百官訓三
農飭百工通商賈使男女不失時以偁老幼不
失時以養此聖人之仁所以保萬民也於是以
擾五典開三物聯師儒節以禮和以樂糾以刑
punctuated: 之仁與天地竝，何哉？今夫盆水在庭，清之終日，未能見眉睫；濁之不過一撓，而不能察方圓。人心易濁而難清，猶盆水之類也。若夫聖人之心，則龍門之津、混沌之源也。滔滔霍霍，亘天地，彌古今，行而不可得窮極也，運而不可得把握也。嗚呼，大哉！其即天地之心乎！蓋聖人通天下爲一身，而其心以天地萬物爲一體。身居九重之尊，而慮周四海之外；高拱穆清之上，而神馳闉闔之微。思天下之有震風凌雨，若塗泥之被已；視民之有疾痛疴癢，若熛疽之刺心。兼容倂包，與天地同其鴻洞也；蟠委錯綜，與萬物要其終始也。然聖人之仁，非徒有是心也。於是以治日月之行，調陰陽之氣，節四時之度，正律曆之數，以財成天地之道，輔相天地之宜。此聖人之仁所以範圍天地也。於是以明上下，正百官，訓三農，飭百工，通商賈，使男女不失時以偁，老幼不失時以養。此聖人之仁所以保萬民也。於是以擾五典，開三物，聯師儒，節以禮，和以樂，糾以刑，
translation_en:
…benevolence stands alongside that of Heaven and Earth—why is this? Consider a basin of water in a courtyard: let it settle all day, and one may still be unable to see one's eyebrows and eyelashes reflected in it; muddy it with a single disturbance, and one cannot distinguish square from round. The human heart is easily muddied and difficult to clear, much like this basin of water. The sage's heart, however, is like the waters at Longmen, the wellspring of primordial chaos. Surging and rushing, it extends throughout Heaven and Earth and fills past and present. Its flow cannot be exhausted; its movement cannot be grasped. Ah, how great it is! Is this not the very heart of Heaven and Earth?

The sage comprehends all under Heaven as a single body, and in his heart regards Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things as one entity. Though he occupies the exalted position within the ninefold palace, his concern extends beyond the Four Seas. Though he sits with hands folded in the lofty serenity of his court, his spirit hastens to the obscure recesses of the city gates. When he thinks of those throughout the realm exposed to violent winds and driving rain, it is as though mud covered his own body. When he sees the people's illnesses, pains, sores, and itching, it is as though a fiery ulcer pierced his own heart. Embracing and encompassing all, he shares the boundless expansiveness of Heaven and Earth; winding, extending, interweaving, and integrating, he comprehends the beginnings and endings of the myriad things.

Yet the sage's benevolence does not consist merely in possessing this heart. Thus he orders the courses of sun and moon, harmonizes the energies of yin and yang, regulates the measures of the four seasons, and corrects the calculations of the pitch standards and calendar. In this way he shapes and completes the Way of Heaven and Earth and assists their fitting operations. This is how the sage's benevolence encompasses Heaven and Earth. Thus he clarifies the distinction between superiors and inferiors, sets the officials in order, instructs the farmers, regulates the artisans, and facilitates commerce, ensuring that men and women are suitably paired at the proper time [?], and that old and young receive timely sustenance. This is how the sage's benevolence protects all the people. Thus he cultivates the five norms of human relationships, propagates the three branches of instruction, unites teachers and scholars, regulates through ritual, harmonizes through music, and corrects through punishments…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
厚載物德合无疆又曰安貞之吉應地无疆夫
天地之所以不息無疆者乃其心也而聖人之
心與之同不息無疆焉此仁之所以爲純也所
謂純亦不已者也雖然聖人之仁且有功於天
地焉豈直如之而已哉蓋自其醇德流乎四海
而誠信著於天下天不變經矣地不易形矣陰
陽訢合日月昭明上下輯睦而兵不試人民悅
懌而命無夭田者不侵畔漁者不爭隈鄙旅之
人不爭得協氣薰蒸鬱爲太和舉天下之民之
===
物咸熈然並登於壽域而不自知也所謂無關
鍵而不可開也無繩約而不可解也至是則聖
人之功烈不惟上際九天下契黃壚而兼有以
贊助之矣嗚呼此聖人所以終天地之功也而
莫非仁也所謂舉斯心加之而已矣道豈遠乎
哉
表
擬宋開天章閣引輔臣入對謝表〔慶曆三年〕
punctuated:
厚載物，德合无疆。又曰：「安貞之吉，應地无疆。」夫天地之所以不息無疆者，乃其心也，而聖人之心與之同不息無疆焉。此仁之所以爲純也，所謂純亦不已者也。雖然，聖人之仁且有功於天地焉，豈直如之而已哉？蓋自其醇德流乎四海，而誠信著於天下，天不變經矣，地不易形矣，陰陽訢合，日月昭明，上下輯睦而兵不試，人民悅懌而命無夭，田者不侵畔，漁者不爭隈，鄙旅之人不爭得。協氣薰蒸，鬱爲太和，舉天下之民之物，咸熈然並登於壽域而不自知也。所謂無關鍵而不可開也，無繩約而不可解也。至是，則聖人之功烈不惟上際九天，下契黃壚，而兼有以贊助之矣。嗚呼！此聖人所以終天地之功也，而莫非仁也。所謂舉斯心加之而已矣，道豈遠乎哉？

表

擬宋開天章閣引輔臣入對謝表〔慶曆三年〕
translation_en:
…in its thickness it bears all things, and its virtue accords with the boundless. It also says: “The good fortune of resting in steadfastness responds to the boundlessness of the earth.” What makes Heaven and Earth unceasing and boundless is their heart; the sage’s heart likewise shares their unceasingness and boundlessness. This is why his benevolence is pure: this is what is meant by saying that purity, too, never ceases. Yet the sage’s benevolence also renders service to Heaven and Earth. How could it merely resemble them?

When his pure virtue spreads throughout the Four Seas and his sincerity and trustworthiness become manifest throughout the world, Heaven does not alter its regular courses, and Earth does not change its form. Yin and yang blend harmoniously; the sun and moon shine brightly. Those above and below live in concord, and weapons are not put to use. The people are joyful, and none die before their time. Farmers do not encroach upon field boundaries; fishermen do not contend over sheltered bends. People in the borderlands and travelers do not vie for gain. Harmonious vital energies permeate all things, gathering abundantly into supreme harmony. All the people and creatures under Heaven together enter joyfully into the realm of longevity without even knowing it. This is what is meant by something that cannot be opened though it has no bolts or locks, and cannot be untied though it has no binding cords. At this point, the sage’s achievements not only reach upward to the nine heavens and accord below with the yellow earth, but also assist Heaven and Earth in their work.

Ah! This is how the sage brings the work of Heaven and Earth to completion, and none of it is other than benevolence. It is simply what is meant by taking this heart and extending it to others. How could the Way be far away?

Memorial

Draft Memorial of Thanks on the Song Emperor’s Opening of the Tianzhang Pavilion and Summoning of His Chief Councillors for an Audience 〔Third year of Qingli〕

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
潛邸賜節共崇保大之規
符瑞集景德以來何啻天球大訓
圖書等乾亨而上寧推帝典神謨
黃樞彤管之藏願治特存乎三鑑
玉牒青緗之貯貽謀燕及於百支顧石生文
動桃花之綽約臨流釃酒效蘭社以歡榮
協上下以承
天休
先帝肇基之志和神人以光
===
祖考
今皇肯構之心
號侈天開猶妨帶職
尊臨日表何幸致身玆蓋伏遇
〇〇〇〇
堯仁舜哲
禹儉湯寬
望道懷未見之憂無逸寓書於座右
視民切如傷之念有災密禱於禁中大辟
punctuated:
潛邸賜節，共崇保大之規。符瑞集景德以來，何啻天球大訓；圖書等乾亨而上，寧推帝典神謨。黃樞彤管之藏，願治特存乎三鑑；玉牒青緗之貯，貽謀燕及於百支。顧石生文，動桃花之綽約；臨流釃酒，效蘭社以歡榮。協上下以承天休，先帝肇基之志；和神人以光祖考，今皇肯構之心。
號侈天開，猶妨帶職；尊臨日表，何幸致身！玆蓋伏遇〇〇〇〇，堯仁舜哲，禹儉湯寬。望道懷未見之憂，無逸寓書於座右；視民切如傷之念，有災密禱於禁中。大辟
translation_en:
…Bestowing tokens of authority at the residence occupied before ascending the throne, together honoring the plan for preserving greatness. Auspicious portents have gathered since Jingde—how much more than the celestial jade and the Great Admonition! Books and charts rank with those of Qianheng and earlier [?]—why give precedence to the imperial canons and divine counsels? Among the writings preserved in the central palace, recorded by the vermilion brush, the desire for good government resides especially in the Three Mirrors; among the jade genealogies and books wrapped in blue silk, plans bequeathed to posterity extend blessings to a hundred branches of the lineage. Beholding patterns emerging from stone, stirring the graceful charm of peach blossoms [?]; straining wine beside the stream, emulating the Orchid Society in joyful celebration. To unite those above and below in receiving Heaven’s blessings was the former emperor’s intention in laying the foundations; to bring spirits and men into harmony and thereby glorify the ancestors is the present emperor’s resolve in carrying on the structure.
The designation, grand as the opening of Heaven, still hinders the concurrent holding of office [?]; with Your Majesty’s august presence before us, how fortunate we are to have attained this position! This, we humbly acknowledge, is because we have encountered 〇〇〇〇: possessing Yao’s benevolence and Shun’s wisdom, Yu’s frugality and Tang’s generosity. Seeking the Way, you harbor the concern of one who has not yet perceived it, keeping the text of Against Idleness beside your seat; regarding the people with the urgent solicitude one feels for the injured, you pray privately within the palace whenever calamity occurs. In capital cases…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
讞疑罪惟嚴於失入諸羌招討人惟任乎推
誠
宫庭施施繒之輕帷苑囿惜
玉清之舊地
煦媮求諫特除越職之條
寤寐親賢屢下直言之
詔崇
三朝之寶訓
顯謨丕啓於後人購
===
三館之逸書資善不衰於幼學當平世而
揚推溝之慮撫治民而
勞馭朽之思
巽命重申期有懷而必吐
豐亨長保責至治以無前
折節敷求
和顏采聽方槩
出和熹之貢慙阮檄以立成鏤毫
頒路扈之工愧禰篇之點綴安世備漢家顧
punctuated: 讞疑，罪惟嚴於失入；諸羌招討，人惟任乎推誠。宫庭施施繒之輕帷，苑囿惜玉清之舊地。煦媮求諫，特除越職之條；寤寐親賢，屢下直言之詔。崇三朝之寶訓，顯謨丕啓於後人；購三館之逸書，資善不衰於幼學。當平世而揚推溝之慮，撫治民而勞馭朽之思。巽命重申，期有懷而必吐；豐亨長保，責至治以無前。折節敷求，和顏采聽。方槩出和熹之貢，慙阮檄以立成；鏤毫頒路扈之工，愧禰篇之點綴。安世備漢家顧
translation_en:
…In adjudicating doubtful cases, you punish especially severely the wrongful imposition of guilt; in pacifying or campaigning against the various Qiang peoples, you entrust the task only to men who extend sincere good faith. In the palace, you hang light curtains of silk [?]; in the imperial parks, you spare the former grounds of Yuqing. Graciously seeking remonstrance, you expressly abolish the provision against exceeding one’s official responsibilities; intent, waking and sleeping, on drawing worthy men close, you repeatedly issue edicts inviting frank speech. You honor the Precious Instructions of the Three Reigns, whose illustrious counsels greatly enlighten later generations; you purchase books missing from the Three Institutes, sustaining the nourishment of virtue in youthful study.

In peaceful times, you nurture the concern of one who feels that he himself has pushed another into a ditch; tending a well-governed people, you trouble yourself as though driving with rotten reins. Your gracious commands are repeatedly proclaimed, in the expectation that whatever anyone has at heart will be fully expressed; enduring prosperity is to be preserved, and you demand governance of unprecedented excellence. You humble yourself to seek advice widely and receive it with a kindly countenance.

Square inksticks [?] come from the tribute associated with Hexi; we feel ashamed before Ruan’s instantly completed proclamation. Ornamented brushes are bestowed, the handiwork of Lu and Hu; we feel abashed before the embellishments of Mi’s composition. Anshi stood ready for the Han court’s inquiries…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
問持槖十年仲宣擅魏代文章屬詞一舉
豈其才由天賦或者事匪時艱登對必先
自盟豈以應酬而曲盡兼總而後臨決亦
由科品以施行臣某等同典
樞衡與參
密勿雖後樂先憂之志在昔已存而
上嘉下樂之心於今難稱仰瞻
羣翰炳雲漢之昭回俯鞠微軀奉
天顏於咫尺空言無補豈敢以應
===
側席之求謙讓未遑安得而稱轉樞之義學
不足以待問惟
仁明矜察其愚事有待於條陳望
神聖終成其美庶幾
革孚巳日而文明之化以彰
德積百年而禮樂之功攸建
太平歌頌日聞天保之章
遵養純熈永息采薇之詠
道與天而無極
punctuated: 問，持槖十年；仲宣擅魏代文章，屬詞一舉。豈其才由天賦，或者事匪時艱？登對必先自盟，豈以應酬而曲盡？兼總而後臨決，亦由科品以施行。臣某等同典樞衡，與參密勿。雖後樂先憂之志在昔已存，而上嘉下樂之心於今難稱。仰瞻羣翰，炳雲漢之昭回；俯鞠微軀，奉天顏於咫尺。空言無補，豈敢以應側席之求？謙讓未遑，安得而稱轉樞之義？學不足以待問，惟仁明矜察其愚；事有待於條陳，望神聖終成其美。庶幾革孚巳日，而文明之化以彰；德積百年，而禮樂之功攸建。太平歌頌，日聞《天保》之章；遵養純熈，永息《采薇》之詠。道與天而無極，
translation_en:
…questions, bearing the satchel in attendance for ten years; Zhongxuan excelled in the literary compositions of the Wei age, completing his writing at a single attempt. Was their ability bestowed by Heaven, or were the affairs they faced free of the difficulties of their times? Before appearing in audience to reply, one must first pledge oneself: how could merely responding to the occasion suffice to address everything fully? One must consider matters comprehensively before deciding them, and implement them according to their categories and ranks.

We, your servants So-and-so and the others, jointly hold responsibility for the pivotal work of government and participate in confidential deliberations. Although we have long cherished the resolve to worry before others and enjoy ease after them, we now find it difficult to fulfill the wish to win approval above and bring joy below. Looking upward, we behold the assembled writings, radiant as the wheeling River of Heaven; bowing our insignificant persons, we attend upon the imperial countenance at close quarters. Empty words offer no benefit: how could we dare use them to answer Your Majesty’s earnest quest for worthy counsel? Nor have we leisure to yield modestly: how else could we fulfill the duty of turning the pivot of government?

Our learning is insufficient to answer your questions; we ask only that Your Majesty, benevolent and discerning, compassionately recognize our ignorance. Matters await our detailed presentation; we hope that Your Majesty, sagely and wise, will bring them to a worthy conclusion. May change win trust when its day has come [?], so that the transforming influence of cultivated enlightenment becomes manifest; may virtue accumulate for a hundred years, so that the achievements of rites and music are established. Amid songs praising great peace, may the verses of “Heaven Protects” (Tian bao) be heard daily; may we nurture pure and radiant virtue, forever putting to rest the singing of “Gathering Bracken” (Cai wei). May the Way, together with Heaven, be without limit…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
治率土以攸同伏願
有大不盈
無斁亦保
明四目達四聰益振合宫之鞀鐸
愼五刑敷五敎丕冒遐服之侏離臣等無任
瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
===
謝以
聞
第叁塲
策
第一問
周思充
同考試官敎諭任批〔我〕
〔聖祖皇上心學淵源純王政迹子能歷歷□□篇涵濡之久而有得者取之〕
punctuated:
治率土以攸同。伏願有大不盈，無斁亦保；明四目，達四聰，益振合宫之鞀鐸；愼五刑，敷五敎，丕冒遐服之侏離。臣等無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。

第叁塲
策
第一問
周思充
同考試官敎諭任批〔我〕〔聖祖皇上心學淵源，純王政迹，子能歷歷□□篇，涵濡之久而有得者，取之。〕
translation_en:
…and governance brings all beneath Heaven into harmony. We humbly pray that, possessing greatness, you remain free of complacency and, never wearying, preserve it. Make clear your vision in all four directions and open your hearing to all quarters, further setting in motion the drum and bell of the ceremonial palace through which counsel is sought. Exercise care in the five punishments and spread the five teachings, extending your beneficence widely to the foreign-speaking peoples of distant lands. We, your servants, gaze toward Heaven and look up to Your Majesty with the utmost fervor and trembling awe. We respectfully submit this memorial to express our gratitude for your hearing.

Third Session
Policy Essays
First Question
Zhou Sichong
Comment by Associate Examiner Ren, Instructor: 〔Our〕〔sagely founding emperor and reigning emperor—the profound sources of their learning of the mind and their achievements in purely kingly government—you have clearly [two illegible characters] in this essay [?]. You have long immersed yourself in this learning and gained understanding from it. I select this essay.〕

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
皇上會千聖於一心通萬古於一理藏諸用爲
日新之
盛德顯諸仁爲富有之
大業蕩蕩乎無能名巍巍乎不可及者抑非
職此之故哉請因明問所及而敬陳之今
夫天之立君以爲民也君之立政以致治
也論治者必基於道論道者必根諸心雖
聖人之治天下亦有不能外者然道豈外
於天乎詩曰維天之命於穆不已言天之
===
神也而聖人心學之精涵於是矣易曰乾
道變化各正性命言天之化也而聖人經
綸之迹蘊於此矣道之大原出於天而道
之精微闡於聖嘗考唐虞三代之世堯舜
禹湯文武之爲君率皆本精一執中之傳
衍爲聖學之家法由典謨訓誥之著布爲
經世之徽猷故語其德則爲天德而天下
之言至聖者必歸焉語其道則爲王道而
天下之言至治者必歸焉嗚呼遐哉不可
punctuated: 皇上會千聖於一心，通萬古於一理，藏諸用爲日新之盛德，顯諸仁爲富有之大業，蕩蕩乎無能名，巍巍乎不可及者，抑非職此之故哉？請因明問所及而敬陳之。今夫天之立君以爲民也，君之立政以致治也。論治者必基於道，論道者必根諸心，雖聖人之治天下，亦有不能外者。然道豈外於天乎？《詩》曰：「維天之命，於穆不已。」言天之神也，而聖人心學之精涵於是矣。《易》曰：「乾道變化，各正性命。」言天之化也，而聖人經綸之迹蘊於此矣。道之大原出於天，而道之精微闡於聖。嘗考唐虞三代之世，堯舜禹湯文武之爲君，率皆本精一執中之傳，衍爲聖學之家法；由典謨訓誥之著，布爲經世之徽猷。故語其德，則爲天德，而天下之言至聖者必歸焉；語其道，則爲王道，而天下之言至治者必歸焉。嗚呼，遐哉！不可
translation_en: Your Majesty unites the thousand sages within a single mind and comprehends all ages through a single principle. Hidden in its functioning, this constitutes your magnificent virtue, renewed daily; manifested in benevolence, it constitutes your great undertaking, abundant in its possessions. So vast that it cannot be named, so lofty that it cannot be reached—is this not precisely owing to this principle? Allow me respectfully to set forth my thoughts on the matters raised in your discerning question. Heaven establishes rulers for the sake of the people; rulers establish government to achieve good order. Those who discuss governance must ground it in the Way, and those who discuss the Way must root it in the mind. Even the sages, in governing all under Heaven, could not depart from this. Yet could the Way lie outside Heaven? The Book of Odes says: “Heaven’s mandate—how profound and unceasing!” This speaks of Heaven’s numinous power, and within it is contained the quintessence of the sages’ learning of the mind. The Book of Changes says: “The Way of Qian changes and transforms, each thing attaining its proper nature and allotted destiny.” This speaks of Heaven’s transforming activity, and within it are contained the patterns of the sages’ ordering of the world. The great source of the Way issues from Heaven, while its subtle profundities are elucidated by the sages. I have examined the ages of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties: as rulers, Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu all took as their foundation the transmitted teaching of refinement, singleness of purpose, and holding fast to the Mean, developing it into the inherited discipline of sagely learning. Through its written expression in the canons, counsels, instructions, and proclamations, they disseminated admirable plans for ordering the world. Thus, when one speaks of their virtue, it is the virtue of Heaven, and all under Heaven who speak of supreme sagehood must turn to them. When one speaks of their Way, it is the Kingly Way, and all under Heaven who speak of consummate governance must turn to them. Ah, how lofty and far-reaching! It cannot …

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
要莫大於脩身矣而至講財用則有德厚
人懷之論謂節用愛人爲治國之良規矣
而至講孟子則有專言仁義之稱自其究
意於史也如
御白虎殿論漢史則於文帝而責以禮樂之
當興焉於武帝而惜其用心之未善焉
御左閤論宋史則於太宗而譏其内藏之治
焉於真宗而鄙其天書之惑焉謂唐之太
宗賞罰服人矣而於玄宗則短其賢能之
===
未用謂元之初年君臣味道矣而於元季
則傷其致亂之有由是所以發明經史而
稽政事之得失者審矣至於
御製文集究天體七曜之循環以原法象之始
咨天地二儀之高厚以闡運數之精少傅
楊士奇以爲深得古人之精蘊
御註洪範先之五行五事八政五紀以推皇極
之體繼之三德稽疑庶徵福極以昭皇極
之用贊善劉三吾謂其爲萬世開太平
punctuated:
要莫大於脩身矣，而至講財用，則有德厚人懷之論；謂節用愛人爲治國之良規矣，而至講孟子，則有專言仁義之稱。自其究意於史也，如御白虎殿論漢史，則於文帝而責以禮樂之當興焉，於武帝而惜其用心之未善焉；御左閤論宋史，則於太宗而譏其内藏之治焉，於真宗而鄙其天書之惑焉；謂唐之太宗賞罰服人矣，而於玄宗則短其賢能之未用；謂元之初年君臣味道矣，而於元季則傷其致亂之有由。是所以發明經史而稽政事之得失者審矣。
至於御製文集，究天體七曜之循環，以原法象之始；咨天地二儀之高厚，以闡運數之精。少傅楊士奇以爲深得古人之精蘊。御註《洪範》，先之五行、五事、八政、五紀，以推皇極之體；繼之三德、稽疑、庶徵、福極，以昭皇極之用。贊善劉三吾謂其爲萬世開太平。
translation_en:
…nothing is more important than cultivating oneself. When he lectured on financial resources and expenditure, he discussed how abundant virtue wins the people's affection. He declared that economizing in expenditure and caring for the people were sound principles for governing a state; when lecturing on the Mencius, he praised its exclusive emphasis on benevolence and righteousness. His close attention to history was evident, for example, when he presided in Baihu Hall and discussed Han history: he faulted Emperor Wen for failing to promote rites and music, and regretted that Emperor Wu had not directed his efforts well. When he presided in the Left Pavilion and discussed Song history, he criticized Taizong's management of the inner treasury and disparaged Zhenzong's delusion concerning the heavenly writings. He observed that Tang Taizong won people's allegiance through rewards and punishments, but faulted Xuanzong for failing to employ worthy and capable men. He said that the rulers and ministers of the early Yuan savored the Way, but lamented the causes that brought disorder in the dynasty's final years. Thus he elucidated the classics and histories and carefully examined successes and failures in government.
As for his collected imperial writings, he investigated the cycles of the celestial bodies—the seven luminaries—to trace the origins of celestial patterns. He inquired into the height and depth of the two powers, Heaven and Earth, to elucidate the subtleties of cosmic cycles and numbers. Junior Preceptor Yang Shiqi considered that he had profoundly grasped the essential wisdom of the ancients. In his imperial commentary on the Great Plan (Hongfan), he began with the Five Phases, Five Activities, Eight Affairs of Government, and Five Regulators of Time to explore the substance of the August Norm. He followed these with the Three Virtues, Examination of Doubts, Various Verifications, and Blessings and Extremities to illuminate the August Norm's operation. Assistant Adviser Liu Sanwu said that it inaugurated great peace for all generations.

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
述以備
圜丘之配尊崇至也
祖德之和淵源通也其見於法
祖之孝者如此祇
玄穹以立心極一文王之於穆也純至道以凝
元精一成湯之日躋也他如翊學有詩以
匡正道除夕有作以示修省而所以敬
身者何弗至耶遇旱澇則祈禱必
躬卽桑林自責之心也重民命則欽恤屢
===
詔卽刑期無刑之意也他如憫農之作以念民
天
內帑之發以溥賑恤而所以勤民者何弗至
耶蓋合
中和而交致舉倫制以兼脩肫肫乎以
心會之而天下之道不見其有餘亹亹然以
身體之而天下之治不見其不足此其
學其政卽
聖祖純天之學也謂之卽天之神可也卽
punctuated: 述以備圜丘之配，尊崇至也；祖德之和，淵源通也。其見於法祖之孝者如此。祇玄穹以立心，極一文王之於穆也；純至道以凝元，精一成湯之日躋也。他如翊學有詩以匡正道，除夕有作以示修省，而所以敬身者何弗至耶？遇旱澇則祈禱必躬，卽桑林自責之心也；重民命則欽恤屢詔，卽刑期無刑之意也。他如憫農之作以念民天，內帑之發以溥賑恤，而所以勤民者何弗至耶？蓋合中和而交致，舉倫制以兼脩，肫肫乎以心會之，而天下之道不見其有餘；亹亹然以身體之，而天下之治不見其不足。此其學其政，卽聖祖純天之學也。謂之卽天之神可也，卽
translation_en:
…set forth to provide for the ancestral co-sacrifice at the Circular Mound [?]: reverence and exaltation reach their utmost; the harmony of ancestral virtue flows from a common source. Such are the manifestations of his filial devotion in following his ancestors’ example. Reverently serving high Heaven to establish his purpose, he is wholly at one with King Wen’s profound solemnity; perfecting the supreme Way to consolidate his fundamental spirit, he is at one, in purity and singleness, with Cheng Tang’s daily advancement. Likewise, he composed poems supporting learning to uphold the correct Way, and writings on New Year’s Eve to demonstrate self-cultivation and self-examination. In what respect, then, did his reverent care for his own conduct fail to reach its utmost? When droughts or floods occurred, he invariably offered prayers in person: this was the same spirit of self-reproach shown at the Mulberry Grove. Valuing the people’s lives, he repeatedly issued edicts calling for reverence and compassion in administering punishment: this expressed the intention of using punishment to bring about an end to punishment. Likewise, his composition expressing sympathy for farmers showed concern for food, which is the people’s Heaven; his disbursement of funds from the imperial treasury extended relief widely. In what respect, then, did his diligent care for the people fail to reach its utmost?

He brought equilibrium and harmony together, fully realizing both, and cultivated human relationships and institutions alike. With utter sincerity he apprehended them in his heart, and nothing in the Way of the world lay beyond his grasp; with tireless diligence he embodied them in his conduct, and nothing was lacking in his governance of the world. His learning and government were precisely the Sagely Ancestor’s learning of complete accord with Heaven. One may say that he was at one with Heaven’s spiritual efficacy, at one with…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
皇上裁酌至精誠萬世彝憲也此篇援古證今鋪張曲盡可謂學識其大矣
同考試官學正李批場中多蕪舊聞能詳
昭代之制者僅見是篇宜錄以式
考試官教諭管批發明祀典戎務詳盡
考試官教諭李批舉爼豆軍旅而兼得者
帝王承天以御世也統宗百神有崇祀之
大禮焉控制六合有經武之大政焉夫禮
以虔祀非徒以備文也由內心之敬而致
外典之仁敬則禮不瀆仁則恩不遺此王
===
者所以建中和之極而精誠達於兩間者
也政以飭戎非徒以耀武也脩內治之德
而振外攘之威德則懷其衷威則懲其玩
此王者所以弘招携之略而神武著於四
國者也是故祀典行則百神受職而天下
莫不化矣戎政飭則萬方順軌而天下莫
不肅矣然訏謨默運神經緯於一心猶之
化工潜孚宰陰陽於一元者也皇皇哉豈
非帝王之宏謨神聖之殊軌哉如此則我
punctuated:
皇上裁酌至精，誠萬世彝憲也。此篇援古證今，鋪張曲盡，可謂學識其大矣。

同考試官學正李批：場中多蕪舊聞，能詳昭代之制者，僅見是篇，宜錄以式。

考試官教諭管批：發明祀典戎務詳盡。

考試官教諭李批：舉爼豆軍旅而兼得者。

帝王承天以御世也，統宗百神，有崇祀之大禮焉；控制六合，有經武之大政焉。夫禮以虔祀，非徒以備文也。由內心之敬，而致外典之仁，敬則禮不瀆，仁則恩不遺。此王者所以建中和之極，而精誠達於兩間者也。政以飭戎，非徒以耀武也。脩內治之德，而振外攘之威，德則懷其衷，威則懲其玩。此王者所以弘招携之略，而神武著於四國者也。是故祀典行，則百神受職，而天下莫不化矣；戎政飭，則萬方順軌，而天下莫不肅矣。然訏謨默運，神經緯於一心，猶之化工潜孚，宰陰陽於一元者也。皇皇哉！豈非帝王之宏謨、神聖之殊軌哉？如此，則我
translation_en:
… His Majesty’s deliberations and adjustments are supremely refined: truly an enduring norm for ten thousand generations. This essay draws upon antiquity to substantiate present practice, developing its exposition fully and exhaustively. Its learning and discernment may indeed be called great.

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, School Instructor: Most scripts in this examination offer a confused treatment of received knowledge [?]. This is the only essay I have seen that can explain in detail the institutions of our illustrious dynasty. It should be recorded as a model.

Comment by Examiner Guan, Instructor: Its elucidation of sacrificial regulations and military affairs is detailed and comprehensive.

Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: It takes up both sacrificial vessels and military affairs, attaining a sound understanding of both.

Emperors and kings receive Heaven’s mandate to govern the world. Presiding over the hundred spirits, they possess the great rites for honoring them with sacrifices; commanding the six directions, they possess the great policies for ordering military affairs. Ritual serves to offer sacrifices reverently, not merely to furnish outward forms. Through reverence within the heart, one realizes benevolence in outward observances. With reverence, ritual is not profaned; with benevolence, none is omitted from gracious favor. This is how the true king establishes the supreme standard of equilibrium and harmony, and his perfect sincerity reaches throughout Heaven and Earth.

Government serves to put military affairs in order, not merely to display martial power. One cultivates the virtue of internal government and arouses the might needed to repel external threats. Virtue wins their hearts; might chastises their insolence. This is how the true king extends his strategy for attracting those who have become estranged, and his numinous martial power becomes manifest throughout the lands of the four quarters. Thus, when sacrificial regulations are carried out, the hundred spirits receive their appointed duties, and none under Heaven fails to be transformed. When military administration is put in order, the myriad regions follow the proper course, and none under Heaven fails to become respectful.

Yet great counsels operate silently, their ordering accomplished wondrously within a single mind, just as the workings of creation exert their influence unseen, governing yin and yang through the single primal source. How magnificent! Are these not the grand counsels of emperors and kings, the extraordinary ways of divine sages? If so, then our …

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
天威迅發以議將為首務則於文武督總之臣
必極一時之選而一不稱則易置之以軍
供為急需則於兵士糧餉之備悉從諸臣
之議而請
內帑則速給之於是封豕殪於塵沙漸以銷
其彎弓竊視之念長鯨斬於瀚海竟以寢
其揚帆鼓譟之謀
神功耀於宇宙而駿烈震乎雷霆豈非增光往
號流聲來諜者哉夫我
===
聖祖開創於往初而
皇上覲揚於今日後先相映浸明浸昌非偶然
也蓋精玄之極孚感百靈合仁與敬而咸
備者
聖人之所以同天德也鼓舞之機光濟六合兼
德與威而並盛者
聖人之所以同王道也猗與盛哉然愚聞之動
天地感鬼神莫近乎禮樂今
國家禮制誠明備矣而樂猶有待焉
punctuated:
天威迅發，以議將為首務，則於文武督總之臣，必極一時之選，而一不稱則易置之；以軍供為急需，則於兵士糧餉之備，悉從諸臣之議，而請內帑則速給之。於是封豕殪於塵沙，漸以銷其彎弓竊視之念；長鯨斬於瀚海，竟以寢其揚帆鼓譟之謀。神功耀於宇宙，而駿烈震乎雷霆，豈非增光往號、流聲來諜者哉？
夫我聖祖開創於往初，而皇上覲揚於今日，後先相映，浸明浸昌，非偶然也。蓋精玄之極，孚感百靈，合仁與敬而咸備者，聖人之所以同天德也；鼓舞之機，光濟六合，兼德與威而並盛者，聖人之所以同王道也。猗與盛哉！
然愚聞之，動天地、感鬼神，莫近乎禮樂。今國家禮制誠明備矣，而樂猶有待焉。
translation_en:
…Heavenly might was swiftly unleashed. Taking the selection of commanders as the foremost task, Your Majesty chose the very best men of the age from among the civil and military officials charged with overall command, replacing any who proved unequal to their duties. Taking military supplies as an urgent necessity, you followed your ministers’ proposals in full concerning provisions and pay for the troops, and promptly granted requests for funds from the imperial treasury. Thus the great boars were slain amid dust and sand, gradually extinguishing their designs to bend their bows and watch for an opening; the great whales were beheaded upon the vast sea, finally putting an end to their schemes to hoist their sails and raise their battle cries. Your divine achievements shine throughout the universe, and your mighty exploits resound like thunder. Does this not add glory to earlier renown [?] and transmit your fame to the records of future ages [?]?
Our sagely ancestor founded the dynasty in former times, while Your Majesty carries forward its glory today. Predecessor and successor illuminate one another, growing ever brighter and more flourishing: this is no accident. Utmost spiritual refinement [?], whose sincerity moves the hundred spirits and in which benevolence and reverence are fully united, is how the sage shares Heaven’s virtue. The animating power that splendidly brings aid throughout the six directions, in which virtue and might flourish together, is how the sage accords with the Kingly Way. Ah, how magnificent!
Yet I, in my ignorance, have heard that nothing approaches ritual and music in moving Heaven and Earth and stirring ghosts and spirits. Today the state’s ritual institutions are indeed clearly established and complete, but music still awaits further attention.

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
廟堂之上得無加意於斯乎愚又聞之聖王
貴未然之防而忠臣謹先事之慮今
國家武功誠大振矣然周公克詰戎兵之訓
召公張皇六師之言非羣工所當共勵者
乎愚生媿無鴻筆以宣昭
國家之盛美乃願自效其一得如此惟執事
採焉
第三問
劉伯淵
===
同考試官教諭韓批〔天人之際未易言者子能洞究微奧取諸家之說而折衷之可以釋羣疑矣〕
同考試官教諭蘇批〔占候一篇場中多剿竊陳言殊厭觀覽此作析理詳明足以破諸說而有裨於敬畏者錄之〕
考試官教諭管批〔詳論候占之法殆盡〕
考試官教諭李批〔是有究心天文者〕
天有至文聖人有至道至文者垂象著明
而經緯於天者也至道者履信思順而綜
理民物者也天之所示無有災祥愆若而
punctuated:
廟堂之上，得無加意於斯乎？愚又聞之：聖王貴未然之防，而忠臣謹先事之慮。今國家武功誠大振矣，然周公克詰戎兵之訓、召公張皇六師之言，非羣工所當共勵者乎？愚生媿無鴻筆以宣昭國家之盛美，乃願自效其一得如此，惟執事採焉。

第三問
劉伯淵

同考試官教諭韓批〔天人之際，未易言者。子能洞究微奧，取諸家之說而折衷之，可以釋羣疑矣。〕
同考試官教諭蘇批〔占候一篇，場中多剿竊陳言，殊厭觀覽。此作析理詳明，足以破諸說而有裨於敬畏者，錄之。〕
考試官教諭管批〔詳論候占之法，殆盡。〕
考試官教諭李批〔是有究心天文者。〕

天有至文，聖人有至道。至文者，垂象著明而經緯於天者也；至道者，履信思順而綜理民物者也。天之所示，無有災祥愆若，而
translation_en:
Might those at court give further attention to this? I have also heard that sage kings prize precautions against troubles before they arise, while loyal ministers carefully consider affairs before they occur. Now the dynasty’s military prowess has indeed been greatly enhanced. Yet are the Duke of Zhou’s injunction to put military forces in good order and the Duke of Shao’s words about displaying the might of the Six Armies not teachings that all officials should together strive to uphold? I, an unworthy scholar, am ashamed that I lack the literary talent to proclaim the dynasty’s magnificent achievements. I nevertheless wish to offer this modest insight in service, and ask that you, honored officials, consider it.

Third Policy Question
Liu Boyuan

Comment by Associate Examiner Han, Instructor: 〔The relationship between Heaven and humanity is no easy matter to discuss. You have thoroughly investigated its subtle profundities and weighed the explanations of various schools to arrive at a balanced judgment. This can resolve many doubts.〕
Comment by Associate Examiner Su, Instructor: 〔In essays on prognostication from celestial phenomena, many candidates have plagiarized stale sayings, making them exceedingly tiresome to read. This essay analyzes the principles clearly and in detail. It can refute the various explanations and help foster reverence and awe. I select it for inclusion.〕
Comment by Examiner Guan, Instructor: 〔The detailed discussion of methods of observation and prognostication is nearly exhaustive.〕
Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: 〔Here is someone who has devoted serious thought to celestial patterns.〕

Heaven has its supreme patterns; the sage has his supreme Way. The supreme patterns are the manifest signs displayed above, forming the warp and weft of Heaven. The supreme Way consists in acting with trustworthiness, considering what accords with proper order, and comprehensively governing the people and all things. Whatever Heaven displays, whether calamitous or auspicious, aberrant or favorable [?], and…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
宰羣動以歸大順者其極則天之極也孔
子曰為政以德辟如此辰居其所而眾星
共之言王者之成象於天也彼中宮之星
列於三垣者為紫微太微天市以象帝居
環以后王宰執百官御事各備其人列為
衛掖車肆權量貨貿各備其事則宅中之
位成矣二十八宿復以次分布於外東方
自角以下則為天闕為內庭為路寢為明
堂正位以及後宮之場皆奠其居北方自
===
斗以下則為襃賢為犧牲為布帛為祝禱
天府以至土功之事圖書之祕皆治其職
西方自奎而參則主武庫苑牧內帑外胡
以至天街邊陲三軍主師之屬莫不秩然
而類聚也南方自井而軫則主水衡天目
厨宰服御以至珍寶樂府輔臣冢宰之司
莫不燦然而羣分也故曰官於中外常明
者百二十有四可名者百有二十為星二
千五百其微則萬有一千五百二十當萬
punctuated: 宰羣動以歸大順者，其極則天之極也。孔子曰：「為政以德，辟如此辰，居其所而眾星共之。」言王者之成象於天也。彼中宮之星，列於三垣者，為紫微、太微、天市，以象帝居；環以后王、宰執、百官御事，各備其人；列為衛掖、車肆、權量、貨貿，各備其事，則宅中之位成矣。二十八宿，復以次分布於外。東方自角以下，則為天闕、為內庭、為路寢、為明堂正位，以及後宮之場，皆奠其居。北方自斗以下，則為襃賢、為犧牲、為布帛、為祝禱、天府，以至土功之事、圖書之祕，皆治其職。西方自奎而參，則主武庫、苑牧、內帑、外胡，以至天街、邊陲、三軍主師之屬，莫不秩然而類聚也。南方自井而軫，則主水衡、天目、厨宰、服御，以至珍寶、樂府、輔臣、冢宰之司，莫不燦然而羣分也。故曰：「官於中外，常明者百二十有四，可名者百有二十，為星二千五百，其微則萬有一千五百二十，當萬
translation_en:
…governing all movements so that they return to perfect concord: its ultimate standard is Heaven’s own ultimate standard. Confucius said: “To govern through virtue is like this star [?]: it remains in its place while the multitude of stars pays it homage.” This speaks of how the king’s rule takes visible form in Heaven. The stars of the central palace, arranged in the Three Enclosures—the Purple Tenuity Enclosure (Ziwei), the Supreme Tenuity Enclosure (Taiwei), and the Celestial Market Enclosure (Tianshi)—represent the imperial residence. Around them are sovereigns, chief ministers, and the various officials charged with duties, each corresponding person being present. They are arrayed as palace guards and side courts, carriages and markets, weights and measures, and goods and trade, each corresponding activity being provided for. Thus the arrangement of the seat at the center is complete.

The Twenty-Eight Lunar Lodges are in turn distributed in sequence around the outside. In the east, beginning with Jiao, they represent the celestial gate towers, the inner court, the principal palace chamber, the principal seat in the Hall of Enlightenment, and the precincts of the rear palace: each has its established abode. In the north, beginning with Dou, they represent the honoring of the worthy, sacrificial animals, cloth and silk, prayers, and the celestial treasury, extending to earthworks and the secrets of charts and writings: each attends to its duties. In the west, from Kui to Shen, they preside over the arsenal, parks and pastures, the inner treasury, and foreign Hu peoples, extending to the celestial avenue, the frontier, and the commanders of the three armies: all are ordered and gathered according to kind. In the south, from Jing to Zhen, they preside over the Superintendent of Waterways, the Celestial Eye, cooks and stewards, and imperial clothing and equipment, extending to precious treasures, the Music Bureau, assisting ministers, and the office of the chief minister: all are brilliantly displayed and divided into groups.

Thus it is said: “Among the celestial offices within and without, those constantly visible number one hundred and twenty-four, and those that can be named number one hundred and twenty; together they comprise two thousand five hundred stars. Their faint stars number eleven thousand five hundred and twenty, corresponding to ten thousand …

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
以令名而不復掌中祕矣再傳而以甘石
巫咸並列三家則星紀遂失其官而不復
達於民故矣其間惟司馬遷盡廢一十七
家之術而本乎星律以脩太初故晦朔弦
望始有其端而粗得乎敬授之意唐一行
盡變二十三家之法而本于蓍策以歸大
衍故章蔀紀元始合於易而不失乎謹始
之義此星數之理最爲獨得而非徒以占
候名者也然則人君者惟能宣節和氣輔
===
相物宜則先天弗違而盡性立命之化昭
矣人臣者惟能祇承上下寅恭協和則後
天時行而調元贊化之功備矣由是夭疾
不作衣食無奪君尊民悅而禮敎行則百
姓和於下矣由是而五穀熟桑麻遂草木
茂鳥獸蕃則百物和於野矣其有不迪不
吉不庭不若之徒莫不應德而至又何憂
乎垂象之失軌而亦事於渾蓋以求合耶
其不然者雖含譽晨明終無補於祥符之
punctuated:
以令名，而不復掌中祕矣。再傳而以甘石、巫咸並列三家，則星紀遂失其官，而不復達於民故矣。其間惟司馬遷盡廢一十七家之術，而本乎星律以脩太初，故晦朔弦望始有其端，而粗得乎敬授之意。唐一行盡變二十三家之法，而本于蓍策以歸大衍，故章蔀紀元始合於易，而不失乎謹始之義。此星數之理最爲獨得，而非徒以占候名者也。
然則人君者惟能宣節和氣，輔相物宜，則先天弗違，而盡性立命之化昭矣。人臣者惟能祇承上下，寅恭協和，則後天時行，而調元贊化之功備矣。由是夭疾不作，衣食無奪，君尊民悅而禮敎行，則百姓和於下矣。由是而五穀熟，桑麻遂，草木茂，鳥獸蕃，則百物和於野矣。其有不迪、不吉、不庭、不若之徒，莫不應德而至，又何憂乎垂象之失軌，而亦事於渾蓋以求合耶？其不然者，雖含譽晨明，終無補於祥符之
translation_en:
…with a fine reputation, but no longer in charge of the palace’s secret records. After a further transmission, Gan and Shi were ranked alongside Wu Xian as the three schools; thus celestial reckoning lost its responsible officials and no longer addressed the affairs of the people. Among these figures, only Sima Qian wholly discarded the techniques of the seventeen schools and grounded his work in celestial and pitch-pipe standards to compile the Taichu calendar. Only then were the last and first days of the lunar month, the quarter moons, and the full moon properly established, approximately realizing the intention of reverently communicating the seasons to the people. Under the Tang, Yixing completely transformed the methods of the twenty-three schools, grounding his work in yarrow-stalk calculations to arrive at the Dayan calendar. Thus the calendrical cycles—zhang, bu, ji, and yuan—at last accorded with the Book of Changes, preserving the principle of attending carefully to beginnings.
