These men attained a uniquely profound understanding of astronomical calculation; their renown did not rest merely on observing celestial signs and interpreting omens.
Thus, if the ruler can disseminate and regulate harmonious vital energy and assist all things in attaining what suits them, he may precede Heaven without contravening it, and the transforming influence that fully realizes innate nature and establishes Heaven’s mandate will become manifest. If ministers can reverently serve those above and below, working together with respectful diligence, they may follow Heaven and act at the proper times, fully accomplishing their work of harmonizing primordial energy and assisting transformation. Consequently, premature death and illness will not arise, none will be deprived of clothing or food, the ruler will be honored, the people content, and ritual instruction put into practice: the common people below will then be in harmony. Consequently, the five grains will ripen, mulberry and hemp flourish, plants and trees grow luxuriantly, and birds and beasts multiply: all things in the countryside will then be in harmony. Even those who do not follow the Way, who are inauspicious, who refuse to attend court, or who are disobedient will all respond to virtue and come. Why, then, worry that the signs displayed in the heavens might depart from their courses, or labor over the spherical-heaven and canopy-heaven systems to seek agreement? If this is not achieved, even Hanyu and Chenming [?] will ultimately contribute nothing to the auspicious tokens of…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
經以事詞勝則爲紀載由伏羲以至堯舜
周孔其心同也其道同也自時厥後七十
子喪而微言絕異端起而大義漓一降而
春秋再降而戰國浸淫于秦漢以極于六
朝五季雖曰先秦西漢其尤也唐文三變
其盛也而不知學無得于心則文弗載乎
道輪轅飾而人弗庸殆虛車也而又奚尚
乎論者猶謂秦漢以前渾然殆非知文者
矣是故國語精而弱柳宗元非之以明巽
===
左氏辨而富韓愈氏卑之以明浮戰國策
利而巧朱子以縱橫闔闢而示譏是先秦
之文也而非三代之文也過秦有論治安
有策賈誼可謂通達國體矣而三表五餌
班固病其失之疎上林子虛諸作司馬相
如可謂詭練奇偉矣而諷一勸百班固病
其失之靡三篇獨對賢良稱首董仲舒正
誼明道之學也而柔行巽入縱陰閉陽朱
子病其失之雜是西漢之文也而非三代
punctuated:
經以事詞勝，則爲紀載。由伏羲以至堯舜、周孔，其心同也，其道同也。自時厥後，七十子喪而微言絕，異端起而大義漓。一降而春秋，再降而戰國，浸淫于秦漢，以極于六朝五季。雖曰先秦西漢其尤也，唐文三變其盛也，而不知學無得于心，則文弗載乎道。輪轅飾而人弗庸，殆虛車也，而又奚尚乎？論者猶謂秦漢以前渾然，殆非知文者矣。
是故《國語》精而弱，柳宗元非之以明巽；左氏辨而富，韓愈氏卑之以明浮；《戰國策》利而巧，朱子以縱橫闔闢而示譏。是先秦之文也，而非三代之文也。《過秦》有論，《治安》有策，賈誼可謂通達國體矣，而三表五餌，班固病其失之疎。《上林》《子虛》諸作，司馬相如可謂詭練奇偉矣，而諷一勸百，班固病其失之靡。三篇獨對，賢良稱首，董仲舒正誼明道之學也，而柔行巽入，縱陰閉陽，朱子病其失之雜。是西漢之文也，而非三代
translation_en:
…When events and diction predominate in a classic, it becomes merely a historical record. From Fuxi down to Yao and Shun, the Duke of Zhou and Confucius, their minds were the same and their Way was the same. Thereafter, the seventy disciples died and the subtle teachings ceased; heterodox doctrines arose and the great principles became diluted. One decline brought the Spring and Autumn period; another, the Warring States. The deterioration spread through the Qin and Han, reaching its utmost in the Six Dynasties and Five Dynasties. Although the writings of the pre-Qin and Western Han periods are called outstanding, and Tang prose, through its three transformations, is said to have flourished, people fail to understand that unless learning is inwardly apprehended, writing cannot convey the Way. With ornamented wheels and shafts but no one using it, it is little more than an empty carriage. What, then, is there to esteem? Critics still maintain that writing before the Qin and Han possessed an undivided wholeness. Surely they do not understand writing.
Thus the Discourses of the States (Guoyu) is refined but weak; Liu Zongyuan criticized it, exposing its submissiveness. Zuo’s commentary is articulate and abundant; Han Yu disparaged it, exposing its superficiality. The Strategies of the Warring States (Zhanguo ce) is incisive and skillful; Master Zhu censured its manipulations of alliances and its tactical openings and closures. These are writings of the pre-Qin period, not writings of the Three Dynasties. With his discourse On the Faults of Qin and his policy essay On Public Order, Jia Yi may be said to have understood the essentials of government. Yet Ban Gu faulted his scheme of the “three demonstrations and five baits” as ill-considered. In such works as the Rhapsody on the Imperial Park and the Rhapsody of Master Zixu, Sima Xiangru may be called remarkably polished, extraordinary, and magnificent. Yet, because his admonition amounted to one part and his encouragement of excess to a hundred, Ban Gu faulted him for extravagance. With three examination responses presented personally, Dong Zhongshu was acclaimed foremost among the worthy and good. His learning sought to uphold righteousness and elucidate the Way. Yet, for “acting pliantly and entering submissively, letting yin loose and shutting yang out” [?], Master Zhu faulted him for doctrinal admixture. These are writings of the Western Han, not of the Three Dynasties…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
周邁陵晉魏駸駸焉三代並隆粹乎無以
議爲也而識者尤懼其學蕪則氣漓文卑
則習敝似當反今而復之古者顧愚生章
句何足與論文耶而蠡見管識竊以爲欲
敦文體在正道術欲端士習在崇恬靜而
二者又繫乎重師儒而已夫天章雲漢一
本自然而聖賢敷文要于中正惟夫虛寂
名家騷詞麗則而后文穿天心句攻月脇
者始漸染失真焉蓋背經離本踵謬煽訛
===
大道以多岐亡羊末學以多方喪性而不
知文不法六經雖古猶今也道不師聖賢
雖是猶非也是故莫要乎正道術夫士習
之壞率由徇名而失實實之不孚而名是
徇此所以趨逐聲華汨沒途徑相率競進
而鮮恬退之風耳昔伊吕王佐望也方耕
莘釣濱若將終身及一出而被澤堯舜會
朝清明弼成商周之業者其養素豫也先
正謂靜退之士內有養見善明用心剛者
punctuated:
周，邁陵晉魏，駸駸焉三代並隆，粹乎無以議爲也。而識者尤懼其學蕪則氣漓，文卑則習敝，似當反今而復之古者。顧愚生章句，何足與論文耶？而蠡見管識，竊以爲欲敦文體，在正道術；欲端士習，在崇恬靜；而二者又繫乎重師儒而已。夫天章雲漢，一本自然，而聖賢敷文，要于中正。惟夫虛寂名家，騷詞麗則，而后文穿天心、句攻月脇者，始漸染失真焉。蓋背經離本，踵謬煽訛，大道以多岐亡羊，末學以多方喪性，而不知文不法六經，雖古猶今也；道不師聖賢，雖是猶非也。是故莫要乎正道術。
夫士習之壞，率由徇名而失實。實之不孚，而名是徇，此所以趨逐聲華，汨沒途徑，相率競進，而鮮恬退之風耳。昔伊吕，王佐望也，方耕莘釣濱，若將終身。及一出而被澤堯舜，會朝清明，弼成商周之業者，其養素豫也。先正謂：「靜退之士，內有養，見善明，用心剛者
translation_en:
…Zhou, surpassing the Jin and Wei, advancing swiftly to equal the flourishing of the Three Dynasties, and so pure that there is nothing to criticize. Yet discerning men are especially concerned that neglected learning will dilute its vital spirit, and debased writing will corrupt scholarly habits. It seems that we ought to turn away from present practice and restore antiquity. But how could an ignorant student like myself, occupied with textual minutiae, be qualified to discuss writing? Nevertheless, with my narrow vision and limited understanding, I venture to think that strengthening literary style depends upon rectifying the teachings of the Way; correcting scholars’ habits depends upon honoring tranquility; and both depend upon esteeming teachers and Confucian scholars. The patterned heavens and the Milky Way arise wholly from nature, while the literary expression of sages and worthies takes balance and correctness as its essentials. Only with those who established schools of emptiness and quiescence, and the ornate yet principled language of the Songs of Chu [?], did writers whose prose pierced heaven’s heart and whose sentences assailed the moon’s flank gradually acquire these influences and lose their authenticity. Turning their backs on the Classics and abandoning the foundations, they perpetuated errors and spread falsehoods. On a great road, a sheep is lost because of its many forks; in derivative learning, one’s nature is lost because of its many methods. They fail to understand that writing which does not take the Six Classics as its model, though ancient, is no different from present-day writing; and that a Way which does not take the sages and worthies as its teachers, though seemingly right, is still wrong. Thus nothing is more essential than rectifying the teachings of the Way.
The corruption of scholars’ habits generally results from pursuing reputation and losing substance. When their substance fails to inspire confidence, yet reputation alone is pursued, they chase renown, become submerged in paths of advancement, and lead one another in competing for promotion. Hence the scarcity of a disposition toward tranquility and withdrawal. In former times, Yi Yin and Lü Shang possessed the stature of counselors to kings. While plowing at Shen and fishing by the riverbank, they seemed prepared to spend their entire lives thus. Yet once they emerged, they extended blessings like those of Yao and Shun, brought clarity and order to the royal court, and assisted in establishing the achievements of Shang and Zhou: this was because they had cultivated their unadorned integrity beforehand. A former worthy said: “Scholars who are quiet and retiring, who possess inward cultivation, discern goodness clearly, and are firm in their resolve…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
太極也程氏之易傳也張子之西銘也安
國之序書也以至蔚然而龍翔鳳舞也燦
然而玉珮瓊琚也悠然沛然而大羹玄酒
也長江大河也不事雕琢有心以擬之而
篤實光輝閎中肆外根茂者枝達膏沃者
光燁殆自然而成章者乎所以植天地之
紀宣民物之秘達古今之變竝軼乎三代
之文而眞才輩出世道攸賴矣易曰觀乎
天文以察時變觀乎人文以化成天下此
聖人用賁之道也愚也竊有望焉
第五問
蔡栢齡
同考試官敎諭周批欑李吳興之地一遇水溢
輒不得其疏洩之術是作歷稽往牒參酌時宜眞得古
人治水之要經世之略于此覘之竒士竒士
考試官敎諭管批浙西近多水患當事者所
隱憂也求其鑿鑿可行以為拯溺之助無踰是篇錄之
考試官敎諭李批治水能知源委識時務之
punctuated:
太極也，程氏之易傳也，張子之西銘也，安國之序書也，以至蔚然而龍翔鳳舞也，燦然而玉珮瓊琚也，悠然沛然而大羹玄酒也、長江大河也，不事雕琢、有心以擬之，而篤實光輝，閎中肆外，根茂者枝達，膏沃者光燁，殆自然而成章者乎？所以植天地之紀，宣民物之秘，達古今之變，竝軼乎三代之文，而眞才輩出，世道攸賴矣。《易》曰：「觀乎天文，以察時變；觀乎人文，以化成天下。」此聖人用賁之道也。愚也竊有望焉。
第五問
蔡栢齡
同考試官敎諭周批：欑李吳興之地，一遇水溢，輒不得其疏洩之術。是作歷稽往牒，參酌時宜，眞得古人治水之要，經世之略于此覘之。竒士！竒士！
考試官敎諭管批：浙西近多水患，當事者所隱憂也。求其鑿鑿可行，以為拯溺之助，無踰是篇，錄之。
考試官敎諭李批：治水能知源委，識時務之
translation_en:
…the Supreme Ultimate; Cheng’s Commentary on the Changes; Master Zhang’s Western Inscription; and Anguo’s preface to the Documents. Their luxuriant splendor resembles soaring dragons and dancing phoenixes; their brilliance resembles jade pendants and precious ornaments. Their unhurried abundance resembles plain broth and unadulterated ritual water, or the Yangzi and Yellow Rivers. They do not depend on carving and polishing or deliberate imitation, but are substantial and radiant, expansive within and freely expressed without. Flourishing roots produce spreading branches; rich oil produces a brilliant flame. Do they not, perhaps, form patterned compositions naturally? Thus they establish the ordering principles of Heaven and Earth, disclose the mysteries of people and things, and comprehend changes across past and present. They rival and surpass the writings of the Three Dynasties, while true talents emerge in succession, sustaining the moral order of the world. The Changes says: “Observe the patterns of Heaven to discern changes in the seasons; observe human patterns to transform and bring order to all under Heaven.” This is the sage’s way of employing Adornment, the hexagram Bi. Foolish though I am, I privately cherish hopes for this.
Fifth Question
Cai Boling
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor: Whenever flooding occurs in the areas of Cuanli [probably Zuili, referring to Jiaxing; ?] and Wuxing, an effective method of drainage invariably proves elusive. This essay thoroughly examines earlier records and weighs what is appropriate to present circumstances. It truly grasps the essentials of the ancients’ management of water. Here one can discern its author’s capacity for ordering the world. An exceptional scholar! An exceptional scholar!
Comment by Examiner Guan, Instructor: Western Zhejiang has recently suffered frequent floods, a source of deep concern to those responsible. For proposals that are concrete and practicable, and that can help rescue people from drowning, nothing surpasses this essay. I select it for inclusion.
Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: In managing water, he understands its sources and courses, and recognizes what, in the affairs of the present time, is…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
要者
執事以吾土水利發策豈以澤處之士或
亦有習於經邦之務者乎而愚非其人也
然明問所及敢不攄一得之慮以効其略
焉夫吳越地鉅麗之區而浸藪之奧也自
天下輿圖按其方隅則東南下流之會相
距不千百里而灌注滙溶水半吞之蓋測
其勢高下溟渤尋丈間耳是故畛畷無數
膏腴兼倍壤異所叢鱗甲所集所謂富中
===
之甿貨殖之選他莫能尚焉則利在水也
而控清引濁潰洰淼漫混濤竝瀨潰薄沸
騰則奠居者病而播種者憂之乃其患亦
在水也然則治水之術自古蓋難之矣昔
禹八年飲至水土既平九州已置而末年
南巡乃舉諸侯爲苗山之會夫夏邑宅中
之後未聞禹遍歷方岳也迺苗山玉帛萬
國攸同則豈事游豫爲哉毋亦云玆地水
所瀇浡而巡狩專行則以考其成觀其定
punctuated:
要者。

執事以吾土水利發策，豈以澤處之士，或亦有習於經邦之務者乎？而愚非其人也。然明問所及，敢不攄一得之慮，以効其略焉？夫吳越，地鉅麗之區，而浸藪之奧也。自天下輿圖按其方隅，則東南下流之會，相距不千百里，而灌注滙溶，水半吞之。蓋測其勢，高下溟渤尋丈間耳。是故畛畷無數，膏腴兼倍，壤異所叢，鱗甲所集，所謂富中之甿、貨殖之選，他莫能尚焉，則利在水也。而控清引濁，潰洰淼漫，混濤竝瀨，潰薄沸騰，則奠居者病，而播種者憂之，乃其患亦在水也。然則治水之術，自古蓋難之矣。昔禹八年飲至，水土既平，九州已置，而末年南巡，乃舉諸侯爲苗山之會。夫夏邑宅中之後，未聞禹遍歷方岳也。迺苗山玉帛，萬國攸同，則豈事游豫爲哉？毋亦云玆地水所瀇浡，而巡狩專行，則以考其成，觀其定
translation_en:
…the essentials.

You, honored examiners, have posed a policy question concerning water management in our region. Is this because, among scholars who dwell amid its wetlands, there might be some versed in the affairs of governing the realm? I am not such a person. Yet, since your discerning question touches upon this subject, how could I fail to set forth what little insight I possess and offer an outline of my thinking?

The lands of Wu and Yue form a vast and splendid region, a heartland of lakes and marshes. Examining their position on a map of the realm, one sees that they lie where the waters flowing down toward the southeast converge. Across a span of less than a thousand or even a hundred li [?], waters pour in, collect, and spread, swallowing half the land. Indeed, if one measures its elevation, its level differs from that of the sea by only a few feet. Thus its field paths and boundaries are innumerable, its fertile lands yield manifold abundance, rare products of the soil gather here [?], and fish and other scaled and shelled creatures congregate. Here are what are called prosperous inhabitants and the choicest opportunities for accumulating wealth; nowhere else can surpass it. Its benefits, then, lie in water.

Yet when clear streams are drawn in and turbid waters admitted, when floods spread boundlessly [?], waves mingle and rapids converge, and the waters surge, batter, and boil, those settled here suffer, and those who sow their crops are anxious. Its calamities, too, lie in water. Thus the art of controlling water has indeed been considered difficult since antiquity.

In former times, after eight years, Yu celebrated his return: the waters and lands had been put in order, and the Nine Provinces established. Yet in his later years he toured the south and summoned the regional lords to an assembly at Miaoshan. After the capital of Xia had been established in the central region, we do not hear that Yu traveled to all the sacred mountains of the quarters. Yet at Miaoshan, the myriad states assembled with their jade and silk offerings. Could this have been merely an excursion for pleasure? Was it not rather that this region was where waters swelled and surged, and that he made this particular inspection tour to examine what had been accomplished and observe whether order had been secured …

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
所以爲治之之術或尚不能忘情於旣平
也三代以後民生日繁而畎畆溝澮所需
益廣是故水利爲玆土一大政而百姓俯
仰之資有國征輸之計取給乎此蓋當寰
宇之半矣吾嘗按之古爲吏境內者開鏡
湖於會稽復漢陂於勾章則漢馬臻晉孔
愉也捍錢塘而築之隄浚廣德而疏其隘
則唐白居易任侗也周因令奉化而濬靈
濟陳渾令餘杭而開南湖陸明允疊龍潭
===
之石李濬築陽陂之湖孟簡觀山陰而新
河北開王濟刺杭州而斗門增置諸賢相
繼卓有成績而興利障患全浙賴之卽今
感其德則廟祀遺其愛則名存或呼爲長
官之碶或稱爲資國之渠數千百年如一
日也然自三江旣入震澤底定之後凡治
吳越水者固不止數賢迺其施設大較如
是焉耳自有宋慶曆欲便糧道遂於吳江
築岸橫絶江流蓋自是水流漸紆泥沙易
punctuated: 所以爲治之之術，或尚不能忘情於旣平也。三代以後，民生日繁，而畎畆溝澮所需益廣。是故水利爲玆土一大政，而百姓俯仰之資、有國征輸之計，取給乎此，蓋當寰宇之半矣。吾嘗按之：古爲吏境內者，開鏡湖於會稽、復漢陂於勾章，則漢馬臻、晉孔愉也；捍錢塘而築之隄、浚廣德而疏其隘，則唐白居易、任侗也。周因令奉化而濬靈濟，陳渾令餘杭而開南湖，陸明允疊龍潭之石，李濬築陽陂之湖，孟簡觀山陰而新河北開，王濟刺杭州而斗門增置。諸賢相繼，卓有成績，而興利障患，全浙賴之。卽今感其德則廟祀，遺其愛則名存，或呼爲長官之碶，或稱爲資國之渠，數千百年如一日也。然自三江旣入、震澤底定之後，凡治吳越水者，固不止數賢，迺其施設，大較如是焉耳。自有宋慶曆，欲便糧道，遂於吳江築岸，橫絶江流。蓋自是水流漸紆，泥沙易
translation_en:
…as for the methods by which he brought the waters under control, perhaps he still could not put them out of his mind even after they had been pacified. After the Three Dynasties, the population steadily increased, and the need for field channels and drainage ditches grew ever greater. Thus water management became a major concern of government in this region. The resources on which ordinary people depend to support their households, and the revenues collected and remitted by the state, draw upon this region for what amounts to almost half the total under Heaven.

I have examined the records: among those who held office within this region in antiquity, it was Ma Zhen of the Han who opened Jinghu at Kuaiji, and Kong Yu of the Jin who restored Hanbei at Gouzhang. It was Bai Juyi and Ren Tong of the Tang who respectively built an embankment to protect Qiantang and dredged the waterways of Guangde, clearing their constrictions. Zhou Yin, as Magistrate of Fenghua, dredged Lingji; Chen Hun, as Magistrate of Yuhang, opened Nanhu; Lu Mingyun piled stones at Longtan; and Li Jun constructed the lake at Yangbei. Meng Jian, while overseeing Shanyin, opened a new channel north of the river [?]; Wang Ji, as Prefect of Hangzhou, added sluice gates. These worthy men succeeded one another and achieved outstanding results. All Zhejiang benefited from their promotion of useful works and prevention of calamities. Even today, gratitude for their virtue finds expression in temple sacrifices, and the lasting affection they inspired preserves their names. One work is called the Magistrate’s Sluice, another the Canal That Sustains the State: for hundreds and thousands of years, this remembrance has remained unchanged.

Yet since the Three Rivers were brought into their channels and Zhenze was stabilized, those who have managed the waters of Wu and Yue have certainly included more than these few worthies. Their works were, however, broadly of this kind. In the Qingli era of the Song, an embankment was built at Wujiang to facilitate grain transport, cutting across the river’s flow. From that time onward, the water’s course gradually became more circuitous, and silt and sand readily…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
子之為議則固不可以偏廢者矣
國朝定鼎金陵之日首鑿溧水石河引之北
注而於五堰築壩以辟宣歙池陽九經之
衝則所以治其上流者何固也繼而遣大
臣夏原吉浚夏駕北貫吳塘通劉家港而
導之海周忱浚顧浦以通吳淞而導之海
此其疏浚隄防之績要不後古人之所為
蓋諸郡農桑實
國家百費之資而經畫平成之計固不止導
===
利閭閻之間已也然邇者汎溢之患較歲
為常今則春夏積雨為災滋甚淪垣屋徙
蓬藿怨咨起而和氣傷目擊之憂誠切於
然眉之急者此豈疏治之法或廢於因循
之久而便宜之政或泥於通變之權乎是
故今之為力莫切乎决三江浚諸浦疏涇
港理岸塍禁圍占夷葑葦而凡古人已試
之迹垂成之功不可以不講矣夫三江之
梗以長橋也或者欲决去長橋以快入海
punctuated:
子之為議，則固不可以偏廢者矣。
國朝定鼎金陵之日，首鑿溧水石河，引之北注，而於五堰築壩，以辟宣歙池陽九經之衝，則所以治其上流者何固也！繼而遣大臣夏原吉浚夏駕，北貫吳塘，通劉家港而導之海；周忱浚顧浦，以通吳淞而導之海。此其疏浚隄防之績，要不後古人之所為。蓋諸郡農桑，實國家百費之資，而經畫平成之計，固不止導利閭閻之間已也。
然邇者汎溢之患，較歲為常，今則春夏積雨，為災滋甚。淪垣屋，徙蓬藿，怨咨起而和氣傷。目擊之憂，誠切於然眉之急者。此豈疏治之法或廢於因循之久，而便宜之政或泥於通變之權乎？是故今之為力，莫切乎决三江，浚諸浦，疏涇港，理岸塍，禁圍占，夷葑葦，而凡古人已試之迹、垂成之功，不可以不講矣。夫三江之梗，以長橋也。或者欲决去長橋，以快入海
translation_en:
…as for your proposals, surely none should be neglected in favor of another.
When our dynasty established its capital at Jinling, it first excavated the stone river at Lishui, directing its waters northward, and built dams at Wuyan to avert the onrush from Xuan, She, Chiyang, and the “nine channels” [?]. How firmly it thus brought the upper reaches under control! Subsequently, the high minister Xia Yuanji was dispatched to dredge Xiajia, extend the watercourse north through Wutang, and connect it with Liujiagang, directing the waters into the sea. Zhou Chen dredged Gupu to connect it with the Wusong and direct the waters into the sea. These achievements in dredging and embankment construction were certainly no less than those of the ancients. Agriculture and sericulture in these prefectures supply the resources for the state's myriad expenditures; plans to regulate the waters and bring the land into order therefore serve more than merely the interests of local households.
Recently, however, flooding has become an almost annual occurrence. Now the prolonged rains of spring and summer have made the disaster still worse. Walls and houses are submerged, and the poor are displaced. Complaints arise, and the harmony of the realm is impaired. The distress at witnessing this is indeed more pressing than the urgency of fire singeing one's eyebrows. Could it be that methods of dredging and water management have fallen into disuse through prolonged inertia, and that expedient measures have become mired in the exercise of discretion in adapting to changing circumstances? Thus, nothing is more urgent today than opening the Three Rivers, dredging the tidal channels, clearing the creeks and waterways, repairing banks and field embankments, prohibiting enclosure and encroachment, and clearing aquatic growth and reeds. All the methods already tried by the ancients, and the works they brought toward completion, must be studied. The obstruction of the Three Rivers is due to Changqiao, the Long Bridge. Some propose demolishing Changqiao to speed the waters' passage into the sea…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之道則
國家之漕輓勢所必賴卽易爲木橋廣開其
硔以通之則衝突之憂亦終爲綱運妨焉
然則二者不可計矣若其港汊經泄之所
爲民間所侵認日漸狹小上源諸漾積受
洪流之處爲蘆埂藕蕩所屯結勢已布護
此可不厲禁以清閼閉之患哉故相視開
掘宋乾道間曾詔於王炎圍田堙塞淳熈
間曾請於傅淇而岸東江尾茭蘆沙泥則
===
單鍔之憂又爲拳拳此皆可稽而行之者
彼其時所謂豪右之家肆意圍築而守倅
縣令輒爲給據今得無尚爾乎是不可不
痛滌其弊也侵圍旣去則圩隄當理彼其
時又所謂穿圩岸以便涇浜破古堤以利
漁捕而開挑減少延連隳壞今得無尚爾
乎是又不可不痛滌其弊也或曰江湖草
蕩計畝有納而圍田耕種者歲增賦焉亦
府庫之一需盡欲禁之則少損于公也夫
punctuated:
之道，則國家之漕輓，勢所必賴；卽易爲木橋，廣開其硔以通之，則衝突之憂，亦終爲綱運妨焉。然則二者不可計矣。若其港汊經泄之所，爲民間所侵認，日漸狹小；上源諸漾積受洪流之處，爲蘆埂藕蕩所屯結，勢已布護。此可不厲禁，以清閼閉之患哉？故相視開掘，宋乾道間曾詔於王炎；圍田堙塞，淳熈間曾請於傅淇；而岸東江尾茭蘆沙泥，則單鍔之憂又爲拳拳。此皆可稽而行之者。彼其時所謂豪右之家肆意圍築，而守倅縣令輒爲給據，今得無尚爾乎？是不可不痛滌其弊也。侵圍旣去，則圩隄當理。彼其時又所謂穿圩岸以便涇浜，破古堤以利漁捕，而開挑減少，延連隳壞，今得無尚爾乎？是又不可不痛滌其弊也。
或曰：「江湖草蕩，計畝有納，而圍田耕種者歲增賦焉，亦府庫之一需。盡欲禁之，則少損于公也。」夫
translation_en:
…the passage to the sea, yet the state’s grain transport necessarily depends upon this bridge. Even if it were replaced with a wooden bridge, with its openings widened to let the water through, the danger of collisions would ultimately still obstruct the grain-transport convoys. Thus neither proposal can be entertained. As for the channels and branches through which water drains, private households encroach upon them and claim them as their own, making them narrower by the day. The pools upstream that collect floodwaters have become clogged with reed embankments and lotus ponds, which now form a widespread barrier [?]. Can strict prohibitions be neglected if these blockages are to be cleared?
In the Qiandao reign of the Song, an imperial order was issued to Wang Yan to survey and dredge the waterways. In the Chunxi reign, Fu Qi petitioned concerning the obstruction caused by enclosed fields. And Shan E was deeply concerned about wild rice, reeds, sand, and mud at the eastern banks and river outlets [?]. These are all precedents that can be examined and put into practice. At that time, it was said that powerful families built enclosures at will, while prefects, assistant prefects, and county magistrates readily issued them documentary authorization. Could this still be happening today? Such abuses must be thoroughly eradicated.
Once encroaching enclosures have been removed, the polder dikes must be repaired. At that time, it was also said that people cut through polder banks to facilitate passage through creeks and channels, and breached old dikes to facilitate fishing; meanwhile, dredging diminished and stretches of embankment fell into ruin. Could this still be happening today? These abuses, too, must be thoroughly eradicated.
Someone may say: “Payments are assessed by the mu on reed marshes along rivers and lakes, while those who cultivate enclosed fields add to the tax revenue each year. These also supply the public treasuries. To prohibit them all would somewhat diminish public revenue.” Now …

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
天下利害當較其重利尋尺之入而養深
長之害奚待智者辨之乎或又曰征輸疲
數民勤于力而驅之畚築則恐沈于衆也
夫逸道使民雖勞不怨即其所有之田議
之遠邇揣之厚薄而量工命日則豈厲民
于公乎至若按禹跡大勢則湖之下流莫
要吳淞今得開吳淞與黃浦會則太湖不
足瀉矣然淤澱旣久工力頗浩議者又謂
黃浦吳淞其勢相敵此盛則彼必衰恐吳
===
淞未必通而黃浦先湮則東南之害愈急
以此則吳淞之開不易言矣然澱湖之西
曰急水曰白蜆東曰小漕曰大瀝皆東江
入海之故道今諸港淺狹而東江遂塞則
支流爲未廣至若范家浜劉家港夏駕安
亭諸處凡以達婁江導之海者則今日所
賴矣然潮汐難遏而浚治久疎則壅滯爲
可慮此可不加之意哉古之沿海三十六
浦今入海者惟茜涇七鴉白茆楊林入
punctuated: 天下利害，當較其重。利尋尺之入，而養深長之害，奚待智者辨之乎？或又曰：「征輸疲數，民勤于力，而驅之畚築，則恐沈于衆也。」夫逸道使民，雖勞不怨。即其所有之田，議之遠邇，揣之厚薄，而量工命日，則豈厲民于公乎？至若按禹跡大勢，則湖之下流莫要吳淞。今得開吳淞，與黃浦會，則太湖不足瀉矣。然淤澱旣久，工力頗浩。議者又謂：「黃浦、吳淞，其勢相敵，此盛則彼必衰。恐吳淞未必通，而黃浦先湮，則東南之害愈急。」以此，則吳淞之開不易言矣。然澱湖之西，曰急水，曰白蜆；東曰小漕，曰大瀝，皆東江入海之故道。今諸港淺狹，而東江遂塞，則支流爲未廣。至若范家浜、劉家港、夏駕、安亭諸處，凡以達婁江、導之海者，則今日所賴矣。然潮汐難遏，而浚治久疎，則壅滯爲可慮，此可不加之意哉？古之沿海三十六浦，今入海者惟茜涇、七鴉、白茆、楊林，入
translation_en:
…In weighing benefits and harms to the realm, one must compare their relative importance. To prize a trifling revenue while nurturing profound and enduring harm—why should it take a wise person to distinguish between them? Others say: “Repeated tax levies and deliveries exhaust the people [?]; they already toil hard, and driving them to carry earth and build embankments may burden the multitude [?].” Yet if the people are employed in ways that secure their ease, they will not resent even hard work. Take the fields they possess, consider their distance, assess their fertility, and accordingly apportion the work and prescribe the days of service: how would this be oppressing the people for public purposes?

As for examining the overall configuration of the waterways traced by Yu, no downstream outlet of the lake is more important than the Wusong River. If the Wusong could now be opened to join the Huangpu, Lake Tai would lack sufficient drainage [?]. But the silting has persisted for a long time, and the labor required would be considerable. Those discussing the matter also say: “The Huangpu and Wusong compete in their flow: when one flourishes, the other must decline. We fear that the Wusong might not become navigable while the Huangpu silts up first, making the danger to the southeast still more urgent.” On these grounds, opening the Wusong is not something to advocate lightly.

Yet west of Lake Dian are the waterways called Jishui and Baixian, and to its east those called Xiaocao and Dali. All are former routes by which the Dongjiang reached the sea. Now these channels are shallow and narrow, and the Dongjiang has consequently become blocked; its subsidiary channels are insufficiently broad. As for such places as Fanjiabang, Liujiagang, Xiajia, and Anting, all the channels that connect with the Loujiang and conduct its waters to the sea are what we rely upon today. But the tides are difficult to restrain, and dredging and maintenance have long been neglected, so blockage is a cause for concern. Can we fail to give this our attention? Of the thirty-six coastal channels of antiquity, those that now enter the sea are only Qianjing, Qiya, Baimao, and Yanglin; those entering …

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
者惟福山許浦而已又能按其未浚者求
而導之則散流之途多而四達之勢沛矣
或曰若開諸浦東風駕海水逆注反病民
田不知百川東流有常西激有時單鍔固
巳辨之而可稽也是故近理之湖則水得
所容而橫汎可銷遠濬之江則水得所趨
而壅噎可達然則所謂障患以興利或者
萬一有裨於是乎至若分瀉浙江之議則
所以殺太湖之受而省專治三江之難也
===
蓋自蕭梁大通三年吳興告災遣王奕督
率三郡大圖鑿泄而有此舉然當其時十
郡流移草竊窺伺故昭明太子有吏一呼
門動爲人蠹出丁之處必妨蠶桑之慮上
書止之夫誠以其時不可爲也而擬之今
日則民窮時詘益非可以舉嬴矣然求逸
者不吝其勞圖遠者不泥於近昔賈讓持
上策論漢庭首謂瀕河十郡治隄之費歲
且萬萬及其大决所殘無數如出數年治
punctuated:
者惟福山、許浦而已。又能按其未浚者，求而導之，則散流之途多，而四達之勢沛矣。或曰：「若開諸浦，東風駕海水逆注，反病民田。」不知百川東流有常，西激有時，單鍔固巳辨之，而可稽也。是故近理之湖，則水得所容，而橫汎可銷；遠濬之江，則水得所趨，而壅噎可達。然則所謂障患以興利，或者萬一有裨於是乎？至若分瀉浙江之議，則所以殺太湖之受，而省專治三江之難也。
蓋自蕭梁大通三年，吳興告災，遣王奕督率三郡，大圖鑿泄，而有此舉。然當其時，十郡流移，草竊窺伺，故昭明太子有「吏一呼門，動爲人蠹；出丁之處，必妨蠶桑」之慮，上書止之。夫誠以其時不可爲也，而擬之今日，則民窮時詘，益非可以舉嬴矣。然求逸者不吝其勞，圖遠者不泥於近。昔賈讓持上策論漢庭，首謂瀕河十郡治隄之費，歲且萬萬；及其大决，所殘無數。如出數年治
translation_en:
…those admitting the incoming water are only Fushan and Xupu. If we can also investigate the channels not yet dredged, seek them out, and open them, there will be many routes for dispersing the flow, allowing abundant discharge in every direction. Some say: “If the various tidal channels are opened, easterly winds will drive seawater back into them, harming the people’s fields instead.” They fail to understand that the rivers flow eastward regularly, whereas water is driven westward only at certain times. Shan E has already explained this distinction, and his account can be consulted. Thus, by putting the nearby lakes in order, water will have space to collect, and uncontrolled flooding can be abated; by dredging the rivers farther away, water will have somewhere to go, and obstructions can be cleared. Might this perhaps contribute, however slightly, to what is called preventing harm and promoting benefit? As for the proposal to divert part of the flow into the Zhejiang River, its purpose is to reduce the water entering Lake Tai and lessen the difficulty of relying exclusively on works along the Three Rivers.
This undertaking dates from the third year of Datong under the Xiao-Liang dynasty, when Wuxing reported a disaster and Wang Yi was dispatched to supervise and direct three commanderies in an extensive plan to excavate drainage channels. At that time, however, people in ten commanderies were displaced, and bandits were watching for opportunities. Crown Prince Zhaoming therefore worried that “whenever an official calls at a household’s gate, it readily becomes a scourge to the people; wherever adult males are levied, sericulture will inevitably be disrupted,” and submitted a memorial to stop the work. Indeed, it was because the undertaking was impracticable at that time. Compared with those circumstances, the people today are impoverished and resources constrained, making it still less possible to undertake such a project [?]. Yet those seeking ease do not begrudge the labor needed to achieve it, and those planning for the distant future do not let immediate concerns constrain them. Formerly, when Jia Rang advocated his highest-ranked proposal before the Han court, he began by saying that the ten commanderies bordering the Yellow River spent as much as a hundred million annually on maintaining embankments; when a major breach occurred, the destruction was beyond reckoning. If funds equivalent to several years’ expenditure on managing…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
河之費以業所徙則河定民安千載無患
愚不能不以讓之見酌今日也蓋甞按地
勢之所歸而訊之長老之智者曰天目以
東之水可以自餘杭入德勝出沈塘遵皐
亭下臨平而瀉之江也如此則太湖所納
止孝豐安吉之流而勢減其半昔之淤浸
之田可以復膏壤之舊矣此非有待於經
濟謀猷之士乎然則毋間於浮言毋滿於
近効毋避於嫌毋遜於勢毋阻於怨毋黷
===
於勞則三吳之所賴在茲舉也已而實存
乎其人也夫上古有五官以治五材秦漢
之間天下猶有水工唐宋而下自安定分
科設教後講治水之學於東南者復何人
哉蘇子云古者將有決塞之事必通知經
術之臣計其利害而又水工行視地勢不
得其工不可以濟也又曰三千年之間無
一人能興水利者其學亡也蓋不能無感
於時也
punctuated:
河之費以業所徙，則河定民安，千載無患。愚不能不以讓之見酌今日也。蓋甞按地勢之所歸，而訊之長老之智者，曰：「天目以東之水，可以自餘杭入德勝，出沈塘，遵皐亭，下臨平，而瀉之江也。」如此，則太湖所納止孝豐、安吉之流，而勢減其半，昔之淤浸之田，可以復膏壤之舊矣。此非有待於經濟謀猷之士乎？然則毋間於浮言，毋滿於近効，毋避於嫌，毋遜於勢，毋阻於怨，毋黷於勞，則三吳之所賴在茲舉也已，而實存乎其人也。

夫上古有五官以治五材，秦漢之間，天下猶有水工。唐宋而下，自安定分科設教後，講治水之學於東南者復何人哉？蘇子云：「古者將有決塞之事，必通知經術之臣計其利害，而又水工行視地勢，不得其工，不可以濟也。」又曰：「三千年之間，無一人能興水利者，其學亡也。」蓋不能無感於時也。
translation_en:
…river-management expenses to provide livelihoods for those relocated, then the river would be settled and the people secure, free from calamity for a thousand years. In my humble judgment, I cannot but weigh present circumstances in light of Jia Rang’s views. I once examined the direction in which the terrain channels the waters and consulted knowledgeable elders. They said: “The waters east of Tianmu can be led from Yuhang into Desheng, out through Shentang, along Gaoting, down to Linping, and discharged into the river.” In this way, Lake Tai would receive only the streams from Xiaofeng and Anji, and the force of the inflow would be reduced by half. Fields formerly silted up and inundated could regain their former fertility. Does this not await men skilled in statecraft and planning? Let them neither be swayed by idle talk nor rest content with immediate results; neither shrink from suspicion nor yield to power; neither be obstructed by resentment nor impose labor heedlessly [?]. Then this undertaking would be what the Three Wu regions could rely upon. Yet its realization truly depends upon finding the right men.

In high antiquity, there were five officials to govern the five materials. During the Qin and Han, the realm still had hydraulic specialists. From the Tang and Song onward, since Master Anding established instruction divided into specialized subjects, who else in the southeast has taught the study of water management? Master Su said: “In antiquity, whenever there was a project to open or block a watercourse, ministers thoroughly versed in classical learning had to calculate its benefits and harms, and hydraulic specialists also had to inspect the terrain. Without obtaining the appropriate specialists, the work could not succeed.” He also said: “That in three thousand years not a single person has been able to develop water conservancy is because the learning concerned has been lost.” Surely he could not remain unmoved by the circumstances of his time.

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
浙江鄉試錄後序
今年秋浙江鄉試旣竣事惟
乾以次當序諸錄後序曰夫
浙爲
國家重地列諸藩首豈直山川
鉅麗物産繁茂稱雄長哉惟
乾甞聞諸長老稽之載籍浙
===
故多魁礨瓌奇之士博大通
方之材藉以翼戴其世功烈
著當年而聲光施後世未易
更僕數也昔人推論賢者爲
品物之宗聖帝明王恒汲汲
勤求之且施及方外焉矧玆
首服多賢豪哉我
punctuated:
浙江鄉試錄後序

今年秋，浙江鄉試旣竣事，惟乾以次當序諸錄，後序曰：夫浙爲國家重地，列諸藩首，豈直山川鉅麗、物産繁茂稱雄長哉？惟乾甞聞諸長老，稽之載籍，浙故多魁礨瓌奇之士、博大通方之材，藉以翼戴其世，功烈著當年，而聲光施後世，未易更僕數也。昔人推論賢者爲品物之宗，聖帝明王恒汲汲勤求之，且施及方外焉，矧玆首服多賢豪哉！我
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Zhejiang Provincial Examination

This autumn, after the Zhejiang Provincial Examination had concluded, it fell to me, Weiqian, in due order to compose a postface to its record. The postface reads: Zhejiang is an important region of the realm and ranks foremost among the provinces. Can its preeminence rest merely on the grandeur and beauty of its mountains and rivers and the abundance of its products? I, Weiqian, have heard from elders and verified in written records that Zhejiang has long abounded in outstanding and extraordinary men, men of broad learning and comprehensive understanding, upon whom their age relied for support. Their achievements shone in their own day, and their renown and glory extended to later generations. They could not easily be enumerated even with successive attendants taking turns at the task. The ancients held that the worthy stand foremost among all beings. Sage emperors and enlightened kings constantly sought them with urgent diligence, extending their search even beyond the realm. How much more should this be so in this foremost province, with its many worthy and eminent men! Our…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
國家制試科甚重品式甚詳蓋
誠急之也乃今御史與諸大
夫舉行愈益虔而惟乾亦幸
濫役大方縱觀羣雋之撰即
古賢聖微眇之指當世宏達
之貫靡不爛然具矣譬諸入
寶藏之肆懸黎夜光隋珠和
===
璧紛列錯陳光英滿目即欲
盡收之其將能乎然吾聞之
白璧有考不得爲寶夏璜有
類不得稱珍則稟稟而懼乃
相與畢精勵意竭晝夜之力
掄選之旣收其粹美者登諸
錄則又輒爲諸士欣艶無巳
punctuated: 國家制試科甚重，品式甚詳，蓋誠急之也。乃今御史與諸大夫舉行愈益虔，而惟乾亦幸濫役大方，縱觀羣雋之撰，即古賢聖微眇之指、當世宏達之貫，靡不爛然具矣。譬諸入寶藏之肆，懸黎、夜光、隋珠、和璧，紛列錯陳，光英滿目，即欲盡收之，其將能乎？然吾聞之，白璧有考，不得爲寶；夏璜有類，不得稱珍。則稟稟而懼，乃相與畢精勵意，竭晝夜之力，掄選之。旣收其粹美者登諸錄，則又輒爲諸士欣艶無巳
translation_en:
…the state attaches the greatest importance to its examination system and prescribes its standards and procedures in the fullest detail, truly regarding the search for worthy men as urgent. Now the censor and the other officials conduct the examination with still greater reverence. I, Qian, have also had the good fortune, unworthy though I am, to serve here among learned men. Surveying the compositions of these many outstanding candidates, I find brilliantly represented in them both the subtle meanings of the ancient worthies and sages and the comprehensive understanding of the accomplished men of our age. It is like entering a treasury: Xuanli jade, night-shining pearls, the pearl of the Marquis of Sui, and the jade disk of He lie arrayed in profusion, their brilliance filling the eyes. Even if one wished to gather them all, how could one do so?
Yet I have heard that a white jade disk with a defect [?] cannot count as a treasure, and a Xia jade pendant with a blemish [?] cannot be called precious. We therefore felt apprehension and fear, and together devoted all our concentration and resolve, exerting ourselves day and night to make our selections. Having chosen the purest and finest compositions and entered them in this record, I could not cease rejoicing for these scholars and admiring their good fortune…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
焉夫士野棲谷汲被寬褐而
食藜藿其視尊官顯人分相
懸矣今旣錄無論異時結駟
乘軒秉鈞握斗大章顯也卽
今宴於方岳之堂與中臺貴
臣及藩臬大吏執爵獻酬而
其州閭之父老子弟皆僕僕
===
奔走服役於下其榮光溢爼
豆間矣夫諸士始進未嘗與
國家效咫尺之義而輒徼寵遇
若此夫安得不重念之哉今
鄕人爲賓客受賜於主人歡
然居之無媿色彼其心自謂
可不旋踵效爾乃若顧其囊
punctuated: 焉。夫士野棲谷汲，被寬褐而食藜藿，其視尊官顯人，分相懸矣。今旣錄，無論異時結駟乘軒，秉鈞握斗，大章顯也；卽今宴於方岳之堂，與中臺貴臣及藩臬大吏執爵獻酬，而其州閭之父老子弟皆僕僕奔走，服役於下，其榮光溢爼豆間矣。夫諸士始進，未嘗與國家效咫尺之義，而輒徼寵遇若此，夫安得不重念之哉？今鄕人爲賓客，受賜於主人，歡然居之，無媿色，彼其心自謂可不旋踵效爾。乃若顧其囊
translation_en:
… Indeed, these scholars have dwelt in the countryside and drawn water from the valleys, wearing loose garments of coarse cloth and eating goosefoot and bean leaves. Their station has been far removed from that of eminent officials and distinguished men. Now that they have been selected, let us leave aside the great distinction they may attain in days to come—riding in lofty carriages drawn by teams of four and wielding the authority of government. Even now they banquet in the hall of the provincial authorities, raising cups and exchanging toasts with honored ministers of the Censorate and senior officials of the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions. Meanwhile, the elders and younger men of their home communities bustle about below, attending to their needs. Their glory already overflows among the ceremonial vessels of the feast.

These scholars are only beginning their advancement and have yet to render the slightest service to the state, yet already they receive such favor. How can they fail to reflect deeply upon it? When a fellow villager becomes a guest and receives gifts from his host, he accepts them gladly and without embarrassment because he believes he can repay them almost at once. But if he looks into his purse …

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
空無以復則未有不內慙而
却者也以吾闚觀諸士蓋皆
懷兼資之器挾鴻鉅之筴非
徒調吻搖筆以文辭振奇而
已吾固知慙而却免矣然自
玆以往被恩益深其於賓客
之賜俎豆之榮又奚啻萬之
===
也寧不思所自效哉人之言
曰烏號之弓谿子之弩不能
無弦而射越舲蜀艇不能無
水而浮言用未具也故夫尹
之耕野也無能利其里及起
佐商則德施乎四海仁非加
益也處便而勢利也今諸士
punctuated:
空，無以復，則未有不內慙而却者也。以吾闚觀，諸士蓋皆懷兼資之器，挾鴻鉅之筴，非徒調吻搖筆，以文辭振奇而已。吾固知慙而却免矣。然自玆以往，被恩益深，其於賓客之賜、俎豆之榮，又奚啻萬之也！寧不思所自效哉？
人之言曰：「烏號之弓，谿子之弩，不能無弦而射；越舲蜀艇，不能無水而浮。」言用未具也。故夫尹之耕野也，無能利其里；及起佐商，則德施乎四海。仁非加益也，處便而勢利也。今諸士
translation_en:
…empty, with nothing to offer in return, there is no one who would not feel inwardly ashamed and withdraw. From what I have observed, you gentlemen all possess manifold abilities and hold grand plans; you do more than merely ply your lips and wield your brushes, displaying extraordinary skill in literary composition. I am therefore certain that you will be spared such shame and withdrawal. Yet from this point onward, the favor you receive will grow ever greater: compared with the gifts bestowed upon guests and the honor of the ceremonial banquet, it will be more than ten thousand times as great! How could you fail to consider how to render service in return?
As people say: “The Wuhao bow and the Xizi crossbow cannot shoot without strings; the boats of Yue and the skiffs of Shu cannot float without water.” This means that the conditions necessary for their use are not yet in place. Thus, when Yi Yin tilled the fields, he could do nothing to benefit his village; once he arose to assist the Shang, his beneficence extended throughout the realm. His benevolence had not increased: his position afforded opportunity, and his circumstances favored its exercise. Now you gentlemen…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
襃然充賦于有司已釋耕而
嚮用矣况今
天子神聖壽考自堯舜周文以來
數千年間始一見焉諸士旣
幸生其時又列首藩多賢之
地豈非千載所希覯哉吾且
計諸士爭欲自效於
===
明時其心有勃勃乎不可遏者誠
無俟於人之慫慂之也乃吾
猶言之不置則以一時相成
之義云爾序旣具先以質御
史御史覽而顧諸大夫曰言
可書也於是遂書之
廣東肇慶府高明縣儒學教
punctuated:
襃然充賦于有司，已釋耕而嚮用矣。况今，天子神聖壽考，自堯舜周文以來，數千年間始一見焉。諸士旣幸生其時，又列首藩多賢之地，豈非千載所希覯哉？吾且計諸士爭欲自效於明時，其心有勃勃乎不可遏者，誠無俟於人之慫慂之也。乃吾猶言之不置，則以一時相成之義云爾。序旣具，先以質御史。御史覽而顧諸大夫曰：「言可書也。」於是遂書之。
廣東肇慶府高明縣儒學教
translation_en:
…have been honorably presented to the responsible authorities as selected candidates, and have already left their plowing behind to be employed in service. Moreover, the present Son of Heaven is divinely sagacious and blessed with longevity: since Yao, Shun, and King Wen of Zhou, such a sovereign has appeared only once in several thousand years. You gentlemen have had the good fortune to be born in his time and, furthermore, to stand among the many worthy men of this foremost province. Is this not an encounter rarely granted in a thousand years? I imagine that you are all eager to offer your service in this enlightened age, your aspirations surging irrepressibly within you, truly needing no encouragement from others. Yet I continue to speak of it without cease, simply out of the duty we owe to help one another fulfill our purposes while we are together.
Once the preface was complete, I first submitted it to the Censor for his judgment. Having read it, the Censor turned to the assembled officials and said, “These words deserve to be recorded.” Accordingly, I set them down.
The Instructor at the Confucian School of Gaoming County, Zhaoqing Prefecture, Guangdong …

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江鄉試錄
text: 諭管惟乾謹序
punctuated: 諭管惟乾謹序。
translation_en: …Instructor Guan Weiqian respectfully composed this preface.
